The audience only needs to understand that she decided to go out. The exact mechanics of opening the umbrella are not evidence in the story. If the scene instead says, “The umbrella rib catches a key hidden inside; the key falls and someone steps on it,” the intermediate action carries the reveal and should be shown in a separate shot.

heading.zh: 首尾帧最常见的失败与修正
heading.en: Common First-and-Last-Frame Failures and Fixes

body.zh:
| 失败 | 后果 | 修正 |
|---|---|---|
| 首帧已经写“打翻后的水迹” | 终点事实提前出现 | 删除尚未发生的结果，只保留起点 |
| 尾帧人物持物与剧本终点不同 | 两套终点互相争夺 | 以镜头终点为准重写尾帧 |
| 两端差异过大 | 中间运动自由度过高 | 缩小变化或拆镜 |
| 关键动作只藏在两帧之间 | 可能没被清楚呈现 | 让动作落在边界，或另设镜头 |
| 两帧分别独立设计构图 | 方位、轴线和光位跳变 | 先定同一空间关系与保持项 |
| 静帧里写“先、再、随后” | 一张图承载时间序列 | 每帧只写可冻结的一瞬 |
body.en:
| Failure | Consequence | Correction |
|---|---|---|
| The first frame already includes “water left after the spill” | An end-state fact appears too early | Remove results that have not happened and retain only the starting state |
| The object held in the last frame conflicts with the script’s endpoint | Two endpoint definitions compete | Rewrite the last frame from the shot endpoint |
| The difference between the frames is too large | The intermediate motion has too much freedom | Reduce the change or split the shot |
| A crucial action exists only between the frames | It may never appear clearly | Put the action on a boundary or give it another shot |
| Each frame receives an independently designed composition | Direction, axis, and light position jump | Define one spatial relationship and its preservation constraints first |
| A still-frame description says “first, then, afterward” | One image is asked to carry a time sequence | Describe only one freezable instant per frame |

q.zh: 首尾帧中间乱动怎么办？
q.en: What if the motion between the first and last frames becomes unstable?

a.zh: 先判断中间路径是否重要。若不重要，缩小两端差异并加强身份、空间和光位保持项；若重要，把关键动作拆成独立镜头或明确动作顺序，不要继续靠两张图猜。
a.en: First decide whether the intermediate path matters. If it does not, reduce the difference between the two frames and strengthen the identity, spatial, and lighting constraints. If it does, split the key action into separate shots or specify the action order instead of asking two images to imply it.

q.zh: 每个镜头都需要首尾帧吗？
q.en: Does every shot need both a first and a last frame?

a.zh: 不需要。默认用能说明起点的一张关键帧即可。只有制作流程确实需要控制终点，且镜头适合插值时才增加尾帧。
a.en: No. One keyframe that defines the start state is often enough. Add a last frame only when the production process genuinely needs to control the endpoint and the shot is suitable for interpolation.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /short-drama-storyboard 判断这个镜头是否适合首尾帧；分别写只属于起点和终点的静态画面，并指出中间必须明确的动作或需要拆镜之处”（Codex 里写作 `$short-drama-storyboard`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/short-drama-storyboard` to decide whether this shot suits first-and-last-frame generation. Write separate static descriptions containing only the start and end states, then identify any intermediate action that must be explicit or should become another shot.” In Codex, write `$short-drama-storyboard`.

title.zh: AI视频不满意：重抽、改提示词还是补拍？
title.en: Unsatisfied with an AI Video? Reroll, Rewrite, Edit, or Reshoot

seo_title.zh: AI视频重抽还是改提示词｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: Fix an AI Video: Reroll or Rewrite the Prompt?

description.zh: AI 视频结果不满意时，先判断缺陷是否受文字控制、是否重复出现。随机失败可有界重抽，结构性失败要改写，局部缺陷可编辑或补拍。
description.en: Ask if text controls the flaw and if it repeats. Reroll random failures sparingly, rewrite structural flaws, and edit or reshoot local defects.

answer.zh: AI 视频不满意时，先别立即堆提示词。若原提示已经清楚，失败看起来随机，可以设上限重抽；若同一缺陷反复出现，说明文字或镜头结构有问题，应拆镜、减少并发动作或改实现路径；若只有一层局部错误，保留正确部分做局部编辑；文字、混音或边缘帧问题则交给后期。
answer.en: When an AI video falls short, do not immediately add more prompt text. If the original prompt is clear and the failure looks random, reroll within a preset limit. If the same defect repeats, revise the text or shot structure: split the shot, reduce simultaneous actions, or change the execution path. If only one local layer is wrong, preserve the correct material and edit that layer. Leave text, mixing, and edge-frame problems to post-production.

heading.zh: AI视频“抽卡”是什么意思？
heading.en: What Does “Rerolling” an AI Video Mean?

body.zh:
“抽卡”通常指在输入基本不变时反复生成，希望随机结果更好。它不是修复方法，只适用于文字已经明确、参考与镜头边界也没有明显矛盾，而一次失败看起来像偶然波动的情况。

如果每次人物都在同一处交错、同一道具都错误易手，继续重抽不会增加理解，只会重复支付同一个问题。此时应改结构。别再叠加“高质量、稳定、不要变形”。
body.en:
“Rerolling” means generating again with substantially the same input in the hope that randomness produces a better result. It is not a repair method. Use it only when the wording is already clear, references and shot boundaries do not conflict, and one failure looks accidental.

If characters cross at the same point every time or the same prop repeatedly changes hands incorrectly, another reroll will not clarify the request; it only pays for the same problem again. Change the structure instead of stacking phrases such as “high quality,” “stable,” or “no deformation.”

heading.zh: 先用两个判断分流
heading.en: Use Two Questions to Choose the Repair Path

body.zh:
**判断一：缺陷是否在提示词能控制的范围？** 字幕拼写、混音、调色、少量边缘帧等问题，未必需要改提示词。身份资产不一致要回到角色或道具参考；空间边界错要回分镜。

**判断二：同一缺陷是否重复出现？** 第一次可能随机；多次在同一位置复现，优先视为要求冲突、动作过载或边界不清。

| 情况 | 处置 |
|---|---|
| 镜头目的已达成，瑕疵不影响理解 | 保留 |
| 问题属于字幕、声音、调色或修剪 | 后期处理 |
| 构图和表演大体正确，只有一层错 | 局部编辑 |
| 文字无明显缺陷，失败像随机波动 | 有上限地重抽 |
| 同一缺陷重复，或要求互相竞争 | 改写、拆镜或换路径 |
body.en:
**Question 1: Is the defect controllable through the prompt?** Subtitle spelling, audio mixing, color grading, and a few bad edge frames may not require a prompt change. An identity mismatch returns to the character or prop reference; a wrong spatial boundary returns to the storyboard.

**Question 2: Does the same defect repeat?** One occurrence may be random. Repetition at the same point suggests competing requirements, overloaded action, or an unclear boundary.

| Situation | Response |
|---|---|
| The shot communicates its purpose and the flaw does not impede understanding | Keep it |
| The problem concerns subtitles, sound, grading, or trimming | Fix in post |
| Composition and performance are largely correct; one layer is wrong | Edit locally |
| The prompt has no obvious defect and the failure looks random | Reroll within a limit |
| The defect repeats or requirements compete | Rewrite, split the shot, or change the path |

heading.zh: 改提示词时只动诊断指向的一层
heading.en: When Rewriting the Prompt, Change Only the Diagnosed Layer

body.zh:
> **镜头目的保持**：观众必须看懂什么？
>
> **直接观察**：只写实际看到的缺陷，不猜原因。
>
> **可能定位**：动作、表演、构图、摄影、参考或起止边界中的哪一层？
>
> **本次只改**：一个必要变量；必须联动时说明原因。
>
> **必须保持**：角色身份、场景方向、已经正确的动作、终点义务。
>
> **预期变化**：下一版应出现什么可观察差异？

没有实际生成结果可看时，只能指出文字风险，不能声称某种失败已经发生。
body.en:
> **Preserve the shot purpose:** What must viewers understand?
>
> **Direct observation:** Describe only the visible defect; do not guess its cause.
>
> **Likely layer:** Action, performance, composition, camera, reference, or start/end boundary?
>
> **Change this time:** One necessary variable; explain any required linked change.
>
> **Must remain:** Character identity, scene direction, actions already working, and endpoint obligations.
>
> **Expected difference:** What observable change should the next version show?

Without an actual generated result to inspect, you may identify textual risks but cannot claim that a particular failure occurred.

heading.zh: 原创范例：售票窗递信镜头
heading.en: Original Example: Delivering a Letter at a Ticket Window

body.zh:
原要求：快递员从窗口递入信封，售票员接住、低头看署名、表情由疑惑变惊恐，背景旅客同时拥挤催促，摄影机绕到窗口内。

**假设观察**：如果生成结果中信封交接不清，但人物和空间正确，可以先核对文字：递交、接住、看署名、情绪变化、群演动作和绕拍同时堆叠，存在要求竞争的风险。此时先简化镜头，再比较交接动作是否更清楚；这是一种诊断示例，不是实际生成记录。

**改写方案**：

- 母版保留快递员递信与售票员接住，固定侧面机位，背景旅客只保持排队压力。
- 补拍一条信封署名特写，承担“看见名字”。
- 再用售票员近景承担惊恐反应。

拆分后要逐项确认：递信由母版承担，署名由补拍承担，反应由近景承担；不能把提示词缩短后，让原来重要的反应无人负责。
body.en:
Original request: a courier passes an envelope through the window; the clerk takes it, looks down at the signature, and changes from confusion to fear. Travelers crowd and complain behind them while the camera moves around to the inside of the booth.

**Hypothetical observation:** If a generated result makes the handoff unclear while character identity and space remain correct, inspect the wording first. Passing, receiving, reading, reacting, crowd movement, and a moving camera compete for attention. Simplify the shot, then compare whether the handoff becomes clearer. This is a diagnostic example, not a record of an actual generation.

**Rewrite plan:**

- Keep the courier’s handoff and the clerk’s receipt in the master shot. Lock a side view; the travelers provide only queue pressure.
- Add a close-up of the name on the envelope to carry “sees the signature.”
- Use a separate close-up for the clerk’s fearful reaction.

After splitting, account for every requirement: the master carries the handoff, the insert carries the name, and the close-up carries the reaction. Shortening a prompt must not leave an important beat without a shot.

heading.zh: 什么时候可以重抽？
heading.en: When Is Another Reroll Worth Trying?

body.zh:
重抽前满足三个条件：原文要求彼此不冲突；起点、终点和参考没有明显错误；你能说明本次重抽是在验证一次随机失败。设定尝试上限，到点就重新判断。

重抽时保持输入版本可比。若每次同时改构图、动作和参考，就无法知道改善来自哪里。反过来，改写时也只改诊断指向的变量，保留已经正确的部分。
body.en:
Reroll only when three conditions hold: the original requirements do not conflict; the start, endpoint, and references contain no obvious error; and you can explain that this reroll tests a likely random failure. Set a limit in advance and reassess when you reach it.

Keep inputs comparable. If every attempt changes composition, action, and reference together, you cannot tell what improved the result. When rewriting, likewise change only the diagnosed variable and preserve what already works.

heading.zh: 生成视频不满意时的常见误区
heading.en: Common Mistakes When an AI Video Falls Short

body.zh:
| 误区 | 正确做法 |
|---|---|
| 所有问题都改提示词 | 先路由到资产、分镜、视频或后期 |
| 加一串“高质量、稳定” | 增加可执行的空间、动作或边界事实 |
| 同一缺陷无限重抽 | 复现后改结构 |
| 一处错就重写整条 | 只编辑错误层，声明保持项 |
| 补拍自动替代母版 | 写清每项原要求由谁承担 |
| 只记录“效果不好” | 写可观察事实和对应版本 |

目标是用最小改动消除已经定位的问题，同时保住镜头原本正确的内容。
body.en:
| Mistake | Better response |
|---|---|
| Rewrite the prompt for every problem | Route the issue to assets, storyboard, video, or post first |
| Add a string of “high quality” and “stable” | Add executable spatial, action, or boundary facts |
| Reroll the same repeating defect indefinitely | Change the structure once it reproduces |
| Rewrite the whole shot because one part is wrong | Edit only the faulty layer and declare what stays fixed |
| Assume a pickup shot replaces the master automatically | State which shot carries every original requirement |
| Record only “the result is bad” | Record an observable fact and its version |

The goal is the smallest change that removes the diagnosed problem while preserving what the shot already does correctly.

q.zh: AI视频生成不满意，先改哪一句？
q.en: If an AI video is unsatisfactory, which line should I change first?

a.zh: 先不要改句子。先写出可观察缺陷，再判断它属于身份资产、空间构图、动作表演、声音文字还是后期。只有定位到提示词层，才改对应要求。
a.en: Do not change a line yet. Describe the observable defect, then classify it as an identity asset, spatial composition, action performance, sound or text, or post-production issue. Rewrite only after the diagnosis reaches the prompt layer.

q.zh: 同一提示词可以重抽几次？
q.en: How many times should I reroll the same prompt?

a.zh: 没有跨项目通用次数。根据成本和风险预先设上限；一旦同一缺陷稳定复现，就停止重抽，改结构或实现路径。
a.en: There is no universal number. Set a limit in advance from cost and risk. Once the same defect repeats consistently, stop rerolling and change the structure or execution path.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /short-drama-review 根据我提供的准确版本和观察，判断应保留、后期、局部编辑、有限重抽还是改写；说明只改什么、保持什么，不虚构生成结果”（Codex 里写作 `$short-drama-review`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/short-drama-review` to decide whether this version should be kept, fixed in post, edited locally, rerolled within a limit, or rewritten, based only on the exact version and observations I provide. State what to change and what to preserve; do not invent generation results.” In Codex, write `$short-drama-review`.

title.zh: 网文大纲怎么写：长篇小说大纲模板与分卷范例
title.en: How to Write a Web-Fiction Outline: Template and Volume Example

seo_title.zh: 网文大纲怎么写：长篇模板｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: Web-Fiction Outline Template and Volume Example

description.zh: 长篇小说大纲先定核心卖点、终点和卷高潮，再倒推阶段目标、障碍与因果。附可复制的全书—分卷—场景三层模板和原创范例。
description.en: Set core appeal, ending, and volume climaxes first; work back through goals, obstacles, and causality. Includes a book–volume–scene template and example.

answer.zh: 网文大纲不要从第一章一路顺写。先用一句话定下主角要完成的事，再确定结局和各卷高潮，倒推每卷必须改变的局面；最后才安排可调整的场景。全书方向要稳定，分卷路径可修，具体对白和小场面留到写作时决定。
answer.en: Do not write a web-novel outline straight through from Chapter One. State in one sentence what the protagonist must accomplish, then decide the ending and each volume climax. Work backward to the situation each volume must change, and only then arrange flexible scenes. Keep the book-level direction stable, allow volume routes to evolve, and leave exact dialogue and minor scenes for drafting.

heading.zh: 长篇大纲先写哪一层？
heading.en: Which Layer of a Long-Form Outline Should You Write First?

body.zh:
大纲让几十万字始终朝同一个终点运动，无需预写正文。最实用的分法是三层：

| 层级 | 回答的问题 | 稳定程度 |
|---|---|---|
| 全书骨架 | 主角最终要完成什么，为什么非他不可 | 尽量稳定 |
| 分卷路线 | 这一卷改变哪种局面，高潮如何证明改变 | 可以调整 |
| 场景备忘 | 哪个场景、线索或对话可能完成节点 | 随写随改 |

这与[章纲模板](/oh-story/chapter-outline-template)不同：全书大纲管方向，章纲只管最近几章怎样落地。若上层目标不清，写再细的章纲也只是把迷路写得更具体。
body.en:
An outline keeps hundreds of thousands of words moving toward one endpoint without prewriting the prose. Three layers are usually enough:

| Layer | Question it answers | Stability |
|---|---|---|
| Book framework | What must the protagonist ultimately accomplish, and why must it be this person? | Keep as stable as possible |
| Volume route | What situation changes in this volume, and how does the climax prove it? | Adjustable |
| Scene notes | Which scene, clue, or line might complete a beat? | Revise while drafting |

This differs from the [chapter-outline template](/oh-story/chapter-outline-template): the book outline governs direction; the chapter outline governs the next few chapters. If the upper-level goal is unclear, a detailed chapter plan only describes getting lost more precisely.

heading.zh: 可复制的长篇小说大纲模板
heading.en: Reusable Web-Novel Outline Template

body.zh:
按下面顺序填，不必一次填满所有支线：

> **核心卖点**：读者持续来看哪种独特体验？
>
> **主角起点**：他缺什么、受什么限制、最怕失去什么？
>
> **全书目标**：他要完成的一件可判断成败的事。
>
> **终局选择**：高潮时他必须在什么之间作选择？选择会证明怎样的成长？
>
> **结局状态**：外部局面、核心关系、主角认知分别变成什么？
>
> **分卷卡**：本卷目标｜主要障碍｜新策略｜高潮对决｜局部兑现｜遗留压力。
>
> **跨卷线**：主线怎样升级；哪条关系或秘密在哪卷推进、在哪卷兑现。
>
> **当前写作窗口**：只细化接下来一段的目标、阻力、结果和下一步期待。

先写终局选择与每卷高潮，再倒推需要提前建立的人物、能力、关系和证据。这样伏笔来自结局需要，避免写到哪儿临时塞到哪儿。
body.en:
Fill these in order; you do not need every subplot at once:

> **Core appeal:** What distinctive experience keeps readers returning?
>
> **Protagonist’s start:** What do they lack, what constrains them, and what do they most fear losing?
>
> **Book-level goal:** One action whose success or failure can be judged.
>
> **Final choice:** What must they choose between at the climax, and what growth does the choice prove?
>
> **Ending state:** How do the external situation, central relationship, and protagonist’s understanding change?
>
> **Volume card:** Volume goal | main obstacle | new strategy | climax | partial payoff | remaining pressure.
>
> **Across-volume lines:** How does the main plot escalate? In which volume does each relationship or secret advance and pay off?
>
> **Current writing window:** Detail only the next segment’s goal, resistance, result, and next expectation.

Write the final choice and volume climaxes first. Then work backward to the characters, abilities, relationships, and evidence that must be established. Setup now grows from the ending’s needs instead of being inserted wherever the draft happens to reach.

heading.zh: 原创分卷范例：《潮汐修复师》
heading.en: Original Volume Example: “Tide Restorer”

body.zh:
**核心卖点**：能“听见”旧机械故障记忆的修复师，在沿海灾害中用手艺追查被人为掩盖的工程真相。

**全书目标**：许澄必须在下一次大潮前修复主闸，并证明连环故障来自人为换件。终局中，她发现父亲当年背锅是为了保住整套临时防线；若立刻公开证据，全城会在撤离前陷入恐慌。她选择先完成封潮，再公开完整责任链。

| 卷 | 阶段目标 | 高潮与改变 | 留给下一卷的压力 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 盐湾旧闸 | 取得维修资格 | 她在众人认定报废时救回支闸，证明手艺可信 | 故障零件被人换过 |
| 城南泵站 | 找到替换链条 | 她公开测试让承包方无法甩锅，却失去行业背书 | 主闸图纸缺了一页 |
| 退潮档案 | 找回当年记录 | 同伴承认藏过图纸，关系破裂又重建 | 大潮提前，证据与救城只能先选一个 |
| 封潮之夜 | 修闸并完成追责 | 手艺、证据与关系线在同一场行动汇合 | 结局展示城市采用透明维护制度 |

具体到第一卷，只需继续拆“拿到资格—第一次误判—发现换件—支闸抢修”几个节点，不必提前写完第四卷的每场对白。
body.en:
**Core appeal:** A restorer who can “hear” memories of failure in old machinery uses her craft during coastal disasters to trace an engineering truth that someone concealed.

**Book-level goal:** Xu Cheng must repair the main floodgate before the next high tide and prove that the chain of failures came from deliberately substituted parts. At the climax, she learns that her father accepted blame to preserve the entire temporary defense line. Publishing the evidence immediately would throw the city into panic before evacuation. She chooses to seal out the tide first, then disclose the complete chain of responsibility.

| Volume | Stage goal | Climax and change | Pressure for the next volume |
|---|---|---|---|
| The Old Gate at Salt Bay | Qualify to perform repairs | She saves an auxiliary gate everyone had written off, proving her skill | Someone replaced the failed part |
| South-City Pumping Station | Trace the replacement chain | Her public test prevents the contractor from shifting blame, but she loses industry backing | One page is missing from the main-gate plans |
| Ebb-Tide Archive | Recover the old records | A companion admits hiding the plans; their relationship breaks and is rebuilt | The tide arrives early, forcing a choice between preserving evidence and saving the city first |
| The Night the Tide Is Sealed | Repair the gate and establish accountability | Craft, evidence, and relationships converge in one action | The ending shows the city adopting transparent maintenance records |

For Volume One, expand only “earn qualification → make the first wrong judgment → discover the substituted part → rush to repair the auxiliary gate.” There is no need to script every conversation in Volume Four.

heading.zh: 从空白到可写：按高潮倒推
heading.en: From Blank Page to Writable Plan: Work Backward from the Climax

body.zh:
先写主角的起点与终点，使变化可见；再写最大冲突中的选择，而不只是“大决战”。接着问：主角凭什么做出这个选择？缺少的能力、关系和证据，就成为前面各卷的节点。

每卷也用同一方法：先定卷末高潮，再给卷初一个可理解的阶段目标；在两者之间安排会迫使主角换策略的障碍。支线只有在帮助主线、制造代价或最终与主线汇合时才保留。写到一半偏航时，先检查当前行动是否仍服务阶段目标，无需立刻推倒全部内容。
body.en:
Define the protagonist’s starting and ending states so the change is visible. Then write the choice inside the greatest conflict, not merely “a final battle.” Ask what enables the protagonist to make that choice. Missing ability, relationship, and evidence become earlier volume beats.

Use the same method within each volume: choose the ending climax, give the opening an understandable stage goal, and place obstacles between them that force a change of strategy. Keep a subplot only when it helps the main plot, creates a cost, or eventually converges with it. If the draft drifts, first ask whether the current action still serves the stage goal; do not immediately discard the entire outline.

heading.zh: 长篇大纲常见失败与改法
heading.en: Common Long-Form Outline Failures and Fixes

body.zh:
| 失败 | 为什么会卡 | 改法 |
|---|---|---|
| 把“升级变强”当主线 | 它是行动，不是可完成的事情 | 改成“为了什么而变强” |
| 从开头顺推到哪算哪 | 后段高潮没有前置条件 | 先写高潮选择，再倒推铺垫 |
| 每卷只是换地图重来 | 局面没有积累性变化 | 让上一卷结果制造下一卷问题 |
| 支线很多但彼此不碰 | 篇幅增加，主线不前进 | 写清支线最终帮助、阻碍或改写什么 |
| 大纲写成场景全文 | 新发现无法进入故事 | 上层固定，细节层保留调整空间 |

判断大纲是否够用，只需看你能否回答：下一阶段追求什么、谁在阻挡、失败会失去什么、高潮将改变什么。
body.en:
| Failure | Why it causes a block | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Treat “level up and grow stronger” as the main plot | It is an activity, not a completable objective | State what the strength is for |
| Plan forward until ideas run out | Later climaxes lack prerequisites | Write the climactic choice first and work backward |
| Every volume restarts on a new map | The situation never accumulates change | Let one volume’s result create the next volume’s problem |
| Many subplots never meet | Length grows while the main plot stands still | State what each subplot ultimately helps, obstructs, or rewrites |
| The outline becomes full scene prose | New discoveries cannot enter the story | Fix the upper layers and leave detail adjustable |

An outline is usable when you can answer four questions: What does the next stage pursue? Who blocks it? What is lost on failure? What will the climax change?

q.zh: 细纲和章纲有什么区别？
q.en: What is the difference between a beat outline and a chapter outline?

a.zh: 细纲描述一段剧情要达到的目的和效果；章纲把最近的关键事件、伏笔与章末期待分配到章节。若看分卷路线已能开写，不必为了完整而补章纲。
a.en: A beat outline describes the purpose and effect of a passage. A chapter outline assigns near-term events, setup, and end-of-chapter expectations to chapters. If the volume route already lets you draft, do not add chapter detail merely for completeness.

q.zh: 长篇大纲写完还能改吗？
q.en: Can I revise a long-form outline after drafting begins?

a.zh: 可以。具体路径和场景应随正文修订，但核心卖点、全书目标和已建立的因果不能无代价改掉。先判断变化发生在哪一层，只改必要层。
a.en: Yes. Specific routes and scenes should evolve with the prose. Changing the core appeal, book-level goal, or established causality carries a larger cost. Identify the layer that changed and revise only that layer.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /story-long-write 只做长篇大纲：先定核心卖点、全书目标与终局选择，再倒推分卷高潮和阶段节点；具体场景只细化当前写作窗口，不写正文”（Codex 里写作 `$story-long-write`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/story-long-write` only to build the long-form outline. Establish the core appeal, book-level goal, and final choice, then work backward through volume climaxes and stage beats. Detail specific scenes only inside the current writing window, and do not draft the prose.” In Codex, write `$story-long-write`.

title.zh: 写小说卡文了怎么办：先诊断，再写下一步
title.en: Stuck Writing a Novel? Diagnose the Block and Write the Next Step

seo_title.en: How to Overcome Writer's Block in Fiction

description.zh: 写小说卡文先分清是目标、阻力、因果、场景还是精力出了问题。用“下一步会改变什么”找到最小可写动作，避免靠新设定和随机事故续命。
description.en: Diagnose goal, resistance, causality, scene or energy. Ask what the next step changes to find one writable action; avoid new lore and random accidents.

answer.zh: 卡文时不要先逼自己多写。先用一句话回答“主角当前要完成什么”，再检查阻力是否会真实反制、上一段结果是否制造了下一步、当前场景是否必须发生。找不到答案就修大纲；答案清楚但句子出不来就先写动作骨架；持续疲惫则缩小任务并休息，别用新角色或天降事故掩盖问题。
answer.en: When you are stuck on a novel, do not force more words. State in one sentence what the protagonist must accomplish now. Check whether the opposition can truly counter, whether the previous result creates the next move, and whether this scene must happen. If you cannot answer, repair the outline. If the answer is clear but sentences will not come, write an action skeleton. If exhaustion persists, reduce the task and rest. Do not hide the problem behind a new character or an arbitrary accident.

heading.zh: 卡文先看是哪一类
heading.en: First Diagnose What Kind of Writer’s Block You Have

body.zh:
| 症状 | 真正缺的东西 | 先做什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 不知道下一章写什么 | 阶段目标或后果 | 写出主角下一步必须完成的事 |
| 有事件但很平 | 能反制的阻力 | 给对方自己的目标和筹码 |
| 每章都像重复 | 策略没有变化 | 让旧方法失效，迫使主角换办法 |
| 知道剧情却写不出句子 | 场景动作骨架 | 先列进入状态、动作、反应、结果 |
| 什么都不想碰 | 注意力或精力耗尽 | 把任务缩成一个场景，必要时停写恢复 |

“卡文”不是单一故障。结构问题靠润色解决不了，疲劳也不该被解释成作者不会写。
body.en:
| Symptom | What is actually missing | First response |
|---|---|---|
| You do not know what the next chapter contains | A stage goal or consequence | State what the protagonist must accomplish next |
| Events happen but feel flat | Opposition capable of counteraction | Give the opposing side its own goal and leverage |
| Every chapter feels repetitive | The strategy never changes | Make the old method fail and force another approach |
| You know the plot but cannot form sentences | A scene-action skeleton | List entry state, action, reaction, and result |
| You cannot bear to touch the draft | Attention or energy is exhausted | Reduce the task to one scene and pause to recover if needed |

Writer’s block is not one fault. Polishing cannot repair a structural problem, and fatigue should not be interpreted as an inability to write.

heading.zh: 用五个问题找回下一步
heading.en: Find the Next Move with Five Questions

body.zh:
1. **主角现在要完成哪一件事？** “变强”太宽，改成“在开市前追回被贴错标签的解毒药”。
2. **谁或什么不允许他顺利完成？** 阻力要能行动，例如药铺掌柜为了保住执照，拒绝承认标签出错。
3. **上一场的结果改变了什么？** 若什么都没变，这一场可能没有完成任务。
4. **原办法为什么失效？** 让人物换策略，别把同一争吵再写一次。
5. **下一场结束后，局面必须哪里不同？** 信息、关系、资源、风险或决定至少有一项真正改变。

五问答完，先写“因为 A，所以主角做 B；B 引来反制 C；C 迫使他选择 D”。这条因果骨架比临时搜索十个新点子更能续上正文。
body.en:
1. **What one thing must the protagonist accomplish now?** “Become stronger” is too broad; use “recover the mislabeled antidote before the market opens.”
2. **Who or what prevents easy success?** Opposition must act. The apothecary owner refuses to admit the labeling error because it could cost the shop its license.
3. **What did the previous scene’s result change?** If nothing changed, that scene may not have completed a job.
4. **Why does the old method fail?** Force a new strategy instead of repeating the same argument.
5. **What must be different when the next scene ends?** Change information, relationship, resources, risk, or a decision.

Then write: “Because A, the protagonist does B; B draws counteraction C; C forces choice D.” This causal skeleton reconnects the draft more reliably than searching for ten unrelated ideas.

heading.zh: 原创示例：药铺学徒卡在追药这一章
heading.en: Original Example: A Pharmacy Apprentice Stalls During a Search for Medicine

body.zh:
**卡住的版本**：学徒阿岑发现一包解毒药贴错标签，焦急地在集市找人。他问了几家摊贩，都说没看见。

这里目标已经成立，缺口是有策略的阻力与能改变局面的询问。

**诊断后的骨架**：

- 目标：开市钟响前找回药包，避免病人误服。
- 反对力量：掌柜若承认失误会被吊销经营资格，于是抢先散布“学徒偷药”的说法。
- 旧策略失效：阿岑公开询问，摊贩反而把他当贼躲开。
- 新策略：他不再找药包，而是追查只有自家药铺使用的蓝蜡封口。
- 局部结果：他在早点摊找到被拆下的蓝蜡，却发现药已被送往城外义诊。
- 下一步压力：他必须借掌柜最不愿外借的快马，而掌柜握有报官的筹码。

现在下一章不靠随机事故启动，而由本章的局部发现与对手反制自然产生。
body.en:
**Blocked version:** Apprentice A-Cen discovers a package of antidote with the wrong label and anxiously searches the market. Several vendors say they have not seen it.

The goal exists. What is missing is strategic opposition and a question that can change the situation.

**Diagnosed skeleton:**

- Goal: recover the package before the market bell so a patient does not take it by mistake.
- Opposition: admitting the error could cost the owner the shop’s license, so he spreads the story that the apprentice stole the medicine.
- Old strategy fails: when A-Cen asks publicly, vendors avoid him as a thief.
- New strategy: stop searching for the package and trace the blue-wax seal used only by his shop.
- Partial result: he finds the discarded blue wax at a breakfast stall, but the medicine has already left for a free clinic outside the city.
- Next pressure: he needs the owner’s fastest horse, while the owner can still report him to the authorities.

The next chapter now grows from this chapter’s discovery and the opponent’s counteraction rather than a random accident.

heading.zh: 如果剧情知道，但正文写不出来
heading.en: When You Know the Plot but Cannot Draft the Prose

body.zh:
把“写好这一章”改成三个小动作：先写人物进入场景时的位置、持物和当下目的；再只写会改变局面的动作与反应；最后写结果如何迫使下一步。暂时跳过景物润色和漂亮转场。

例如先写：“阿岑冲到早点摊—看见蓝蜡—摊主藏手—他用药味指出蜡来自毒柜—摊主承认包裹已上车。”骨架成立后，再补气味、语气和人物细节。若骨架本身无因果，说明仍是剧情卡，不是文笔卡。
body.en:
Replace “write this chapter well” with three smaller tasks. Record the character’s position, held object, and immediate purpose on entering the scene. Then write only actions and reactions that change the situation. Finally state how the result forces the next move. Skip atmospheric polish and elegant transitions for now.

For example: “A-Cen runs to the breakfast stall → sees blue wax → the vendor hides his hand → A-Cen identifies the wax by the medicine smell → the vendor admits the package is already on a cart.” Once the skeleton works, add smell, tone, and character detail. If the skeleton has no causality, the block is still in the plot rather than the prose.

heading.zh: 越解越卡的几种做法
heading.en: Common Fixes That Make Writer’s Block Worse

body.zh:
| 做法 | 为什么恶化 | 替代方案 |
|---|---|---|
| 突然增加陌生反派 | 新问题没有旧因 | 从已有结果中找受损者 |
| 临时给主角新能力 | 困境被绕过 | 让已有能力换一种用法并付代价 |
| 重复上一轮冲突 | 人物策略和结果没变 | 封住旧路，要求新选择 |
| 一直改开头 | 不面对当前缺口 | 只修与下一步因果相关的上游节点 |
| 强迫疲惫时完成整章 | 质量和判断一起下降 | 留下一条可接续的动作骨架后休息 |

当你能写出“当前目标—有效阻力—策略变化—局部结果—新压力”，卡点就已经从模糊焦虑变成可修改的问题。
body.en:
| Response | Why it worsens the block | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| Add an unfamiliar villain | The new problem has no old cause | Find who was harmed by an existing result |
| Give the protagonist a new ability | The dilemma is bypassed | Use an established ability differently and attach a cost |
| Repeat the previous conflict | Strategy and result remain unchanged | Close the old route and require a new choice |
| Keep rewriting the opening | The current gap remains untouched | Repair only upstream beats that affect the next causal step |
| Force an entire chapter while exhausted | Quality and judgment decline together | Leave a resumable action skeleton, then rest |

Once you can write “current goal → effective opposition → strategy change → partial result → new pressure,” the block has become a specific, repairable problem.

q.zh: 不知道下一章写什么，最先看哪里？
q.en: I do not know what to write next. Where should I look first?

a.zh: 先看上一章的结果。谁因此失去东西、知道新事实、改变立场或必须付代价？让这个已发生的变化启动下一章，比凭空加入事故更自然。
a.en: Start with the previous chapter’s result. Who lost something, learned a fact, changed position, or incurred a cost? Let that completed change initiate the next chapter instead of adding an unrelated accident.

q.zh: 卡文时应该重写大纲吗？
q.en: Should I rewrite the whole outline when I get stuck?

a.zh: 先定位层级。若主线目标和阶段高潮仍成立，只修最近一段的阻力与因果；只有核心目标本身不可执行或不再吸引时，才回到全书大纲。
a.en: First locate the level. If the main goal and stage climax still work, revise only the nearest resistance and causality. Return to the book-level outline only if the central goal cannot be pursued or no longer carries the story.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /story-long-write 帮我诊断卡文，不续写正文。依次检查当前目标、有效阻力、因果、策略变化和下一步状态改变，只给最小修复方案”（Codex 里写作 `$story-long-write`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/story-long-write` to diagnose why I am stuck without continuing the prose. Check the current goal, effective resistance, causality, change of strategy, and next state change in order. Give only the smallest repair plan.” In Codex, write `$story-long-write`.

title.zh: 小说简介怎么写：从正文卖点到可读文案
title.en: How to Write a Novel Blurb from the Story's Real Selling Point

seo_title.zh: 小说简介怎么写：模板范例｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Write a Compelling Novel Blurb

description.zh: 小说简介不是剧情摘要。它要交代主角处境、核心冲突和行动方向，同时让读者看见这本书会兑现的情绪。附模板与同一故事的多种写法。
description.en: A blurb is not a synopsis: show protagonist situation, conflict, action direction, and promised emotion. Includes a template and versions of one story.

answer.zh: 小说简介要把正文最稳定的卖点压缩成一个阅读承诺：谁陷入什么局面，他将采取什么独特行动，读者会得到哪种情绪回报。可以在行动处截断留悬念，也可以提前暗示一次成功给安全感，但不能承诺正文没有的身份、关系或爽点。
answer.en: A novel blurb compresses the story’s most durable selling point into a reading promise: who enters what situation, what distinctive action they take, and what emotional reward readers can expect. You may cut away during an action to create suspense or hint at one success to create security, but do not promise an identity, relationship, or payoff the prose does not contain.

heading.zh: 小说简介不是全书梗概
heading.en: A Novel Blurb Is Not a Synopsis of the Whole Book

body.zh:
这里的“简介”指放在正文外、供读者选书的作品介绍；短篇投稿中有些栏目把正文开头的导语也叫“简介”，那类文字还要承担开场叙事，不能直接套用这里的书籍文案。

梗概帮助作者掌握全局，简介帮助读者判断“这是不是我想看的故事”。因此简介不需要依次交代所有角色和转折，而要优先呈现三件事：主角的可代入处境、会反复推动正文的矛盾、最有辨识度的行动方式。

书名、简介和开篇是同一承诺的三道门。书名若强调“失物修复”，简介就不该只写豪门身份；简介若承诺主角靠修复旧物揭开关系秘密，开篇就应尽快让这种能力真正参与冲突。
body.en:
Here, “blurb” means the description outside the prose that helps readers choose a book. Some short-story venues also call an opening lead a “description”; that text performs narrative work and cannot simply use this book-blurb method.

A synopsis helps the author see the whole. A blurb helps readers decide whether this is the experience they want. It need not list every character and turn. Prioritize the protagonist’s relatable situation, the conflict that repeatedly drives the prose, and the story’s most distinctive mode of action.

Title, blurb, and opening are three gates to the same promise. If the title emphasizes restoring lost objects, the blurb should not discuss only a wealthy-family identity. If the blurb promises that restoring old objects reveals relationship secrets, the opening should quickly put that ability into conflict.

heading.zh: 一份够用的小说简介模板
heading.en: A Practical Novel-Blurb Template

body.zh:
> **情境**：{主角身份}原本{日常状态}，直到{不可忽略的变化}。
>
> **冲突**：他想{明确目标}，但{对手、规则或关系}使正常办法失效。
>
> **独特行动**：于是他决定{能体现本书卖点的做法}。
>
> **阅读承诺**：这会带来{读者期待的回报}，同时逼他面对{更深代价或问题}。
>
> **收束句**：在答案揭开前，留下一个会影响行动的问题，而不是空泛地问“真相究竟是什么”。

轻松、成长或事业线可以暗示主角会赢一次，让读者知道回报确实存在；悬疑故事可以更早截断，但仍要让读者理解主角正在做什么。
body.en:
> **Situation:** {Protagonist identity} used to {ordinary state}, until {unignorable change}.
>
> **Conflict:** They want to {clear goal}, but {opponent, rule, or relationship} makes the normal method fail.
>
> **Distinctive action:** They decide to {action that expresses the book’s central appeal}.
>
> **Reading promise:** This brings {expected reward} while forcing them to face {deeper cost or problem}.
>
> **Closing line:** Leave a question that changes action before its answer, rather than asking vaguely, “What is the truth?”

For a light, growth, or career story, hint at one victory so readers know the reward exists. A mystery may cut away sooner, but readers still need to understand what the protagonist is doing.

heading.zh: 根据故事选择文案结构
heading.en: Choose a Blurb Structure That Fits the Story

body.zh:
| 故事重心 | 适合的结构 | 何时停下 |
|---|---|---|
| 事业成长 | 情境—冲突—行动 | 在行动即将改变局面处 |
| 轻松或甜感 | 情境—转折—一次成功 | 让读者先尝到主要情绪 |
| 强悬疑 | 情境—矛盾证据 | 留下能重排意义的问题 |
| 强压迫关系 | 情境—冲突—反抗—受挫 | 在主角准备换策略处 |
| 复合类型 | 一次局部成功—新的未知 | 同时给安全感和好奇心 |

结构不是越复杂越好。连续抛出身份、世界观、阴谋和感情谜题，会让简介像谜语。只保留能代表正文主要体验的一条。
body.en:
| Story focus | Useful structure | Where to stop |
|---|---|---|
| Career growth | Situation → conflict → action | Just before the action changes the situation |
| Light or sweet tone | Situation → turn → one success | Give readers an early taste of the main emotion |
| Strong mystery | Situation → contradictory evidence | Leave a question capable of rearranging meaning |
| Oppressive relationship | Situation → conflict → resistance → setback | When the protagonist prepares to change strategy |
| Hybrid | One partial success → a new unknown | Offer security and curiosity together |

More complexity is not automatically better. A sequence of identity, worldbuilding, conspiracy, and relationship mysteries makes the blurb read like a riddle. Keep the one line that best represents the prose’s main experience.

heading.zh: 原创范例：《替遗憾上釉》
heading.en: Original Example: “Glazing Regret”

body.zh:
**正文卖点**：陶瓷修复师能从裂纹里辨认器物最后一次破损的方式，却无法知道人的动机。

**行动型版本**：

> 宋遥接手母亲留下的旧物修复铺，只想还清欠款关门。开业第一天，一只被认定死于意外的旧茶盏告诉她：它是在主人争执时被人刻意摔碎的。此后，每件送来的残器都牵着一段被说错的往事。宋遥决定只修物、不判人，直到父亲失踪前修过的最后一只碗被送回柜台。

**成功加悬疑版本**：

> 宋遥修好了全城无人敢接的百片瓷屏，也因此保住母亲的铺子。庆功当晚，瓷屏裂纹里浮出的却不是破损现场，而是她父亲写下的一句警告：别相信送屏来的人。

前者适合突出事业行动，后者先给能力兑现，再把成功转成新问题。两版都没有罗列后续案件，也没有把能力夸成“看见全部真相”。
body.en:
**Core appeal in the prose:** A ceramics restorer can identify how an object was last broken from its cracks, but cannot know a person’s motive.

**Action-led version:**

> Song Yao inherits her mother’s antique-restoration shop and wants only to pay its debts and close it. On opening day, an old teacup said to have shattered by accident reveals that someone deliberately smashed it during an argument between its owners. Every damaged object that follows is tied to a past told incorrectly. Song Yao decides to repair objects, not judge people—until the last bowl her father repaired before he disappeared returns to the counter.

**Success-plus-mystery version:**

> Song Yao restores a hundred-piece porcelain screen no one else in the city will touch and saves her mother’s shop. On the celebration night, the cracks reveal not the moment of damage but a warning left by her father: Do not trust the person who brought the screen.

The first version emphasizes professional action. The second demonstrates the ability, then turns success into a new problem. Neither lists later cases or inflates the ability into “seeing the whole truth.”

heading.zh: 简介写不好，通常错在这几处
heading.en: When a Blurb Fails, the Problem Is Usually Here

body.zh:
| 失败 | 读者感受 | 修正 |
|---|---|---|
| 从世界创世史讲起 | 不知道要跟谁走 | 第一段就给主角和变化 |
| 只写“命运齿轮转动” | 看不见具体行动 | 写清主角接下来要做什么 |
| 把所有反转都剧透 | 没有发现空间 | 只揭一次局部结果，保留行动问题 |
| 一味藏信息 | 不知道故事卖什么 | 至少交代冲突和独特手段 |
| 简介比正文更刺激 | 入文后货不对板 | 用正文早期能兑现的卖点 |
| 形容词堆满 | 情绪没有事实支撑 | 用处境、选择和代价代替评价 |
body.en:
| Failure | Reader experience | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Begin with the creation history of the world | No one knows whom to follow | Put the protagonist and change in the first paragraph |
| Say only that “the wheels of fate turn” | No concrete action is visible | State what the protagonist does next |
| Spoil every twist | Nothing remains to discover | Reveal one partial result and preserve an action-driving question |
| Hide everything | The story’s appeal is unknown | Establish at least the conflict and distinctive method |
| Make the blurb more exciting than the prose | The book feels like a mismatch | Promise what the early prose can deliver |
| Stack adjectives | Emotion lacks factual support | Use situation, choice, and cost instead |

q.zh: 小说简介一般写多长？
q.en: How long should a novel blurb be?

a.zh: 没有脱离发布场景的统一字数。先用足够篇幅讲清主角、冲突、独特行动和阅读承诺，再删掉不改变选择的背景；目标是读者一遍能复述卖点。
a.en: There is no universal length outside a publication context. Use enough space to establish the protagonist, conflict, distinctive action, and reading promise, then remove background that does not change a choice. Readers should be able to repeat the central appeal afterward.

q.zh: 简介要不要写结局？
q.en: Should a blurb reveal the ending?

a.zh: 不必交代最终结局，但可以展示一次局部成功或失败，以证明故事会兑现哪种情绪。真正该保留的是仍会推动主角行动的问题。
a.en: It need not state the final outcome. One partial success or failure may demonstrate the emotion the story will deliver. Preserve the unanswered question that continues to drive the protagonist’s action.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /story-long-write 根据这本书真实的核心卖点写小说简介，给出行动型和成功加悬疑型各一版，并检查书名、简介和开篇是否承诺同一种阅读体验”（Codex 里写作 `$story-long-write`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/story-long-write` to write a novel blurb from the book’s real core appeal. Give one action-led version and one success-plus-mystery version, then check whether the title, blurb, and opening promise the same reading experience.” In Codex, write `$story-long-write`.

title.zh: 短剧分集大纲怎么写：分集地图模板与范例
title.en: How to Write a Short-Drama Episode Outline: Map and Example

seo_title.en: Short-Drama Episode Outline Template

description.zh: 短剧分集要让每集完成一次可见的状态变化，不能平均切段。附进入状态、压力、选择、兑现、出去状态模板和原创分集范例。
description.en: Cut episodes at visible state changes, not equal intervals. Includes an entry, pressure, choice, payoff, exit template and original episode example.

answer.zh: 短剧分集要按状态变化切，不按固定时长或固定集数均分。每集从可验证的进入状态开始，让压力迫使人物选择，选择遭遇反制并产生局部结果，最后形成已经启动的新决定或危险，并把准确的出去状态交给下一集。
answer.en: Divide a short drama into episodes at changes of state, not by a fixed runtime or episode count. Each episode begins from a verifiable entry state. Pressure forces a choice, the choice meets counteraction and produces a partial result, and that result initiates a new decision or danger. Record the precise exit state so the next episode has an exact starting point.

heading.zh: 什么是短剧分集大纲？
heading.en: What Is a Short-Drama Episode Outline?

body.zh:
分集大纲是一张“每集为什么必须发生”的地图。它不复述全部剧情，而是记录本集独有的变化：人物从什么状态进入，想改变什么，谁如何阻挡，哪次选择使局面转向，本集兑现了什么，结束时哪些事实已经不同。

因此，集尾钩子不是突然有人推门或一句“你竟然是……”。有效的下一集压力应来自本集结果：胜利伤害了谁、代价何时到期、新证据迫使谁换立场，或者一个决定已经开始执行。
body.en:
An episode outline is a map of why every episode must happen. It does not retell the whole plot. It records the change unique to that episode: the state in which characters enter, what they want to change, who blocks them and how, which choice turns the situation, what the episode delivers, and which facts differ at the end.

An episode-ending hook is therefore more than a door suddenly opening or a line such as “You are actually….” Effective exit pressure grows from the result: who was harmed by the victory, when a cost comes due, whom new evidence forces to change sides, or which decision has already begun to take effect.

heading.zh: 可复制的单集卡与分集地图
heading.en: Reusable Episode Card and Episode Map

body.zh:
每一集填写：

> **进入状态**：位置、持物、伤势、已知信息、关系主动权，以及必须接住的上一集动作。
>
> **当前压力**：为什么此刻不能拖？
>
> **本集目标**：谁想让什么在本集结束前发生怎样的变化？
>
> **反对力量**：对方自己的目标、筹码和反制动作。
>
> **关键选择与转折**：旧策略为何失效，人物换了什么策略？
>
> **局部兑现**：观众这集实际得到什么结果？
>
> **出去压力**：由本集结果启动的下一步。
>
> **出去状态**：谁知道什么、关系或资源怎样改变、人物在哪里并能否行动。

整季地图只需把这些字段压缩成一行一集。若因果只有一步，不必另造复杂流程栏；字段越多不等于剧情越清楚。
body.en:
Fill in each episode:

> **Entry state:** Location, held objects, injuries, known information, relationship leverage, and any action inherited from the previous episode.
>
> **Current pressure:** Why can this not wait?
>
> **Episode goal:** Who wants which state to change before the episode ends?
>
> **Opposition:** The other side’s goal, leverage, and counteraction.
>
> **Key choice and turn:** Why does the old strategy fail, and what replaces it?
>
> **Partial payoff:** What result does the audience actually receive?
>
> **Exit pressure:** Which next step begins because of this result?
>
> **Exit state:** Who knows what, how relationships or resources changed, where everyone is, and whether they can act.

Compress these fields to one row per episode for a season map. If the causality has only one step, do not invent a complicated process column. More fields do not automatically produce a clearer story.

heading.zh: 原创范例：《后台最后一件戏服》
heading.en: Original Example: “The Last Costume Backstage”

body.zh:
社区剧团演出前夜，镇馆戏服失踪。服装管理员林絮既要找回戏服，也要阻止剧团借机赶走患病的老裁缝。

| 集 | 进入状态与压力 | 选择、反制与转折 | 当集兑现 | 出去状态与新压力 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 戏服柜空了，演出次日开场 | 林絮封锁后台；团长以“影响彩排”逼她开门 | 找到被剪断的旧锁，不是忘记归还 | 老裁缝持有唯一备用钥匙，众人去找他 |
| 2 | 老裁缝失联，团长掌握舆论 | 林絮查维修单；团长公开指责老人偷卖戏服 | 维修单证明钥匙早已失效 | 戏服曾被送去洗护，洗护车正要离镇 |
| 3 | 林絮追上洗护车，却只有空箱 | 她放弃追物，改查谁签收空箱 | 门卫承认团长秘书取走戏服 | 秘书愿交代，但要求先保证老裁缝上台谢幕 |
| 4 | 演出将开，团长必须公开选择 | 林絮把备用戏服交给演员，留原戏服作证 | 演出正常开始，老人恢复署名 | 团长承认藏衣为逼退老人；剧团面临董事会调查 |

每集都先完成一个局部问题，再由结果启动下一集。集数来自故事所需的状态变化，不来自预设配额。
body.en:
On the eve of a community troupe’s performance, its signature costume disappears. Costume manager Lin Xu must recover it and stop the troupe from using the incident to expel an ill, elderly tailor.

| Episode | Entry state and pressure | Choice, counteraction, and turn | Episode payoff | Exit state and new pressure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The costume cabinet is empty; the show opens tomorrow | Lin Xu seals backstage; the director demands she reopen it so rehearsal can continue | The old lock was cut, so this was not a forgotten return | The elderly tailor has the only spare key; everyone goes to find him |
| 2 | The tailor is missing; the director controls the public story | Lin Xu checks repair orders; the director publicly accuses the tailor of selling the costume | The order proves the key stopped working long ago | The costume went to a cleaner, whose van is about to leave town |
| 3 | Lin Xu catches the van but finds only an empty case | She stops chasing the object and asks who signed for the empty case | The gatekeeper admits the director’s secretary collected the costume | The secretary will talk only if the tailor is guaranteed a final bow onstage |
| 4 | The performance is about to begin; the director must choose publicly | Lin Xu gives the backup costume to the actor and preserves the original as evidence | The show begins and the tailor’s credit is restored | The director admits hiding the costume to force the tailor out; the board opens an investigation |

Each episode resolves a local question, and its result initiates the next. The episode count comes from necessary state changes rather than a preset quota.

heading.zh: 钩子、兑现和出去压力各管什么
heading.en: What Do the Hook, Payoff, and Exit Pressure Each Do?

body.zh:
**钩子**回答“为什么现在要看”，可以是高代价行动、证据矛盾、倒计时或必须公开作出的决定。它必须连着本集目标。

**兑现**回答“这一集给了什么”，可以是局部真相、关系变化、一次不可撤回的选择或真实代价。开放结尾也要有局部结果。

**出去压力**回答“为什么状态还会继续动”。把“可能有人报复”改成“失去职位的副团长已经拿走账本”，下一集才有可执行的起点。
body.en:
A **hook** answers “Why watch now?” It may be a high-cost action, contradictory evidence, a countdown, or a decision that must be made publicly. It must connect to the episode goal.

A **payoff** answers “What did this episode deliver?” It may be a partial truth, a changed relationship, an irreversible choice, or a real cost. Even an open ending needs a local result.

**Exit pressure** answers “Why will the state keep moving?” Replace “someone may retaliate” with “the demoted deputy director has already taken the ledger.” The next episode now has an executable starting point.

heading.zh: 分集大纲常见失败与改法
heading.en: Common Episode-Outline Failures and Fixes

body.zh:
| 失败 | 改法 |
|---|---|
| 按时长平均切剧情 | 在选择造成状态变化处切集 |
| 每集只交代背景 | 给本集一个可判断的局部结果 |
| 钩子与本集无关 | 让开场压力直接逼出本集目标 |
| 结尾靠藏一句信息 | 写清谁已决定行动、哪个后果已启动 |
| 下一集忘记伤势、持物或认知 | 用出去状态直接生成下一集进入状态 |
| 为每集填满相同栏目 | 只保留删掉后会让创作失去约束的事实 |

拿到已有多集剧本时，先按原文实际分集逐集读取，再补状态和因果；不要为了迎合模板改写原稿的集界。
body.en:
| Failure | Fix |
|---|---|
| Divide the plot evenly by runtime | Cut when a choice creates a state change |
| Use an episode only for background | Give it a local result that can be judged |
| Use a hook unrelated to the episode | Let opening pressure produce the episode goal directly |
| End by hiding one line of information | State who has decided to act and which consequence has begun |
| Forget injuries, held objects, or knowledge next episode | Generate the next entry state from the previous exit state |
| Fill every episode with identical columns | Keep only facts whose removal would weaken creative constraints |

When given an existing multi-episode script, read it episode by episode at its actual boundaries, then add state and causality. Do not move the boundaries merely to satisfy the template.

q.zh: 短剧分集大纲一定要写固定集数吗？
q.en: Must a short-drama outline use a fixed episode count?

a.zh: 集数由故事规模、交付要求和每次状态变化决定。先排必要的目标、转折与兑现，再决定怎样分集，不要用数字形式证明剧情质量。
a.en: No. Let story scale, delivery requirements, and state changes determine the count. Arrange necessary goals, turns, and payoffs first, then divide the episodes. A number does not prove plot quality.

q.zh: 每集结尾都必须大反转吗？
q.en: Must every episode end on a major twist?

a.zh: 不必。关系位置变化、代价到期、新决定启动或已有后果抵达，都能形成出去压力。钩子形态应服从本集运动和作品气质。
a.en: No. A changed relationship, a cost coming due, a new decision set in motion, or an established consequence arriving can all create exit pressure. Let the hook follow the episode’s movement and the work’s tone.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /short-drama-develop 排分集大纲，逐集写进入状态、压力、目标与反制、关键选择、局部兑现、出去压力和出去状态，不按固定集数凑内容”（Codex 里写作 `$short-drama-develop`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/short-drama-develop` to arrange the episode outline. For each episode, write the entry state, pressure, goal and counteraction, key choice, partial payoff, exit pressure, and exit state. Do not pad the story to a fixed episode count.” In Codex, write `$short-drama-develop`.

title.zh: 短篇小说大纲模板：从情绪落点倒推每一节
title.en: Short-Story Outline Template: Work Backward from the Emotional Landing

seo_title.en: Short-Story Outline Template | ZenStory

description.zh: 短篇大纲以情绪落点和核心兑现为中心，逐节写事件改变、因果、读者新知与承接。附精简模板和原创完整范例。
description.en: Build from emotional landing and core payoff; track change, causality, reader knowledge, handoff. Includes a concise template and full example.

answer.zh: 短篇大纲先定读者最后应获得的情绪，再定核心兑现或反转，倒推前面需要哪些选择、证据和关系变化。每一节至少要改变信息、风险、关系、资源、决定或行动中的一项；没有真实改变的段落，不要靠多加栏目制造充实感。
answer.en: Begin a short-story outline by deciding the emotion readers should carry away, then choose the core payoff or twist and work backward to the choices, evidence, and relationship changes it requires. Every section should change at least one of information, risk, relationship, resources, decision, or action. Do not make an unchanged passage look substantial by adding more template fields.

heading.zh: 短篇大纲和长篇大纲有什么不同？
heading.en: How Does a Short-Story Outline Differ from a Long-Form Outline?

body.zh:
长篇要管理跨卷目标与持续循环，短篇更在意有限篇幅内的一条情绪曲线和因果闭环。短篇不必把完整世界观、所有人物档案塞进大纲；它需要让作者一眼看出：这一节发生了什么变化，为什么导致下一节，以及结尾的关键元素是否早有来处。

先写一句话梗概：**主角 + 困境 + 核心兑现 + 情绪落点**。若故事没有反转，就把“核心兑现”换成报应、和解、成长或关系承诺，不必硬造身份秘密。
body.en:
A long-form outline manages goals and recurring loops across volumes. A short-story outline concentrates on one emotional arc and a closed causal chain within limited space. It need not contain the entire worldbuilding system or every character file. It should let the author see at a glance what changes in each section, why that change causes the next section, and whether every crucial ending element appeared earlier.

Start with a one-sentence premise: **protagonist + predicament + core payoff + emotional landing**. If the story has no twist, make the core payoff retribution, reconciliation, growth, or a relationship commitment rather than inventing an identity secret.

heading.zh: 可复制的短篇大纲模板
heading.en: Reusable Short-Story Outline Template

body.zh:
> **暂定标题**：
>
> **一句话梗概**：{谁}因{困境}采取{关键行动}，最终{核心兑现}，让读者感到{情绪落点}。
>
> **主角当下最想要**：
>
> **阻挡他的力量**：对方想要什么，有什么真实筹码？
>
> **核心兑现**：结尾要证明、推翻或完成什么？
>
> **提前建立**：结尾使用的人物、物件、信息或能力，分别在哪里出现？

逐节使用轻量表：

| 段落功能 | 主事件 | 状态改变 | 因果与后果 | 读者新知 | 承接 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 开头/铺垫/升级/转折/结尾 | 谁做了什么 | 信息、风险、关系、资源、决定或行动改变了什么 | 为什么发生，造成什么 | 读者现在多知道什么 | 下一节为何必须发生 |

对话、回忆和气氛只有在改变选择或读者理解时才单列；否则把它们放进主事件，不要让形式冒充推进。
body.en:
> **Working title:**
>
> **One-sentence premise:** {Who} responds to {predicament} with {key action}, ultimately {core payoff}, leaving readers with {emotional landing}.
>
> **What the protagonist wants most right now:**
>
> **Opposing force:** What does the other side want, and what real leverage does it possess?
>
> **Core payoff:** What must the ending prove, overturn, or complete?
>
> **Establish in advance:** Where do the people, objects, information, or abilities used by the ending first appear?

Use this lightweight table section by section:

| Section function | Main event | State change | Cause and consequence | New reader knowledge | Handoff |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Opening / setup / escalation / turn / ending | Who does what | What changes in information, risk, relationship, resources, decision, or action | Why it happens and what it causes | What readers now know | Why the next section must happen |

List dialogue, memory, or atmosphere separately only when it changes a choice or the reader’s understanding. Otherwise include it in the main event; do not mistake formatting for progress.

heading.zh: 原创范例：《没有取走的盐》
heading.en: Original Example: “The Salt Left Behind”

body.zh:
**一句话梗概**：新来的夜班保安周苒清理楼道物品时，发现独居老人门前放着两包标有连续日期的盐；她原本准备按规定收走，却因邻居的解释改为敲门查问，最终发现老人摔倒未能求救，情绪从不耐烦落到互助。

**先定结尾**：周苒不再把门口日用品一概当作杂物，和住户约定有人负责联系、无人回应时及时查问的互助办法。倒推需要提前建立：谁送盐、为什么写日期、没取走为何值得担心。

| 功能 | 主事件 | 状态改变 | 因果与后果 | 读者新知 | 承接 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 开头 | 周苒收到楼道杂物投诉，在老人门前发现两包盐，袋上写着昨天和今天的日期 | 她决定收走并登记 | 日期显示物品分两天送来 | 昨天那包始终没有动过 | 对门邻居阻止她清理 |
| 铺垫 | 邻居说昨天老人托她买盐，她送到后老人隔门答应稍后取；今天看到盐还在，误以为老人没注意，又放了一包并写上日期提醒 | “杂物”变成未完成的日常约定 | 老人昨天还答过话，后来为何没开门成了问题 | 两包盐来自同一人，日期就是送达时间 | 周苒决定先联系老人 |
| 升级 | 电话在门内响，却始终无人接听；周苒敲门后听见微弱应答 | 她从清理物品转为求助救援 | 不能再用外出解释无人接听 | 老人在屋内，需要帮助 | 她联系救援人员并留在门口回应 |
| 转折 | 救援人员打开门，发现老人摔倒后无法起身，也够不到手机 | 盐袋的含义从占道物品变为异常迹象 | 邻居以为对方只是忘记，老人却一直无法开门 | 昨天的回应与此后的沉默形成完整时间线 | 周苒和邻居协助联系家属 |
| 结尾 | 老人得到救助，周苒与住户商量后续联系办法 | 生硬执行转为有责任人的互助 | 没取走的物品会引出一次查问，而不只是一次清理 | 周苒仍清理楼道，但会先查明异常 | 邻居收起第二包盐，记下负责联系的人 |

结尾的发现依赖开头已经出现的日期和未取物品；电话、敲门进一步改变判断，救助由人物连续行动促成。盐袋只是异常线索，不能单凭它断定老人出了事。
body.en:
**One-sentence premise:** While clearing objects from an apartment corridor, new night-shift security guard Zhou Ran finds two bags of salt marked with consecutive dates outside an older resident’s door. She intends to remove them under the rules, but a neighbor’s explanation leads her to knock and investigate. She discovers the resident fell and could not call for help, moving the emotion from irritation to mutual care.

**Set the ending first:** Zhou Ran stops treating every daily object outside a door as mere clutter. She and the residents agree on a mutual-aid process: one person maintains contact, and an unanswered check prompts an inquiry. Work backward to establish who delivered the salt, why the dates were written, and why an uncollected bag is concerning.

| Function | Main event | State change | Cause and consequence | New reader knowledge | Handoff |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Opening | Zhou Ran receives a corridor-clutter complaint and finds two bags of salt outside the resident’s door, dated yesterday and today | She decides to remove and log them | The dates show two separate deliveries | Yesterday’s bag never moved | The neighbor across the hall stops her from clearing them |
| Setup | The neighbor says the resident asked her to buy salt yesterday and answered through the door that she would collect it later. Seeing it still there today, the neighbor assumes she forgot and leaves another dated bag | “Clutter” becomes an unfinished everyday arrangement | The resident answered yesterday; why has she not opened the door since? | Both bags came from the same person, and the dates record delivery | Zhou Ran decides to contact the resident first |
| Escalation | A phone rings inside with no answer. After Zhou Ran knocks, she hears a faint response | She shifts from clearing objects to arranging help | Absence can no longer explain the silence | The resident is inside and needs help | Zhou Ran calls rescuers and stays at the door to answer her |
| Turn | Rescuers open the door and find the resident unable to rise after a fall and unable to reach her phone | The salt changes from an obstruction into an anomaly | The neighbor thought she had forgotten; in fact, she could not open the door | Yesterday’s response and the silence afterward form a complete timeline | Zhou Ran and the neighbor contact the family |
| Ending | The resident receives help, and Zhou Ran discusses a future contact process with the residents | Rigid enforcement becomes mutual aid with clear responsibility | An uncollected object prompts a check rather than only removal | Zhou Ran still clears the corridor, but investigates anomalies first | The neighbor removes the second bag and records the designated contact person |

The ending depends on the dates and uncollected object established at the beginning. The phone and knock revise the judgment, and rescue follows from a continuous chain of character actions. The salt is only an anomalous clue; it cannot prove by itself that something happened to the resident.

heading.zh: 写完大纲后做两次倒查
heading.en: After Drafting the Outline, Run Two Backward Checks

body.zh:
**从结尾往前查来处**：列出结尾依赖的人、物件、能力和信息，逐项找到更早的建立位置。找不到，就补铺垫或删除结尾便利。

**从开头往后查后果**：每节的决定是否造成下一节？若拿掉一节，后面仍完全成立，这一节可能只有气氛而没有结构功能。反转故事还要检查错误解释是否真的影响过人物决定；若大家只是等人公布答案，反转没有参与剧情。
body.en:
**Trace the ending backward to its sources:** List every person, object, ability, and piece of information the ending uses, then locate where each was established. If one has no source, add setup or remove the convenient ending element.

**Trace the opening forward to its consequences:** Does each section’s decision cause the next? If removing a section leaves everything afterward intact, it may contribute atmosphere but no structural function. In a twist story, also ask whether the wrong explanation actually influenced a decision. If everyone merely waits for someone to announce the answer, the twist never entered the plot.

heading.zh: 短篇细纲常见失败与修正
heading.en: Common Short-Story Outline Failures and Fixes

body.zh:
| 失败 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 每节只写“争吵、回忆、反转” | 改成谁做了什么，改变了哪种状态 |
| 为了显得丰富硬添阻碍 | 只保留服务情绪、证据、关系或行动的节点 |
| 反转靠结尾新角色口述 | 把关键证据提前放进会被误解的行动 |
| 揭晓后立刻结束 | 留出人物基于新事实行动、付代价或改变关系 |
| 把短篇套成长篇多线结构 | 守住一条主要情绪与因果链 |

如果写完仍不知道第一段怎么落笔，回到[从创意到短篇的写作流程](/oh-story/short-story-from-idea)；大纲负责结构，开头负责把结构变成正在发生的场景。
body.en:
| Failure | Correction |
|---|---|
| Every section says only “argument,” “memory,” or “twist” | State who acts and which state changes |
| Add obstacles merely to make the outline look rich | Keep only beats that serve emotion, evidence, relationships, or action |
| A new character explains the twist at the ending | Put the key evidence earlier inside an action that can be misread |
| End immediately after the reveal | Leave room for action, cost, or relationship change based on the new fact |
| Force a short story into a multi-threaded long-form structure | Protect one main emotional and causal chain |

If you still do not know how to begin the first paragraph, return to [From Idea to Short Story](/oh-story/short-story-from-idea). The outline governs structure; the opening turns that structure into a scene already in progress.

q.zh: 短篇一定要有反转吗？
q.en: Does a short story need a twist?

a.zh: 短篇可以没有反转。此时，把大纲中心换成报应兑现、关系递进、和解或某个不可撤回的选择，并确保前文持续积累对应期待。
a.en: No. Center the outline on a reckoning, relationship progression, reconciliation, or an irreversible choice, and make sure earlier sections keep building the matching expectation.

q.zh: 短篇大纲要写多少节？
q.en: How many sections should a short-story outline contain?

a.zh: 由故事的动作和情绪变化决定，不存在通用固定节数。先列必要的因果节点，再按阅读节奏合并或拆分；不要反过来凑表格。
a.en: There is no universal number. Let actions and emotional changes determine it. List the necessary causal beats first, then merge or split them for reading rhythm instead of padding a table.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /story-short-write 只做短篇大纲：从结尾情绪和核心兑现倒推，逐节写主事件、状态改变、因果、读者新知和承接，不写正文”（Codex 里写作 `$story-short-write`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/story-short-write` only to build the short-story outline. Work backward from the ending emotion and core payoff, recording each section’s main event, state change, causality, new reader knowledge, and handoff. Do not draft the prose.” In Codex, write `$story-short-write`.

title.zh: 小说系统面板怎么写：规则、代价与显示模板
title.en: How to Write a System Panel in Fiction: Rules, Costs, and Display

seo_title.en: How to Write a Fictional System Panel | ZenStory

description.zh: 系统面板要先写作者掌握的能力边界、失效条件和代价，再决定角色此刻能看到多少。附读者可见面板模板与原创示例。
description.en: Define capability limits, failure conditions, and costs before deciding what the character sees. Includes a panel template and original example.

answer.zh: 小说系统面板好看，不靠栏目多，而靠它改变人物选择。作者先确定系统能做什么、不能做什么、何时失效、使用要付什么可见代价；正文只显示当前行动需要的信息。已公布的次数、时限和条件要持续守住，不能在主角脱困时临时增加无代价的新功能。
answer.en: A fictional system panel works because it changes a character’s choices, not because it contains many fields. First decide what the system can and cannot do, when it fails, and what visible cost its use imposes. In the prose, show only the information needed for the current action. Track every announced use, deadline, and condition consistently; do not invent a cost-free function merely to rescue the protagonist.

heading.zh: 先分清系统规则和面板显示
heading.en: Separate the System’s Rules from the Panel Display

body.zh:
**系统规则**是作者必须掌握的完整边界：能力范围、失效条件、代价、信息是否可靠。**面板显示**是角色和读者此刻看到的部分。两者不必同时公开，但不能互相矛盾。

这种分层让你既能保留未知，又不靠事后改规则救场。系统可以说谎，但“它会在什么情况下误导”应先存在于设定中；否则每次矛盾都能用“系统骗了主角”解释，读者就无法判断选择的风险。
body.en:
**System rules** are the complete boundaries the author must know: capability range, failure conditions, cost, and information reliability. **Panel display** is the portion the character and reader can see now. They may be disclosed at different times and must remain consistent.

This separation preserves mystery without allowing rules to change after the fact. A system may lie, but the conditions under which it misleads should already exist in the design. Otherwise every contradiction can be dismissed as “the system deceived the protagonist,” and readers lose any basis for judging risk.

heading.zh: 作者先填的系统规则卡
heading.en: The Author’s System-Rules Card

body.zh:
> **系统给什么**：信息、能力、任务或交换机会？
>
> **明确不能做什么**：它不能代替主角完成哪类决定或行动？
>
> **触发条件**：什么具体行为让功能生效？
>
> **失效条件**：何时不能使用，或结果不可靠？
>
> **可见代价**：时间、身体、关系、名声、机会或下次可用性会怎样受损？
>
> **可靠程度**：信息准确、有限，还是会按已知规则误述？
>
> **公开进度**：哪些规则已经让角色与读者知道？

代价必须落在主角在意、读者能看见的东西上。“消耗能量”若从不影响行动，这种代价便没有压力。系统可以给选项和限期，但关键选择要由人物承担。
body.en:
> **What the system provides:** Information, an ability, tasks, or exchange opportunities?
>
> **What it explicitly cannot do:** Which decisions or actions can it never perform for the protagonist?
>
> **Trigger:** Which concrete behavior activates a function?
>
> **Failure condition:** When is it unavailable or unreliable?
>
> **Visible cost:** How does use affect the protagonist’s time, body, relationships, reputation, opportunities, or future access?
>
> **Reliability:** Accurate, limited, or misleading according to an established rule?
>
> **Disclosed so far:** Which rules do the character and reader already know?

A cost must affect something the protagonist values and readers can observe. “Consumes energy” creates no pressure if it never changes action. The system may offer options and deadlines, but the character must make the crucial choice and bear its consequences.

heading.zh: 正文中显示的系统面板模板
heading.en: A System-Panel Template for the Prose

heading.zh: 原创范例：失物招领系统
heading.en: Original Example: The Lost-and-Found System

body.zh:
**作者规则卡**：顾临触碰失物时，可看见物主最后一次主动放下它的地点；看不见之后被谁移动，也无法判断物主意图。每次查询会让他忘掉自己当天的一段路线记忆，连续使用会妨碍他回家。系统只在物主确实“主动放下”时给出画面。

**顾临本章的目标**：他答应在闭馆前找到校徽的真正物主，归还后再带妹妹回家。这是他自己的安排。

**本章面板**：

> **可查询线索**：最后主动放置地点
>
> **本次代价**：遗失今天一段路线的记忆（具体哪一段未知）
>
> **提示**：校徽是否曾被他人移动——未知

顾临没有立刻查询，因为闭馆后他还要带妹妹回家。他先根据磨损找到旧社团名单；名单失败后才决定付代价。面板因此制造选择，没有替他破案。
body.en:
**Author’s rules card:** When Gu Lin touches a lost object, he can see the place where its owner last set it down voluntarily. He cannot see who moved it afterward or infer the owner’s motive. Each query erases one segment of his route memory from that day; repeated use interferes with his ability to find his way home. The system shows an image only when the owner truly put the object down voluntarily.

**Gu Lin’s chapter goal:** He has promised to find the school badge’s true owner before closing, return it, and then take his younger sister home. This schedule is his own decision.

**Panel in this chapter:**

> **Available clue:** Last place the object was set down voluntarily
>
> **Cost of this query:** Lose one segment of today’s route memory (which segment is unknown)
>
> **Note:** Whether another person later moved the badge—unknown

Gu Lin does not query immediately because he must still take his sister home after closing. He first follows the wear marks to an old club roster. Only when the roster fails does he choose to pay the cost. The panel creates a choice; it does not solve the case for him.

heading.zh: 系统面板常见失败与修正
heading.en: Common System-Panel Failures and Fixes

body.zh:
| 失败 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 困境中突然解锁正好需要的功能 | 提前建立能力来源，并给新限制或代价 |
| 公布精确次数后随意变化 | 只公布能长期守住的数值与条件 |
| 系统直接告诉主角正确答案 | 给信息或选项，把判断留给人物 |
| 代价只有抽象“精神力” | 写出眩晕造成的错过、关系误会或机会损失 |
| 每章重复整张属性表 | 只显示这次选择需要的变化 |
| 面板与正文分别新增规则 | 先改统一规则卡，再决定何时披露 |

章尾可以用系统提示制造期待，但提示要对应下一步真实选择，避免单独响一声就结束。
body.en:
| Failure | Correction |
|---|---|
| A perfect function unlocks during the crisis | Establish its source earlier and give it a new limit or cost |
| The announced number of uses changes arbitrarily | Publish only values and conditions you can maintain |
| The system gives the correct answer directly | Offer information or options; leave judgment to the character |
| The only cost is abstract “mental energy” | Show the missed event, relationship misunderstanding, or lost opportunity caused by dizziness |
| Every chapter repeats the full attribute table | Display only what changes the current choice |
| The panel and prose invent rules independently | Update one rules card first, then decide when to disclose it |

A system notification may create expectation at chapter end, but it should point to a real next choice rather than sounding once in isolation.

q.zh: 小说系统面板需要很多数值吗？
q.en: Does a fictional system panel need many numerical values?

a.zh: 不需要。数值一旦公开就会成为读者核对的规则。只保留会影响策略的数值；无法长期维护或不改变选择的项目，用定性条件更清楚。
a.en: No. Once disclosed, a number becomes a rule readers can check. Keep only values that affect strategy. Use qualitative conditions for anything you cannot maintain consistently or that never changes a choice.

q.zh: 系统可以故意欺骗主角吗？
q.en: Can the system deliberately deceive the protagonist?

a.zh: 可以，但“不可靠”本身要是稳定设定，并留下可判断的边界或代价。不能等剧情矛盾出现后，才用系统说谎解释所有问题。
a.en: Yes, provided unreliability is itself a stable rule with a discernible boundary or cost. Do not wait for a contradiction and then use “the system lied” to explain every problem.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /story-long-write 设计系统设定：先写能力边界、失效条件、可见代价和可靠程度，再给本章只显示必要信息的面板，不写正文”（Codex 里写作 `$story-long-write`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/story-long-write` to design the fictional system. Define capability limits, failure conditions, visible costs, and reliability first, then provide a panel for this chapter that displays only necessary information. Do not draft the prose.” In Codex, write `$story-long-write`.

title.zh: 打脸剧情怎么写：让反应真正改变局面
title.en: How to Write a Face-Slapping Scene That Changes the Situation

seo_title.en: How to Write a Face-Slapping Scene | ZenStory

description.zh: 打脸戏要先建立被低估的依据，再用主角行动推翻判断，并让旁观者按各自利益改变决定。附完整原创场景与失败修正。
description.en: Set up underestimation, overturn it with action, and let witnesses respond according to their interests. Includes a full scene and failure fixes.

answer.zh: 打脸剧情的核心，是主角用行动推翻了一个有分量的错误判断，并因此改变资源、关系或话语权。先让读者看懂谁在用什么标准低估主角，再让主角完成可验证的结果；旁观者的反应要影响各自计划，不能只轮流说“怎么可能”。
answer.en: The core of a face-slapping scene is the protagonist overturning a consequential false judgment through action and thereby changing resources, relationships, or authority. Show who underestimates the protagonist and by what standard, then let the protagonist produce a verifiable result. Witnesses’ reactions must affect their plans; they cannot merely take turns saying, “How is that possible?”

heading.zh: 网文打脸是什么意思？
heading.en: What Does a “Face-Slapping” Scene Mean in Web Fiction?

body.zh:
打脸是一种期待兑现：某人公开判断主角做不到、没资格或不值得，主角随后用事实让这个判断失效。它与[爽点](/oh-story/satisfaction-beats)的关系是“表现方式”和“更大类别”的关系；爽点还可以来自目标完成、成长、重逢和收获，打脸专门处理被轻视后的认知翻转。

一场打脸要有三项可核对内容：错误判断依据、主角的验证行动、验证后的实际变化。少了第三项，众人震惊完仍照旧办事，情绪就没有落地。
body.en:
A face-slapping scene delivers on an expectation: someone publicly judges the protagonist incapable, unqualified, or unworthy, and the protagonist later invalidates that judgment with facts. It is one expression of the larger category of [payoff beats](/oh-story/satisfaction-beats). Payoff may also come from achievement, growth, reunion, or gain; face-slapping specifically handles a reversal after the protagonist has been dismissed.

The scene needs three checkable elements: the basis of the wrong judgment, the protagonist’s verifying action, and a practical change after verification. Without the third, everyone may be shocked while business continues as before, leaving the emotional reward undelivered.

heading.zh: 写打脸戏的四步
heading.en: Four Steps for Writing a Face-Slapping Scene

body.zh:
1. **定标价人**：谁最有资格判断这项能力？路人只能制造声量，真正懂行或握资源的人才能改变分量。
2. **立错误判断**：低估要有信息差或利益原因，别让所有人凭空辱骂主角。
3. **用行动验真**：主角完成一件可见、可比较的事，少靠自报身份。
4. **让反应改局面**：有人改价、撤单、让位、求合作或开始反制。不同角色按照自己的损益行动。

反应可以从目击者传到关键人物，再反向影响原先轻视主角的人。传递的重点是信息和利益发生变化，不是把“震惊”复制很多遍。
body.en:
1. **Choose the qualified evaluator.** Who has the standing to judge this ability? Bystanders create noise, but an expert or resource holder gives the result weight.
2. **Establish the wrong judgment.** Underestimation should come from an information gap or self-interest, not universal abuse without cause.
3. **Verify through action.** Let the protagonist complete something visible and comparable rather than winning by announcing an identity.
4. **Make reactions alter the situation.** Someone changes a price, withdraws an order, yields a position, requests cooperation, or starts a countermeasure. Each character acts from their own gains and losses.

Reactions may travel from a witness to a decision-maker and then back to the person who dismissed the protagonist. What matters is changed information and interests, not repeating the word “shocked.”

heading.zh: 原创范例：旧桥载重验收
heading.en: Original Example: The Old Bridge Load Test

body.zh:
镇上旧桥修复验收，承包商认定临时工岑禾只会补漆，当众拒绝她查看主梁。低估有依据：她没有公开资历，承包商也怕停工赔款。

岑禾不争称号，只把一枚粉笔塞进梁缝，要求试车先减半载重。车刚上桥，粉笔应声折断，裂缝扩到承包商刚刷过的新漆下。她沿铆钉锈迹指出受力方向，又拿出三天前拍下的水位线，证明桥墩沉降仍在继续。

反应按利益展开：司机拒绝继续上桥；监理收回验收章，要求开梁检查；材料商发现承包商隐瞒用量，暂停供货；承包商不再只丢脸，他失去工期主动权并开始销毁记录。岑禾获得的是临时检测授权，同时招来下一步反制。

这场戏的爽感来自判断被事实击穿，后续动力来自权力和资源重新分配。
body.en:
During acceptance testing for a restored town bridge, the contractor assumes temporary worker Cen He can only touch up paint and publicly refuses to let her inspect the main beam. The underestimation has a basis: she has not disclosed her qualifications, and the contractor fears compensation for a work stoppage.

Cen He does not argue about titles. She wedges a piece of chalk into a beam crack and asks that the test vehicle carry half its planned load. As soon as the vehicle enters the bridge, the chalk snaps and the crack spreads beneath fresh paint applied by the contractor. She traces the load direction through rust marks on the rivets, then produces a photograph of the waterline from three days earlier, proving that the pier is still settling.

Reactions follow interests. The driver refuses to continue. The inspector withdraws the acceptance stamp and orders the beam opened up for inspection. A materials supplier discovers that the contractor concealed quantities and suspends deliveries. The contractor is no longer merely embarrassed: he loses control of the schedule and begins destroying records. Cen He receives temporary inspection authority and also draws the next countermove.

The satisfaction comes from facts shattering the judgment. The next movement comes from a redistribution of power and resources.

heading.zh: 围观者震惊怎么写才不重复？
heading.en: How to Show Onlookers’ Shock Without Repeating Yourself

body.zh:
给每个有镜头的人一个自己的账：

| 人物 | 他在乎什么 | 看见结果后的动作 |
|---|---|---|
| 普通目击者 | 安全 | 退下桥面、叫停车辆 |
| 同行 | 专业判断 | 复核数据、改口请教 |
| 掌权者 | 责任与成本 | 暂停验收、重新授权 |
| 利益受损者 | 地位或收益 | 遮掩证据、改变策略 |

一句沉默、一次撤章或一张被改写的报价单，常比连续的惊叹更有力。最重要的一层反应，应落在以后还有戏、且能改变主角处境的人身上。
body.en:
Give everyone in the scene a stake of their own:

| Character | What matters to them | Action after seeing the result |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary witness | Safety | Step off the bridge and stop vehicles |
| Peer professional | Expert judgment | Recheck the data and ask for guidance |
| Decision-maker | Responsibility and cost | Pause acceptance and grant new authority |
| Party that loses | Position or revenue | Hide evidence and change strategy |

Silence, a withdrawn stamp, or a revised quote often carries more force than repeated exclamations. Put the most important reaction on someone who remains active later and can change the protagonist’s circumstances.

heading.zh: 打脸写了却不爽：常见原因
heading.en: Why a Face-Slapping Scene Can Still Feel Flat

body.zh:
| 失败 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 对手无缘无故辱骂 | 给他信息差、利益或偏见来源 |
| 主角靠报姓名获胜 | 用可验证行动证明能力 |
| 所有人同声惊叹 | 按各自损益写不同动作 |
| 打完脸没有收获 | 改变权限、资源、关系或后续目标 |
| 压抑太久却未建立人物投入 | 先让读者看见主角付出和真正想守住的东西 |
| 每次都在同一群人前重复 | 提高判断者分量，或让结果影响更大的局面 |

打脸不能替代人物动机。主角为什么非赢不可，仍需回到[人物动机写法](/oh-story/character-motivation)。
body.en:
| Failure | Correction |
|---|---|
| The opponent insults the protagonist without cause | Give the opponent an information gap, self-interest, or source of bias |
| The protagonist wins by announcing an identity | Prove the ability through verifiable action |
| Everyone exclaims in unison | Write different actions based on each person’s gains and losses |
| The scene produces no gain | Change access, resources, relationships, or the next objective |
| The protagonist is kept down too long without reader investment | Show what the protagonist has worked for and truly wants to protect |
| The same audience sees the same display repeatedly | Raise the evaluator’s weight or let the result affect a larger situation |

Ground the scene in character motivation: why must the protagonist win? Continue with [Writing Character Motivation](/oh-story/character-motivation).

q.zh: 打脸剧情一定要让反派当众道歉吗？
q.en: Must the antagonist apologize publicly?

a.zh: 不用。撤回决定、交出权限、失去盟友或被迫换策略，都能完成认知与局面的翻转。道歉只有在关系结算需要时才有价值。
a.en: No. Reversing a decision, surrendering authority, losing allies, or being forced to change strategy can all overturn the judgment and situation. An apology matters only when the relationship itself requires that settlement.

q.zh: 短剧打脸和小说打脸有什么不同？
q.en: How does a face-slapping scene differ between short drama and fiction?

a.zh: 核心相同：错误判断、可见验证、局面改变。短剧更依赖能立刻看懂的物件、动作和权力变化；小说可以多承载信息差与人物内心，但仍需把结果落成行动。
a.en: The core is the same: a wrong judgment, visible verification, and a changed situation. Short drama leans more heavily on immediately legible objects, actions, and shifts of power. Fiction can carry more interiority and information gaps, but the result still has to become action.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /story-long-write 只设计这场打脸戏，写清错误判断、标价人、主角验证行动、每个在场者的利益反应和局面变化，不写正文”（Codex 里写作 `$story-long-write`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/story-long-write` only to design this face-slapping scene. Record the false judgment, qualified evaluator, protagonist’s verifying action, each witness’s interest-driven reaction, and the resulting change in the situation. Do not draft the prose.” In Codex, write `$story-long-write`.

title.zh: 小说伏笔怎么埋：伏笔和悬念的区别与回收方法
title.en: How to Plant Foreshadowing: Setup, Suspense, and Payoff

seo_title.zh: 小说伏笔怎么埋：区别、铺垫与回收
seo_title.en: Foreshadowing: Setup, Suspense, and Payoff

description.zh: 分清伏笔和悬念，用演出名单被改的原创例子讲清自然埋线、可信误导、揭示顺序和回收时机，修正硬藏答案与拖延剧情。
description.en: Altered-list example: separate foreshadowing from suspense, plant and misdirect fairly, order and pay off clues, fix hidden answers and plot delay.

answer.zh: 埋伏笔先想清后面要揭示的事实，再把能支持它的细节放进前面的正常行动里。初读时，细节有眼前用途；揭示后，读者能重新理解它。悬念则让读者当下想知道某个问题的答案。两者可以配合：先让人问“名单为什么变了”，再让早先不起眼的纸张痕迹成为答案的一部分。
answer.en: Foreshadowing begins by defining the fact that will be revealed later, then placing details that can support it inside earlier, ordinary actions. On first reading, the detail has an immediate purpose; after the reveal, readers can reinterpret it. Suspense instead makes readers want an answer now. They can work together: first ask, “Why did the list change?” then let an earlier, unremarkable mark on the paper become part of the answer.

heading.zh: 伏笔和悬念有什么区别
heading.en: What Is the Difference Between Foreshadowing and Suspense?

body.zh:
区分时先问读者此刻会做什么：是等待一个答案，还是暂时把细节当作普通信息记下？伏笔通常在后面显出意义，悬念通常在眼前牵引阅读；跨度长短可以辅助判断，具体仍要看这条信息在故事里起什么作用。

| 判断角度 | 伏笔 | 悬念 |
|---|---|---|
| 读者当下的反应 | 先接受一个看似自然的细节 | 明确想知道谁、为什么、怎么办 |
| 作者要安排的事 | 前面的细节与后面的事实相互支持 | 给问题提供推进、可能答案和兑现 |
| 揭示后的效果 | 回头看，原来早有迹象 | 等待得到回应，并看到后果 |
| 本页例子 | 名单纸角有两组订孔 | 主唱的名字为何从名单消失 |

同一个细节可以改变作用。纸角订孔第一次出现时是整理材料中的小事；主角发现名单被换后，它就成为正在追查的线索。写作时明确这一刻要让读者注意到哪一层意思，胜过给所有细节贴上“重大伏笔”的标签。
body.en:
Ask what the reader does at this moment: wait actively for an answer, or accept a detail as ordinary information for now? Foreshadowing usually gains significance later; suspense usually pulls the reader forward immediately. Duration can help distinguish them, but their function in the story is decisive.

| Question | Foreshadowing | Suspense |
|---|---|---|
| Reader’s immediate response | Accept a seemingly natural detail | Explicitly wonder who, why, or what happens next |
| Author’s task | Make the earlier detail and later fact support each other | Give the question progress, possible answers, and a payoff |
| Effect after revelation | Looking back, the signs were already there | The question is answered, and consequences follow |
| Example on this page | Two sets of staple holes in the corner of the list | Why did the lead singer’s name disappear? |

One detail may change functions. The staple holes first appear as a minor feature while materials are organized. After the protagonist realizes the list was replaced, they become evidence under investigation. Decide which layer readers should notice now instead of labeling every detail “major foreshadowing.”

heading.zh: 伏笔怎么埋得自然：先让细节在眼前有用
heading.en: How to Plant Foreshadowing Naturally: Give the Detail an Immediate Purpose

body.zh:
按下面的顺序设计，再写成场景：

1. 写清将来的揭示。谁做了什么，为什么做，主角知道后会怎样选择？
2. 找到可以提前出现的迹象。它应当来自已经发生的事、人物习惯或确实存在的条件。
3. 给迹象一个眼前用途。人物正在整理、争执、工作或解决小麻烦，细节随行动出现。
4. 分开事实和解释。读者看到了事实，人物可以暂时把它解释错；揭示时再改变解释。
5. 回收后推动行动。知道真相要改变选择、关系或代价，不能只让作者宣布“这里早有伏笔”。

原创新例从一张演出名单展开：主唱许沅发现自己的名字被删，怀疑与她争主唱的唐宁。实际情况是策划周澄为临时加入赞助方推荐的独唱节目，重新排了节目顺序，却没有通知所有人。

前面的正常行动可以这样写：

> 许沅抱着签到本进排练室。周澄把名单从纸板上拆下来，顺手递给她订书机：“这一版字大，贴出去好看。”她按住纸角，发现旁边还有两排细孔，便往里挪了挪，免得纸裂。

这段先完成换名单、借订书机和避免纸裂的眼前动作。读者知道名单换过，却还不知道换版会删掉谁。后来追查时，两组订孔可以提示“这份名单确实替换过”，但单凭孔眼还不能认定周澄改了节目，更不能证明他的动机。
body.en:
Design in this order, then turn the design into a scene:

1. Define the later reveal. Who did what, why, and what choice will the protagonist make after learning it?
2. Find an earlier sign. It should grow from something that happened, a character habit, or an existing condition.
3. Give the sign an immediate use. Let it appear while someone organizes, argues, works, or solves a small problem.
4. Separate fact from explanation. Readers see the fact; the character may interpret it incorrectly until the reveal changes that explanation.
5. Make the payoff drive action. The truth must alter a choice, relationship, or cost rather than merely proving that the author planted a clue.

Original example: lead singer Xu Yuan finds her name removed from a performance list and suspects Tang Ning, who competed for the role. In fact, planner Zhou Cheng rearranged the running order to add a solo recommended by the sponsor and failed to notify everyone.

An earlier ordinary action might read:

> Xu Yuan carried the sign-in book into the rehearsal room. Zhou Cheng removed the list from its board and handed her the stapler. “The type is larger on this version. It’ll look better on display.” As she held down the corner, she noticed two rows of tiny holes nearby and moved the staple inward so the paper would not tear.

The passage completes the immediate actions of replacing the list, lending the stapler, and preventing a tear. Readers know the list was replaced but not whose item disappeared. Later, the two sets of holes support “this version replaced another,” but the holes alone cannot prove Zhou Cheng changed the program or establish his motive.

heading.zh: 四种信息顺序：同一个问题怎样讲出不同效果
heading.en: Four Information Orders: Different Effects from the Same Question

body.zh:
Oh Story 的悬念方法按信息出现的顺序区分直接揭晓、探索推进、误导后揭晓和连续改判。先选你要的阅读效果，再决定在哪一步提供事实和解释。

| 写法 | 信息怎样出现 | 名单案例怎么用 |
|---|---|---|
| 直接揭晓 | 抛出问题，较快交代答案 | 许沅问谁重排了节目，周澄直接承认；下一场写她怎样争取原定演出 |
| 探索推进 | 问题之后给可验证的提示，再揭晓 | 从纸角订孔查到旧版，再把新旧节目的变化对照起来 |
| 一次误判后揭晓 | 给出可信但不完整的指向，再用新事实改判 | 唐宁刚争过主唱，看似最有动机；旧版却显示她自己的独唱也被删了 |
| 连续改判后揭晓 | 两种看似合理的解释先后被事实修正 | 先怀疑争位置，后以为只是压缩时长；新增赞助节目和排练群里的通知补全真实原因 |

误导要有依据。唐宁与许沅争过位置，所以怀疑能成立；她也失去节目，才有力量改变读者的判断。不要为了反转，在叙述里把“唐宁亲手改了名单”写成确定事实，结尾再否认。
body.en:
Oh Story distinguishes direct revelation, investigative progress, revelation after one plausible misreading, and successive reinterpretation by the order in which information appears. Choose the reading effect first, then decide where each fact and explanation arrives.

| Method | Information order | Use in the list example |
|---|---|---|
| Direct revelation | Raise the question and answer it quickly | Xu Yuan asks who reordered the program; Zhou Cheng admits it; the next scene shows how she fights for her original performance |
| Investigative progress | Offer verifiable indications after the question, then reveal | Trace the staple holes to the old version, then compare the old and new programs |
| One misreading, then reveal | Point credibly but incompletely in one direction, then revise with a new fact | Tang Ning just competed for lead singer and appears motivated; the old version shows her solo was also removed |
| Successive reinterpretation, then reveal | Facts successively correct two plausible explanations | First suspect competition, then assume the show was shortened; the added sponsor solo and the notice in the rehearsal group complete the real cause |

Misdirection needs evidence. Tang Ning previously competed with Xu Yuan, so suspicion is plausible. The loss of her own solo can then revise that belief. Do not narrate “Tang Ning personally changed the list” as a fact and deny it at the end merely to manufacture a twist.

heading.zh: 伏笔多久回收合适：看等待期间有没有推进
