The causal frame remains stable: forced uniformity causes the joint rehearsal to fail, the proposal to split the program brings Bai Qiu’s independent goal into the main line, and her alternative requires Li Zhen to give up unilateral arrangement control for this piece. The joint concert fulfills this volume’s contract while passing the long-term leadership question into the next volume.

heading.zh: 把已批准事实交给AI，未知项单独返回
heading.en: Give AI Approved Facts and Keep Unknowns Separate

body.zh:
AI适合帮助检查因果缺口、整理单元顺序和提出备选连接。先提供作者已经批准的事实，再限定它只处理一卷。下面是本文原创的交接模板；将方括号替换为你的内容。

> 我正在规划长篇小说中的一卷。只使用下列作者已批准事实，不要补写新的正史设定：  
> 全书阶段与本卷位置：[内容]  
> 卷首状态：[内容]  
> 本卷读者约定：[内容]  
> 主推进线与阻力：[内容]  
> 已成立的支线、关系与世界规则：[内容]  
> 必须保留到后续的答案或能力：[内容]  
> 期望的卷末变化：[内容]
>
> 请输出：一份简洁的单卷工作表；一组因果相连的情节单元，每个单元写进入原因、阻碍、决定、可见结果和下一单元触发；各支线改变主线条件的位置；本卷兑现与保留的内容；卷末交接。  
> 将材料无法确定的内容集中列入“待作者决定”，说明缺少哪项信息，并提供至多两个不互相冒充既定事实的备选方向。不要替我选定新人物背景、世界规则、幕后真相或终局答案，也不要展开成逐章正文。

收到结果后，先审“待作者决定”，再看单元链。模型若把备选写成事实，就退回该项；若新增内容改变全书方向，也要先由作者批准，再进入卷纲。
body.en:
AI can help expose causal gaps, arrange plot units, and suggest alternative connections. Supply author-approved facts first and limit the task to one volume. The following handoff template was written for this article; replace the bracketed fields with your material.

> I am planning one volume of a long novel. Use only the author-approved facts below, and do not add new canon:  
> Book phase and this volume’s place in it: [content]  
> Opening state: [content]  
> Reader contract for the volume: [content]  
> Principal progression line and resistance: [content]  
> Established supporting lines, relationships, and world rules: [content]  
> Answers or abilities reserved for later: [content]  
> Intended end-state change: [content]
>
> Return a concise volume worksheet; a causal set of plot units, each with an entry cause, obstacle, decision, visible result, and trigger for the next unit; the points where supporting lines change main-line conditions; what the volume fulfills and preserves; and the handoff at the ending.  
> Put anything the supplied material cannot determine in a separate “Author decision needed” list. State what information is missing and offer no more than two alternatives, clearly labeled as proposals rather than canon. Do not choose new character histories, world rules, hidden truths, or endgame answers for me, and do not expand the plan into chapter prose.

Review “Author decision needed” before the unit chain. Return any proposal presented as an established fact. If a new idea would alter the book direction, approve it explicitly before adding it to the volume outline.

heading.zh: 用五个检查修理松散卷纲
heading.en: Use Five Checks to Repair a Loose Volume Outline

body.zh:
完成初稿后，按下面五种症状检查。每次只修因果和阶段功能，再决定是否增加情节。

| 症状 | 检查问题 | 修理方式 |
|---|---|---|
| 支线彼此断开 | 这条线在哪个可见节点改变主线条件？ | 写出改变前后；找不到变化时合并、缩短或移除。 |
| 全卷都像高潮 | 每个单元是否同时使用最大危险、最大揭示和最大代价？ | 保留卷末最需要的升级，把中段改成取得条件、承受损失或改变联盟。 |
| 回报没有铺垫 | 兑现所需的人、物、规则或承诺此前在哪里进入故事？ | 在较早单元放入可辨认的进展标记，让兑现来自累积结果。 |
| 提前透支终局 | 本卷是否用了后续阶段才该出现的答案、能力或对手底牌？ | 把完整答案留后，只交付本卷能承担的证据、局部胜利或新问题。 |
| 卷末什么也没变 | 删除本卷后，下一卷的目标、关系、信息、资源和代价是否完全相同？ | 重写卷末选择，让至少一项条件被取得、失去、公开、锁定或重新解释。 |

还可以选择维护三份轻量记录：已经建立但尚未兑现的承诺、各推进线最近一次可见变化、连续承压后该轮换的压力来源。它们只在帮助你发现遗漏时使用；不要为了填表新增剧情，也不要求所有线路平均推进。
body.en:
After the first pass, check the outline against five common symptoms. Repair causality and stage function first, then decide whether the story needs more material.

| Symptom | Question | Repair |
|---|---|---|
| Disconnected lines | At which visible point does this line change a main-line condition? | Write the before and after states. If nothing changes, merge, shorten, or remove the line. |
| Every unit feels like a climax | Does each unit spend the greatest danger, revelation, and cost at once? | Reserve the escalation the ending needs. Let middle units obtain conditions, absorb losses, or change alliances. |
| Unearned payoff | Where did the person, object, rule, or promise required by the payoff enter the story? | Add recognizable progress earlier so the payoff grows from accumulated results. |
| Premature endgame reveal | Does this volume use an answer, ability, or opponent asset assigned to a later phase? | Preserve the complete answer and deliver only the evidence, partial victory, or new question this volume can support. |
| Nothing changes at the ending | If the volume disappears, are the next volume’s goals, relationships, facts, resources, and costs identical? | Rewrite the ending choice so at least one condition is gained, lost, revealed, locked, or reinterpreted. |

You can also keep three lightweight records when useful: promises established but not yet fulfilled, the most recent visible change on each progression line, and a pressure source that may need rotation after repeated use. Use them only to expose omissions. Do not add plot to fill a table, and do not force every line to advance equally.

q.zh: 卷纲要写到每一章吗？
q.en: Should a Volume Outline Cover Every Chapter?

a.zh: 不需要。卷纲先确定读者约定、主推进线、情节单元的因果交接和卷末变化。等某个单元准备进入正文时，再把它拆成章节目标、场景冲突和结尾落点；这样既保留方向，也能根据实际写作调整章节安排。
a.en: No. First establish the reader contract, principal progression line, causal handoffs between plot units, and end-state change. Break a selected unit into chapter goals, scene conflicts, and endings only when it is approaching draft stage. This preserves direction while leaving the chapter arrangement adjustable.

q.zh: 一卷需要几条支线和几个情节单元？
q.en: How Many Supporting Lines and Plot Units Does One Volume Need?

a.zh: 没有统一数量。保留能够独立产生选择、并会改变主线条件的支线；情节单元则以完成本卷阶段变化所需的因果步骤为准。功能重复的线路可以合并，无法把结果交给下一单元的事件需要重写或删除。
a.en: There is no universal count. Keep supporting lines that create meaningful choices and change a main-line condition. Use as many plot units as the causal path to the volume’s stage change requires. Merge duplicate functions, and revise or remove incidents that pass no changed condition forward.

q.zh: AI补出的设定很精彩，可以直接放进卷纲吗？
q.en: Can I Put an Appealing AI-Invented Detail Straight into the Outline?

a.zh: 先把它标成提案，检查它是否改写人物经历、世界规则、幕后真相或后续阶段安排。只有作者明确批准后，它才进入事实清单；未批准时放在待决定区，避免后面的单元把一个临时想法当成既定前提。
a.en: Label it as a proposal first. Check whether it changes a character history, world rule, hidden truth, or later phase. Add it to the fact list only after explicit author approval. Until then, keep it in the decision-needed section so later units do not treat a temporary idea as canon.

text.zh: story-long-write 可以在只讨论结构的阶段协助整理单卷工作表、因果单元和卷末交接。提供作者已批准事实与保留项，并要求把材料不足处单列为待决定问题；确认卷纲后，再进入章节或正文规划。
text.en: story-long-write can help organize a one-volume worksheet, causal plot units, and the ending handoff while the work remains at the structural stage. Supply author-approved facts and reserved material, ask for unsupported areas to be listed as decisions, and approve the volume plan before moving into chapter or prose planning.

title.zh: AI写小说字数不够怎么办：先补漏掉的情节点
title.en: AI Novel Chapter Too Short? Restore the Missing Beats

seo_title.zh: AI写小说字数不够怎么办｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: AI Novel Chapter Too Short? | ZenStory

description.zh: AI生成的小说章节比目标短时，先核对已批准情节点。只补漏写的行动、阻碍、选择与结果；情节点齐全就由作者调整目标或接受当前长度。
description.en: AI chapter too short? Audit approved beats. Add only missing action, resistance, choice, and results; revise the plan or accept the current length.

answer.zh: AI写出的小说章节比目标短，先把已批准的情节点逐项对照正文，找出真正漏写的行动、阻碍、选择或结果。只扩写这些缺口，并保持既定事实、视角、关系和后续安排不变。若所有必要情节点都已落到正文中，就停止补写：作者可以接受当前长度，也可以修改字数目标或细纲后重写。字数目标是规划参照，不能成为新增剧情和重复描写的理由。
answer.en: When an AI-generated novel chapter comes in short, compare the draft against the approved beats and locate any missing action, resistance, choice, or result. Expand only those gaps while preserving established facts, point of view, relationships, and later plans. If every required beat is already on the page, stop adding prose: the author can accept the current length or revise the target or outline before rewriting. A word target is a planning constraint, not permission to invent plot or repeat description.

heading.zh: 先查缺失情节点，再处理字数差额
heading.en: Audit Approved Beats Before Addressing the Shortfall

body.zh:
先记下目标长度与当前长度，用它们确认差额；接下来的编辑判断要回到本章已经批准的内容。把细纲中的必要情节点列在左边，把正文中真正完成它的位置列在右边。

| 核对项 | 正文中要找到的证据 |
|---|---|
| 人物目标 | 人物在当前场景具体想完成什么 |
| 阻碍 | 原计划为什么无法直接完成 |
| 关键选择 | 人物选了哪条路，又放弃了什么 |
| 可见结果 | 目标、风险、信息、关系或资源发生了什么变化 |
| 章节交接 | 这个结果怎样改变下一步 |

“提过”不等于“写到了”。如果细纲要求人物在两种代价之间选择，正文却一句话跳到结果，这一拍仍然缺失。补写时让读者看见阻碍怎样出现、人物依据什么作出选择、选择造成什么后果。

同一个情节点已经用动作、对白和结果完成后，不要再换几组形容词复述。感官、反应或环境细节只在改变人物判断、行动或场面结果时加入。
body.en:
Record the target and current length to establish the size of the gap, then base the editorial decision on the chapter's approved material. List each required beat on the left and the place where the prose actually delivers it on the right.

| Check | Evidence to locate in the draft |
|---|---|
| Character goal | What the character is trying to accomplish in this scene |
| Resistance | Why the original approach cannot work directly |
| Key choice | Which path the character takes and what that choice gives up |
| Visible result | What changes in the goal, risk, information, relationship, or resources |
| Chapter handoff | How that result changes the next step |

A mention does not always complete a beat. If the outline requires a choice between two costs and the draft jumps straight to the outcome, the choice is still missing. The repair should let the reader see the obstacle arrive, understand the basis of the decision, and witness its consequence.

Once action, dialogue, and result have completed a beat, do not restate it through extra sets of adjectives. Add perception, reaction, or setting detail only when it changes the character's judgment, action, or the outcome of the scene.

heading.zh: 按核对结果选择补写、改纲或收下
heading.en: Choose Expansion, Replanning, or Acceptance

body.zh:
核对后只有两种编辑结果。

1. **必要情节点有缺口。** 只补缺失的拍点。优先补能形成场景推进的行动、阻碍、选择与后果，让这一拍从规划标签变成读者看得见的过程。
2. **必要情节点全部完成。** 停止扩写。作者决定接受当前长度，或者调整细纲与字数目标后重写。新的支线、人物、秘密、世界设定和冲突都需要先由作者批准，不能作为凑字方案混进正文。

补写范围可以写成一句可核对的任务，例如：“展开门被锁住之后的应对，让林澈尝试原方案、发现失败，并在两个已批准选项中作出选择；结尾保持原定结果。”这种任务限定了缺口、过程和落点，也把其他剧情排除在外。

若你无法指出新增段落对应哪个已批准情节点，这段文字就没有进入本轮补写的依据。
body.en:
The audit leads to two editorial outcomes.

1. **A required beat is missing.** Add only that beat. Favor action, resistance, choice, and consequence that turn a planning label into a process the reader can witness.
2. **Every required beat is complete.** Stop expanding. The author decides whether to accept the current length or revise the outline and target before rewriting. A new subplot, character, secret, world fact, or conflict needs author approval before it enters the chapter; it cannot serve as word-count padding.

Define the repair as a testable sentence: “Expand what happens after Lin Che finds the door locked. Let him try the original approach, discover why it fails, and choose between the two approved options. Preserve the planned result.” This identifies the gap, process, and endpoint while excluding unrelated plot.

If you cannot map a proposed paragraph to an approved beat, it has no basis for entering this repair pass.

heading.zh: 可复制提示词：先报告缺口，再补写
heading.en: Copyable Prompt: Report the Gaps Before Expanding

body.zh:
把方括号替换成你的内容。第一次先要核对表，不要让模型立即续写。

> 我在检查一章比目标短的小说草稿。目标长度只作规划参照，请先判断已批准情节点是否漏写，不要为了接近数字新增内容。  
> **既定事实与连续性：** [人物关系、时间、地点、物件状态、视角、已公开信息]  
> **本章必须完成的情节点：** [逐项列出目标、阻碍、选择、结果和章尾交接]  
> **必须保留到后文的内容：** [秘密、能力、人物、关系变化或答案]  
> **当前草稿：** [粘贴正文]  
> 先输出一张核对表：每个情节点标为“已完成”或“缺失”，引用或概括对应正文作为证据。不要改写正文。若判断需要新增人物、支线、设定、秘密或事件才能补足，请列入“待作者决定”，不要自行采用。

确认核对表后，再发送补写要求：

> 只补写核对表中确认缺失的情节点：[列出项目]。把已批准的行动、阻碍、选择和结果演成连续场景；保持既定事实、视角、人物声音、信息揭露顺序和章尾结果。每个新增段落都应推进所列情节点。不要新增人物、支线、世界设定、秘密、回忆或后续伏笔，也不要用同义复述、形容词、无后果的感官和反应凑长度。材料不足时停下并列出需要作者决定的问题。若情节点已全部完成，请不要补写，只返回“接受当前长度”与“修改目标或细纲后重写”两个作者选项。

先分开诊断与改写，可以避免模型一看到“字数不足”就直接制造材料。作者确认缺口后，补写范围也更容易复核。
body.en:
Replace the bracketed fields with your material. Ask for an audit first instead of requesting an immediate continuation.

> I am reviewing a novel chapter that came in below its target. Treat the target as a planning reference. First determine whether any approved beats are missing; do not add material merely to approach the number.  
> **Established facts and continuity:** [relationships, time, place, object states, point of view, revealed information]  
> **Required chapter beats:** [list the goal, resistance, choice, result, and ending handoff]  
> **Material reserved for later:** [secrets, abilities, characters, relationship changes, or answers]  
> **Current draft:** [paste the prose]  
> Return an audit table first. Mark each beat “complete” or “missing” and quote or summarize the relevant evidence from the draft. Do not revise the prose yet. If completing a beat would require a new character, subplot, setting fact, secret, or event, put it under “Author decision needed” and do not adopt it.

After confirming the audit, send the scoped expansion request:

> Expand only these confirmed missing beats: [list them]. Dramatize the approved action, resistance, choice, and result as a continuous scene. Preserve established facts, point of view, character voice, reveal order, and the planned ending. Every added paragraph must advance one of the listed beats. Do not introduce characters, subplots, world facts, secrets, memories, or future setup. Do not pad with paraphrase, adjectives, or sensory and emotional reactions that have no consequence. If the supplied material is insufficient, stop and list the author decisions required. If every beat is complete, do not expand; return two author options: accept the current length, or revise the target or outline before rewriting.

Separating diagnosis from revision keeps a shortfall from turning into automatic invention. Once the author confirms the gaps, the expansion also has a clear review boundary.

heading.zh: 原创示例：补回被跳过的阻碍与选择
heading.en: Original Example: Restore the Omitted Obstacle and Choice

body.zh:
下面的片段为本文原创。已经批准的情节点是：乔岑必须在末班车前归还档案馆钥匙；侧门上锁后，她要在“把钥匙留进无人确认的投信口”与“按铃叫醒值夜的唐姨，并承认自己抄过一页登记”之间选择；她选择按铃；唐姨收回钥匙，把那页登记留到第二天一起查看；乔岑错过末班车。

### 过短草稿

> 乔岑在末班车前赶到档案馆，把钥匙还给值夜的唐姨，也承认自己抄了那页登记。唐姨让她第二天再来。

草稿写了开头与结果，却跳过门锁造成的阻碍、两个选项之间的取舍，以及承认行为怎样改变两人的下一步。这些都是已批准内容，可以补回。

### 限定范围后的补写

> 乔岑赶到档案馆时，侧门的铁链已经扣死。她把钥匙贴近投信口，试了试宽度。只要松手，她还赶得上末班车；可钥匙落进黑暗里，没人能确认它已经交还。  
> 她收回手，按响值夜铃。  
> “谁？”唐姨隔着门问。  
> “是我。”乔岑握住钥匙，“我用它抄了那页登记。”  
> 铁链响了一声。唐姨开门接过钥匙：“明早再来。那一页，我们一起看。”  
> 末班车从街口驶过。乔岑站在门外，点了点头。

补写后的第一段完成阻碍与代价，第二至四段完成选择，第五段给出关系和信息处理上的新状态，末句兑现错过末班车的代价。新增内容都能对应已批准情节点，没有另开支线，也没有引入未经批准的新剧情前提。
body.en:
The following passage was written for this article. Its approved beats are: Qiao Cen must return an archive key before the last bus; when she finds the side door locked, she must choose between dropping the key through an unattended mail slot and ringing for Aunt Tang, the night custodian, which also means admitting that she copied a registry page; she rings; Aunt Tang takes the key and postpones reviewing the page until they can do it together the next morning; Qiao Cen misses the bus.

### Short draft

> Qiao Cen reached the archive before the last bus, returned the key to Aunt Tang, and admitted that she had copied the registry page. Aunt Tang told her to come back the next day.

The draft supplies the opening and outcome, then skips the locked-door obstacle, the tradeoff between the approved options, and the way the admission changes what happens next. Those approved beats can be restored.

### Scoped expansion

> When Qiao Cen reached the archive, a chain held the side door shut. She tested the key against the mail slot. If she let it fall, she could still catch the last bus, but the key would land in darkness with no one to confirm its return.  
> She drew her hand back and pressed the night bell.  
> “Who is it?” Aunt Tang called through the door.  
> “Me.” Qiao Cen closed her fingers around the key. “I used it to copy the registry page.”  
> The chain shifted. Aunt Tang opened the door and took the key. “Come back in the morning. We will look at that page together.”  
> The last bus passed the end of the street. Qiao Cen remained outside and nodded.

The first added paragraph delivers the obstacle and cost. The next three deliver the choice. Aunt Tang's response establishes the new relationship and information state, and the final line pays the approved cost of missing the bus. Every addition maps to an approved beat; no unrelated subplot or unapproved story premise was introduced.

heading.zh: 补写后做一次状态、连续性与段落检查
heading.en: Finish With State, Continuity, and Paragraph Checks

body.zh:
补写完成后，不要只看字数。用下面的检查决定这次修订是否成立。

- [ ] **状态变化清楚。** 删掉补写段落后，人物目标、风险、信息、关系或资源会失去一项已批准变化。
- [ ] **每段都有归属。** 每个新增段落都能标回一个缺失情节点；无法标注的段落删除或退回作者决定。
- [ ] **连续性未改变。** 时间、地点、物件位置、人物已知信息、视角和关系与前后文一致。
- [ ] **保留项仍然保留。** 后文才揭晓的答案、人物、能力和伏笔没有提前出现。
- [ ] **场景完成了目标—阻碍—变化。** 人物做了事情，阻碍影响了行动，结尾留下可见结果。
- [ ] **没有重复功能。** 同一选择或情绪没有被动作、解释、感官和总结反复说多次。

全部通过后，作者仍然可以接受一个低于原目标的章节。章节完成度由它兑现了哪些必要变化来判断；字数只帮助发现可能的缺口。
body.en:
After the expansion, do not evaluate the revision by length alone. Use these checks to decide whether the repair holds.

- [ ] **The state change is clear.** Removing the added passage would erase an approved change in goal, risk, information, relationship, or resources.
- [ ] **Every paragraph has a beat.** Each added paragraph maps to a confirmed gap. Delete anything that cannot be mapped or return it for an author decision.
- [ ] **Continuity remains intact.** Time, place, object locations, character knowledge, point of view, and relationships agree with the surrounding chapters.
- [ ] **Reserved material stays reserved.** Answers, characters, abilities, and setups assigned to later chapters have not appeared early.
- [ ] **The scene completes goal, resistance, and change.** The character acts, the obstacle affects the action, and the ending leaves a visible result.
- [ ] **No function is repeated.** The same choice or feeling is not restated through action, explanation, sensation, and summary.

The author can still accept a chapter that remains below its original target after every check passes. Completion depends on the required changes the chapter delivers; length helps reveal possible omissions.

q.zh: AI写的章节字数不足，一定要让它续写吗？
q.en: Must I ask the AI to continue every short chapter?

a.zh: 不用。先核对必要情节点。存在漏写时，只补对应缺口；情节点齐全时，由作者接受当前长度，或修改细纲与目标后重写。
a.en: No. Audit the required beats first. Add only a confirmed omission. When every beat is complete, the author can accept the current length or revise the outline and target before rewriting.

q.zh: 怎样让AI精确写到指定字数？
q.en: How do I make AI hit an exact word count?

a.zh: 把字数当作规划参照，不承诺精确落点。先明确必须完成的情节点和禁止新增的内容，再按实际草稿检查遗漏；最终长度由作者结合章节完成度决定。
a.en: Treat the number as a planning reference rather than a guaranteed endpoint. Define required beats and prohibited additions, audit the actual draft for omissions, and let the author judge the final length alongside chapter completeness.

q.zh: 情节点都写到了，章节还是显得薄怎么办？
q.en: What if every beat is present but the chapter still feels thin?

a.zh: 回到作者层面检查这章承担的任务、细纲密度和字数目标。若需要新的冲突、关系变化或剧情结果，先修改细纲并批准这些变化，再重写；不要在现稿里临时塞入。
a.en: Revisit the chapter's assigned job, outline density, and target. If it needs a new conflict, relationship change, or plot result, revise and approve the outline before rewriting instead of inserting that material during a length repair.

text.zh: 请先核对这章的已批准情节点与当前正文，标出漏写的行动、阻碍、选择和结果。只补确认缺失的拍点，保持既定事实、视角、人物声音与后续安排；情节点齐全时停止补写，并把接受当前长度或修改细纲与目标交给作者决定。
text.en: Audit the chapter against its approved beats and identify any omitted action, resistance, choice, or result. Expand only confirmed gaps while preserving facts, point of view, character voice, and later plans. When every beat is complete, stop and leave the choice between accepting the current length and revising the outline or target to the author.

title.zh: SRT字幕和AI配音不同步：分清偏移、漂移与单条错误
title.en: SRT Subtitles Out of Sync with AI Narration: Offset, Drift, or One Bad Cue?

seo_title.en: SRT Subtitles Out of Sync with AI Voice | ZenStory

description.zh: 导入SRT后字幕提前、延后或越播越偏？用成片开头、中段、结尾的实测检查点，区分整体偏移、持续漂移与单条时间码错误，再重播终版验证。
description.en: SRT early, late, or drifting from AI narration? Check the final video’s start, middle, and end, diagnose the pattern, repair it, and replay the render.

answer.zh: SRT字幕与AI配音不同步时，不要先凭感觉拖整条轨道。固定要发布的最终视频和实际采用的旁白，在开头、中段、结尾各选一句起止都清楚的台词，同时记录声音起止与字幕显示起止。分别计算“字幕开始－声音开始”和“字幕结束－声音结束”：各处起止误差都大致相同，是整体偏移；误差沿片长持续增大或减小，是漂移；只有个别字幕的开始或结束异常，是单条边界错误。按证据修正后重新导出，并在成片中复查起止点。旁白有改动，或剪辑改变了字幕相关的时间、顺序、时长或时间轴位置时，必须对新终版重做检查；只改颜色等不影响时间轴的操作不会自动使旧检查失效。
answer.en: When an imported SRT does not match AI narration, do not begin by dragging the entire track by feel. Freeze the final video and the narration actually used, then choose a line with clear spoken start and end points near the beginning, middle, and end. Record both speech boundaries and both displayed cue boundaries. Calculate subtitle start minus speech start and subtitle end minus speech end. If start and end errors are roughly alike across the runtime, you have a global offset; if they grow or shrink through the runtime, you have drift; if only certain cue starts or ends are wrong, you have local boundary errors. Apply only the correction supported by those observations, export again, and replay both boundaries in the render. Recheck after a narration change or an edit that changes subtitle-relevant timing, order, duration, or timeline position; a color-only edit does not by itself invalidate the timing evidence.

heading.zh: 先固定终版，再记录三个以上检查点
heading.en: Freeze the Final Output, Then Record at Least Three Checkpoints

body.zh:
在 ZenStory 的视频解说工作流中，字幕时间使用最终输出时钟。若字幕最初按原素材计时，先建立从原素材到剪辑成片的时间映射，再把每条字幕边界落到成片时钟。完成时间映射后，创作者仍要重播**准备发布的视频画面 + 这版成片实际采用的旁白**，亲自确认声音与字幕的开始和结束。

先给成片和旁白版本做清楚标记，在开头、中段、结尾各选一句起音和收音都容易辨认的台词。若某处有叠音、含混起音或难以判断的句尾，就换一个更清楚的句子。记录表中的时间必须来自实际播放观察；看不清的值写“未知”，不要猜。

| 位置 | 台词标记 | 声音开始 | 声音结束 | 字幕开始显示 | 字幕结束显示 | 开始误差（字幕－声音） | 结束误差（字幕－声音） | 备注 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 开头附近 | [原句或唯一标记] | [已观察/未知] | [已观察/未知] | [已观察/未知] | [已观察/未知] | [正数=字幕晚出现；负数=字幕早出现] | [正数=字幕晚消失；负数=字幕早消失] | [叠音、含混句尾等] |
| 中段附近 | [原句或唯一标记] | [已观察/未知] | [已观察/未知] | [已观察/未知] | [已观察/未知] | [同上] | [同上] | [说明] |
| 结尾附近 | [原句或唯一标记] | [已观察/未知] | [已观察/未知] | [已观察/未知] | [已观察/未知] | [同上] | [同上] | [说明] |

开始误差只支持开始边界的判断，结束误差只支持结束边界的判断。某条字幕只有开始时间可辨时，把结束边界保留为“未知”，先补测再决定是否修改。开头、中段、结尾三个位置构成第一轮模式检查；发现转场、分段或局部重剪附近有异常时，在该处追加检查点。
body.en:
In ZenStory's video-recap workflow, subtitle times use the final output clock. If cues were first timed to source media, establish a source-to-edit mapping before placing every cue boundary on the edited output clock. After that mapping, the creator still replays the **video picture intended for release plus the narration actually adopted in that output** and confirms the speech and cue starts and ends.

Label the exact video and narration versions. Choose one line with a clear spoken start and end near the beginning, one near the middle, and one near the end. If a line contains overlapping speech, an indistinct onset, or an unclear ending, choose a clearer line. Every time in the log must come from playback observation; write “unknown” when the evidence is unclear instead of guessing.

| Position | Line marker | Speech start | Speech end | Cue display start | Cue display end | Start error (subtitle − speech) | End error (subtitle − speech) | Note |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Near beginning | [verbatim line or unique marker] | [observed/unknown] | [observed/unknown] | [observed/unknown] | [observed/unknown] | [positive=appears late; negative=appears early] | [positive=disappears late; negative=disappears early] | [overlap, unclear ending, etc.] |
| Near middle | [verbatim line or unique marker] | [observed/unknown] | [observed/unknown] | [observed/unknown] | [observed/unknown] | [same sign rule] | [same sign rule] | [note] |
| Near end | [verbatim line or unique marker] | [observed/unknown] | [observed/unknown] | [observed/unknown] | [observed/unknown] | [same sign rule] | [same sign rule] | [note] |

A start error supports a decision about the start boundary only; an end error supports a decision about the end boundary only. When only a cue's start is observable, keep its end marked “unknown” and measure it before deciding whether to edit that boundary. The beginning, middle, and end form an initial pattern check. Add checkpoints around transitions, sections, or local recuts where another problem appears.

heading.zh: 按误差形状分别处理三类问题
heading.en: Choose the Repair from the Error Pattern

body.zh:
这套人工方法比较终版媒体中实际观察到的开始误差与结束误差，再为证据选择相符的修正范围。字幕轨以最终输出时钟记录边界；创作者通过重播成片确认这些边界与实际语音的关系。

| 观察到的形状 | 诊断 | 证据支持的修正 |
|---|---|---|
| 开头、中段、结尾的开始误差与结束误差都以相近方向和幅度提前或延后 | **整体偏移**：整条字幕的边界整体错开，但各条显示时长大致保持 | 按已核对的共同误差整体平移字幕；字幕晚就前移，字幕早就后移，并保持各条原有时长。这个判断需要开始和结束两侧都有相符证据 |
| 开头接近，中段更偏，结尾偏得更多；开始或结束误差沿片长持续变化 | **持续漂移**：字幕与终版声音没有共享同一套时长变化 | 先核对SRT、旁白和视频是否来自同一最终版本；对最终旁白重新建立开始与结束时间，必要时按已验证的分段锚点重定时。一次整体平移只校正一个位置 |
| 大部分检查点相符，只有某一句或相邻几句的开始或结束异常 | **单条边界错误**：局部边界或局部剪辑需要修正 | 只改有实测证据支持的开始或结束边界，并重播该条与相邻交接；未观察到的另一侧保持不动，直到补齐证据 |

一条轨道也可能同时有整体偏移和少量单条错误。先修共同偏移，然后在新导出中重新观察每个检查点的字幕开始、字幕结束、声音开始和声音结束；这轮复测仍显示局部边界异常时，再对该边界单独重定时。若结束仍是未知，就保持结束边界不动并补测。检查点太少或方向互相矛盾时，将分类保持为“证据不足”并增加实测点。
body.en:
This manual method compares observed start and end errors in the final media, then chooses a repair scope supported by that evidence. The subtitle track records boundaries on the final output clock; the creator confirms how those boundaries relate to actual speech by replaying the render.

| Observed shape | Diagnosis | Evidence-supported repair |
|---|---|---|
| Start and end errors near the beginning, middle, and end are early or late by roughly the same amount | **Global offset:** the full set of cue boundaries is displaced while cue durations remain broadly intact | Shift the complete track by the verified common error: move late cues earlier and early cues later while preserving each cue's duration. This diagnosis requires matching evidence at both start and end boundaries |
| The beginning is close, the middle is farther off, and the end is farther still; start or end errors change steadily through the runtime | **Growing drift:** the captions and final voice track do not share the same runtime change | First confirm that the SRT, narration, and video belong to the same final version; rebuild start and end times against the final narration, using verified segment anchors when needed. One global shift corrects only one position |
| Most checkpoints agree, but one cue or a small neighboring group has a bad start or end | **Local boundary error:** a local boundary or edit needs correction | Change only the start or end boundary supported by observed evidence, then replay that cue and its neighboring handoffs. Keep the unobserved boundary unchanged until evidence is available |

A track can contain a global offset plus a few local errors. Fix the shared offset first, then re-observe subtitle start, subtitle end, speech start, and speech end for every checkpoint in the new export. Apply local retiming when that playback still shows a boundary error. If an end remains unknown, leave that boundary unchanged and measure it before editing. When evidence is sparse or contradictory, keep the classification at “insufficient evidence” and add observed checkpoints.

heading.zh: AI只能整理已观察数据，不能从文字证明同步
heading.en: AI Can Organize Observations, Not Prove Synchronization from Text

body.zh:
模型可以把你记录的误差排成表格、指出可能的形状，并列出下一轮要复查的位置；它没有播放终版媒体时，不能知道真实起止点，也不能替你发明时间码。可复制下面的模板。方括号没有实测值时保留“未知”。

> 我在检查最终视频与实际采用旁白的字幕同步。只能使用下列人工播放记录，不得补写、推算或假设缺失时间。  
> **最终视频版本：** [文件名/版本]  
> **采用旁白版本：** [文件名/版本]  
> **SRT版本：** [文件名/版本]  
> **检查点：**  
> - 开头：[台词标记]；声音开始 [已验证/未知]；声音结束 [已验证/未知]；字幕开始显示 [已验证/未知]；字幕结束显示 [已验证/未知]  
> - 中段：[台词标记]；声音开始 [已验证/未知]；声音结束 [已验证/未知]；字幕开始显示 [已验证/未知]；字幕结束显示 [已验证/未知]  
> - 结尾：[台词标记]；声音开始 [已验证/未知]；声音结束 [已验证/未知]；字幕开始显示 [已验证/未知]；字幕结束显示 [已验证/未知]  
> - 额外异常：[台词标记与四个已验证时间；没有观察到的字段写未知]  
> 只为数据完整的边界计算误差：开始误差=字幕开始－声音开始，结束误差=字幕结束－声音结束。按现有证据归为整体偏移、持续漂移、单条边界错误、混合问题或证据不足；未知项必须保持未知。说明依据，但不要声称已经同步。若证据不足，列出需要我回到成片补测的具体边界。最后只给与证据相符的修正范围，并列出重新导出后必须人工重播的开始与结束检查点。

模型给出的分类仍然是工作建议。最终判断来自修正后成片的播放结果，而不是表格或提示词本身。
body.en:
A model can arrange the errors you recorded, identify a possible shape, and list positions for another review pass. Without playing the final media, it cannot know the true start or end points and must not invent timestamps. Copy the template below, leaving “unknown” wherever you lack an observed value.

> I am checking subtitle sync against the final video and the narration actually used. Use only the manual playback observations below. Do not fill, infer, or assume missing times.  
> **Final video version:** [file/version]  
> **Adopted narration version:** [file/version]  
> **SRT version:** [file/version]  
> **Checkpoints:**  
> - Beginning: [line marker]; speech start [verified/unknown]; speech end [verified/unknown]; cue display start [verified/unknown]; cue display end [verified/unknown]  
> - Middle: [line marker]; speech start [verified/unknown]; speech end [verified/unknown]; cue display start [verified/unknown]; cue display end [verified/unknown]  
> - End: [line marker]; speech start [verified/unknown]; speech end [verified/unknown]; cue display start [verified/unknown]; cue display end [verified/unknown]  
> - Additional anomaly: [line marker and four verified times; mark every unobserved field unknown]  
> Calculate an error only when both values for that boundary are available: start error = cue start − speech start; end error = cue end − speech end. Classify only the available evidence as global offset, growing drift, local boundary error, mixed problem, or insufficient evidence. Preserve every unknown. Explain the evidence, but do not claim the track is synchronized. If evidence is insufficient, list the exact boundaries I must measure in the rendered video. Finally, propose only a correction scope supported by the evidence and list the start and end checkpoints that require manual replay after a new export.

The model's classification remains a working recommendation. The deciding evidence is playback of the corrected render, not the table or prompt itself.

heading.zh: 原创示例：共同晚0.8秒，另有一条局部异常
heading.en: Original Example: A Shared 0.8-Second Delay Plus One Local Error

body.zh:
下面是本文原创的虚构项目记录，用来演示计算与修正顺序，不报告真实媒体测试结果。一条五分钟的纸灯笼折叠教程采用最终旁白 `lantern-fold-final-03`。创作者播放终版后记录：

| 位置 | 台词标记 | 声音开始 | 声音结束 | 字幕开始 | 字幕结束 | 开始误差 | 结束误差 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 开头 | “把方纸沿对角线对折” | 00:12.4 | 00:15.6 | 00:13.2 | 00:16.4 | +0.8秒 | +0.8秒 |
| 中段 | “撑开纸袋，再压平折痕” | 02:18.1 | 02:21.7 | 02:18.9 | 02:22.5 | +0.8秒 | +0.8秒 |
| 结尾 | “把流苏穿过下方纸环” | 04:41.6 | 04:45.0 | 04:42.4 | 04:45.8 | +0.8秒 | +0.8秒 |
| 额外异常 | “把折起的尖角转向中心” | 03:06.0 | 03:09.4 | 03:08.0 | 03:10.2 | +2.0秒 | +0.8秒 |

开头、中段、结尾的开始和结束都稳定晚 `+0.8秒`，这份双边界证据支持把整条字幕前移0.8秒，同时保持各条显示时长。额外字幕的开始比共同偏移多晚 `1.2秒`，但结束只晚共同的0.8秒。

创作者先整体前移0.8秒并重新导出，不直接改额外字幕。随后在新成片中重新观察四个检查点：前三条的开始与结束误差都变为0；额外字幕变为开始 `03:07.2`、结束 `03:09.4`，相对声音仍是开始晚 `+1.2秒`、结束误差为0。复测证明只有这条的开始边界仍有问题，因此创作者把它的开始改到 `03:06.0`，保留已有证据支持的结束 `03:09.4`，再检查前一条结束、这一条起止和后一条开始，确认没有意外重叠、显示区间被截短或过长空档。

修完后，创作者重新导出视频，重播所有开始与结束检查点，再顺序观看整片。这些数字只用于说明这份虚构记录的计算；实际项目应使用各自终版中观察到的边界。若实际观察到的开始与结束误差沿片长从 `+0.2` 增至 `+1.1`、再增至 `+2.0`，就不应照抄“整体前移0.8秒”，而应按漂移路径核对版本并重新定时。
body.en:
The following original fictional project log illustrates the arithmetic and repair order; it does not report a media test. A five-minute paper-lantern folding tutorial uses the final narration version `lantern-fold-final-03`. Playback of the final output produced these observations:

| Position | Line marker | Speech start | Speech end | Cue start | Cue end | Start error | End error |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Beginning | “Fold the square paper corner to corner” | 00:12.4 | 00:15.6 | 00:13.2 | 00:16.4 | +0.8 s | +0.8 s |
| Middle | “Open the paper pocket, then press the crease flat” | 02:18.1 | 02:21.7 | 02:18.9 | 02:22.5 | +0.8 s | +0.8 s |
| End | “Thread the tassel through the lower paper loop” | 04:41.6 | 04:45.0 | 04:42.4 | 04:45.8 | +0.8 s | +0.8 s |
| Additional anomaly | “Turn the folded point toward the center” | 03:06.0 | 03:09.4 | 03:08.0 | 03:10.2 | +2.0 s | +0.8 s |

The beginning, middle, and end are consistently `+0.8 s` late at both boundaries. That two-boundary evidence supports shifting the complete track 0.8 seconds earlier while preserving each cue's display duration. The additional cue starts another `1.2 s` late beyond the shared offset, but its end carries only the shared 0.8-second delay.

The creator first applies the global 0.8-second shift and exports again without editing the anomalous cue separately. Playback of the new render then re-observes all four checkpoints. The three representative cues now have zero start and end error. The anomalous cue now starts at `03:07.2` and ends at `03:09.4`, leaving its start `+1.2 s` late and its end error at zero. This new evidence supports changing only that cue's start to `03:06.0` while retaining the observed end at `03:09.4`. The creator then checks the preceding cue's end, this cue's start and end, and the following cue's start for an unintended overlap, a truncated display interval, or a long gap.

After the repair, the creator exports again, replays every start and end checkpoint, and then watches the video in sequence. These numbers illustrate this fictional record only; use boundaries observed in your own final media for a real project. If both start and end errors instead grow through the runtime from `+0.2` to `+1.1` and then `+2.0`, do not copy the 0.8-second global shift. Follow the drift path: verify the versions and rebuild the timing.

heading.zh: 修正后重播成片；旁白变化或影响时间的剪辑后重新检查
heading.en: Replay the Final Render; Recheck Narration Changes and Timing-Affecting Edits

body.zh:
时间表记录预期边界；渲染后的媒体显示字幕实际何时开始、何时结束，以及它与语音起止的听感是否同步。用这份只针对时间的清单收尾：

- [ ] 本轮使用的是准备发布的视频、实际采用的旁白和完整SRT，而不是混用旧版本。
- [ ] 开头、中段、结尾的声音起止与字幕显示起止已经在新成片中重播。
- [ ] 每个局部异常及其相邻字幕的起止边界已经重播，没有意外重叠、显示区间被截短或过长空档。
- [ ] 转场、分段、局部变速或改变字幕相关时间顺序的重剪附近已增加检查点。
- [ ] 已从头到尾顺序播放一次，确认各条字幕按预期顺序出现和结束，没有残留到下一句或提前消失。
- [ ] 准备发布的文件就是刚刚检查的那一版。

旁白一旦重录、改词、换语速或调整停顿，需要在新成片中重新检查相关起止点；如果变化改变了总时长，还要复查后续检查点。视频剪辑只有在改变字幕相关的时间、顺序、时长或时间轴位置时，才会使对应时间证据失效。单纯调色、改封面或其他不改变时间轴的操作，不需要因此重做字幕计时检查。
body.en:
A timing table records the intended boundaries; the rendered media shows the actual cue start and end and how those boundaries feel against the spoken start and end. Finish with this timing-only checklist:

- [ ] This pass uses the video intended for release, the narration actually adopted, and the complete SRT, with no old version mixed in.
- [ ] Speech start and end plus cue display start and end near the beginning, middle, and end have been replayed in the new render.
- [ ] Every local anomaly and the boundaries of its neighboring cues have been replayed, with no unintended overlap, truncated display interval, or long gap.
- [ ] Checkpoints were added around transitions, sections, local speed changes, or recuts that change subtitle-relevant timing or order.
- [ ] The video was played in sequence from start to finish to confirm that cues appear and end in the intended order, without lingering into the next line or disappearing early.
- [ ] The file being published is the same version that was reviewed.

Recheck the relevant boundaries in a new render whenever narration is rerecorded, rewritten, repaced, or given different pauses. If that change alters total duration, recheck later checkpoints too. A video edit invalidates the corresponding timing evidence only when it changes subtitle-relevant timing, order, duration, or timeline position. Color grading, cover changes, and other edits that leave the timeline unchanged do not require a new subtitle-timing pass by themselves.

q.zh: 为什么SRT开头对得上，越到后面越不同步？
q.en: Why does my SRT start in sync and drift later?

a.zh: 这更像持续漂移，而不是单纯的起点偏移。先分别检查开头、中段、结尾的声音起止与字幕显示起止，再确认SRT、旁白和视频来自同一终版。若开始或结束误差沿片长增长，应依据最终旁白重建对应边界；一次整体平移只能修好某一个位置。
a.en: That pattern points to growing drift rather than a simple starting offset. Compare speech and cue start and end near the beginning, middle, and end, then verify that the SRT, narration, and video come from the same final version. If either boundary error grows through the runtime, rebuild that timing against the final narration; one global shift can correct only one position.

q.zh: 可以让AI直接根据SRT文本判断字幕是否同步吗？
q.en: Can AI tell whether subtitles are synchronized from the SRT text alone?

a.zh: 不能。仅看文字无法知道终版声音何时开始和结束，也不能知道字幕在渲染后何时出现和消失，更不能证明观看时已经同步。AI可以整理你从成片中人工核对的起止时间、计算有完整数据的误差和提出复查范围，但未知值必须保留为未知。
a.en: No. Text alone does not reveal when speech starts and ends in the final media or when a rendered cue appears and disappears, so it cannot prove synchronization. AI can organize manually verified boundary times, calculate errors where both values exist, and suggest a review scope, but unknowns must remain unknown.

q.zh: 只改了一句AI旁白，还要重新检查整条字幕吗？
q.en: Do I need to recheck subtitles after changing one narration line?

a.zh: 要在新成片中复查改动句的声音起止与字幕起止。若替换句改变了时长、停顿或后续字幕的时间轴位置，还要重测改动前、改动处和片尾；若只是视频调色等不改变字幕相关时间轴的操作，则不需要因此重做计时检查。旧旁白版本的结果不能证明新旁白同步。
a.en: Recheck the changed line’s speech and cue start and end in the new render. If the replacement changes duration, pauses, or later cue positions, also remeasure before the edit, at the edit, and near the end. A color-only video edit that leaves subtitle-relevant timing unchanged does not require a new timing pass. Observations from the old narration do not prove the new narration is synchronized.

text.zh: 使用 /video-recap（Codex 中用 $video-recap）整理字幕同步问题时，请提供准备发布的视频版本、实际采用的旁白版本，以及你从成片人工核对的开头、中段、结尾声音起止和字幕显示起止。要求它只按实测数据区分整体偏移、持续漂移或单条边界错误，并保留未知项；不要让它发明时间码或声称仅凭文本已经同步。
text.en: When using `/video-recap` (or `$video-recap` in Codex) to organize a subtitle-sync problem, provide the release video version, the narration version actually adopted, and manually verified speech and cue start and end times near the beginning, middle, and end. Ask it to classify only the observed evidence as global offset, growing drift, or local boundary error and to preserve unknowns. Do not ask it to invent timestamps or claim synchronization from text alone.

title.zh: AI写的小说能签约吗：投稿规则、来源与最终文件检查
title.en: AI-Assisted Novel Submission Checklist

seo_title.en: AI-Assisted Novel Submission Checklist | ZenStory

description.zh: AI辅助小说投稿前，核对目标入口规则与AI输入输出来源，并确认最终文件和附件。附检查表、审稿提示词和原创示例。
description.en: Check route rules and AI-source provenance before submission. Includes a checklist, audit prompt, original example, and final-file check.

answer.zh: AI辅助小说是否符合签约投稿条件，要以你实际选择的投稿入口、当前官方作者规则和待签协议为准。先记录平台、频道或活动、作品类型、官方页面及日期，把规则没有回答的具体用法继续标为“待外部确认”，不要从第三方文章或泛用服务协议推断允许或禁止。再建立AI参与记录：哪些材料送入AI、AI生成或改了哪些内容、来源能否追溯、作者采用或拒绝了什么。提交前核对最终正文、简介、样章和其他附件确实来自作者读完的同一版本。这套表帮助你评估AI相关投稿问题；一般剧情与文笔审查应交给对应的独立流程。
answer.en: Assess an AI-assisted novel against the current official materials for the exact destination and submission route. Record the platform, channel or program, work type, official page, and date. Keep any use the rules do not address under “External confirmation needed” rather than inferring permission or prohibition from third-party posts or a general service agreement. Then document what went into AI, what it generated or changed, which sources are traceable, and what the author accepted or rejected. Before upload, confirm that the manuscript, synopsis, sample chapters, and other attachments all come from the same final version the author read. This checklist helps assess AI-related submission issues; use the separate editorial workflows for general story or prose review.

heading.zh: 先记录实际投稿入口，不用泛用协议替它回答
heading.en: Record the Exact Route Instead of Letting General Terms Answer for It

body.zh:
“平台通常怎么处理”不能代替你将要使用的投稿入口。先把目的地写完整：平台、频道或征集活动、作品类型、是否申请签约，以及届时出现的协议。然后只记录能回到官方页面的证据。

| 记录项 | 要写下什么 |
|---|---|
| 实际去向 | 平台、频道或活动、作品类型、具体入口 |
| 官方材料 | 作者规则、投稿说明、活动规则、待签协议的标题与链接 |
| 时点 | 页面标示的更新或生效日期；没有标示时记访问日期 |
| 直接相关文字 | 与AI辅助、内容来源、声明或投稿资格直接相关的位置 |
| 未回答的问题 | 规则没有覆盖的具体用法，例如只用AI整理大纲或生成部分初稿 |
| 当前状态 | 已核对、待作者决定、待外部确认 |

证据要和问题同一层级。一份泛用服务协议可以约束账号和内容，却未必说明某类小说能否进入某个签约流程。以本文核对过的起点[用户服务协议](https://acts.qidian.com/pact/user_pact.html)为例，页面标示的版本更新及生效日期为2024年4月28日；第13.4和15.2条涉及合成或不真实信息、内容来源，但没有给出AI辅助小说签约资格的通用答案。不能由此推断“能签”或“不能签”。

真正准备投稿时，继续找该入口当前的作者规则和待签协议。若仍没有覆盖你的具体用法，可以把问题写清楚，通过官方渠道询问并保存回复；没有回复时，状态仍是“待外部确认”。这项未决记录不会自动变成允许、禁止或面向所有平台的停止规则。作者要依据实际入口已有的官方材料和明确要求作出自己的投稿决定。
body.en:
A claim about what platforms usually do cannot replace the route you will actually use. Define the destination completely: platform, channel or call, work type, whether you are applying for a contract, and the agreement presented in that route. Record only evidence that leads back to an official page.

| Field | What to record |
|---|---|
| Actual destination | Platform, channel or program, work type, and exact route |
| Official material | Titles and links for author rules, submission instructions, program rules, and proposed agreement |
| Time | Stated update or effective date; if none appears, the access date |
| Directly relevant text | The location of language about AI assistance, content sources, declarations, or eligibility |
| Unanswered question | The precise use the material does not cover, such as AI used only to organize an outline or generate part of a draft |
| Current status | Checked, Author decision needed, or External confirmation needed |

The evidence must match the question. A general service agreement can govern accounts and content without defining eligibility for a particular fiction-contract route. For example, the Qidian [User Service Agreement](https://acts.qidian.com/pact/user_pact.html) checked for this article displays an update and effective date of April 28, 2024. Sections 13.4 and 15.2 concern synthetic or non-real information and content sources, but they do not provide a general answer about contract eligibility for AI-assisted novels. They support neither “eligible” nor “ineligible” as a universal conclusion.

For a real submission, continue to the current author rules and proposed agreement for that exact route. If they still do not address your use, describe it precisely, ask through an official channel, and save the response. Without a response, keep the row under External confirmation needed. That open status does not automatically become permission, prohibition, or a universal stop rule. The author makes the submission decision from the official material and explicit requirements available for the chosen route.

heading.zh: 把AI输入、输出、来源和作者处理动作连起来
heading.en: Connect AI Inputs, Outputs, Sources, and Author Actions

body.zh:
平台记录回答“投到哪里、依据什么”。另一张表回答“AI碰过什么、作者能说明什么”。按输入、输出和作者处理动作逐项记录，不用一句“AI辅助过”概括整本书。

| 字段 | 记录方法 |
|---|---|
| 输入编号 | 给大纲、人物表、资料、参考片段和旧稿分别编号 |
| 来源与位置 | 写作者自有材料、外部页面或文件名；无法确认就明确标出 |
| 交给AI的任务 | 例如整理章节顺序、生成连接段、改写指定段落 |
| 输出位置 | 对应草稿版本、章节和段落，不写模糊的“部分内容” |
| 作者处理 | 采用、拒绝、重写或仍待决定；写明最终版本落在哪里 |
| 当前状态 | 已核对、待作者决定、待外部确认 |

“已核对”只表示记录能够回到具体材料和版本，不代表对来源、合同或投稿资格作出了法律结论。无法说明来源的内容继续放在“待外部确认”；模型提出但作者尚未选定的情节或表达放在“待作者决定”。AI不能用一段听起来确定的说明替你关闭这两种状态。

这张表只检查AI参与和来源链。若要判断人物动机、剧情因果或改稿范围，转到[审稿与修改](/oh-story/review-and-revise)；只有局部表达需要处理时，看[局部正文修订](/oh-story/revise-ai-prose)。需要记录本书主动选择的文风时，用[保留作者文风](/oh-story/preserve-author-voice)。不要在本轮重新发明一套通用剧情审查流程。
body.en:
The route record answers “where am I submitting, and on what official basis?” A second record answers “what did AI touch, and what can the author account for?” Log inputs, outputs, and author actions separately instead of describing the whole book as merely “AI-assisted.”

| Field | How to record it |
|---|---|
| Input ID | Assign an ID to each outline, character sheet, research item, reference excerpt, and earlier draft |
| Source and location | Name the author's own material, external page, or file; mark an unconfirmed source explicitly |
| Task given to AI | For example, organize chapter order, generate a connective passage, or revise a named paragraph |
| Output location | Identify draft version, chapter, and passage rather than writing “some content” |
| Author action | Accepted, rejected, rewritten, or still undecided; identify where the final version lives |
| Current status | Checked, Author decision needed, or External confirmation needed |

Checked means only that the record leads back to specific material and a version. It does not make a legal conclusion about sources, contracts, or eligibility. Material with an origin you cannot account for stays under External confirmation needed. A model proposal the author has not selected stays under Author decision needed. A confident explanation from AI cannot close either status.

This record is limited to AI contribution and source provenance. For character motivation, plot causality, or a general revision brief, use [review and revise](/oh-story/review-and-revise). For a bounded wording problem, use [prose revision](/oh-story/revise-ai-prose). To record deliberate stylistic choices, use [preserving author voice](/oh-story/preserve-author-voice). Do not rebuild those general editorial workflows inside this submission check.

heading.zh: 可复制提示词：只查规则、来源与文件版本缺口
heading.en: Copyable Prompt: Audit Rules, Provenance, and File Versions Only

body.zh:
把方括号替换成你的材料。这个提示词只找投稿规则、来源记录和文件版本的缺口，不审剧情，也不宣布能否签约。

> 我在核对一部AI辅助小说的投稿材料。只整理证据缺口，不补写平台规则、来源、授权状态或投稿结论。  
> **实际投稿去向：** [平台、频道或活动、作品类型、具体入口]  
> **官方材料记录：** [页面标题、链接、更新/生效/访问日期、相关位置；没有答案的写“待外部确认”]  
> **AI输入记录：** [输入编号、材料名称、来源与位置、交给AI的任务]  
> **AI输出与作者处理：** [草稿版本、章节或段落、采用/拒绝/重写/待定]  
> **准备提交的文件清单：** [正文文件、版本号或校验值、章节数、简介、样章及其他附件]  
> **作者实际读完的版本：** [文件名、版本号或校验值、完成日期]
>
> 返回一张核对表。每行只使用“已核对”“待作者决定”“待外部确认”三种状态，并写出：记录项、现有证据、缺少什么、下一步由谁处理。检查实际入口是否明确；官方材料是否能回到链接和日期；每项AI输入、输出与作者动作是否能对应；来源不明处是否仍保持未确认；最终正文和附件是否都来自作者读完的同一版本。不要审查人物、情节或文风，不要改正文，也不要给出可以投稿、不能投稿或能够签约的判断。

收到表后，作者补齐能够补齐的记录，把选择题留在“待作者决定”，把需要平台或来源回答的问题留在“待外部确认”。若发现一般剧情问题，另开审稿流程；不要把它混进来源账本。
body.en:
Replace the bracketed fields with your material. This prompt looks only for gaps in route rules, source records, and file versions. It does not review the story or announce contract eligibility.

> I am checking submission materials for an AI-assisted novel. Organize evidence gaps only. Do not invent platform rules, sources, permission status, or a submission conclusion.  
> **Actual destination:** [platform, channel or program, work type, exact route]  
> **Official-material record:** [page title, link, update/effective/access date, relevant location; write “External confirmation needed” where it gives no answer]  
> **AI-input record:** [input ID, material name, source and location, task given to AI]  
> **AI output and author action:** [draft version, chapter or passage, accepted/rejected/rewritten/undecided]  
> **Files prepared for submission:** [manuscript filename, version ID or checksum, chapter count, synopsis, sample chapters, and other attachments]  
> **Version the author actually read:** [filename, version ID or checksum, completion date]
>
> Return one audit table. Use only Checked, Author decision needed, and External confirmation needed as statuses. For each row, state the item, current evidence, what is missing, and who handles the next step. Check whether the exact route is identified; whether official material has a link and date; whether every AI input, output, and author action maps to a record; whether an unknown source remains explicitly unconfirmed; and whether the final manuscript and attachments come from the same version the author read. Do not review character, plot, or style. Do not rewrite the manuscript or decide that it can be submitted, cannot be submitted, or can receive a contract.

After receiving the table, the author completes records that can be completed, leaves choices under Author decision needed, and leaves questions requiring the platform or a source under External confirmation needed. If a general story problem appears, open the separate review workflow instead of putting it into the provenance ledger.

heading.zh: 原创示例：《雨巷印刷所》的投稿记录
heading.en: Original Example: The Submission Record for The Print Shop on Rain Lane

body.zh:
以下作品、平台和记录均为本文原创虚构，不代表任何真实平台政策。陈蕊准备提交长篇《雨巷印刷所》。AI帮她整理过大纲，也生成过两段场景连接。她没有问AI“这本能不能签”，而是把投稿入口、AI材料和最终文件放进同一张记录表。

| 记录项 | 现有证据与处理 | 状态 |
|---|---|---|
| 投稿入口 | 她选了虚构的“纸桥长篇征集”，保存了活动页和访问日期；页面没有回答她这种AI用法 | 待外部确认 |
| 输入 A-01 | 她自己的故事大纲，文件为 outline-v3；AI只按原有章节整理顺序 | 已核对 |
| 输入 A-02 | 她曾把另一部当代小说的一段正文贴入提示词作语感参考；AI生成的第4章连接段含一处她无法说明来源的独特比喻 | 待作者决定 |
| 输出 O-04 | 她决定不用原连接段，回到自己的角色表和场景目标重写；新段落记录在 manuscript-v12，原输出保留在不提交的工作记录中 | 已核对 |
| 输出 O-09 | 第9章连接段由AI生成，陈蕊逐句核对后采用；输入编号、初稿和最终位置都有记录 | 已核对 |
| 投稿附件 | 正文是 manuscript-v12，简介却从 v10 导出，仍写着后来删掉的角色 | 待作者决定 |

陈蕊先从 manuscript-v12 重做简介，并核对样章和章节目录，附件一项随后改为“已核对”。A-02不是靠同义替换变得“可用”；她撤下无法说明形成过程的输出，再用能够追溯的本书材料重写。这个处理只说明她如何整理自己的记录，不替任何人作来源或权利结论。

活动页仍未回答她的具体AI用法，因此该行继续保持“待外部确认”。她可以向虚构平台的官方渠道询问，也可以继续比较其他有明确规则的入口；是否依据现有材料提交，由她结合那个实际入口的要求决定。本文不会把沉默改写成允许、禁止或面向所有人的统一停投规则。
body.en:
The work, platform, and records below are original fiction created for this article. They do not represent any real platform policy. Chen Rui is preparing a novel titled *The Print Shop on Rain Lane*. AI helped organize its outline and generated two connective passages. Instead of asking AI whether the novel could get signed, she placed the route, AI materials, and final files in one record.

| Record | Present evidence and action | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Submission route | She selects the fictional Paper Bridge Novel Call and saves its program page and access date; the page does not answer her particular AI use | External confirmation needed |
| Input A-01 | Her own story outline, outline-v3; AI only organizes its existing chapter order | Checked |
| Input A-02 | She pasted a paragraph from another contemporary novel into a prompt as a tonal reference; an AI-generated Chapter 4 transition contains a distinctive comparison whose formation she cannot account for | Author decision needed |
| Output O-04 | She rejects the transition and rewrites from her own character sheet and scene goal; the replacement is in manuscript-v12, while the old output remains in a work record that will not be submitted | Checked |
| Output O-09 | AI generated a Chapter 9 transition that Chen reviewed line by line and accepted; its input ID, first draft, and final location are recorded | Checked |
| Submission attachments | The manuscript is manuscript-v12, but the synopsis was exported from v10 and still names a character later removed | Author decision needed |

Chen rebuilds the synopsis from manuscript-v12, then checks the sample chapters and table of contents. The attachment row can now move to Checked. She does not make A-02 “usable” through synonym replacement. She removes the output whose formation she cannot account for and rewrites from traceable material belonging to this project. This describes her recordkeeping choice; it makes no source or rights conclusion for another author.

The program page still does not answer her specific AI use, so that row remains under External confirmation needed. She can ask the fictional program through an official channel or compare another route with clearer materials. Whether to proceed on the available evidence is her decision under the actual route's requirements. This article does not turn silence into permission, prohibition, or a universal stop rule.

heading.zh: 提交前核对最终正文和每一个附件
heading.en: Check the Exact Final Manuscript and Every Attachment

body.zh:
提交前只核对准备上传的那一套文件，不用旧草稿的审查记录代替。给最终正文一个明确版本号或校验值，并把简介、样章、目录、封面说明等附件一并列入清单。

- [ ] 平台、频道或活动和具体入口与规则记录一致。
- [ ] 官方页面的链接与日期已经重新核对；未回答的问题仍明确标为“待外部确认”。
- [ ] 每项AI输入、输出和作者采用、拒绝或重写的动作都能回到编号和位置。
- [ ] 作者已经读完准备上传的正文版本，而不是相近文件名的旧稿。
- [ ] 简介、样章和目录来自同一正文版本；人名、章节顺序和结局表述没有停在旧版。
- [ ] 文件清单记录了文件名、版本号或校验值、章节数和完成日期。
- [ ] 上传预览中的正文顺序、缺章、截断与附件选择已经核对。
- [ ] “待作者决定”和“待外部确认”没有被AI的流畅回答自动改成“已核对”。

这里的停止条件很具体：你已经核对将要上传的实际文件，来源账本与版本清单能指回它，未决项仍按真实状态保留，作者知道自己正在依据哪些官方材料作决定。故事质量问题另见[审稿与修改](/oh-story/review-and-revise)；局部措辞问题另见[局部正文修订](/oh-story/revise-ai-prose)。
body.en:
Check only the file set you are about to upload. Do not treat a review of an older draft as evidence about the current one. Give the final manuscript a clear version ID or checksum, and include the synopsis, sample chapters, contents, cover note, and any other attachment in the same manifest.

- [ ] Platform, channel or program, and exact route match the rule record.
- [ ] Official links and dates have been reopened; unanswered questions remain under External confirmation needed.
- [ ] Every AI input, output, and author action—accepted, rejected, or rewritten—maps to an ID and location.
- [ ] The author has read the manuscript version being uploaded, not an older file with a similar name.
- [ ] Synopsis, sample chapters, and contents come from the same manuscript version; names, chapter order, and ending language are not stranded in an earlier draft.
- [ ] The manifest records filenames, version IDs or checksums, chapter count, and completion date.
- [ ] Upload preview, chapter order, omissions, truncation, and attachment choices have been checked.
- [ ] A fluent AI answer has not moved Author decision needed or External confirmation needed to Checked.

The stop condition is concrete: you have checked the actual upload set, the provenance ledger and version manifest point to it, open items retain their real status, and the author knows which official material informs the decision. Use [review and revise](/oh-story/review-and-revise) for story-quality issues and [prose revision](/oh-story/revise-ai-prose) for bounded wording work.

q.zh: 平台协议提到合成信息，能直接推断AI小说能否签约吗？
q.en: Does a Reference to Synthetic Information Settle AI-Fiction Eligibility?

a.zh: 不能只凭词语相似推断。先看条款约束的对象和场景，再找实际投稿入口的作者规则、投稿说明与待签协议。它们仍未覆盖你的具体用法时，保持“待外部确认”，不要扩大条款含义。
a.en: Not from a matching phrase alone. Check what the clause governs, then locate the author rules, submission instructions, and proposed agreement for the actual route. If they still do not cover your use, keep the item under External confirmation needed instead of expanding the clause beyond its scope.

q.zh: 正文读完了，为什么还要单独核对简介和样章？
q.en: Why Check the Synopsis and Samples After Reading the Manuscript?

a.zh: 附件可能来自更早版本，保留已经删除的人物、旧章节顺序或旧结局。把正文、简介、样章和目录写进同一份版本清单，逐项确认它们来自作者读完的最终稿。
a.en: Attachments may come from an earlier version and retain a removed character, old chapter order, or superseded ending. Put the manuscript, synopsis, samples, and contents in one version manifest and confirm that each comes from the final draft the author read.

text.zh: 用 story-review 处理一般剧情与人物问题；本页的投稿检查只整理实际入口规则、AI输入输出来源记录和最终文件清单。把未决项保留为待作者决定或待外部确认，不让模型补写平台政策、来源或投稿结论。
text.en: Use story-review for general story and character issues. Keep this submission check limited to route-specific rules, AI input/output provenance, and the final-file manifest. Leave open items under Author decision needed or External confirmation needed, and do not let the model invent platform policy, sources, or a submission verdict.

title.zh: 扮猪吃虎怎么写：用连载循环安排隐藏实力
title.en: How to Write a Protagonist Who Hides Their Strength

seo_title.zh: 扮猪吃虎怎么写：隐藏实力循环
seo_title.en: How to Write a Protagonist Who Hides Their Strength

description.zh: 把扮猪吃虎写成可重复的连载循环：默默推进、挑战、可见证明、配角反应、下一步发展；附三方信息卡、原创案例和AI提示词。
description.en: Plan a secretly powerful protagonist with a repeatable loop, a three-party information card, an original example, and a bounded AI prompt.

answer.zh: 本文采用一种具体的期待型写法：主角知道自己能做什么，读者已经看过证明这项能力存在的证据，但不一定知道它的完整范围，观察主角的配角还不知道。先决定读者要等待哪种隐藏实力证明，再安排可重复的五步循环：主角默默推进，新的挑战逼近，他用已经建立的本领给出可见证明，配角据此改变判断或行动，新的权限、阻力或任务又把主角送进下一轮发展。每轮开写前分别记录三方掌握的信息；这不是扮猪吃虎的唯一通用定义，而是本页用于连载循环的配置。
answer.en: This guide uses one specific anticipation setup: the protagonist knows what they can do, the reader has already seen evidence establishing that the competence exists, though not necessarily its full range, and the observing supporting character does not yet know. Decide which proof of hidden strength the reader is waiting for, then build a repeatable five-beat loop: quiet progress, a challenge, visible proof using an established ability, an observer who changes judgment or action, and a new opportunity, obstacle, or assignment that starts the next stage of development. Record the three information positions before each loop. This is the configuration used by this guide, not a universal definition of every hidden-strength story.

heading.zh: 先定持续体验，再写五步连载循环
heading.en: Choose the Ongoing Experience, Then Build the Five-Beat Loop

body.zh:
扮猪吃虎的核心不是“藏到最后”，而是让隐藏与被发现反复形成期待和兑现。先用一句话写清本书持续提供的体验，例如：**读者看得出主角正在完成别人无法识别的准备，并等待旁人被事实迫使重新判断他。** 再把具体事件装进这条循环：

1. **默默推进：** 主角在完成自己的目标、训练、调查或准备；这一步本身要有效，不能只是站着等人挑衅。
2. **挑战出现：** 某件事让现有判断接受检验。挑战可以来自任务、竞争、误判或资源限制，不必每次都有人辱骂主角。
3. **可见证明：** 主角用故事已经建立的本领改变一个可核对的结果。证明应落在行动和结果上，而不是由旁白宣布“他其实很强”。
4. **配角反应：** 观察者根据证据改变信任、权限、策略、立场或针对方式。单写一句“众人震惊”还没有推动发现线。
5. **下一步发展：** 反应带来新任务、入口、对手、责任或限制，主角据此继续默默推进，下一轮自然开始。

主角的行动线负责做成事情，配角的发现线负责逐步修正认识。两线在“可见证明”处相交，又在“下一步发展”处分开。这样写的是可复用的连载发动机，不是一次性的身份翻牌；单次秘密揭示不属于本文。若要把本轮目标、阻力、证明和下一步安排成可执行的章节节点，可使用[章纲模板](/oh-story/chapter-outline-template)。
body.en:
The engine is not “hide everything until the end.” It is the recurring movement from concealment to discovery, which creates anticipation and payoff more than once. Begin with one sentence that defines the continuing experience, such as: **The reader can see the protagonist completing preparations that other characters cannot interpret, and waits for observable facts to force those characters to reassess them.** Then place each event inside this loop:

1. **Quiet progress:** The protagonist pursues a goal, practices, investigates, or prepares. This beat must accomplish something; the protagonist should not merely wait to be challenged.
2. **Challenge:** A situation tests the current judgment of the protagonist. It may come from a task, competition, mistaken assessment, or limited resources. It does not require another character to insult them every time.
3. **Visible proof:** The protagonist uses an already established ability to change a result that others can verify. Show action and outcome instead of letting narration declare that the protagonist was powerful all along.
4. **Observer reaction:** Someone changes their trust, access, strategy, allegiance, or countermeasure because of the evidence. A line saying “everyone was shocked” does not advance the discovery line by itself.
5. **Next development:** That reaction creates an assignment, opening, opponent, responsibility, or restriction. The protagonist begins making quiet progress under these new conditions, which starts the next loop.

The protagonist’s action line gets something done; the supporting character’s discovery line revises an understanding. The lines meet at the visible proof and separate again at the next development. This creates a reusable serial engine rather than a one-time unmasking; a single secret reveal falls outside this guide. To arrange the loop’s goal, obstacle, proof, and next step as usable chapter beats, use the [chapter-outline template](/oh-story/chapter-outline-template).

heading.zh: 每轮先填三方信息卡，再填行动链
heading.en: Map the Three Information Positions Before the Action Chain

body.zh:
本页只使用一种信息配置：主角知道，读者已经看见证明这项能力存在的证据，但不一定知道它的完整范围，观察主角的配角还不知道。这是本文选择的期待型变体，不是对所有扮猪吃虎故事的通用定义。复制这张卡时，只填写故事已经建立的事实。

| 卡片字段 | 本轮要填写的内容 |
|---|---|
| 主角知道 | 他确认自己能做什么、为什么暂不公开、本轮愿意展示到哪一步 |
| 读者已经看见 | 哪些已展示事实证明这项能力存在、还有什么范围未知；正在等待哪项可见证明 |
| 观察者还不知道 | 他目前怎样判断主角、依据是什么、什么证据足以迫使他更新判断 |
| 默默推进 | 主角正在完成的有效准备或阶段目标 |
| 挑战 | 什么局面检验当前判断；若不处理，会失去什么当前结果 |
| 可见证明 | 主角用哪项既有本领完成什么可核对结果 |
| 配角反应 | 哪个观察者怎样改变信任、权限、行动或对抗方式 |
| 下一步发展 | 这项改变为下一轮带来什么新目标、条件或压力 |

先检查前三栏，再写后五栏。如果读者栏只写“主角很强”，却列不出读者已经见过的证据，期待仍然悬空；如果观察者在证明前后采取同样行动，反应就没有进入剧情；如果下一步与本轮证明毫无关系，这一轮只是独立表演。
body.en:
This guide uses one information arrangement: the protagonist knows, the reader has already seen evidence establishing that the competence exists, though not necessarily its full range, and the observing supporting character does not yet know. It is the anticipation variant chosen for this guide, not a universal definition of every hidden-strength story. Copy the card and fill it only with facts the story has already established.

| Card field | What to record for this loop |
|---|---|
| Protagonist knows | What they know they can do, why they are not advertising it, and how much they will show in this loop |
| Reader has seen | Which established facts have shown the reader that the competence exists, what remains unknown about its range, and which visible proof the reader is waiting for |
| Observer does not yet know | How this character currently judges the protagonist, what supports that judgment, and what evidence could force an update |
| Quiet progress | The useful preparation or stage objective the protagonist is completing |
| Challenge | What tests the current judgment, and what immediate result will be lost if no one handles it |
| Visible proof | Which established ability produces what verifiable result |
| Observer reaction | Which observer changes trust, access, action, or opposition, and how |
| Next development | What new goal, condition, or pressure that change creates for the next loop |

Check the first three rows before planning the remaining five. If the reader row says only “the protagonist is powerful” without listing evidence the reader has already seen, the anticipation has no clear object. If the observer behaves identically before and after the proof, the reaction has not entered the plot. If the next development has no causal connection to the proof, the loop is merely an isolated performance.

heading.zh: 循环可以重复，但每轮要继承上一轮的反应
heading.en: Repeat the Loop, but Inherit the Previous Reaction

body.zh:
循环不是把同一场“轻视—出手—惊叹”换名字再写。每轮都要继承上轮留下的新条件：有人开始信任主角，他便获得此前进不去的场所；有人把他视为威胁，对方就会改变试探方法；主角接下更重要的职责，下一次证明也要服务这项职责。这样，配角的发现线会积累，主角的行动线也会向前。

可以从四处检查是否只在原地复读：

- **默默推进是否有效：** 主角即使没有被挑战，也在靠近自己的阶段目标。
- **证明是否可见：** 观察者能指出发生了什么，不必听主角解释完整底牌。
- **反应是否具体：** 至少有一个配角采取了与之前不同的行动，而不只是换一种惊叹句式。
- **下一轮是否由本轮生成：** 新入口、新责任或新敌意来自刚发生的证明与反应。

不要为了“升级”临时添加新能力、隐藏代价或世界规则；本页默认能力边界已经写好，不在这里设计。若主角隐瞒实力的理由还不成立，先用[人物动机](/oh-story/character-motivation)把目标、顾虑和选择接上。要把循环卡写成具体场景行动，可转到[大纲转章节](/oh-story/outline-to-chapter)；要跨章保存谁已经知道什么，则使用[长篇连续性](/oh-story/long-novel-continuity)。这里不规定固定章数或强度增幅。
body.en:
Repeating the loop does not mean renaming the same “dismissal, display, amazement” scene. Each loop should inherit the conditions created by the previous observer reaction. If someone begins to trust the protagonist, that trust may open a place that was previously inaccessible. If someone now sees the protagonist as a threat, the next test may change. If the protagonist receives greater responsibility, the next proof should serve that responsibility. The discovery line then accumulates while the action line continues forward.

Use four checks to catch repetition without development:

- **Does quiet progress matter?** Even without a challenge, the protagonist is moving toward a stage objective.
- **Is the proof observable?** An observer can name what happened without receiving a full explanation of the protagonist’s hidden capability.
- **Is the reaction concrete?** At least one supporting character acts differently instead of merely finding a new way to express amazement.
- **Does this loop generate the next one?** The new access, responsibility, or hostility follows from the proof and reaction that just occurred.

Do not invent a new ability, hidden cost, or world rule merely to escalate a loop. This guide assumes the ability boundary already exists and does not design it. If the reason for concealing strength is not yet convincing, connect the character’s goal, concern, and choice with [character motivation](/oh-story/character-motivation). To turn the loop card into concrete scene action, use [outline to chapter](/oh-story/outline-to-chapter). To preserve who already knows what across chapters, use [long-novel continuity](/oh-story/long-novel-continuity). This method imposes no fixed chapter count or escalation rate.

heading.zh: 原创案例：街区棋社的临时替补
heading.en: Original Example: A Last-Minute Substitute at a Neighborhood Chess Club

body.zh:
下面是原创纸面案例，不取自已发表作品，也不是固定题材模板。

周岑在一家街区棋社做周末志愿记分员。故事已经建立三项事实：闭馆后，他会根据当天棋谱独自复盘，常在翻看教练批注前就找到决定胜负的那一步；他能把同一局面改成适合学员练习的题目；他主动不占青少年队员的对局席位，因为他答应负责人，自己的志愿工作是把有限的棋盘时间留给学员，而他的当前目标是整理出一套供他们复盘的练习题。读者已经看过他的闭馆复盘，因此知道他的棋力确实存在，但尚不清楚能力范围；队员只见他摆棋钟、收棋谱，仍把他当作不参赛的后勤人员。这正是本页采用的“主角知道、读者已有证据、观察者不知道”配置。

**默默推进：** 周岑把最近几场练习赛的关键局面抄到卡片上，闭馆后逐一试走，再删掉不能清楚检验选择的题目。他没有争取队员名额，准备工作仍服务于学员复盘。

**挑战：** 一场街区友谊赛开场前，一名队员因家中临时有事离开，棋社没有候补。双方原本排好的最后一桌将被取消。负责人询问是否有不在名单里的成年人愿意临时补位；这个位置已经空出，不会挤掉任何学员，因此周岑的承诺仍然成立，他可以只为完成本场练习赛而上桌。

**可见证明：** 周岑只使用前文已经展示过的局面判断能力。他在对手持续进攻时保住局面，随后抓住一处失误取得胜势，对手最终认输。赛后，他按照双方留下的棋谱重新摆出转折点，旁观队员能逐步核对他为什么从那一步改变计划。证明落在对局结果和可复盘的棋谱上，不靠旁白宣布他其实很强。

**配角反应：** 负责人没有只说“没想到”。他当场在志愿排班表上给周岑增加“成人练习搭档”职责，同时保留青少年队员的正式席位，并请他主持下一次赛后复盘。原本只把他当记分员的队长则拿来自己上一场失利的棋谱，请他把转折点改成一道训练题。

**下一步发展：** 新职责让周岑可以定期与学员对练，但不改变他不占正式席位的原则。他的下一个目标是从队长的棋谱中整理三道能反复练习的局面，并在复盘课上解释不同选择会带来什么结果。负责人的信任扩大了行动空间，公开讲解又提高了被观察压力；下一轮由本轮结果直接生成。

这个案例没有在临时补位时给周岑增加新本领，也没有让一次胜局取消他长期保留学员席位的理由。第一轮只让读者早已见过的判断能力得到可见验证，并让配角据此改变后续安排。
body.en:
This is an original planning example, not a plot taken from a published work or a required genre template.

Zhou Cen volunteers as a weekend scorekeeper at a neighborhood chess club. The story has already established three facts: after closing, he replays the day’s recorded games and often finds the decisive move before reading the coach’s notes; he can turn the same position into a useful exercise for trainees; and he deliberately does not take a youth player’s board because he promised the coordinator that his volunteer role would preserve the club’s limited playing time for its trainees. His current objective is to assemble a set of review exercises for them. The reader has seen his after-hours analysis and therefore knows that this skill exists, though its full range remains unknown. The players see him setting clocks and collecting score sheets, so they still regard him as a nonplaying helper. This is the arrangement used throughout the guide: the protagonist knows, the reader has evidence, and the observer does not.

**Quiet progress:** Zhou Cen copies key positions from recent practice games onto cards, tests each one after closing, and removes any exercise that does not present a clear choice. He does not seek a place on the youth team; the work still serves their review sessions.

**Challenge:** Just before a neighborhood friendly match begins, one player must leave because of an urgent family obligation, and the club has no substitute. The final board in the planned practice match will be canceled. The coordinator asks whether an adult who is not on the roster can fill the empty place. No trainee will lose a board, so Zhou Cen’s promise still holds: he can step in only to complete this practice match.

**Visible proof:** Zhou Cen uses only the ability to read positions that the story has already shown. He preserves his position through the opponent’s pressure, takes advantage of one mistake, and reaches a winning position before the opponent resigns. Afterward, he reconstructs the turning point from their recorded moves, allowing the watching trainees to follow why he changed plans at that moment. The proof lies in the result and a game record that others can review; narration never needs to announce that he was secretly strong.

**Observer reaction:** The coordinator does more than say that he is surprised. He adds “adult practice partner” to Zhou Cen’s volunteer duties while preserving every youth player’s official board, then asks him to lead the next post-match review. The team captain, who had regarded him only as a scorekeeper, brings over the record of a previous loss and asks Zhou Cen to turn its decisive position into a training exercise.

**Next development:** The new role lets Zhou Cen practice regularly with the trainees without violating his rule against taking their official places. His next objective is to create three reusable positions from the captain’s game and explain the consequences of different choices during the review session. The coordinator’s trust expands his room to act, while public explanation increases the pressure of being observed. Both conditions grow directly from the completed loop.

The temporary substitution does not grant Zhou Cen a new ability, and one victory does not erase his durable reason for preserving trainee board time. The first loop validates judgment the reader has already seen and causes supporting characters to change later arrangements.

heading.zh: 让 AI 只规划下一轮，不改写既有设定
heading.en: Ask AI to Plan One Loop Without Rewriting Established Facts

body.zh:
先把已确认的能力、事实和当前人物判断放进提示词。资料不够时，让 AI 标出缺口，不要自动补设定。

> 请为下一段剧情规划一轮“隐藏实力”循环。
>
> 已建立的主角能力与边界：
> 已建立的故事事实：
> 主角当前目标：
> 读者已经看过、证明这项能力存在（不必揭示完整范围）的证据：
> 观察角色当前判断及依据：
>
> 只输出：主角知道什么、读者已经看过什么、观察者还不知道什么，默默推进，挑战，可见证明，配角的具体行动反应，以及由此产生的下一步发展。
> 必须沿用已建立的能力、边界、人物、关系和事实；不得新增能力、代价、身份、组织、关键道具或过去事件。信息不足处标记“缺少事实”，不要补写。证明必须可观察，反应必须改变后续行动。

拿到结果后，先核对“可见证明”是否真的由既有能力完成，再核对配角反应是否造成下一轮条件。若 AI 只是换词重复“众人震惊”，删掉评价句，要求它改写为某个角色实际授予、收回、调查、合作或阻拦的动作。
body.en:
Put the confirmed ability, story facts, and current character judgments into the prompt first. When the material is insufficient, require the model to mark the gap instead of filling it with new canon.

> Plan one hidden-strength loop for the next story segment.
>
> Established protagonist ability and boundaries:
> Established story facts:
> Protagonist’s current objective:
> Evidence the reader has already seen that establishes the competence exists, without revealing its full range:
> The observing character’s current judgment and evidence:
>
> Output only: what the protagonist knows, what the reader has already seen, what the observer does not yet know, quiet progress, challenge, visible proof, the supporting character’s concrete action in response, and the next development produced by that response.
> Preserve every established ability, boundary, character, relationship, and fact. Do not add abilities, costs, identities, organizations, key objects, or past events. Mark missing information as ‘fact needed’ instead of inventing it. The proof must be observable, and the reaction must change a later action.

After generation, first verify that the visible proof truly uses an established ability. Then verify that the observer reaction changes the conditions of the next loop. If the model merely paraphrases “everyone was shocked,” remove the evaluative sentence and ask for an action in which a specific character grants access, withdraws trust, investigates, cooperates, or obstructs.

q.zh: 扮猪吃虎一定要让读者提前知道主角很强吗？
q.en: Must the Reader Know in Advance That the Protagonist Is Powerful?

a.zh: 在本文这套期待型循环里，需要。读者不必知道主角的全部底牌，但必须已经看过证明这项能力存在的证据（不必揭示完整范围），才能领先于观察者等待证明。若读者和配角在同一时刻才第一次得知结果，那属于另一种揭示任务，不在本页采用的信息配置内。这只是本文的明确边界，不是所有扮猪吃虎故事的通用定义。
a.en: For the anticipation loop taught here, yes. The reader does not need the protagonist’s complete history or full range, but must already have evidence establishing that the competence exists, though not necessarily its full range, and therefore wait for proof ahead of the observer. If the reader and supporting character first learn the result at the same moment, that is a different reveal task outside this guide’s information setup. This is the guide’s boundary, not a universal definition of every hidden-strength story.

q.zh: 配角每次都要先看不起主角吗？
q.en: Does a Supporting Character Need to Look Down on the Protagonist Every Time?

a.zh: 不需要。观察者可以低估、误解、怀疑、谨慎信任，或已经认可一部分能力但不知道边界。挑战只需检验当前判断；反应则要让判断转化成不同的行动。反复辱骂再震惊，容易让发现线停在同一层。
a.en: No. An observer may underestimate, misunderstand, suspect, trust cautiously, or recognize part of the ability without knowing its limits. The challenge only needs to test the current judgment, and the reaction should turn the updated judgment into a different action. Repeating insult followed by amazement leaves the discovery line at the same stage.

q.zh: 隐藏实力应该什么时候全部公开？
q.en: When Should the Protagonist Reveal Their Full Strength?

a.zh: 这套循环不要求某个固定节点全部公开。每轮只决定当前挑战需要展示什么，以及展示后谁会怎样行动。若你要安排一次彻底揭露并重写人物关系，那是单次反转与后果设计；若你仍要继续循环，就保留尚未被观察者确认的部分，同时不要否认已经出现过的证据。
a.en: This loop does not impose a fixed point for complete disclosure. Each round decides only what the current challenge requires the protagonist to show and how particular observers act afterward. A total unmasking that rewrites relationships is a one-time reveal-and-consequence problem. If the loop will continue, leave some capability unconfirmed while preserving every piece of evidence already shown.

text.zh: 准备好已确认的能力边界、当前目标，以及主角、读者、观察者各自知道的事实后，在 Claude Code 中使用 /story-long-write（Codex 中使用 `$story-long-write`），要求它只填写下一轮的默默推进、挑战、可见证明、配角行动反应和下一步发展，不新增任何故事事实，先给纸面方案，不写正文。
text.en: Prepare the confirmed ability boundaries, current objective, and the facts known by the protagonist, reader, and observer. Then use /story-long-write in Claude Code (or `$story-long-write` in Codex) and ask it to fill only the next loop's quiet progress, challenge, visible proof, supporting-character action, and next development. Require it to add no story facts and to return a planning outline rather than prose.

title.zh: 双男主感情线怎么写出潜台词：用信息差与行动痕迹
title.en: How to Write Subtext Between Two Male Leads

seo_title.zh: 双男主潜台词怎么写：信息差与行动细节
seo_title.en: How to Write Subtext Between Two Male Leads

description.zh: 把人物说出口的话、实际选择、对方看见的痕迹与读者掌握的信息分开，写出可推理的双男主潜台词；含场景例子和AI提示词。
description.en: Plan subtext between two male leads with dialogue, action, visible evidence, and viewpoint. Includes a scene example and a bounded AI prompt.

answer.zh: 写双男主关系戏的潜台词，可先列出四层：一方公开说什么、实际做什么、另一方能观察到什么、读者此时知道什么。为行动安排可见痕迹，再选择发现顺序和角色解释，并决定后续证据如何重构理解。根据人物设定确定关系性质与视角安排，让信息差服务当前场景。
answer.en: To write subtext between two male leads, track four layers: what one says publicly, what he does, what the other can observe, and what the reader knows. Give actions visible traces, choose the order of discovery and interpretation, then decide how later evidence may reshape that reading. Let established character facts determine the bond and viewpoint.

heading.zh: 先区分说出口的立场与实际做出的选择
heading.en: Separate the Spoken Position from the Actual Choice

body.zh:
潜台词通过人物公开说法、实际行动和可见结果共同呈现。先列出人物愿意说什么，再列出他做出的具体选择。两者可以一致，也可以保留一段读者能追踪的距离；动作、物件、记录或结果会让读者获得推理线索。

为这段距离安排一个可查证的痕迹，再分别写下两位主角可能如何理解它。解释应当来自当下证据和既有关系经历，后续材料可以支持、修正或搁置判断。

公开与私下的落差可以表现克制、戒备、愧疚、职业分歧或依赖，具体含义由人物关系和已建立的故事事实决定。对白与行动一致、场景意图清楚时，就让对话直接完成任务；把潜台词留给确实承担信息作用的细节。
body.en:
Subtext emerges through a character’s public words, actual choices, and visible results. List what he is willing to say, then the specific action he takes. Those layers can align or leave a distance readers can follow; an action, object, record, or outcome gives readers evidence to interpret.

Give that distance a trace the other lead can verify, then list how each protagonist might read it. Ground interpretations in present evidence and established relationship history; later material can support, revise, or leave a reading unresolved.

A public/private gap may express restraint, caution, guilt, professional disagreement, or dependence. Established character and story facts determine its meaning. When dialogue and action align and the scene’s purpose is clear, let the exchange do its job directly; reserve subtext for details that carry information.

heading.zh: 用信息账本控制甲、乙和读者各自知道什么
heading.en: Track What A, B, and the Reader Each Know

body.zh:
动笔前记下信息边界，让每个人依据已经看到、听到或被告知的线索作判断。把已发生的事实和人物对事实的解释分开：

- **甲知道：** 甲亲自看到、听到或被告知了什么？
- **乙知道：** 乙依据哪些现成证据作判断？
- **读者知道：** 读者比谁多知道一项行动，或暂时和谁共享有限视角？
- **待核实信息：** 哪项动机还需要后续线索？

同一痕迹可以让甲和乙得出不同结论。让每种解读都对应关系经历与当下证据。例如，乙看到自己提出的第12句改写被标为待核，可能以为甲在否定他的校订；内部目录若同时保留“校订者：乙”，就为乙提供了另一条线索。

视角决定读者获得信息的时机：单一视角让读者和一位主角一起观察；双视角可以提前展示另一人的行动，也可以让读者与两人一样等待证据。让当前场景的信息需要决定采用何种视角。需要梳理视角边界时，可参照[人物视角指南](/oh-story/narrative-point-of-view)；本页专门讨论视角如何承载双男主之间的潜台词。
body.en:
Record the information boundaries before drafting so each lead reasons from evidence he has seen, heard, or received. Keep an established fact separate from a character’s reading of it:

- **What A knows:** What has A seen, heard, or been told directly?
- **What B knows:** Which available evidence supports B’s judgment?
- **What the reader knows:** Does the reader know one action early, or share one character’s limited view?
- **Evidence to come:** Which motive needs a later clue?

The same trace can lead A and B to different conclusions. Ground each reading in relationship history and current evidence. For example, B sees his proposed rewrite of line 12 marked pending and may think A dismisses his editing work; an internal catalog that still lists B as proofreader offers another clue.

Viewpoint sets the timing of reader knowledge. A single viewpoint lets the reader observe alongside one lead; dual viewpoints can reveal the other’s action early, or leave readers waiting for evidence alongside both men. Let the information needs of the scene guide the viewpoint. For viewpoint boundaries, see the [point-of-view guide](/oh-story/narrative-point-of-view); this page focuses on how viewpoint carries subtext between two male leads.

heading.zh: 让痕迹支持推理，再决定是否安排后续重释
heading.en: Let Evidence Support an Inference Before You Decide to Reframe It

body.zh:
写一场承担关系潜台词的戏时，逐项回答：

1. **公开话语：** 这句话在当前场合完成什么实际任务？例如划定责任、拒绝请求或结束谈话。
2. **另一项选择：** 说话的人做了什么选择，又给对方留下哪些可见结果？用行动线索承载情绪。
3. **可见痕迹：** 对方通过什么细节有机会发现行动？把发现路径写出来。
4. **暂时解释：** 对方依据手头信息会怎样理解？若存在另一种读法，它也要有情境依据。
5. **后续证据：** 旧痕迹是否会在后文获得新解释？如会，补充一项事实、视角或背景，让读者据此判断。

按叙事节奏决定何时保留、何时揭开信息差。挑选承载隐情的关键场景；其他场景可以呈现坦率交流、事务推进或沉默。若多个叙事单元后关系张力重复，检查是否反复使用同一种否认、暗中帮助或误读，再为后续选择有依据的新线索。把揭示留给能改变读者理解的时刻。
body.en:
For a scene that carries relationship subtext, answer these questions:

1. **Public line:** What practical job does the statement do in this setting—set a boundary, refuse a request, or end a conversation?
2. **Other choice:** What does the speaker choose, and what visible result follows? Use action as evidence for emotion.
3. **Observable trace:** Through which detail could the other lead discover the action? Write the path of discovery.
4. **Provisional reading:** How would the other lead interpret the evidence available now? If there is another reading, give it a basis in the situation.
5. **Later evidence:** Will a later scene reframe the old trace? If so, add a fact, viewpoint, or context that lets readers interpret it.

Let the story’s pace govern when information gaps remain open and when evidence surfaces. Choose scenes that carry concealed meaning; other scenes can use direct speech, practical action, or silence. When the same tension repeats across several narrative units, examine whether the story relies on one denial, hidden favor, or misreading. Reserve reveals for moments when evidence can change a reader’s interpretation.

heading.zh: 原创场景：一张被单独保存的校订页
heading.en: Original Scene: A Correction Sheet Kept Apart

body.zh:
甲乙曾合编一套口述史录音。上一次校订，乙发现一处录音缺漏；甲将成稿的“校订者”一栏归为项目组，没有列乙的名字，乙因此担心自己的贡献再次被隐去。这次审校会上，甲指着第12句说：“这句改写暂缓采用，等原始录音复核。”他在公开审校表上把乙提出的改写标为“待核”，乙将这项决定理解为甲再次否定他的校订工作。

如果叙述跟随甲的有限视角，读者可以看到散会后的内部目录：甲将“校订者：乙”和“第12句改写：乙提出，录音待核”分别登记。乙此时只看见公开审校表。读者先知道，甲保留了乙作为校订者的贡献，同时把校订内容的核实状态单独标出。

后来乙查看校订记录，发现自己的名字仍在“校订者”一栏，第12句改写则等待复核。乙由此重读甲的公开决定：甲暂缓采用的是校订内容，内部目录仍正式记录了他的工作。结合旧有署名争议与眼前目录，乙可以把这个选择读成归档程序、对过去贡献的重新承认，或两者兼有；甲的完整动机留给后续线索。
body.en:
A and B once co-edited a collection of oral-history recordings. During an earlier review, B found a gap in one recording. A credited the finished edition to the project team without listing B in its proofreader field, so B worries that his contribution will disappear again. At a new review, A points to line 12 and says, “We’ll hold this rewrite until the source recording is checked.” He marks B’s proposed wording as pending on the public review sheet, and B reads the decision as another dismissal of his editing work.

With A as the limited viewpoint, readers can see the internal catalog after the meeting: A enters “proofreader: B” and “line 12 rewrite: proposed by B; source pending verification” as separate fields. B has seen only the public review sheet. Readers learn first that A preserved B’s contribution as proofreader while marking the proposed wording for verification.

Later, B checks the correction record and finds his name still in the proofreader field, with the rewrite of line 12 awaiting review.
