> [画面文字] 提交时间：16:52
> [画面文字] 补打时间：18:10
> 办事员把打印回执交给林遥。
> [连续性] 林遥拿着打印回执；手写回执仍摊在柜台上。

场景标题交代何时何地；动作写能看到的行为；角色名锁定说话人；屏显文字和画外对白只在故事需要时出现；最后一条记录交接后两张回执分别在哪里。若后续分镜要改变场景事实，应先回到剧本所有者确认，而不是在分镜或提示词中悄悄改掉。
body.en:
This original fictional excerpt demonstrates formatting; it is not a filmed or verified result:

> # EP001 【Receipt Check】
> ## EP001-SC001 内 · Community service desk · Evening
> Lin Yao slides the handwritten receipt back across the counter, pointing to the handwritten 18:10 in its top corner.
> Lin Yao: But I submitted it before five.
> [OS] Colleague in the hallway: The printed receipt is ready.
> The clerk takes the fresh printout from the printer and turns it toward Lin Yao.
> [画面文字] Submission time: 16:52
> [画面文字] Reprint time: 18:10
> The clerk hands the printed receipt to Lin Yao.
> [连续性] Lin Yao holds the printed receipt; the handwritten receipt remains on the counter.

The heading establishes when and where. The action is visible. Character names identify each speaker. On-screen text and off-screen dialogue appear only because the story needs them. The final line records where each receipt is after the handoff. If a later storyboard would change a story fact, confirm it with the script owner instead of silently changing it in the board or prompt.

heading.zh: 用 AI 整理剧本后，对照原稿复核
heading.en: Compare an AI-Formatted Script with Its Source

body.zh:
把原稿、已选格式和角色名单一起交给 AI，并要求它只做结构整理：标出集/场景标题、分开动作与对白、按已选规则添加必须的标签。格式未说明、说话人不明或原文有歧义时列为“待确认”，不要让模型猜。

复核时对照原稿，重点看四件事：说话人是否被替换；动作和对白的先后是否变化；标签有没有把角色内心自动改成 VO/OS；场景、时间和物件交接有没有被补写或删除。剧本格式化不能替代作者对语义变化的确认。分集节奏与事件顺序应在大纲阶段决定；本页只检查每场落到剧本文字后是否清楚。
body.en:
Give the AI the source draft, the chosen format, and the character list. Ask it only to organize structure: add episode/scene headings, separate action from dialogue, and apply required labels under the selected rules. If the format is undefined, a speaker is unclear, or the source is ambiguous, mark it “Needs confirmation” instead of guessing.

Compare the result with the original. Check whether speakers changed, the order of action and dialogue shifted, a character's inner thought was automatically labeled as VO/OS, or scene/time/object handoffs were added or removed. Formatting does not replace the author's review of semantic changes. Plan episode pacing and event order at outline stage; this page only checks whether each scene is clear in the written script.

q.zh: △ 和 ▲ 是短剧剧本的固定行业标准吗？
q.en: Are △ and ▲ universal standards for vertical-drama scripts?

a.zh: 本页引用的来源把这组符号列为特定项目方言的约定；同一来源也单独说明 Markdown 剧本格式。开稿前选定所用格式，再按该格式的符号含义执行。
a.en: The cited source defines these marks as one project dialect and documents the Markdown screenplay format separately. Choose the format before drafting, then follow the meanings defined for it.

q.zh: 剧本里的 OS 和 VO 有什么区别？
q.en: What is the difference between OS and VO in a script?

a.zh: 要看所用格式。本页的 Markdown 格式把 `[OS]` 用于同一场景里的画外对白，把 `[VO]` 用于非现场主观或叙述声音；另一个项目方言可把角色 `(OS)` 定义为内在声音。项目应明确采用哪一份说明，不能把两套定义混在一场戏里。
a.en: It depends on the selected format. The Markdown format on this page uses `[OS]` for off-screen dialogue in the same scene and `[VO]` for non-local subjective or narrative voice. Another project dialect may define a character's `(OS)` as inner voice. A project should name its convention; do not mix the two in one scene.

q.zh: 剧本里要写景别、推拉摇移和焦段吗？
q.en: Should a screenplay include shot size, camera movement, and focal length?

a.zh: 这套故事剧本格式把这些交给分镜或摄影方案；剧本保留场景边界、可见动作、对白和必要制作信息。团队若采用其他格式，应先在项目约定中写明。
a.en: This story-script format leaves those details to the storyboard or camera plan. Keep scene boundaries, visible action, dialogue, and necessary production information in the script. If the team uses another format, document it first.

q.zh: AI 能直接把旧剧本转换成新格式吗？
q.en: Can AI convert an old script directly into a new format?

a.zh: 可以先让 AI 提出格式整理稿，但要保留原稿并逐项比对。说话人、动作顺序、对白、时间和物件状态都可能在规范化时改变；不确定项应交给作者确认，不让模型静默补全。
a.en: AI can propose a formatted copy, but keep the source and compare the result line by line. Speakers, action order, dialogue, time, and object states can shift during normalization. Send uncertain items to the author for review instead of letting the model fill them in silently.

text.zh: 可选：按我明确指定的本项目剧本格式，整理我提供的原稿，只处理集/场景标题、可见动作、角色对白和我要求的制作标签。只使用原文与角色名单；不得新增人物、对白、动作、因果、时间、声源或物件交接，不得改写台词含义。遇到 OS/VO 定义、说话人或格式不确定处，标为“待确认”，不要自动套用另一种方言。输出整理稿和逐项差异供我复核，不要声称已替我确认剧情或生产可用性。
text.en: Optional: Reformat only the episode/scene headings, visible action, character dialogue, and production labels I request, using the specific project format I name. Use only the source text and character list; do not add characters, dialogue, action, causality, time, sound sources, or object handoffs, and do not change a line's meaning. Mark unclear OS/VO definitions, speakers, or formatting as “Needs confirmation”; do not apply another dialect automatically. Return the formatted draft and a change list for my review. Do not claim that you have approved story meaning or production readiness.

title.zh: AI写小说动作描写重复怎么办：合并同一瞬间的改稿法
title.en: How to Fix Repetitive Actions in AI-Assisted Fiction

seo_title.zh: AI写小说动作描写重复怎么办
seo_title.en: How to Fix Repetitive Actions in AI Fiction

description.zh: AI写小说把同一情绪拆成动作、身体反应和解释反复写？先标出同一瞬间，保留影响选择与结果的细节，再合并成连续正文。附原创示例、检查表和改稿提示词。
description.en: Fix AI fiction that repeats one beat as action, bodily reaction, and explanation. Use a mark-and-merge worksheet, example, checklist, and prompt.

answer.zh: AI写小说动作描写重复，先把发生在同一瞬间、传递同一信息的“动作—身体或感官反应—情绪解释”标成一组。逐句做删除测试，保留会改变人物选择、关系、物件状态、动作结果或空间判断的细节；再按实际先后把这一组合并成一段连续正文。最后对照原文核查人物、地点、物件、因果和时间线，并朗读检查作者语气是否还在。第二次出现若带来升级、转义或新后果，就不是该删的重复。
answer.en: When AI-assisted fiction repeats a beat, group lines that cover the same instant and deliver the same information: the action, a bodily or sensory response, then an explanation of the feeling. Delete-test each line, keeping details that affect a choice, relationship, object, outcome, or spatial understanding. Rebuild the survivors into one continuous passage in event order, then compare facts and voice with the original. Keep an echo when it escalates, changes meaning, or causes something new.

heading.zh: 先判断：三句话是不是在写同一个瞬间
heading.en: First, check whether the lines describe the same beat

body.zh:
这类重复不靠某个禁用词判断，而看**时间和信息有没有前进**。常见结构是：先写人物做了什么，再单独写一个手抖、胸闷或声音发紧，最后由叙述者解释“他其实很害怕”。三层都指向同一次反应，人物没有作出新选择，场面也没有出现新结果。

给相邻句做三个标记：

- **A｜发生**：人物做了什么，物件或位置发生了什么变化。
- **B｜感知或身体反应**：人物看见、听见、疼痛、失手，或动作因此受阻。
- **C｜解释**：叙述者给情绪、动机或意义下结论。

如果 A、B、C 共享同一个时间点，删掉其中一句后读者仍得到完全相同的信息，就把它们圈成一组。若后一句让时间前进、改变选择、补上因果锚点或造成新后果，它属于下一拍，不要为了“去重复”硬并。
body.en:
This is not a banned-word problem. Ask whether **time or information moves forward**. A common pattern states the action, isolates a trembling hand or tightened voice, then explains that the character is frightened. All three may point to one response while the character makes no new choice and the scene produces no new result.

Mark neighboring lines:

- **A | Event**: what the character does, or what changes in an object or position.
- **B | Sensation or body response**: what they notice, feel, drop, miss, or fail to do.
- **C | Explanation**: the narrator labels the emotion, motive, or meaning.

Group A, B, and C when they occupy the same instant and removing one leaves the reader with identical information. Do not merge a later line that advances time, changes a decision, supplies a necessary causal anchor, or creates a new consequence. That is a new beat.

heading.zh: 标记—保留—合并：可复制的短检查表
heading.en: A copyable mark, keep, and merge worksheet

body.zh:
不要先把身体反应全部删掉。先问每个细节是否承担功能，再决定保留、合并还是删除。

| 步骤 | 写下什么 | 判断标准 |
|---|---|---|
| 1. 标记同一拍 | A 发生 / B 感知或身体 / C 解释 | 是否处在同一时刻、传递同一情绪或动作信息 |
| 2. 圈出必须保留项 | 人物选择、关系变化、物件状态、动作结果、空间位置、必要因果 | 删掉后，读者是否会误判发生了什么或人物为何这样做 |
| 3. 删除纯复述 | 只给前一句换说法的总结、标签或套式反应 | 删掉后事实、情绪力度和衔接都不变 |
| 4. 按事件顺序合并 | 动作 → 受阻或感知 → 选择或结果 | 读起来像一个连续镜头，而不是动作清单 |
| 5. 对照原文 | 人物、地点、物件、先后、因果、叙述口吻 | 没有新增设定、关系、事件或时间跳跃 |

身体细节是否值得留，看它有没有作用。例如，手抖导致钥匙插不进锁，这是动作结果；伤口让人物留下证据，这是情节后果。若“手指发白”只是在“她很紧张”后又贴一次标签，可以删掉或并入真正发生的动作。合并也不是把所有动词挤成一串；无关紧要的拿起、转身、放下应压缩，承担情绪、情节或空间信息的动作要留下。
body.en:
Do not begin by deleting every physical response. Test what each detail does, then keep, merge, or cut it.

| Step | What to note | Test |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Mark one beat | A event / B sensation or body / C explanation | Same instant, same emotional or action information? |
| 2. Circle required details | Choice, relationship shift, object state, outcome, position, necessary cause | Would cutting it make the reader misread what happened or why? |
| 3. Cut restatement | A label, stock response, or summary that only rephrases the previous line | Do facts, force, and continuity survive without it? |
| 4. Merge in event order | Action → interruption or perception → choice or result | Does it read as one shot rather than an action inventory? |
| 5. Compare with the source | People, place, objects, order, causality, narrative voice | No new setting, relationship, event, or time jump? |

A bodily detail earns its place through function. A shaking hand that prevents a key entering the lock changes the outcome; a cut that leaves evidence affects the plot. White knuckles that merely repeat “she was nervous” can go. Merging does not mean packing every verb into a list: compress trivial handling, but keep actions that carry emotion, plot, or spatial information.

heading.zh: 原创示例：把动作、身体反应和解释还原成一个镜头
heading.en: Original example: turn three layers into one continuous moment

body.zh:
下面的车站片段为本页原创。四句都围绕程雾是否去北城这一拍，信息没有必要分四段重复交付。

**改写前：**

> 程雾把去北城的车票递向检票员。
>
> 她的手指忽然发僵，车票掉到了地上。
>
> 她很害怕去北城，因为哥哥失踪前最后一通电话就是从那里打来的。
>
> 她把票捡起来，重新递给检票员。

先做标记：第一句是 A（递票），第二句是 B（身体反应改变动作结果），第三句前半只是情绪标签，后半却提供了不能丢的因果；第四句给出人物最终选择。应删的是“她很害怕”这层重复，不是北城来电，也不是她重新递票的决定。

**合并后：**

> 程雾把去北城的车票递向检票员，指尖忽然发僵，票掉在地上。哥哥失踪前的最后一通电话，来自北城。她弯腰捡起票，还是递给了检票员。

改后没有添新事故，也没有把恐惧换成另一套华丽描写。掉票让身体反应产生结果，来电说明北城为何有分量，“还是递给了检票员”让这一个瞬间落在选择上。四个分段变成连续正文，但关键信息一项未少。
body.en:
This station scene is original to this page. Every line belongs to the moment when Cheng Wu must decide whether to travel to Beicheng, so the information does not need four separate deliveries.

**Before:**

> Cheng Wu held out her Beicheng ticket to the inspector.
>
> Her fingers suddenly locked, and the ticket slipped to the floor.
>
> She was afraid to go to Beicheng because her brother's last call before he vanished had come from there.
>
> She picked up the ticket and handed it to the inspector again.

The first line is A, the attempted handoff. The second is B, a physical response that changes the action's outcome. “She was afraid” labels what the stumble already shows, but the brother's call is necessary cause. The last line carries her decision. Cut the duplicated label, not the call or the choice.

**After:**

> Cheng Wu held out her Beicheng ticket to the inspector, but her fingers locked and it slipped to the floor. Her brother's last call before he vanished had come from Beicheng. She bent to retrieve the ticket and handed it to the inspector anyway.

The revision invents no incident and reaches for no decorative substitute. Dropping the ticket gives the physical response an outcome, the call explains the destination's weight, and “anyway” lands the beat on a choice. Four isolated deliveries become one continuous passage without losing a fact.

heading.zh: 别误删：有升级、转义或后果的重复要保留
heading.en: Do not cut echoes that escalate, turn, or cause something

body.zh:
重复一个动作或声音，有时是在控制节奏。判断第二次出现是否完成了新工作：

- **升级**：第一次门铃响，屋里没人动；第三次响时，门外开始试钥匙。声音相同，威胁变了。
- **转义**：人物先把“没关系”说给别人听，后来独自重复时成了自我说服。字面相同，意图变了。
- **新后果**：受伤的手第一次发抖只是疼，第二次让他没接住证物。动作结果变了。
- **刻意节奏**：重复构成回环、对照或角色口头习惯，而且删掉会破坏声音。

若第二次只再次证明“他紧张”“她生气”，既没有强度变化，也没有新的选择、关系、物件或结果，就属于可压缩的信息。保留功能性回声，不等于给每一种情绪机械配一个身体动作。

本页只处理**同一拍的信息重复**。要做整章的三遍去 AI 味流程，看[去AI味改稿法](/oh-story/revise-ai-prose)；要研究参考小说如何安排技巧，看[小说拆书模板](/oh-story/learn-from-fiction)。这里不做词汇黑名单，也不泛讲情绪写作；若删完已经像提纲，应恢复必要连接，而不是继续压缩。
body.en:
Repeating an action or sound can control rhythm. Keep the second occurrence when it does new work:

- **Escalation**: no one moves at the first ring; by the third, someone outside is trying a key. Same sound, greater threat.
- **Changed meaning**: “It doesn't matter” comforts someone else first, then becomes self-persuasion when repeated alone.
- **New consequence**: an injured hand trembles from pain once, then fails to catch the evidence later.
- **Deliberate rhythm**: the recurrence creates a refrain, contrast, or character habit, and cutting it damages the voice.

If the second occurrence only proves again that a character is nervous or angry, with no change in intensity, choice, relationship, object, or result, compress it. Keeping a functional echo does not mean attaching a body motion to every emotion.

This page fixes **duplicate information inside one beat**. For a full three-pass revision, use [the AI-prose revision workflow](/oh-story/revise-ai-prose); to extract craft from reference fiction, use [the novel deconstruction template](/oh-story/learn-from-fiction). This is neither a word blacklist nor a general lesson in writing emotion. If your edit already reads like notes, restore connective prose instead of cutting further.

heading.zh: 可复制改稿提示词与最后核查
heading.en: Copyable revision prompt and final check

body.zh:
把提示词限制在这一个问题上，避免模型顺手重写剧情或统一作者语气。

**短提示词（可复制）：**

> 只修改下面片段中，同一瞬间被拆写成“动作 → 身体/感官反应 → 情绪解释”的重复。先列出重复组；保留会改变人物选择、关系、物件状态、动作结果、空间判断或必要因果的细节；再把每组合并为连续正文。第二次出现若有升级、转义或新后果则保留。不得新增剧情、设定、关系或时间线，不得统一或美化作者语气。最后列出删改内容和不确定处。正文：〔粘贴片段〕

拿到改稿后，不要只看字数是否变少。逐项核对：

- [ ] 人物、地点、物件及其状态与原文一致
- [ ] 动作先后、因果和时间线没有变化
- [ ] 有功能的身体细节、选择和后果仍在
- [ ] 没有把重复换成新比喻、新套话或动作清单
- [ ] 叙述视角、用词习惯、句子松紧仍像原作者
- [ ] 朗读时同一镜头连得起来，也没有压成电报体

最后再把改后段落与原文并排看一遍。凡是改后才出现的人物判断、道具用途、关系变化或事件，都先撤回；无法确定是否重复的句子，标出来交给作者决定。
body.en:
Keep the prompt bounded to this failure so the model does not rewrite the plot or standardize the author's voice.

**Short prompt (copyable):**

> Revise only places where one instant is repeated as action → bodily or sensory response → explanation of the same feeling. First list the duplicate groups. Keep details that affect a choice, relationship, object state, action outcome, spatial understanding, or necessary cause. Merge each group into continuous prose. Keep later echoes that escalate, change meaning, or create a new consequence. Do not add plot, setting, relationships, or timeline changes, and do not polish away the author's voice. End with a list of edits and uncertainties. Text: [paste passage]

Do not judge the result only by its lower word count. Check:

- [ ] Characters, places, objects, and object states match the source
- [ ] Event order, causality, and timeline are unchanged
- [ ] Functional body details, choices, and consequences remain
- [ ] Repetition was not replaced with fresh clichés, metaphors, or an action inventory
- [ ] Point of view, diction, and sentence rhythm still sound like the author
- [ ] The shot reads continuously aloud without becoming telegraphic

Finish with a side-by-side comparison. Revert any judgment, prop function, relationship change, or event that exists only in the revision. Flag uncertain cases for the author instead of silently deleting them.

q.zh: 小说里动作加身体反应，出现两次就算重复吗？
q.en: Is an action plus a bodily response automatically repetitive?

a.zh: 不算。身体反应若让动作失败、暴露伤势、改变选择，或给关系与情节带来后果，就在传递新信息。只有当动作、反应和解释停在同一瞬间，反复证明同一件事，删掉一层也不影响事实、力度和衔接时，才需要合并或删除。刻意回声若带来升级、转义或新后果，也应保留。
a.en: No. A bodily response carries new information when it makes an action fail, reveals an injury, changes a choice, or affects a relationship or the plot. Merge only layers that occupy the same instant, prove the same point, and can lose one layer without changing facts, force, or continuity. Keep a deliberate echo when it escalates, changes meaning, or produces a new consequence.

q.zh: 合并重复描写后，小说变短、变平了怎么办？
q.en: What if merging repetition makes the prose flat or too compressed?

a.zh: 先回到原文恢复被误删的功能信息：人物为什么停顿、哪件物品变了、动作是否成功、他最终作了什么选择。再补回必要的指代、连接和自然句长，让同一镜头顺着读下去。不要为了“有画面”新增比喻、套式身体反应或原文没有的事件；若原文确实缺少关键因果，把它标为待作者补充，而不是代写。
a.en: Return to the source and restore functional information first: why the character pauses, what changes in an object, whether the action succeeds, and what choice follows. Then restore the connective phrasing and sentence length needed for the shot to flow. Do not compensate with new metaphors, stock body language, or invented events. If the source truly lacks a causal link, flag it for the author rather than making one up.

text.zh: 把小说片段交给 story-deslop，并要求“只修改同一瞬间重复表达的信息，保留会改变人物选择、关系、物件状态、动作结果、空间判断或必要因果的细节；不得新增剧情或统一作者语气。先标出重复组，再给有限改写和待作者确认项”。作者核对事实与口吻后再采用。
text.en: Give the passage to story-deslop and ask it to revise only information repeated within one beat. Preserve details that affect choices, relationships, object state, action outcome, spatial understanding, or necessary causality; add no plot facts or standardize the author’s voice. Ask it to list duplicate groups, bounded edits, and uncertainties. Review facts and voice before using the edits.

title.zh: AI写小说前后矛盾怎么查：证据链审稿法
title.en: How to Check AI-Assisted Fiction for Continuity Errors

seo_title.zh: AI写小说前后矛盾怎么查
seo_title.en: How to Check AI Fiction for Continuity Errors

description.zh: AI写小说前后矛盾，先搜索明文，再核对设定、时间线、因果与代价。用证据表标明证据不足或证据支持的候选，交给作者裁决，并复查后续章节。
description.en: Audit AI-assisted fiction for factual, rule, timeline, causal, and cost conflicts. Cite both sides, separate evidence from severity, and recheck later chapters.

answer.zh: 审计 AI 辅助小说的前后矛盾，先限定章节范围，按人物名、物件、规则、地点和时间词搜索明文；再为每个可疑点列出前提或规则、触发事件、表面冲突和待作者回答的问题。任何一端缺少原文依据，都标“证据不足”；证据支持的冲突仍是候选，不自动等于错误。先独立记录证据状态，再按项目 story-review 的统一 S1–S4 口径排序影响。报告只给证据和待裁决项；作者确认是否存在刻意揭示或适用例外后，再修改并复查依赖它的后续章节。
answer.en: To audit continuity in AI-assisted fiction, define the chapter range and search explicit claims about people, objects, rules, places, and time. For each concern, record the premise or rule, triggering event, apparent contradiction, and question for the author. If either side lacks textual support, mark it Insufficient evidence; even a supported clash remains a candidate, not an automatic error. Record evidence status separately, then prioritize impact using the project’s shared story-review S1–S4 rubric. The report supplies evidence and questions; the author decides whether an intentional reveal or applicable exception explains the passage, then revises and checks dependent later chapters.

heading.zh: 先定范围：这次产出是一份成稿审计报告
heading.en: Set the scope: this pass produces a manuscript audit report

body.zh:
这套方法用于**已经写出的正文**。输入是明确的章节范围、相关设定或细纲，以及可引用的追踪记录；输出是一份带位置、双端证据、证据状态、项目统一严重度和待答问题的审计报告。重点检查六类事实关系：

- **实体**：人物属性、身份、亲属、位置、持有物和已知信息。
- **规则**：世界规则、能力边界、制度权限、例外条件和术语。
- **时间线**：日期、时长、事件先后、旅行与恢复时间。
- **因果**：原因、必要条件、行动、结果和后果能否接上。
- **代价**：能力、交易、治疗或突破的既定成本是否兑现。
- **明文事实**：同一对象是否被写成两个无法同时成立的状态。

如果担心写到后面忘记前文，就在创作过程中持续更新状态、角色知情和未结事项；本页则拿已经写出的正文反向取证。它不评价文笔、人物弧线或情节是否精彩，也不直接改稿。作者批准问题及处理方向后，再用[审稿意见改稿流程](/oh-story/review-and-revise)将决定变成有范围的修订任务。
body.en:
Use this method on **prose that already exists**. Its inputs are a defined chapter range, relevant setting or outline material, and citable tracking records. Its output is an audit report with locations, evidence on both sides, evidence status, the project-wide severity label, and questions for the author. Check six kinds of factual relationship:

- **Entities**: attributes, identity, family, location, possessions, and character knowledge.
- **Rules**: world rules, ability limits, institutional authority, exceptions, and terminology.
- **Timeline**: dates, durations, event order, travel, and recovery time.
- **Causality**: whether cause, necessary condition, action, result, and consequence connect.
- **Cost**: whether an established price for an ability, bargain, treatment, or breakthrough is paid.
- **Explicit facts**: whether the same subject receives two states that cannot both hold.

If your concern is forgetting established facts while drafting, keep states, character knowledge, and open matters current as chapters change. This page instead gathers evidence from prose that is already written. It does not judge prose quality, character arcs, or whether a plot is exciting, and it makes no edits. After the author approves a finding and its direction, use the [review-to-revision workflow](/oh-story/review-and-revise) to make it a bounded revision task.

heading.zh: 先搜明文，再查规则、因果和代价链
heading.en: Search explicit claims, then test rule, causal, and cost chains

body.zh:
连续通读容易让作者用脑内设定补齐缺口。先搜索，再推理，可以把“感觉不对”变成能复核的证据。

1. **限定范围。** 写明要审第几章到第几章，以及哪些设定、细纲或追踪记录可以作证。
2. **建立搜索词。** 收集人物本名、别名、地点、关键物件、规则术语、日期、数量、代价和限制词。
3. **保存所有命中。** 每条记录章节、段落或行号和最短必要引文，连同来源类型一起保存。
4. **核对明文。** 比较人物属性、位置、知识、物件状态、术语和事件顺序。
5. **补一轮推理。** 对核心事件写出“原因 → 条件 → 行动 → 结果 → 后果”，并单独检查规则的适用条件、例外、边界和代价。
6. **搜索可能的解释。** 查找授权、伪装、谎言、不可靠叙述、规则变化、一次性道具或已支付代价的证据。

每个候选都先写四个字段：**前提/规则、触发事件、表面冲突、需要作者裁决的问题**。两段文字看似冲突，但尚未查到规则适用范围，状态应为“证据不足”。两端引文已经互斥，同时没有找到已写明的例外，可以标“证据支持的候选”，严重度仍是排查优先级。作者随后确认它是否构成需要修改的错误。
body.en:
A straight read encourages the author to fill gaps with intentions that never reached the page. Search first, then reason, so a vague concern becomes reproducible evidence.

1. **Define the range.** Name the chapters under review and the setting, outline, or tracking records that may supply evidence.
2. **Build search terms.** Collect names, aliases, places, key objects, rule terms, dates, quantities, costs, and limit words.
3. **Save every hit.** Record the chapter, paragraph or line, the shortest necessary quotation, and its source type.
4. **Compare explicit claims.** Check attributes, locations, knowledge, object states, terminology, and event order.
5. **Add a reasoning pass.** For each load-bearing event, map cause → condition → action → result → consequence. Separately test each rule's conditions, exceptions, boundary, and cost.
6. **Search for explanations.** Look for evidence of authorization, disguise, lies, unreliable narration, rule changes, one-use devices, or a cost already paid.

Give every candidate four fields first: **premise/rule, trigger, apparent contradiction, and question for the author**. If two passages appear to conflict but the rule's scope is missing, use the status insufficient evidence. If both cited claims are mutually exclusive and no written exception appears in the audited range, use evidence-supported candidate. Severity still sets review priority; the author decides whether the candidate becomes an error to revise.

heading.zh: 可复制的证据表与 S1–S4 分诊
heading.en: A copyable evidence table and S1–S4 triage

body.zh:
把每条审计项写成一行，方便按证据裁决，也方便修改后复查。

| ID | 证据状态 | 类型 | 严重度 | 前提/规则引文 | 触发引文 | 表面冲突 | 可能解释/缺证 | 待作者裁决的问题 | 下游复查范围 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-01 | 证据不足 / 证据支持的候选 / 作者已裁决 / 已排除 | 实体 / 规则 / 时间线 / 因果 / 代价 / 事实 | S1–S4 | 文件或章节 + 位置 + 短引文 | 文件或章节 + 位置 + 短引文 | 两端为何暂时不能同时成立 | 例外、叙述视角或缺失材料 | 一个可回答的问题 | 受影响章节、人物、物件或规则 |

严重度沿用项目 story-review 的统一口径，回答“这件事影响多大”，不回答证据有多确定：

- **S1**：会损害主线、人物动机、世界规则或读者信任的问题。
- **S2**：明显影响章节效果、节奏、人物可信度或阅读留存的问题。
- **S3**：局部问题，如轻微细节、格式或措辞差异。
- **S4**：建议项或可选优化；例如伏笔已经超过计划回收点仍未兑现，先作为提醒，不自动判错。

先判证据状态，再标严重度。没有位置和原文依据的条目退回“证据不足”；引用支持的矛盾仍需作者确认其意图和影响。纯粹的“人物这样做不够聪明”“这个反转可以更精彩”不属于事实一致性审计。
body.en:
Put each audit item on one row so the author can rule on evidence and the same record can guide the post-revision check.

| ID | Evidence status | Type | Severity | Premise/rule citation | Trigger citation | Apparent contradiction | Possible explanation/missing evidence | Question for author | Downstream range |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-01 | Insufficient evidence / Evidence-supported candidate / Author ruled / Cleared | Entity / Rule / Timeline / Causal / Cost / Fact | S1–S4 | File or chapter + location + short quote | File or chapter + location + short quote | Why the claims currently cannot both hold | Exception, viewpoint, or missing material | One answerable question | Affected chapters, people, objects, or rules |

Use the project’s shared story-review severity rubric to answer “how much does this matter?” Severity is not evidence confidence:

- **S1**: threatens the main story, character motivation, world rules, or reader trust.
- **S2**: substantially affects a chapter, pacing, character credibility, or reader retention.
- **S3**: a local issue such as a minor detail, format, or wording mismatch.
- **S4**: an advisory or optional improvement; for example, a clue that has passed its planned payoff point can be flagged for follow-up, not declared an error.

Assign evidence status before severity. Return any item without a location and textual support to Insufficient evidence; even a supported conflict still needs the author’s ruling on intent and impact. Claims such as “the character should act smarter” or “the twist could be more exciting” are outside factual-consistency review.

heading.zh: 原创示例：双钥匙档案库出现单人开启
heading.en: Original example: one person opens a two-key archive

body.zh:
下面的档案库片段与审计结果均为本页原创。假定审查范围是第 3–19 章。

> **第 3 章，第 12 段：**“密封档案库只有在东、西两把钥匙分别由两名不同的库守同时转动时才会打开。每把钥匙固定由一人保管，单人操作不能启动。”
>
> **第 19 章，第 4 段：**“乔青禾独自走到门前，拧动东钥匙。西钥匙还挂在值班室墙上。锁舌缩回，门向内滑开。”

搜索“两把钥匙”“库守”“西钥匙”“备用”“授权”“应急”和“远程”等词后，第 3–19 章没有找到规则变化、单人模式或例外条件。报告行可以这样写：

| ID | 状态 | 类型 | 严重度 | 前提/规则 | 触发事件 | 表面冲突 | 需要作者裁决的问题 | 后续复查 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-01 | 证据支持的候选 | 规则 | 暂定 S1 | 第3章¶12：两名库守分别转动两把钥匙；单人不能启动 | 第19章¶4：乔青禾独自用东钥匙开门，西钥匙留在墙上 | 正文事件没有满足明示的双人、双钥匙条件 | 第19章是否要揭示一个适用于此情形的例外？例外的条件和证据在哪里？ | 后续所有档案库进入、钥匙归属、知情人与影响主线的结果 |

两端引文互相冲突，且限定范围内没有找到适用例外，因此可以记为“证据支持的候选”；由于它直接触及世界规则，暂按 S1 排在前面。作者仍要判断这是不是有意揭示。如果确有例外，只有当正文说明的条件适用于第 19 章这次开启时，才可以排除该项；同时记录适用边界、知情人和证据位置，再检查后文是否一致使用。若作者确认是失误，由作者裁定要保留哪条事实并批准修改。改完后从第 19 章向后搜索档案库访问、钥匙持有人、谁知道这次开启、谁因此受益或被怀疑，直到下游引用都与裁决一致。
body.en:
The archive excerpts and audit result below are original to this page. Assume the review covers Chapters 3–19.

> **Chapter 3, paragraph 12:** “The sealed archive opens only when two different keepers turn the east and west keys at the same time. Each key stays with its assigned keeper; one person cannot operate the lock alone.”
>
> **Chapter 19, paragraph 4:** “Qiao Qinghe approached alone and turned the east key. The west key still hung on the wall in the duty room. The bolts slid back, and the door opened inward.”

Searches for “both keys,” “keeper,” “west key,” “spare,” “authorization,” “emergency,” and “remote” find no rule change, single-person mode, or applicable exception in Chapters 3–19. The report row can read:

| ID | Status | Type | Severity | Premise/rule | Trigger | Apparent contradiction | Question for author | Downstream check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-01 | Evidence-supported candidate | Rule | Provisional S1 | Ch. 3 ¶12: two keepers turn two keys; one person cannot operate the lock | Ch. 19 ¶4: Qiao Qinghe opens it alone with the east key while the west key remains on the wall | The event does not meet the stated two-person, two-key conditions | Is Chapter 19 meant to reveal an exception that applies here? Where are its conditions and evidence? | All later archive entries, key custody, informed characters, and main-story consequences |

The two quotations conflict, and no applicable exception appears in the defined range, so this can be recorded as an evidence-supported candidate. Because it directly touches a world rule, it receives provisional S1 priority. The author still decides whether the passage intentionally reveals an exception. Clear the item only if the text shows an exception whose conditions apply to this opening; record its boundary, informed characters, and evidence location, then check later uses. If the author confirms an error, the author chooses which fact remains and approves the change. After revision, search forward from Chapter 19 for archive access, key custody, who knows about the opening, who benefits or becomes suspect, and any downstream consequence until each later reference agrees with the ruling.

heading.zh: 可复制的只读审计提示词与改后复查
heading.en: A copyable read-only audit prompt and follow-through check

body.zh:
下面的提示词把 AI 限制在取证与报告，不让它顺手代写。

> 对我提供的小说正文与参考材料做只读一致性审计。范围：〔章节/文件〕。先搜索人物名与别名、地点、物件、规则术语、日期、数量、限制和代价，再检查实体、规则、时间线、因果、代价和明文事实。不要改写正文，不评价文笔、人物弧线或情节好坏，不补设定，不提出创意方案，不修改任何文件或运行会产生副作用的命令，只输出审计报告。每条候选必须给出：ID、证据状态、类型、按项目统一口径标注的严重度、前提/规则的精确位置与短引文、触发事件的精确位置与短引文、表面冲突、可能的例外或缺失证据、待作者裁决的问题、受影响的后续章节。缺少任一端引文时标“证据不足”；只有当正文能证明某项例外的条件适用于当前触发事件时，才标“已排除”并引用该例外及其适用依据；否则仍保留为候选或证据不足。严重度按 S1 主线/规则/读者信任、S2 重大章节影响、S3 局部问题、S4 建议项排序，严重度不代替证据判断。把结论写成待作者裁决项。材料：〔粘贴或附上正文与参考文件〕

作者裁决并获准改稿后，再做一次定向复查：

- [ ] 裁决选定的事实、规则或例外有唯一清楚的表述
- [ ] 触发场景所需条件、权限和代价已经对齐
- [ ] 后续章节的人物知识、物件状态、关系和行动后果同步更新
- [ ] 删除或移动场景后，后文没有引用已不存在的原因、线索或承诺
- [ ] 新增例外没有被无成本扩大到其他人物或场景
- [ ] 报告中的每条关闭项都能引用改后正文，而不是只引用作者说明

复查范围沿因果链走，不只看被改的那一段。章节改动若改变了谁知道什么、谁持有什么或哪条规则可用，就一直查到最后一次依赖该状态的章节。
body.en:
This prompt confines the AI to evidence collection and reporting rather than an unrequested rewrite.

> Run a read-only consistency audit on the fiction and reference material I supply. Scope: [chapters/files]. Search names and aliases, places, objects, rule terms, dates, quantities, limits, and costs first. Then check entity, rule, timeline, causal, cost, and explicit-fact conflicts. Do not rewrite the prose, judge prose quality, evaluate character arcs or plot quality, invent setting facts, offer creative solutions, modify any file, or run side-effecting commands. Output only the audit report. Every candidate must include: ID, evidence status, type, severity using the project-wide rubric, exact location and short quotation for the premise/rule, exact location and short quotation for the trigger, apparent contradiction, possible exception or missing evidence, question for the author, and affected later chapters. If either side lacks a quotation, mark Insufficient evidence. Mark Cleared only when the text establishes an exception whose conditions apply to this trigger, citing both the exception and its applicability; otherwise retain the candidate or mark it Insufficient evidence. Order severity as S1 main-story/rule/reader-trust harm, S2 substantial chapter impact, S3 local issue, and S4 advisory; severity does not replace evidence review. Present conclusions as items awaiting the author’s ruling. Material: [paste or attach manuscript and reference files]

After the author rules on a finding and approves a revision, run a focused follow-through check:

- [ ] The selected fact, rule, or exception has one clear expression
- [ ] The trigger scene now matches the required conditions, authority, and cost
- [ ] Later character knowledge, object state, relationships, and consequences reflect the ruling
- [ ] A cut or moved scene leaves no later reference to a cause, clue, or promise that no longer exists
- [ ] A new exception has not expanded without cost to unrelated people or scenes
- [ ] Every closed report item cites revised prose rather than relying only on the author’s explanation

Follow the causal chain beyond the edited paragraph. If a chapter change alters who knows something, who holds something, or which rule applies, continue through the last chapter that depends on that state.

q.zh: AI说小说前后矛盾，却不给章节证据怎么办？
q.en: What if the AI claims a continuity error without chapter evidence?

a.zh: 把它退回“证据不足”，暂不改稿。要求 AI 给出冲突两端的章节、段落或行号和最短必要引文，再搜索适用范围与例外。只找到一端、引用与结论不匹配，或无法在原文复现时，这条就不能升级为证据支持的候选。
a.en: Return it to Insufficient evidence and leave the manuscript unchanged. Ask for the chapter, paragraph or line and the shortest necessary quotation on both sides, then search for scope and exceptions. A claim cannot become an evidence-supported candidate when only one side exists, the quotation does not support the conclusion, or the result cannot be reproduced in the text.

q.zh: 隐藏真相、不可靠叙述或规则例外会被误报吗？
q.en: Can a hidden truth, unreliable account, or rule exception be falsely flagged?

a.zh: 会，所以报告把每条结果当候选。若正文已经给出谎言、伪装、视角限制或例外条件的证据，引用该证据并标“已排除”或“作者已裁决：刻意”。若解释只存在于作者脑中，候选仍需作者决定是否让正文提供足够依据。裁决后继续检查后文的知情范围、适用边界和后果。
a.en: Yes, which is why every result starts as a candidate. If the prose already supports a lie, disguise, viewpoint limit, or exception, cite that support and mark the item Cleared or Author ruled: intentional. If the explanation exists only in the author's intent, the author still decides whether the manuscript needs evidence. Then check later knowledge, scope, and consequences against that ruling.

text.zh: 如果使用项目的 /story-review lean（Codex 用 $story-review lean），先注意它不只是连续性检查：该模式还会运行 story-architect。对本页任务，只把 consistency-checker 中带双端精确引文的事实/连续性项列入审计：前提或规则可引用已提供的设定、细纲或追踪材料，触发事件引用正文；文学或结构建议另行处理，不当作事实矛盾。若要严格只读、只输出这份审计报告，可直接使用上方提示词，并明确不修改文件、不运行有副作用的命令。
text.en: If you use the project’s /story-review lean mode (or $story-review lean in Codex), note that it is broader than a continuity check: it also runs story-architect. For this task, include only consistency-checker items with precise citations on both sides: a premise or rule may cite supplied setting, outline, or tracking material; the triggering event should cite the prose. Handle literary or structural suggestions separately rather than labeling them factual contradictions. For a strictly read-only audit report, use the prompt above and explicitly prohibit file edits and side-effecting commands.

title.en: How to Write a Satisfying Novel Ending
title.zh: 小说结尾怎么写才满足：兑现承诺，也留下余味

seo_title.en: Write a Satisfying Novel Ending
seo_title.zh: 小说结尾怎么写才满足

description.en: Trace the story’s promises, make the final choice cost something, and give the protagonist a concrete new state in the last scene.
description.zh: 从开篇承诺倒推结尾，让最终选择付出代价，并在末场交代主角的新处境。

answer.en: A satisfying ending pays off the story’s main promise, makes the protagonist choose under pressure, and shows what that choice changes. List the questions you opened, decide which must be answered on-page, then let the final scene demonstrate the cost and the new normal.
answer.zh: 满足感来自兑现故事的核心承诺、让主角在压力下作出选择，并展示选择改变了什么。先列出开篇留下的问题，确定哪些必须在正文回答，再用末场呈现代价和新的日常。

heading.en: Trace the Promises You Made
heading.zh: 先盘点故事答应过读者什么

body.en:
Before drafting the last chapters, reread the opening and write down its promises: a mystery to solve, a relationship to repair, a home to protect, or a question about the protagonist’s identity. Mark each as **answer**, **deliberately open**, or **no longer central**. A secondary clue may stay open in a series; the emotional question that drove this book usually needs a clear answer.

For a story about a tenant trying to save a neighborhood bakery, the ending cannot only reveal who bought the building. It should also answer whether the tenant is willing to risk a secure job to keep the shop alive. That is the promise with emotional weight.
body.zh:
开写最后几章前，重读开篇，把它许下的承诺列出来：要解开的谜、要修复的关系、要守住的家，或关于主角身份的问题。逐条标成**回答**、**有意留白**或**已非主线**。系列里的支线谜题可以留着；支撑本书情感体验的核心问题通常需要明确回应。

比如，主角想保住街区面包店，结尾不能只揭晓谁买下了房子，还要回答主角是否愿意放弃稳定工作来承担经营风险。真正有分量的是这个选择。

heading.en: Make the Climax Cost the Protagonist Something
heading.zh: 让高潮选择真的有代价

body.en:
A win feels earned when the protagonist gives up a real option, resource, belief, or relationship to get it. The cost should grow from choices already made, rather than arrive as a random punishment. Ask: what easier path could the protagonist still take, and why can they no longer take it?

In the bakery story, the tenant can expose the landlord’s forged safety report, but doing so also reveals that her brother signed it. The choice protects the shop and strains the family. The ending does not need to make the outcome tragic; it needs to show that the decisive action changed the protagonist’s situation.
body.zh:
主角要放弃一条真实的退路、资源、信念或关系，胜利才显得来之不易。代价应从此前的选择中长出来，而不是临时降下的惩罚。问自己：主角此刻还能走哪条更轻松的路？为什么已经不能再走？

面包店故事里，主角可以揭穿房东伪造的安全报告，却也会暴露哥哥签过字。她保住了店，家人关系却受到冲击。结果不必悲惨，关键是决定性行动确实改变了处境。

heading.en: End on a Changed, Visible State
heading.zh: 用可见的新状态收尾

body.en:
After the climax, give readers enough aftermath to understand the result. Show a changed routine, relationship, responsibility, or piece of public evidence. A short epilogue works when it answers “what is different now?”; it drags when it repeats every victory.

Try drafting the last image before the final paragraph: the tenant unlocks the bakery at dawn with her own name on the lease, while her brother waits outside with the repaired sign. This image can carry the business result and the unresolved family tension at once. Check that its details were prepared earlier.
body.zh:
高潮之后要给读者足够的余波，让结果看得明白。展示日常、关系、责任或公开证据中发生的一项变化。尾声若回答“现在有什么不同”就有用；若逐项重报所有胜利便会拖沓。

可以先设计最后一个画面：天亮时，主角用自己的名字签下租约并打开面包店；哥哥拿着修好的招牌站在门外。这个画面同时交代经营结果和尚未完全修复的亲情。再检查其中细节是否提前铺垫。

q.en: Does every subplot need to be resolved at the ending?
q.zh: 结尾必须把每条支线都解决吗？

a.en: Resolve the subplots that carry this book’s central emotional or causal promises. A smaller thread can remain open if the reader can tell it is intentionally continuing and the main story still lands. Do not leave a core relationship or goal unresolved by accident.
a.zh: 回应承担本书核心情感或因果承诺的支线。较小的线索可以继续开放，但读者应看得出这是有意延续，而且主线已经落地。不要意外遗漏关键关系或目标。

text.en: Use the long-form writing workflow to compare the final chapters with the opening promise, volume outline, and current character state before drafting an epilogue.
text.zh: 用长篇写作流程对照开篇承诺、分卷大纲和人物当前状态，再决定是否需要尾声。

title.en: Show vs. Tell in Fiction: When to Use Each
title.zh: 小说展示还是概述：什么时候该写场景，什么时候该略过

seo_title.en: Show vs. Tell in Fiction

description.en: Choose scene detail for decisions and change; summarize routine, elapsed time, and information the reader needs without replaying.
description.zh: 关键决定写成场景，重复过程和时间跨度用概述带过。

answer.en: Use scene-level showing when readers need to witness a choice, conflict, or emotional turn. Tell or summarize when the event is routine, repeated, or less important than its result. The goal is not to eliminate summary; it is to spend page time where the story changes.
answer.zh: 当读者需要亲眼看见选择、冲突或情绪转折时写成场景；事件重复、例行或结果比过程更重要时，用概述带过。目标不是消灭概述，而是把篇幅留给真正改变故事的地方。

heading.en: Slow Down Where a Choice Changes the Story
heading.zh: 在改变故事的选择处放慢

body.en:
A scene earns its space when something can go differently by the end: the character learns a fact, loses an option, changes a relationship, or commits to a plan. Put the reader close enough to see the pressure and the decision.

Instead of summarizing “Mina argued with the committee and got the permit,” dramatize the moment the chair asks her to remove the wheelchair ramp from the budget. Mina has one minute before the vote. Her answer reveals both her goal and what she will risk. The meeting can still be compressed before and after that hinge.
body.zh:
一场戏值得占篇幅，通常因为结束时出现了不同结果：人物得知事实、失去退路、改变关系或决定采取计划。让读者靠近压力和选择。

与其概述“敏娜和委员会争论后拿到了许可”，不如写出主席要求她从预算中删掉无障碍坡道的瞬间。投票前只剩一分钟，她如何回答，既暴露目标，也暴露愿意承担的风险。转折前后的会议流程仍可压缩。

heading.en: Summarize Repetition and Travel
heading.zh: 概述重复过程与路途

body.en:
Summary is useful when several similar events produce one result. “For the next three mornings, Mina called every contractor; two declined and one offered a cheaper ramp” moves time while preserving the information that changes the choice. Do not stage three identical calls unless each call adds a new obstacle.

You can also summarize travel, routine research, or recovery between major scenes. Keep one concrete detail if it helps the reader feel the passage of time, then return to scene when a new decision becomes possible.
body.zh:
当多次相似事件只产生一个结果时，概述很有效。“接下来的三个早晨，敏娜联系了所有施工队；两家拒绝，一家愿意低价安装坡道。”这句话压缩时间，同时保留影响决定的信息。除非每通电话都增加新阻碍，否则不必写三场相同对话。

路程、例行查资料和重要场景之间的恢复过程也可概述。留一个能让人感到时间流逝的细节，然后在出现新选择时回到场景。

heading.en: Keep Summary Specific to This Character
heading.zh: 让概述仍然属于这个人物

body.en:
A summary can carry voice and judgment. “Mina learned the city’s permit portal has three different definitions of ‘temporary’” tells us what she notices. A neutral calendar report would move time but reveal less.

During revision, underline paragraphs that explain feelings after a scene already showed them. Keep the explanation only if it adds a new interpretation or consequence. If it merely names what the action made clear, cut it and let the action stand.
body.zh:
概述也可以带出人物的观察和判断。“敏娜发现市政许可网站对‘临时’有三种定义。”这句话透露她注意到什么；平铺日期只是在移动时间。

改稿时，标出场景已经表现情绪、后文又解释一次的段落。只有在解释增加了新理解或后果时才留下；若只是给读者已看懂的动作贴标签，就让动作自己成立。

q.en: Is showing always better than telling?
q.zh: 展示一定比概述好吗？

a.en: No. Showing uses more page time and can make a story feel slow when applied to routine events. Choose the form that gives the reader the right information at the right pace; a chapter often needs both.
a.zh: 不是。展示占用更多篇幅，用在例行事件上会拖慢节奏。根据读者需要的信息和节奏选择写法，一章通常两者都需要。

text.en: Use the writing-craft references to decide which beats need a full scene, then use revision passes to remove repeated explanation around those beats.
text.zh: 用写作技法材料判断哪些情节点需要完整场景，再在改稿时删去这些场景周围重复的解释。

title.en: How to Write a Scene That Changes the Story
title.zh: 小说场景怎么写：让目标、阻力和结果都发生变化

seo_title.en: Write a Scene That Changes the Story
seo_title.zh: 小说场景怎么写出变化

description.en: Give a scene a character goal, active resistance, a meaningful choice, and a result that changes the next scene.
description.zh: 给场景安排人物目标、有效阻力、关键选择和能推动下一场的结果。

answer.en: A strong scene starts with a specific goal, meets resistance that forces adjustment, and ends in a result that changes what the character can do next. Before drafting, write one sentence for the goal and one for the ending state. If the second sentence is unchanged, the scene may be setup or repetition rather than a turning scene.
answer.zh: 有力的场景从具体目标开始，遇到迫使人物调整的阻力，并以改变下一步行动条件的结果结束。动笔前各用一句话写清目标和结束状态。如果结束状态毫无变化，这场戏可能只是铺垫或重复，而不是转折场景。

heading.en: Give the Character an Immediate Goal
heading.zh: 先给人物一个眼前目标

body.en:
The scene goal should be playable in the current location and time: get a signature before the office closes, persuade a friend to return a key, or hide a letter before a guest enters. “Find happiness” is too broad to guide the next action.

A clear goal lets the reader understand why the character chooses one tactic over another. It also gives you a way to test every beat: does this action pursue the goal, respond to resistance, or reveal a cost?
body.zh:
场景目标应能在当下的地点和时间里执行：下班前拿到签字、说服朋友归还钥匙，或在客人进门前藏好信。“找到幸福”太宽泛，无法指导下一步行动。

目标清楚，读者才能理解人物为何更换策略；作者也能逐个检查情节点：这个动作是在追目标、应对阻力，还是暴露代价？

heading.en: Make the Resistance Force a New Tactic
heading.zh: 让阻力迫使人物换办法

body.en:
Resistance is more than someone saying no. A locked office, a deadline, a missing document, or a helper with a competing need can narrow the available options. Let each obstacle change the approach rather than repeat the same refusal.

For example, a clerk will not sign without the original receipt. The protagonist can call the landlord, search the public record, or admit that she discarded the receipt. Each route reveals a different cost. Pick the route that best expresses who she is becoming.
body.zh:
阻力不只是有人说“不”。上锁的办公室、截止时间、缺失的文件，或有自己需求的帮手，都能缩小可选方案。每次障碍都应促使人物换策略，而不是重复遭拒。

例如，办事员没有原始收据就不肯签字。主角可以联系房东、查公开档案，也可以承认自己丢掉了收据。每条路都暴露不同代价，选择最能体现人物变化的一条。

heading.en: End with a New Condition for the Next Scene
heading.zh: 用新条件交给下一场

body.en:
Write the ending state as a fact: the permit is signed but the landlord now knows; the friend returns the key but asks for the truth; the letter is safe but the protagonist has missed the train. The next scene should inherit that fact.

After drafting, check the scene’s opening and closing lines. If the character has the same information, options, and relationships at both ends, identify the one beat that needs to change—or combine the scene with its neighbor.
body.zh:
把结束状态写成一条事实：许可签了，但房东已得知此事；朋友还了钥匙，却要求听真话；信保住了，主角却错过了火车。下一场应接住这条事实。

完成后检查场景的首尾：如果人物的信息、选项和关系都没有变化，就找出需要改变的关键动作，或把这场戏与相邻场景合并。

q.en: Can a scene end in failure and still move the plot?
q.zh: 场景以失败结束也能推动剧情吗？

a.en: Yes. A failed attempt can reveal a cost, expose new information, damage a relationship, or remove an option. The result matters when the character cannot simply try the same thing again unchanged.
a.zh: 可以。失败可能暴露代价、带来新信息、损害关系或封死一条路。只要人物不能毫无变化地再试一次，结果就推动了剧情。

text.en: Use the outline workflow to set the scene’s initial and ending states before prose, then update continuity notes when the result changes knowledge, objects, or relationships.
text.zh: 用细纲流程先确定场景起点和结束状态；若结果改变了人物认知、物件归属或关系，再更新连续性记录。

title.en: How to Plan a Novel Series Without Losing Momentum
title.zh: 长篇系列怎么规划：每一卷有回报，也有新问题

seo_title.en: Plan a Novel Series

description.en: Give each book a complete emotional payoff, a larger unresolved question, and a changing protagonist goal that earns the next installment.
description.zh: 让每卷完成一条情感线，再留下升级的问题与主角的新目标。

answer.en: Plan a series as a sequence of complete reading experiences. Each installment needs a central problem that reaches a satisfying result, while the wider conflict changes enough to create a specific next goal. Track what the protagonist knows, wants, and can risk at the end of every book.
answer.zh: 把系列规划成一连串完整的阅读体验：每一卷解决一个核心问题，同时让更大的冲突发生变化，形成具体的下一卷目标。记录每卷结尾主角知道什么、想要什么、愿意承担什么风险。

heading.en: Give Every Book Its Own Payoff
heading.zh: 让每卷都有自己的完成感

body.en:
Write a one-line promise for each book, not just for the whole series. Book one might answer whether the apprentice can earn a place in the archive; book two might ask whether she will expose the archive’s false history. The setting can continue, but the question and emotional result should develop.

If a volume ends only because the page count is up, readers may feel that the story withheld its reward. Close the volume’s main conflict even when the series mystery remains open.
body.zh:
每卷都单独写一句承诺，别只规划整个系列。第一卷可以回答学徒能否进入档案馆；第二卷则追问她是否愿意揭穿档案馆伪造的历史。世界可以延续，但问题和情感结果要发展。

若一卷只是写到字数便结束，读者会觉得回报被扣住。即使系列谜团未解，也要收束本卷的主要冲突。

heading.en: Escalate Through Consequences
heading.zh: 用后果升级，而不是只加更大敌人

body.en:
A larger threat is not the only way to raise stakes. A victory can make the protagonist more visible, place a friend in danger, or force a public position. Let the prior book’s result create the next book’s pressure.

Map three columns for each installment: what the protagonist gains, what that gain costs, and which old strategy no longer works. This keeps escalation connected to character decisions instead of turning every sequel into a louder version of the first.
body.zh:
升级不必只靠更强的敌人。一次胜利可能让主角暴露在公众面前、连累朋友，或迫使她公开站队。让上一卷的结果制造下一卷的压力。

为每卷列三栏：主角获得什么、为此付出什么、哪种旧办法从此失效。这样升级来自人物选择，不会让每部续作都只是把第一部的音量开大。

heading.en: Track the Series State Between Books
heading.zh: 记录卷与卷之间的状态变化

body.en:
Maintain a short series ledger with unresolved questions, established facts, relationship changes, and promises already paid off. Separate confirmed canon from ideas you may still change. Before outlining a new volume, review the ledger and write what the protagonist now believes—not only what is objectively true.

A sequel can surprise readers without contradicting the first book. The reveal should reinterpret evidence already present or introduce a new fact with a clear source; it should not erase a settled cost just to restore the old status quo.
body.zh:
维护一页系列记录，收纳未解问题、已确认事实、关系变化和已兑现的承诺。将正史和仍可调整的想法分开。写新卷前先回顾记录，写出主角现在相信什么，而不只是客观上发生过什么。

续作可以惊喜读者，但不应推翻第一卷。新揭示可以重新解释已有证据，也可以清楚引入新事实；不要为了恢复旧状态而抹掉已结算的代价。

q.en: How much should I outline before publishing the first book?
q.zh: 第一卷发布前需要规划多少？

a.en: Plan the first book’s complete arc and the next installment’s likely pressure point. Record the series-level question and a few possible outcomes, but keep room to revise based on the story and reader response. Do not promise a specific number of books unless you can deliver the middle and ending.
a.zh: 先规划第一卷完整弧线和下一卷可能遇到的压力点，记录系列核心问题及几种可能结果，同时给创作和读者反馈留出调整空间。除非中段和结尾都有把握，否则不要先承诺固定卷数。

text.en: Use the volume workflow and tracking files to carry reader promises, character state, and unresolved questions across installments.
text.zh: 用分卷流程和追踪文件在各卷间传递读者承诺、人物状态和未解问题。

title.en: How to Write Character Backstory That Matters Now
title.zh: 人物前史怎么写才有用：让过去影响眼前选择

seo_title.en: Write Character Backstory

description.en: Choose past events that shape a present strategy, reveal them when the current scene gives them meaning, and avoid biography dumps.
description.zh: 挑选会影响当下策略的往事，在场景需要时揭示，避免整段人物小传。

answer.en: Backstory belongs in a story when it changes how a character reads the present, chooses a tactic, or pays a cost. Give readers only the past detail needed to understand the current action, then let later scenes add context. A full biography is useful for planning; the finished story needs selected evidence.
answer.zh: 当一段过去会改变人物如何理解当下、选择策略或承担代价时，它才值得进入正文。先给读者理解眼前行动所需的信息，再由后续场景补充背景。完整小传可供作者规划，正文只需要经过筛选的线索。

heading.en: Connect a Past Event to a Present Strategy
heading.zh: 把往事连到当下的应对方式

body.en:
Do not stop at “she was betrayed as a child.” Decide what rule she learned from that event: never share credit, keep a spare exit, or test every promise. Then put that strategy under pressure in the current plot.

A character who hides spare keys after a childhood eviction may be sensible in one scene and harmful in another. The backstory becomes story when a friend asks for trust and the character has to choose whether to hand over the key.
body.zh:
不要只写“她小时候被背叛过”。进一步确定她从那件事学会了什么规则：不与人共享功劳、永远留一条退路，或先验证每个承诺。再让当前剧情挑战这条规则。

小时候被赶出家门后总藏备用钥匙，可能让人物在一场戏里谨慎，在另一场戏里伤害关系。当朋友请她信任自己时，她必须决定是否交出钥匙，往事就进入了故事。

heading.en: Reveal Only What the Scene Needs
heading.zh: 只揭示当前场景需要的信息

body.en:
A remembered smell, a sentence the character refuses to say, or an object they will not touch can introduce the past without stopping the scene. Add explanation only when the reader might otherwise misunderstand the action.

Try three passes: first show the present trigger, then give one concrete memory detail, then return to the present decision. If the memory lasts longer than the choice it is supposed to illuminate, shorten it or move the fuller account to a later moment.
body.zh:
气味、人物不肯说出口的一句话，或不愿碰的物件，都能把过去带进场景而不暂停剧情。只有读者可能误解当前行动时，才增加解释。

可以按三步写：先呈现眼前的触发点，再给一个具体记忆细节，最后回到当下选择。如果回忆比它要照亮的决定还长，就缩短，或把完整经历移到之后更合适的时刻。

heading.en: Keep the Full Biography in Your Notes
heading.zh: 完整小传留在作者笔记里

body.en:
For planning, record formative events, dates, relationships, and the character’s interpretation of each event. In the manuscript, reveal those facts selectively. Some past events may never need to appear if they do not affect the character’s choices.

Review each backstory paragraph by asking: what new action, belief, or relationship does this information explain? If the answer is “none,” keep it in the notes rather than asking readers to memorize it.
body.zh:
规划时可以记录关键经历、时间、关系，以及人物如何理解这些经历；写正文时再选择性揭示。若某段往事从不影响选择，它可能无需出现。

逐段追问：这条背景信息解释了什么新行动、信念或关系？若答案是“没有”，就把它留在笔记里，不必要求读者记住。

q.en: Should I reveal a character’s backstory early?
q.zh: 人物前史应该尽早交代吗？

a.en: Reveal the piece that changes the reader’s understanding of the current conflict. The rest can wait until a present choice makes it relevant. Early disclosure is useful when it creates a question; it is not required simply because the author knows the answer.
a.zh: 先揭示会改变读者对当前冲突理解的部分，其余等到当下选择让它变得相关时再写。早期披露若能引出问题就有价值；作者知道答案，不代表读者必须立刻听完。

text.en: Use the character design and emotional arc references to record formative events as causes of present strategies, then reveal only the parts the current chapter needs.
text.zh: 用人物设计和情绪弧线资料把关键经历记录为当下策略的成因，再只在章节需要时揭示相关部分。

title.en: How to Write Believable Character Motivation
title.zh: 人物动机怎么写可信：把需要变成眼前选择

seo_title.en: Believable Character Motivation

description.en: Connect a character’s immediate goal to a deeper need, a concrete fear, and a choice that costs them something.
description.zh: 把眼前目标连到深层需要、具体恐惧和必须付出代价的选择。

answer.en: A believable motive links what a character wants right now to what they fear, need, or believe. Make the link visible through a choice with a cost. A short explanation can help, but repeated claims like “she wanted success” cannot replace behavior that proves what she will risk for it.
answer.zh: 可信的动机把人物眼前想要的东西，连到其恐惧、需要或信念。让两者之间的联系通过有代价的选择显现。简短解释可以辅助，但反复说“她想成功”不能替代行动证据。

heading.en: Separate the Immediate Want from the Deeper Need
heading.zh: 区分眼前目标和深层需要

body.en:
The want is the task: win the audition, keep the family shop, get an apology. The need is the change that would make the task meaningful: trust a collaborator, accept help, or stop measuring worth by approval. A character does not need to understand the need at the start.

Write both in plain language. Then put them in conflict. An actor may want the lead role but need to admit that a friend’s stronger performance deserves the part. The story begins when the easy route to the want threatens the deeper need.
body.zh:
“想要”是具体任务：拿到试镜角色、保住家里的店、得到道歉。“需要”是让任务有意义的改变：信任合作者、接受帮助，或不再用认可衡量自我价值。人物开篇时不必理解自己的需要。

用朴素的话分别写下两者，再让它们发生冲突。演员想拿主角，却需要承认朋友演得更好。故事在追求目标的捷径威胁到深层需要时开始。

heading.en: Make the Motive Visible Through Cost
heading.zh: 让动机通过代价变得可见

body.en:
A motive becomes convincing when the character gives up time, comfort, status, money, or a relationship. Choose a cost that matches the thing they fear losing. If she fears being seen as unreliable, she may work through the night rather than admit that the schedule is impossible.

Use a ladder of choices: first a small sacrifice, then a riskier one, then the choice that exposes the motive to another person. Each step should follow from the previous result, not from an author suddenly explaining the character.
body.zh:
人物愿意放弃时间、安逸、地位、金钱或关系，动机才有说服力。代价应对应她害怕失去的东西。若她怕别人认为自己不可靠，她可能熬夜硬撑，而不肯承认工期根本不可能。

把选择排成阶梯：先是小牺牲，再是更大的风险，最后是会让别人看见真实动机的决定。每一步都应来自上一结果，而不是作者突然补一段解释。

heading.en: Test the Motive Under Pressure
heading.zh: 在压力下检验动机

body.en:
Ask what the character does when two important values cannot both be protected. This is more revealing than asking what they say they value. If loyalty and fairness collide, whom do they disappoint? What explanation do they offer afterward, and does their later behavior support it?

When an action feels unbelievable, keep the action and check for missing setup: a fear, dependency, deadline, or mistaken belief may explain it. Add the smallest earlier beat that makes the choice legible; do not add a speech that explains away every contradiction.
body.zh:
当人物无法同时保护两种重要价值时，观察他们怎么做。这比问他们口头上重视什么更能揭示动机。忠诚与公平冲突时，他们会让谁失望？事后如何解释？后续行动是否支持这套解释？

行为显得不可信时，先检查是否缺少铺垫：恐惧、依赖、截止时间或错误信念都可能解释它。只补足让选择可理解的最小线索，不要加一段把所有矛盾都解释掉的演讲。

q.en: Can a character have more than one motivation?
q.zh: 人物可以同时有多个动机吗？

a.en: Yes. Give the scene one immediate priority, while letting competing motives shape tactics and hesitation. Readers can follow complexity when they can see which choice is urgent now.
a.zh: 可以。让场景有一个眼前优先目标，同时让其他动机影响策略和犹豫。只要读者看得出此刻最紧急的选择，就能跟上复杂性。

text.en: Use the character design references to connect wants, fears, and choices; update the character state after a costly decision.
text.zh: 用人物设计资料连接目标、恐惧与选择；在人物作出有代价的决定后更新其状态。

title.en: How to Write Natural Dialogue in Fiction
title.zh: 小说对白怎么写自然：让每句话带着目的

seo_title.en: Write Natural Fiction Dialogue

description.en: Give each speaker a private goal, let them respond to what was actually said, and cut lines that only explain known facts.
description.zh: 给说话人各自的目的，让回答回应对方刚说的话，删掉只复述已知信息的台词。

answer.en: Natural dialogue is not a transcript of everyday speech. It is a shaped exchange in which each speaker wants something, hears the other imperfectly, and adjusts. Draft for intention and change first; then read aloud to remove lines that sound explanatory, interchangeable, or too polished for the moment.
answer.zh: 自然对白不是日常谈话的逐字记录，而是经过组织的交锋：每个人都想得到什么，对对方的话也未必全盘接受，并会调整策略。先写意图和变化，再朗读删掉解释感过重、谁说都一样或过于工整的句子。

heading.en: Give Every Speaker a Private Purpose
heading.zh: 给每个说话人一个私下目的

body.en:
Before writing a conversation, note what each person wants from the other: permission, reassurance, information, distance, or a chance to change the subject. Their spoken words can pursue that goal indirectly.

A daughter asking “Did you keep the blue folder?” may actually be checking whether her mother saved the eviction papers. If the scene is only about exchanging facts, make the question carry a relationship risk or cut the exchange.
body.zh:
写对话前，记下双方各自想从对方那里得到什么：许可、安慰、信息、距离，或转移话题的机会。说出口的话可以绕着目标走。

女儿问“蓝色文件夹你还留着吗”，真正想确认的可能是母亲有没有留下驱逐通知。如果场景只是交换事实，就让问题带上关系风险，否则删掉这轮对话。

heading.en: Write Reactions, Not Prepared Speeches
heading.zh: 写回应，不写互不相干的演讲

body.en:
A convincing reply connects to the previous line, including its omission or tone. Let speakers interrupt, ask a narrower question, answer only one part, or change tactics after hearing a detail. Keep these deviations readable; random non sequiturs do not create subtext.

Try a pass that labels each line with its function: answer, dodge, test, bargain, threaten, comfort, or redirect. If three consecutive lines serve the same purpose without escalation, combine them or let an action carry one beat.
body.zh:
可信的回应会接住上一句，包括对方的停顿或语气。人物可以打断、追问更窄的问题、只答一部分，或在听到细节后换策略。偏离应当看得懂，随机答非所问并不会自动产生潜台词。

给每句台词标功能：回答、回避、试探、交换、威胁、安慰或转移。若连续三句都在做同一件事又没有升级，可合并，或让动作承担其中一个节拍。

heading.en: Read Aloud and Cut the Explanation
heading.zh: 朗读并删去解释性台词

body.en:
Read the exchange aloud at the speed and emotional temperature of the scene. Replace lines you cannot say in one breath only when the character has a reason to speak that way. A polished aphorism can work at a prepared public speech and feel false during a panicked phone call.

Remove dialogue that tells another character something both already know merely for the reader’s benefit. Move essential context into an object, a disagreement about the fact, or a direct question from someone who genuinely lacks it.
body.zh:
按场景的速度和情绪朗读对白。只有当人物确实有理由长篇表达时，才保留读一口气读不完的台词。漂亮格言适合准备好的公开发言，却可能不适合惊慌的电话。

删掉仅为读者介绍背景、而对话双方早已知道的台词。必要信息可以放进物件、人物对事实的争执，或由确实不知情的人直接提问。

q.en: Should I use filler words and interruptions?
q.zh: 对白要加入语气词和打断吗？

a.en: Use them when they reveal hesitation, control, intimacy, or a failed attempt to speak. A transcript full of filler can slow the exchange without adding character. Keep the few disruptions that change how the line lands.
a.zh: 当语气词和打断能表现犹豫、控制、亲密或说不出口时再用。堆满口头禅的逐字记录会拖慢对白，却不一定增加人物感。留下真正改变台词效果的中断。

text.en: Use the dialogue reference to check intention, turn-taking, subtext, and line length in the scene, then revise by reading aloud.
text.zh: 用对白资料检查场景中的意图、轮次、潜台词和句长，再通过朗读改稿。

title.en: How to Avoid Info Dumps in a Novel
title.zh: 小说怎么避免设定堆砌：让信息解决眼前问题

seo_title.en: Avoid Info Dumps in Novels
seo_title.zh: 小说怎么避免设定堆砌

description.en: Keep world details that affect the current choice, reveal the rest through use, and check every explanatory paragraph for a story job.
description.zh: 保留影响当前选择的设定，其余通过使用逐步呈现，并检查解释段落是否推动故事。

answer.en: Readers need enough context to understand the current action, not the whole history of the world at once. Introduce a fact when it changes a decision, blocks a plan, or reshapes a relationship. Keep a note of deferred facts so you can reveal them when a later scene gives them a reason to matter.
answer.zh: 读者只需理解眼前行动所需的信息，不必一次听完整个世界的历史。当一条设定改变决定、挡住计划或重塑关系时，再把它带进正文。暂缓的信息可以留在笔记里，等后续场景为它提供意义。

heading.en: Start with the Reader’s Current Question
heading.zh: 从读者眼下的问题开始

body.en:
At any point, ask what the reader needs to know to understand the next action. If the hero is deciding whether to cross a bridge, the load limit matters now; the bridge guild’s founding story may not.

Write the scene without the background paragraph first. Add only the fact that changes how the action is understood. If a detail does not affect expectation, choice, or consequence in this scene, save it for later or omit it.
body.zh:
随时问：读者理解下一步行动需要知道什么？主角要决定是否过桥时，承重上限现在就重要；桥梁行会的创立史可能不重要。

先不写背景段落，把场景写完。只补充会改变读者如何理解行动的事实。如果某条信息没有影响此场景中的预期、选择或后果，就留待后文或删掉。

heading.en: Attach World Facts to Use and Consequence
heading.zh: 让设定跟使用方式和后果连在一起

body.en:
A custom works better when readers see someone follow or break it. A magic rule is easier to remember when a character pays its cost. A political title matters when it determines who can enter the room.

Instead of pausing to define the village’s guest law, show the innkeeper refusing a traveler because no resident has spoken their name at the door. The character can ask what the rule means after it blocks the plan. The explanation now answers a live question.
body.zh:
读者看到有人遵守或违反习俗时，更容易理解它；角色为魔法规则付出代价时，规则也更容易记住；头衔决定谁能进屋时，政治等级才变得重要。

别停下来定义村里的待客法，写旅店老板拒绝旅客，因为门口没有居民报出他的名字。计划受阻后，角色再追问规则含义，解释就回应了眼前问题。

heading.en: Revise Exposition Paragraph by Paragraph
heading.zh: 逐段检查说明文字

body.en:
Mark each explanatory paragraph with its job: orient the reader, explain a constraint, complicate a choice, or create a question. If you cannot name a job, test deleting it. If the next paragraph becomes confusing, replace the missing detail with one precise sentence.

Watch for several paragraphs that deliver facts without an action, question, or change in viewpoint. Break the passage by returning to what a character notices, misunderstands, or does with the information. The goal is clarity, not hiding every fact.
body.zh:
给每个解释段落标一项工作：定位读者、说明限制、增加选择难度或引出疑问。若说不出它的作用，试着删掉；如果后文难以理解，就用一句准确的话补回必要信息。

留意连续几段只传递事实，却没有行动、问题或视角变化的情况。回到人物注意到、误解或利用信息的过程。目标是清楚，而不是把每项事实都藏起来。

q.en: Is it okay to put worldbuilding in dialogue?
q.zh: 可以通过对白交代世界设定吗？

a.en: Yes, when the speaker has a reason to explain it to this listener and the explanation changes the exchange. If both characters already know the rule, let them disagree about its application instead of reciting it.
a.zh: 可以，但说话人要有理由向这个听者解释，而且说明应改变这轮交谈。若两人都知道规则，就让他们争论如何适用，而非背诵规则。

text.en: Use the worldbuilding and exposition references to tie setting facts to action and constraints; defer unused facts in project notes.
text.zh: 用世界观与信息呈现资料把设定连到行动和限制；暂时用不到的内容留在项目笔记里。

title.en: How to Write a Romance Confession Scene
title.zh: 言情告白场景怎么写：让关系变化落在选择上

seo_title.en: Write a Romance Confession Scene

description.en: Build a confession from earlier trust, give the speaker a specific risk, and let the response change what both characters can do next.
description.zh: 从此前建立的信任出发，让告白者承担具体风险，并让回应改变双方下一步。

answer.en: A confession lands when it grows from the relationship’s history and asks for a real answer. Give the speaker something to risk, then let the other character respond according to their own goal and fear. The scene should change the relationship state, whether the answer is yes, no, or not yet.
answer.zh: 告白若从关系经历中生长出来，并需要一个真实回应，就更有分量。让告白者承担风险，也让对方按自己的目标和恐惧回答。无论回答是接受、拒绝还是暂时不能，这场戏都应改变关系状态。

heading.en: Build Trust Before the Confession
heading.zh: 告白前先建立信任

body.en:
Readers need evidence of why these two people choose one another. Show a small act of reliability, a repaired misunderstanding, or a moment when one respects the other’s boundary. Attraction can start the relationship; trust makes the confession feel earned.

Review the preceding chapters for scenes where care changed a choice. If all intimacy comes from descriptions of appearance or fate, add an interaction in which both characters notice and answer a specific need.
body.zh:
读者需要看到两人为何选择彼此。写一次可靠的小行动、一次修复误会，或一方尊重另一方边界的时刻。吸引力可以开启关系，信任让告白显得来之不易。

回看前文，找出关心曾改变选择的场景。如果亲密只靠外貌描写或命定设定，就补一段互动，让双方注意并回应某个具体需要。

heading.en: Give the Speaker a Real Risk
heading.zh: 让告白者真的有所冒险

body.en:
The risk should fit the relationship: losing a friendship, changing a working partnership, giving up plausible deniability, or revealing a need they usually hide. A dramatic public declaration is not automatically more vulnerable than a quiet one.

Choose a setting that affects the conversation. A missed train gives the speaker a deadline; an empty classroom lets the other person leave. Make the pressure specific without trapping the listener or treating persistence as proof of love.
body.zh:
风险应来自这段关系：失去友谊、改变合作关系、放弃装作无所谓，或暴露平时隐藏的需要。公开大声告白并不一定比私下表达更脆弱。

选择会影响交谈的场景。错过末班车给告白者一个时间限制；空教室则让对方可以离开。压力要具体，但不要把听者困住，也不要把纠缠写成爱的证明。

heading.en: Let the Answer Change the Relationship
heading.zh: 让回应改变关系

body.en:
Write the response as a decision, not only a feeling. “I feel the same” may be followed by a boundary, a practical question, or a request to go slowly. A refusal can still show care while ending the expectation of romance.

After the exchange, name the new state in your outline: dating, friendship with a boundary, a postponed answer, or distance. The next chapter should reflect it in behavior. If both characters speak as though nothing happened, the confession has not yet done its story work.
body.zh:
把回应写成决定，而不只是感觉。“我也喜欢你”后面仍可以有边界、现实问题或慢慢来的请求。拒绝也可以表达关心，同时结束恋爱期待。

在大纲里明确标出新状态：开始交往、有边界的朋友关系、延后答复或暂时拉开距离。下一章的行为要体现变化。如果两人之后说话像什么都没发生，告白还没有完成故事任务。

q.en: Does every romance confession need to succeed?
q.zh: 言情里的告白每次都要成功吗？

a.en: No. A confession can clarify a boundary, expose a mismatch, or give the relationship a new question. It should still produce a change the next scene can build on.
a.zh: 不需要。告白可以明确边界、暴露期待差异，或给关系提出新问题，但仍应产生能推动下一场的新变化。

text.en: Use the emotional arc and dialogue references to make the confession follow established trust, then record the relationship change for later chapters.
text.zh: 用情绪弧线和对白资料让告白承接已建立的信任，再把关系变化记录给后续章节。

title.en: How to Design a Magic System Readers Can Follow
title.zh: 魔法体系怎么设计清楚：先定边界，再让规则影响剧情

seo_title.en: Design a Clear Magic System
seo_title.zh: 魔法体系怎么设计清楚

description.en: Define what magic can do, what it cannot do, and what it costs before using it to solve a major plot problem.
description.zh: 先明确魔法能做什么、不能做什么、代价是什么，再用它解决重大难题。

answer.en: Readers can follow a magic system when its limits and costs are clear before a major payoff depends on them. Decide what magic changes, what it cannot change, how someone learns to use it, and what consequence follows. Reveal rules through choices and failures instead of a glossary of powers.
answer.zh: 只要魔法的边界和代价在关键回报前清楚，读者就能跟上。确定魔法能改变什么、不能改变什么、如何学会使用，以及使用后有什么后果。通过选择和失败揭示规则，而不是给读者一份能力词典。

heading.en: Define What Magic Cannot Do
heading.zh: 先定魔法做不到什么

body.en:
Start with the story problem your magic is meant to shape. Then set a boundary that prevents it from removing every obstacle: healing closes wounds but cannot restore lost memory; a portal moves people but cannot carry living plants; a spell can reveal a lie but not tell why it was spoken.

A limit is useful when it creates a choice. If characters can bypass it with no cost, it is decoration. Write the rule in one sentence and test it against the largest conflict in the outline.
body.zh:
先确定魔法要如何影响故事问题，再设下边界，避免它抹平所有障碍：治疗可以愈合伤口，却不能恢复失去的记忆；传送门能运送人，却带不走活植物；咒语可以揭穿谎言，却不能说明说谎原因。

限制能制造选择时才有用。如果人物毫无代价就绕过去，它只是装饰。用一句话写清规则，再拿大纲里的最大冲突检验。

heading.en: Make the Cost Follow from the Use
heading.zh: 让代价由使用行为产生

body.en:
A cost can consume time, a scarce material, health, social trust, or a future option. Pick a consequence that fits the source of the power and persists long enough to matter. Avoid costs that disappear after a scene unless the scene itself is the payoff.

If a messenger can cross shadows but loses the ability to recognize one familiar face for each crossing, the choice becomes personal. Track the cost across chapters so the character cannot use the ability repeatedly without carrying the established consequence.
body.zh:
代价可以消耗时间、稀缺材料、健康、社会信任或未来选择。选一种与力量来源相符、持续到足以影响剧情的后果。若代价在一场戏后就消失，除非那场戏本身已完成结算，否则它很难令人信服。

信使每穿过一次影子就失去辨认一张熟悉面孔的能力，选择便带有个人分量。跨章节记录代价，避免人物反复使用却不用承担已建立的后果。

heading.en: Teach Rules Through Attempts and Results
heading.zh: 通过尝试与结果让读者学会规则

body.en:
Introduce a rule when a character needs it: show the attempted action, the visible result, and any cost. A second scene can complicate the rule by changing one condition. This gives readers a fair basis for predicting outcomes without halting the plot.

Keep a private rule sheet with confirmed limits, known exceptions, and unresolved questions. Before drafting a clever solution, check whether it was prepared. If a new exception is necessary, name the condition and price on-page rather than adding a broad loophole.
body.zh:
人物需要规则时再介绍：呈现尝试的动作、看得见的结果和代价。第二场戏可以改变一个条件来增加复杂性。读者因此能公平地预测结果，剧情也不用停下来讲课。

作者自己维护一份规则表，记录已确认的边界、已知例外和未决问题。写巧妙解法前先检查是否做过铺垫。若确实要加入新例外，就在正文说明条件和代价，不要开一个宽泛漏洞。

q.en: Do I need to explain every magic rule before the first chapter?
q.zh: 第一章前要解释所有魔法规则吗？

a.en: No. Explain only the rule needed to understand the current action. Keep deeper rules for the scenes where they shape a decision, and make sure readers learn a critical limit before it determines a major outcome.
a.zh: 不需要。先解释理解眼前行动所必需的规则；更深的规则等它影响选择时再出现。关键限制必须在决定重大结果前让读者知道。

text.en: Use the setting and continuity workflow to track confirmed rules, exceptions, and costs before a plot solution relies on them.
text.zh: 用设定和连续性流程记录已确认规则、例外与代价，避免剧情解法依赖未铺垫的设定。

title.en: How to Write a Novel Prologue That Earns Its Place
title.zh: 小说序章怎么写：让它提供正文开篇给不了的信息

seo_title.en: How to Write a Novel Prologue

description.en: Use a prologue only when an earlier event, viewpoint, or scale changes how readers understand chapter one.
description.zh: 只有更早的事件、视角或时间跨度能改变读者对第一章的理解时，才写序章。

answer.en: A prologue earns its place when it gives readers a meaningful lens that the main opening cannot provide: an earlier cause, a different viewpoint, or a glimpse whose meaning will change later. Keep it short enough to create a question, then make chapter one begin the protagonist’s active story.
answer.zh: 序章只有在提供正文开篇无法给出的有效视角时才有必要：更早的成因、不同人物的视角，或之后会改变含义的片段。把它写到能引出问题即可，再让第一章开始主角正在经历的故事。

heading.en: Name the Prologue’s Unique Job
heading.zh: 说清序章独有的作用

body.en:
Write one sentence explaining what readers learn here that they cannot learn in the first chapter. Useful jobs include showing the cost of an old decision, establishing a viewpoint the protagonist cannot access, or setting up a time gap that matters to the plot. “The world is interesting” is not a job.

If the opening chapter can carry the same fact through action, move it there. Starting sooner is valuable only when the earlier moment creates a different question, not when it delays the real story.
body.zh:
用一句话说明读者在序章能知道什么，而第一章无法提供。有效作用包括展示旧决定的代价、呈现主角无法接触的视角，或建立与剧情有关的时间差。“世界观很有趣”不是作用。

若开篇章节能通过行动带出同一事实，就把信息移过去。提早开场只有在引出不同问题时才有价值，不能只用来推迟真正的故事。

heading.en: Orient Readers Without Explaining Everything
heading.zh: 让读者知道身在何处，但别讲完背景

body.en:
Give the prologue a person, a concrete objective, and an immediate pressure. Readers can tolerate missing names or history when they understand what the viewpoint character is trying to do and what may go wrong.

A watchmaker hiding one unfinished clock before an inspection can create curiosity without a page of political history. Add only the detail needed to understand the concealment and its cost. The later chapter can widen the context.
body.zh:
给序章一个人物、一个具体目标和眼前压力。读者可以暂时不知道姓名或历史，只要看得出视角人物要做什么、可能失去什么。

钟表匠在检查前藏起一只未完工的钟，就能引出好奇心，无需先讲一页政治史。只补充理解藏匿行为及其代价所需的信息，后续章节再扩展背景。

heading.en: Make Chapter One Answer or Deepen It
heading.zh: 让第一章回应序章或把它变得更复杂

body.en:
The opening chapter should give the prologue a new relationship to the present. It may reveal who inherited its consequence, repeat an image with a changed meaning, or contradict what the prologue’s viewpoint believed.

Compare the last paragraph of the prologue with the first page of chapter one. If no question, fact, or tension travels between them, test removing the prologue. The novel should not require readers to remember a detached teaser that never affects a choice.
body.zh:
第一章要让序章和当下产生新关系：揭示谁继承了序章的后果、让意象再次出现却含义不同，或推翻序章视角人物曾经的判断。

对照序章最后一段和第一章第一页。如果没有任何问题、事实或张力从前者传到后者，就试着删掉序章。小说不应让读者记住一个从未影响选择的孤立预告。

q.en: How long should a novel prologue be?
q.zh: 小说序章写多长合适？

a.en: Long enough to complete its one job and create a useful question, then stop. There is no fixed page count; compare its length with the opening chapter and cut background that the present story can reveal later.
a.zh: 写到完成一项作用并提出有效问题即可。没有固定页数；可以对照第一章长度，删掉能由正文之后带出的背景。

text.en: Use the opening-design reference to compare the prologue’s promise with chapter one, and retain it only if it changes the reader’s question.
text.zh: 用开篇设计资料比较序章和第一章各自的承诺；只有它改变读者的问题时才保留。

title.en: How to Write a Novel Synopsis That Shows the Whole Story
title.zh: 小说投稿梗概怎么写：讲清主线、转折和结局

seo_title.en: Write a Novel Synopsis

description.en: Summarize the protagonist’s goal, major turns, causal links, and ending in plain language; a synopsis is not a blurb.
description.zh: 用直白文字写清主角目标、主要转折、因果关系和结局；梗概不同于简介。

answer.en: A synopsis lets an editor understand the complete story, including the ending. State who the protagonist is, what they pursue, which decisions change the plan, and how the central conflict resolves. Keep the cause-and-effect chain; remove scene-by-scene detail and promotional questions meant for a blurb.
answer.zh: 梗概让编辑理解完整故事，包括结局。写清主角是谁、追求什么、哪些决定改变了计划，以及核心冲突如何解决。保留因果链，删去逐场复述和简介式的宣传问句。

heading.en: State the Protagonist and the Central Problem
heading.zh: 交代主角和核心问题

body.en:
Open with the protagonist’s situation, goal, and the event that makes the goal urgent. Add the minimum context needed to explain the obstacle. A reader should be able to picture the story’s main line before meeting secondary characters.

For example: “When a coastal town’s only clinic loses its license, new doctor Lin must prove the records were falsified before the next inspection—or return to the city that rejected her.” This introduces character, goal, pressure, and stakes without listing every subplot.
body.zh:
从主角处境、目标以及让目标变得紧迫的事件写起，只补充理解阻碍所需的背景。读者应该先看清主线，再遇见次要人物。

例如：“海边小镇唯一的诊所被吊销执照后，新来的医生林必须在下一次检查前证明记录遭到篡改，否则就要回到曾拒绝她的城市。”这句话同时交代人物、目标、压力和利害，不必罗列支线。

heading.en: Keep the Major Turns and Their Causes
heading.zh: 保留主要转折和转折成因

body.en:
Choose the events that force the protagonist to change tactics: a discovery, a failed attempt, a betrayal, or an irreversible choice. Explain why one event leads to the next. A synopsis that says “then many obstacles arise” hides the story’s design.

Name only the supporting characters whose actions alter the main conflict. Replace detailed dialogue and scene choreography with the decision and consequence. The goal is to prove the plot holds together, not to recreate the reading experience.
body.zh:
挑出迫使主角改变策略的事件：发现、失败、背叛或不可逆的选择，并说明前一件事为何导致后一件事。只说“随后困难不断”会掩盖故事的结构。

只介绍会改变主线冲突的配角。用决定和后果代替详细对白与场面调度。梗概要证明情节因果连贯，不必重现阅读体验。

heading.en: Include the Ending and the Protagonist’s Change
heading.zh: 写出结局和主角的变化

body.en:
Tell how the central conflict ends and what the protagonist chooses. Do not stop at a cliffhanger or say “the rest is revealed in the novel”; an editor needs to evaluate the whole arc.

End with the new condition: what has changed in the world or relationship, and what has the protagonist learned or refused to learn? Keep this concise. A full synopsis is a plot document, not a chapter-by-chapter inventory or a second marketing pitch.
body.zh:
交代核心冲突如何结束，以及主角作了什么选择。不要停在悬念处，也不要说“其余请看正文”；编辑需要判断完整弧线。

最后说明新处境：世界或关系发生了什么变化，主角学到了什么，或拒绝学什么。保持简洁。完整梗概是情节文件，不是章节清单，也不是第二份宣传文案。

q.en: Should I reveal the ending in a submission synopsis?
q.zh: 投稿梗概要透露结局吗？

a.en: Yes. A synopsis is for evaluating the complete story, so include the resolution and its consequence. Keep the suspense for the novel’s readers, not for a professional reviewing the submission.
a.zh: 要。梗概用于评估完整故事，应写出解决方式及后果。悬念留给小说读者，不必留给审核投稿的编辑。

text.en: Use the project setup and outline materials as a factual source, then compress the causal spine into the requested submission length.
text.zh: 用项目设定和大纲作为事实依据，再按投稿要求的篇幅压缩因果主线。

title.en: How to Revise the First Draft of a Novel
title.zh: 小说初稿怎么修改：先看结构，再改句子

seo_title.en: Revise a Novel First Draft

description.en: Review the story’s promise, causality, and character choices before polishing paragraphs, then work through focused revision passes.
description.zh: 先检查故事承诺、因果和人物选择，再润色段落，并按单一目标分轮改稿。

answer.en: Revise from large decisions to small ones. First check whether the draft delivers its main promise and whether each major turn follows from a choice. Repair missing or repeated scenes next; polish sentences only after the structure holds. Keep a change log so revisions do not quietly break later chapters.
answer.zh: 改稿按大问题到小问题推进。先检查初稿是否兑现核心承诺、主要转折是否来自人物选择；再补缺失场景或合并重复段落；结构站稳后才润色句子。记录改动，避免悄悄破坏后续章节。

heading.en: Read for the Whole Story Before Line Editing
heading.zh: 逐句修改前先通读全书

body.en:
On the first pass, do not polish every sentence. Mark where the protagonist’s goal changes, where a plan fails, what each section promises, and whether the ending pays it off. Note confusion without fixing it in the margins immediately.

Make a short revision map: keep, cut, move, expand, or investigate. Attach each note to a reader effect—unclear goal, repeated beat, missing consequence—rather than a vague verdict such as “slow.”
body.zh:
第一轮不要逐句润色。标出主角目标变化处、计划失败处、各部分的承诺，以及结尾是否兑现。先记下疑问，不要马上在页边修补。

做一张简短改稿图：保留、删除、移动、扩写或核查。每条意见都对应一种读者感受——目标不清、情节重复、缺少后果——而不是模糊地写“太慢”。

heading.en: Repair Structure and Causality in Separate Passes
heading.zh: 分轮修复结构与因果

body.en:
Choose one kind of change per pass. A structure pass checks scene order and missing turns. A character pass checks whether actions match established motives. A continuity pass checks knowledge, objects, dates, rules, and costs. Mixing every concern into one edit makes it harder to see what changed.

After moving or deleting a scene, read the chapters that depend on it. Search for a clue, promise, or relationship shift that later scenes still assume. Update the outline and tracking notes when a revision changes a fact.
body.zh:
每轮只处理一类变化。结构轮检查场景顺序和缺失转折；人物轮检查行动是否符合已建立的动机；连续性轮核对认知、物件、日期、规则与代价。一次混改所有问题，很难看清哪里变了。

移动或删除场景后，继续阅读依赖它的章节，查找后文仍假设存在的线索、承诺或关系变化。修改改变事实时，同步更新大纲和追踪记录。

heading.en: Polish Prose After the Story Holds Together
heading.zh: 故事成立后再打磨文字

body.en:
Once the causal structure is stable, revise paragraphs for clarity, rhythm, point of view, and repeated explanation. Read dialogue aloud and compare each scene’s first and last state. Keep a copy of the previous draft before large cuts.

Use a stopping rule: finish the current pass, record remaining questions, and avoid rewriting a settled chapter because of one stylistic preference. If outside feedback changes the story plan, update the map before starting another pass.
body.zh:
因果结构稳定后，再从清晰度、节奏、视角和重复解释改段落。对白要朗读，每场都比较起点和结束状态。大幅删改前保留旧稿副本。

设定停止规则：完成本轮、记下未决问题，不要因一项风格偏好就重写已定稿章节。外部反馈若改变故事方向，先更新改稿图再开始下一轮。

q.en: Should I fix grammar in my first revision pass?
q.zh: 第一轮改稿就要修语法吗？

a.en: Fix an error that blocks comprehension, but postpone routine copyediting until major scenes and the ending are stable. Otherwise you may spend time polishing paragraphs that later move or disappear.
a.zh: 影响理解的错误可以马上修；普通文字校对等主要场景和结局稳定后再做，否则可能精修后来会移动或删除的段落。

text.en: Use the revision workflow to separate structural edits, prose edits, and continuity checks, preserving a clear source draft between passes.
text.zh: 用改稿流程分开结构修改、文字润色和连续性检查，每轮之间保留清晰的原稿版本。

title.en: How to Build a Realistic Daily Writing Routine
title.zh: 怎么建立可持续的写作习惯：让下一步足够清楚

seo_title.en: Build a Daily Writing Routine
seo_title.zh: 怎么建立日常写作习惯

description.en: Set a repeatable time and a small finish line, prepare the next scene before stopping, and review progress without punishing missed days.
description.zh: 固定时段与可完成目标，停笔前准备下一场，并复盘进度而非惩罚断更。

answer.en: A writing routine works when it fits the time and energy you actually have. Choose a repeatable session, define a concrete task small enough to finish, and leave a clear next action for tomorrow. Track completed sessions or scenes as well as word count, so planning and revision count as real progress.
answer.zh: 可持续的写作习惯要适合你实际拥有的时间和精力。选一个容易重复的时段，设定足够小且具体的任务，停笔前写明明天的下一步。除了字数，也记录完成的场次和规划工作。

heading.en: Choose a Session You Can Repeat
heading.zh: 选择能够重复的写作时段

body.en:
Anchor writing to a time or event you can control: after breakfast, during a lunch break, or for 25 minutes before checking messages. A modest routine repeated four times a week beats an ambitious schedule you abandon after one missed day.

Protect the first few minutes from setup work. Open the current outline and chapter, reread the last paragraph, then begin the next action. If you need tools or references, place them within reach before the session starts.
body.zh:
把写作固定在你能控制的时间或事件上：早餐后、午休，或查看消息前的25分钟。每周重复四次的小安排，通常胜过一次断档就放弃的宏大计划。

保护开头几分钟，别全花在准备上。打开当前大纲和章节，重读上一段，然后开始下一步。需要的工具与参考材料提前放好。

heading.en: Set a Finish Line Beyond Word Count
heading.zh: 目标不只设字数

body.en:
