A quest can include travel, investigation, dialogue, and a challenge, but each step should reveal information or change access, trust, risk, or resources. Vary the action when repetition has stopped teaching the player anything.

Show progress with clear feedback: a clue added to the journal, a door unlocked, or an ally agreeing to help. The player should understand why the next objective appeared.
body.zh:
任务可以包括移动、调查、对话和挑战，但每一步都应揭示信息或改变权限、信任、风险、资源。重复动作不再教会玩家任何东西时，就换一种行动。

用清楚反馈展示进度：日志新增线索、门锁打开，或盟友同意帮忙。玩家要知道下一个目标为何出现。

heading.en: Connect the Reward to the Story and Next Choice
heading.zh: 让奖励连到故事和下一项选择

body.en:
Rewards can be items, access, information, relationship change, or a new responsibility. A reward is more satisfying when it answers the effort: the medicine helps one person but consumes supplies needed later.

End the quest with a state change and point toward the next decision. Update dialogue and objectives so the world remembers what the player did.
body.zh:
回报可以是物品、权限、信息、关系变化或新责任。奖励回应付出时更有满足感：药救了一个人，却消耗之后需要的物资。

任务以状态变化收尾，再指向下一项决定。同步更新对白和目标，让世界记得玩家做过什么。

q.en: Does every quest need combat?
q.zh: 每个游戏任务都需要战斗吗？

a.en: No. Investigation, negotiation, exploration, craft, or a relationship decision can make a complete quest when the player’s actions change the state.
a.zh: 不需要。调查、谈判、探索、制作或关系决定，只要玩家行动能改变状态，都能构成完整任务。

text.en: Use game-concept and core-loop planning to connect quest objectives, player actions, feedback, and changed world states.
text.zh: 用游戏概念和核心循环规划连接任务目标、玩家行动、反馈与世界状态变化。

title.en: How to Write an Explainer Video Script
title.zh: 科普讲解视频脚本怎么写：先回答一个问题，再逐步拆解

seo_title.en: Write an Explainer Video Script

description.en: Start with the audience’s question, explain one concept at a time, use examples to make ideas visible, and recap the answer.
description.zh: 从观众问题出发，一次解释一个概念，用例子让抽象内容可见，并在结尾总结答案。

answer.en: An explainer video makes a difficult idea easier to understand by answering one focused question. Define the audience’s starting knowledge, organize the explanation from simple to complex, and pair each concept with a visual example. Use sources for factual claims and remove detail that does not help the viewer understand or act.
answer.zh: 讲解视频通过回答一个聚焦问题，让难懂概念更容易理解。确定观众已有知识，从简单到复杂安排内容，为每个概念配视觉例子。事实性论断要有来源，删掉无助于理解或行动的细节。

heading.en: Define the Audience and One Question
heading.zh: 明确受众和一个核心问题

body.en:
Name who the video is for and what they are trying to understand. “Explain climate” is too broad; “why does a city feel hotter after sunset?” gives you a teachable path.

Write down what the viewer already knows, what term may confuse them, and what they should be able to explain or do afterward. This keeps the script at the right level.
body.zh:
写清视频面向谁、他们想弄懂什么。“解释气候”范围太宽；“为什么城市日落后仍然很热？”则有清楚讲解路径。

记录观众已有知识、可能困惑的术语，以及看完后应能解释或完成什么。这样脚本难度更合适。

heading.en: Move from an Example to the Explanation
heading.zh: 从例子走向解释

body.en:
Open with a recognizable example, then name the idea that explains it. Break the concept into a few steps, define necessary terms at first use, and connect each step to a diagram, demonstration, or comparison.

If an analogy is helpful, state where it stops matching reality. Do not let a memorable comparison become a false explanation.
body.zh:
先用熟悉例子开场，再点出能解释它的概念。把概念拆成几步，首次出现时定义必要术语，并让每步都对应图示、演示或对比。

类比有帮助时，也要说明它不适用的部分。不要让好记的比喻变成错误解释。

heading.en: Check Evidence and the Viewer’s Takeaway
heading.zh: 核对证据与观众收获

body.en:
Keep source links in the working script beside statistics, quotations, and causal claims. Use primary or authoritative material when available, and distinguish a known fact from a simplified model.

At the end, answer the opening question in one clear sentence. Ask a viewer unfamiliar with the topic to summarize the explanation; revise any step they cannot retell.
body.zh:
在工作脚本中把统计数字、引文和因果判断的来源放在旁边。尽可能使用一手或权威资料，并区分已知事实与简化模型。

结尾用一句清楚的话回答开场问题。请不熟悉主题的观众复述解释，再修改他们说不清的步骤。

q.en: How many concepts should one explainer video cover?
q.zh: 一条讲解视频应该涵盖多少概念？

a.en: Cover enough to answer one viewer question. If a second concept needs its own examples and caveats, make it a follow-up video and link the series.
a.zh: 只涵盖回答一个观众问题所需的内容。若第二个概念需要独立例子和限制说明，就做成后续视频并建立系列链接。

text.en: Use research and narration planning to distinguish sourced facts, explanatory examples, and the video’s visual proof.
text.zh: 用资料研究和旁白规划区分来源事实、解释性例子和视频中的视觉证明。

title.en: How to Write a Documentary Video Script from Research
title.zh: 纪录片视频脚本怎么写：用资料证据搭建人物和事件

seo_title.en: Write a Documentary Video Script
seo_title.zh: 纪录片视频脚本怎么写

description.en: Build the narrative from verified events, distinguish records from interpretation, and connect interviews and footage to a clear question.
description.zh: 从核实过的事件搭建叙事，区分记录和解释，并让访谈与素材回应一个清楚问题。

answer.en: A documentary script combines a question, verified evidence, people affected by the events, and images that let viewers examine what happened. Build a source timeline, label what is documented versus inferred, and do not make interview lines carry claims the record cannot support.
answer.zh: 纪录片脚本结合一个问题、核实后的证据、受事件影响的人，以及帮助观众检视事件的画面。先整理来源时间线，标出有记录的事实和推断，不要让访谈替缺乏依据的结论背书。

heading.en: Build a Timeline from Verifiable Sources
heading.zh: 用可核实来源搭建时间线

body.en:
Collect dates, records, interviews, and footage in one research table. For each claim, note who or what supports it, what remains uncertain, and whether another source disagrees.

Separate “the record says” from “this may mean.” That distinction helps narration stay clear and keeps an interpretation from sounding like a proven fact.
body.zh:
把日期、记录、访谈和素材放进同一份研究表。逐条注明论断由谁或什么支持、哪些仍不确定、是否有来源存在分歧。

区分“记录写明”和“这可能意味着”。这能让旁白更清楚，避免把解释说成已证实事实。

heading.en: Find the Human Story Without Forcing a Hero
heading.zh: 找到人物故事，但别强造英雄

body.en:
Identify who made decisions, who lived with the consequences, and whose perspective is missing. A character’s ordinary goal—a safe commute, a stable job, a promised visit—can make a large event legible.

Let interviewees retain their own language and uncertainty. Do not trim a quote in a way that reverses its meaning. If voices conflict, show what each person knows and what the record can verify.
body.zh:
找出谁作了决定、谁承担后果、谁的视角缺席。人物的日常目标——安全通勤、稳定工作、兑现探访承诺——能让宏大事件变得可理解。

保留受访者自己的表达和不确定性，不要剪辑到颠倒原意。若说法冲突，就展示各自知道什么，以及记录能核实什么。

heading.en: Match Narration Claims to Images and Records
heading.zh: 让旁白论断对应画面和记录

body.en:
For every section, decide what viewers can see: an original document, a map, a location, an interview, or a clearly labeled reconstruction. Do not imply archival footage shows an event it merely resembles.

Include uncertainty and corrections where relevant. At the end, state what the evidence establishes and what remains unanswered. A responsible ending can leave questions open without making the whole account vague.
body.zh:
逐段决定观众能看见什么：原始文件、地图、地点、访谈，或明确标注的情景重现。不要暗示相似的档案画面就是当时事件本身。

适当呈现不确定性和更正。结尾说明证据支持了什么，还有哪些问题未解。负责任的结尾可以留下问题，而无需让整体叙述模糊。

q.en: Should a documentary script explain every source on screen?
q.zh: 纪录片脚本需要在画面上解释每个来源吗？

a.en: Provide enough attribution for viewers to identify important records and claims, using on-screen labels or notes where appropriate. Keep fuller source documentation with the production materials.
a.zh: 用适当屏幕标注或说明，让观众能识别重要记录和论断；完整来源文档保留在制作材料中。

text.en: Use research notes and narration mapping to keep claims, sources, interviews, and footage aligned throughout the edit.
text.zh: 用研究笔记和旁白映射让论断、来源、访谈与画面在剪辑中保持对应。

title.en: How to Turn a Case Study into a Clear Video Story
title.zh: 案例视频怎么写成故事：呈现问题、尝试、结果和限制

seo_title.en: Turn a Case Study into a Video Story

description.en: Build a case-study video around the original problem, the decisions made, measurable results, and what the example cannot prove.
description.zh: 围绕原始问题、实际决定、可核实结果及案例不能证明的部分搭建视频。

answer.en: A case-study video should show how a real problem changed through specific decisions, not make a success claim from a highlight reel. Verify the starting conditions, show the process and result, and name important limitations. Get permission for private material and distinguish client quotations from the creator’s conclusions.
answer.zh: 案例视频应展示真实问题如何因具体决定而变化，不能只靠精彩片段宣称成功。核实初始条件，呈现过程和结果，说明重要限制。使用私人材料前取得许可，并区分客户原话与创作者结论。

heading.en: Define the Question the Case Can Answer
heading.zh: 确定案例能回答的问题

body.en:
Choose one question, such as how a small team reduced handoff errors or how a writer revised a stalled opening. Do not imply that one project proves a universal method.

Confirm the baseline: what was happening before, how it was measured, and which conditions shaped the work. If the starting point is an estimate, label it as one.
body.zh:
选择一个问题，例如小团队如何减少交接错误，或作者如何修改停滞的开篇。不要暗示单个案例证明了通用方法。

确认基线：此前发生什么、如何衡量、哪些条件影响了工作。若起始数据只是估算，就清楚标注。

heading.en: Show Decisions and Tradeoffs, Not Only Results
heading.zh: 展示决定和取舍，不只展示结果

body.en:
Select two or three turning decisions and show what alternatives were available. A useful case explains why the team chose one path, what it cost, and what changed afterward.

Use screen recordings, drafts, or interviews as evidence where permitted. Match each narration claim to a visible source and avoid reenacting an unverified event as if it were original footage.
body.zh:
挑出两三个转折决定，说明当时还有哪些选项。有效案例解释团队为何选这条路、付出什么代价、之后改变了什么。

在许可范围内使用屏幕录制、草稿或访谈作证。每条旁白论断都对应可见来源，不要把未经核实的重演当成原始素材。

heading.en: Report Results and Limits Clearly
heading.zh: 清楚说明结果与局限

body.en:
Define how the outcome was measured and over what period. Include a relevant failure or tradeoff so viewers understand what did not improve.

End with what others can try and what depends on this case’s conditions. A useful takeaway is specific and modest; it does not claim every viewer will get the same result.
body.zh:
说明结果如何衡量、覆盖多长时间。纳入相关失败或取舍，让观众知道哪些方面没有改善。

结尾说明别人可以尝试什么，以及哪些效果依赖此案例条件。有用的结论应具体而克制，不承诺所有观众都能得到相同结果。

q.en: Can I use a customer story in a case-study video?
q.zh: 案例视频可以讲客户故事吗？

a.en: Yes, with permission for the names, materials, and claims shown. Confirm that quotes and metrics are accurate and agree on how private or sensitive details will be presented.
a.zh: 可以，但需要对姓名、材料和展示的论断取得许可。核实引文和数据准确，并确认隐私或敏感细节的呈现方式。

text.en: Use source research and narration planning to keep the case timeline, evidence, and interpretation distinct.
text.zh: 用来源研究和旁白规划区分案例时间线、证据和解释。

title.en: How to Turn a Long Video into Short Clips That Stand Alone
title.zh: 长视频怎么剪成短片段：每条保留完整问题和结果

seo_title.en: Turn a Long Video into Short Clips

description.en: Choose moments with a complete point, add only the context needed to understand them, and make each clip’s title match its evidence.
description.zh: 挑选能讲完整观点的片段，补足必要背景，并让标题符合素材证据。

answer.en: A useful short clip carries one complete idea from setup to payoff. Find a moment with a clear question, decision, or result; add enough context for someone who has not seen the full video; and remove pauses that do not aid comprehension. Do not cut a sentence so its meaning changes.
answer.zh: 有效短片段要从铺垫到结果讲完一个完整想法。寻找有明确问题、决定或结果的时刻，为没看过长视频的人补足背景，并删去不助理解的停顿。不要把句子剪到意思改变。

heading.en: Select a Moment with Its Own Beginning and Payoff
heading.zh: 选择有独立开端和回报的时刻

body.en:
Look for a complete explanation, demonstration, disagreement, or decision. A moment that depends on ten minutes of prior context may work poorly as a standalone clip unless you add a brief setup.

Write the clip’s main point in one sentence. If you cannot do that without describing several unrelated sections, choose a narrower moment.
body.zh:
寻找完整解释、演示、分歧或决定。若片段依赖前十分钟背景，单独发布可能难懂；除非补一段简短交代。

用一句话写出片段主旨。若不得不概述多个无关部分才能说清，就选一个更聚焦的时刻。

heading.en: Preserve Context, Meaning, and Speaker Intent
heading.zh: 保留语境、原意和说话者意图

body.en:
Keep the question that prompts the answer, the qualification that limits a claim, and enough of the result to complete the thought. Use captions to clarify names or terms, not to replace context.

Replay the cut with the surrounding source available. Check that edits do not turn uncertainty into certainty or make a response appear to answer a different question.
body.zh:
保留引出回答的问题、限制论断的说明，以及完成意思所需的结果。字幕可解释姓名或术语，不能替代语境。

剪完后对照完整素材回放，确认剪辑没有把不确定改成确定，也没有让回答看似回应另一个问题。

heading.en: Package Each Clip Around What It Delivers
heading.zh: 按片段实际交付来包装

body.en:
Write a title that states the clip’s actual point and add on-screen text only when it helps viewers follow the argument. Keep speaker names, dates, and visual labels readable.

If one long video yields several clips, give each a different takeaway and avoid repeating the same setup. A series can point to the full video, but every clip should still make sense by itself.
body.zh:
标题要说明片段真正的观点，屏幕文字只在有助跟进时添加。说话人姓名、日期和画面标注要读得清。

一条长视频剪出多个片段时，每条都要有不同收获，避免反复铺同一背景。系列可链接完整版，但每条片段仍应独立成立。

q.en: How long should a clip from a long video be?
q.zh: 从长视频剪出的片段应该多长？

a.en: Long enough to preserve its setup and payoff, short enough to remove irrelevant pauses. Let the idea determine the cut and confirm the current platform’s limits before publishing.
a.zh: 长度要足以保留铺垫与结果，也要删掉无关停顿。按内容决定剪辑，并在发布前确认当前平台限制。

text.en: Use the multi-clip editing and title workflow to preserve narrative context, visual evidence, and a distinct takeaway in every cut.
text.zh: 用多片段剪辑和标题流程，让每条剪辑都保留叙事语境、画面证据和独立收获。

title.en: How to Plan a YouTube Video Series Viewers Can Follow
title.zh: YouTube系列视频怎么规划：每集有答案，也有下一步

seo_title.en: Plan a YouTube Video Series

description.en: Give the series one audience goal, make each video answer a complete question, and order episodes so knowledge builds naturally.
description.zh: 为系列设定一个受众目标，让每集完整回答一个问题，并按知识递进安排顺序。

answer.en: Plan a video series around a viewer journey, but make each episode useful on its own. Define what viewers should know or do by the end, give each installment one question, and link episodes through a clear progression. Avoid splitting one answer into several parts only to increase episode count.
answer.zh: 围绕观众的学习或行动路径规划系列，同时确保每集单独有用。定义观众看完应知道或能做什么，让每集回答一个问题，并通过清楚进阶连接各集。不要只为增加集数，把一个答案硬拆开。

heading.en: Define the Outcome for the Whole Series
heading.zh: 定义整个系列的最终收获

body.en:
Choose an audience and a capability: write a first short story, understand a basic editing workflow, or prepare a research-backed recap. Use the outcome to decide what belongs and what should be a separate series.

List the viewer’s likely starting knowledge and the skills they need next. This keeps the series grounded in audience needs rather than the creator’s topic inventory.
body.zh:
选择受众和能力目标：写完第一篇短篇、掌握基础剪辑流程，或准备有来源支撑的解说。根据目标决定哪些内容属于本系列，哪些应另开系列。

列出观众已有知识和下一步所需技能，让系列围绕受众需要，而非创作者的话题清单。

heading.en: Make Each Episode Answer One Complete Question
heading.zh: 让每集回答一个完整问题

body.en:
An episode can set up the next one while still delivering a clear answer. A writing series might cover choosing a premise, outlining a scene, drafting, and revision; each step should have its own example and takeaway.

Avoid ending every episode before the promised method is explained. A preview can invite viewers onward, but it should not withhold the answer they came for.
body.zh:
每集可以引出下一集，同时仍交付明确答案。写作系列可以依次讲选题、场景细纲、起草和修改；每一步都应有自己的例子和收获。

不要每集都在方法讲清前戛然而止。预告能邀请观众继续看，但不能扣住他们本集要的答案。

heading.en: Order Episodes by What Viewers Need Next
heading.zh: 按观众下一步需要安排集数

body.en:
Put prerequisites before advanced decisions, then link backward when an episode uses earlier material. Use consistent titles and a playlist description that explains the sequence.

Review the full run for duplicated introductions and missing transitions. If two episodes answer the same question, combine them or give each a different audience task.
body.zh:
把基础内容放在进阶决策之前；某集引用前文时，再链接回去。使用稳定标题，并在播放列表说明学习顺序。

检查整个系列是否重复开场或缺少衔接。若两集回答同一问题，就合并，或让每集面向不同任务。

q.en: Should viewers watch a YouTube series in order?
q.zh: YouTube系列视频需要按顺序看吗？

a.en: Only when earlier episodes provide necessary background. Otherwise make each entry self-contained and use links or a playlist for viewers who want the full progression.
a.zh: 只有当前集需要此前背景时才必须按序观看。否则让每集独立成立，再为想完整学习的人提供链接或播放列表。

text.en: Use topic research and script planning to order audience questions, preserve complete answers, and connect each installment to the next useful step.
text.zh: 用主题研究与脚本规划排列观众问题，确保答案完整，并连接到下一项有用步骤。

title.en: How to Write a Romance Novel from Meet-Cute to Payoff
title.zh: 言情小说怎么写：让相遇、关系变化和结局互相呼应

seo_title.en: How to Write a Romance Novel

description.en: Build a complete relationship arc, give both leads independent goals, and resolve the emotional promise through choices and change.
description.zh: 为双方安排独立目标和完整关系弧线，用选择与变化兑现情感承诺。

answer.en: A romance novel centers a relationship that changes through choices, conflict, and growing trust. Give both leads goals beyond getting together, create obstacles that test how they treat one another, and make the ending answer the book’s emotional promise. A subplot can deepen the relationship but should not replace it.
answer.zh: 言情小说以一段通过选择、冲突和信任增长而变化的关系为核心。双方都要有恋爱以外的目标，障碍应检验他们如何对待彼此，结局则要回应全书情感承诺。支线可以加深关系，却不能替代关系主线。

heading.en: Define the Relationship Promise
heading.zh: 明确关系承诺

body.en:
Decide what kind of emotional experience the novel offers: learning to trust again, choosing between independence and partnership, or discovering that a familiar rival has changed. This promise guides the opening and ending.

Give the leads a reason to meet and a reason that closeness is difficult. Attraction alone does not sustain a novel; a difference in goals, risk, or assumptions creates decisions.
body.zh:
确定小说提供哪种情感体验：重新学会信任、在独立与伴侣关系间选择，或发现熟悉的对手已经改变。这个承诺要贯穿开篇和结尾。

让主角有相遇理由，也有亲近困难的理由。吸引力不足以支撑长篇；目标、风险或假设的差异才能制造选择。

heading.en: Give Both Leads Independent Goals and Arcs
heading.zh: 给双方独立目标和人物弧线

body.en:
Each lead should act when the other is not present. Their goals may collide with the relationship: one needs to leave town while the other cares for a family business, or both want the same promotion for different reasons.

Track what each person believes about love, what evidence challenges that belief, and what action changes their behavior. Avoid making one lead the prize for the other’s growth.
body.zh:
每位主角在对方不在时也要行动。目标可以与恋情冲突：一人要离开小镇，另一人照顾家族生意；或两人都想晋升，但理由不同。

记录每个人对爱情的看法、挑战这种看法的证据，以及改变行为的行动。别把一位主角写成另一人的成长奖励。

heading.en: Pay Off the Relationship Through a Final Choice
heading.zh: 用最终选择兑现关系变化

body.en:
The ending should show both characters choosing the relationship under the conditions the story established. Address the central obstacle rather than solving it with a declaration alone. A practical agreement, changed boundary, or shared risk can make commitment visible.

Resolve the main couple’s promise clearly. An open question about a future job or family plan can remain, but the book should not leave readers unsure whether the core relationship has changed.
body.zh:
结尾要让双方在故事已建立的条件下选择关系，并回应核心障碍，不能只靠一句告白解决。现实约定、边界变化或共同承担风险，都能让承诺变得可见。

清楚兑现主线恋情承诺。未来工作或家庭计划可以留问号，但读者不应怀疑核心关系是否发生变化。

q.en: Does a romance novel need a happy ending?
q.zh: 言情小说一定要大团圆结局吗？

a.en: Set the ending according to the genre promise and audience expectation. Whatever the outcome, resolve the central relationship arc the book has asked readers to follow.
a.zh: 按类型承诺和受众预期决定结局。无论结果如何，都要回应读者一路追随的核心关系弧线。

text.en: Use relationship and emotional arc references to plan both leads’ goals, turning points, and final choice.
text.zh: 用关系和情绪弧线资料规划双方目标、关系转折与最终选择。

title.en: How to Write a Fantasy Novel with a Clear Story Engine
title.zh: 奇幻小说怎么写：让世界规则推动人物目标和冲突

seo_title.en: How to Write a Fantasy Novel

description.en: Choose a central fantasy promise, connect world rules to the protagonist’s goal, and make every major ability or institution carry consequences.
description.zh: 选定奇幻核心承诺，把世界规则连到主角目标，并让力量或制度产生后果。

answer.en: A fantasy novel combines an imagined world with a character goal readers can follow. Choose the story’s central promise, define only the world rules that shape the conflict, and reveal them through use. Give the protagonist a plan, opposition, and costs that keep magic or lore from solving every problem.
answer.zh: 奇幻小说把想象世界与读者能跟随的人物目标结合。选定故事核心承诺，只定义会塑造冲突的世界规则，并通过使用逐步揭示。让主角拥有计划、阻力和代价，避免魔法或设定解决所有问题。

heading.en: Choose a Fantasy Promise Readers Can Name
heading.zh: 选择读者说得出的奇幻承诺

body.en:
Decide whether readers are following a dangerous journey, a succession struggle, a school mystery, or a community defending its home. This promise helps you decide which parts of the world deserve attention.

Write the protagonist’s concrete goal beside the fantasy element. “Restore the river before the harvest” is easier to dramatize than “save the realm” unless the realm’s danger affects a character we know.
body.zh:
确定读者要跟随危险旅程、继承权斗争、校园谜案，还是社区守护家园。核心承诺能帮助筛选值得描写的世界部分。

把主角的具体目标和奇幻设定放在一起。“收获季前恢复河流”比“拯救王国”更容易写成行动，除非王国危机正影响熟悉的人物。

heading.en: Connect World Rules to the Main Conflict
heading.zh: 让世界规则连到主要冲突

body.en:
Rules about magic, class, travel, or inheritance should affect who can act and at what cost. Show a rule when a character relies on it, breaks it, or pays for it.

Keep a private reference sheet with limits and exceptions. Before using a new ability to solve a crisis, check that readers know its conditions and that it does not cancel an earlier cost.
body.zh:
魔法、阶层、交通或继承规则应影响谁能行动、要付什么代价。人物依赖、违反或为规则付费时，再展现它。

作者维护包含边界与例外的参考表。使用新能力解危机前，确认读者已知道条件，而且它没有抵消先前代价。

heading.en: Balance World Discovery with Character Change
heading.zh: 平衡世界探索和人物变化

body.en:
Let each new location, creature, or institution complicate a choice. A market may offer a forbidden tool but require exposing a friend; a border crossing may test the protagonist’s loyalty.

Cut details that do not change expectation, action, or consequence. The imagined world feels large when characters move through it and face tradeoffs, not when the book lists everything the author invented.
body.zh:
让每个新地点、生物或制度增加选择难度。市场可能出售违禁工具，却要求暴露朋友；越境可能考验主角忠诚。

删去不会改变预期、行动或后果的细节。人物在世界中行动、面对取舍时，世界才显得辽阔，而不是靠罗列作者想出的设定。

q.en: Should I build the whole fantasy world before writing?
q.zh: 动笔前要把整个奇幻世界搭完吗？

a.en: Build enough to make the opening choices and major constraints coherent. Expand the reference as later chapters create specific questions, and keep established facts separate from ideas still open to change.
a.zh: 先搭建足以支撑开篇选择和主要限制的部分。后续章节提出具体问题时再扩展参考资料，并把已定事实与仍可调整的想法分开。

text.en: Use worldbuilding, outline, and continuity workflows to connect setting rules to scenes, character choices, and later consequences.
text.zh: 用世界观、大纲和连续性流程把设定规则连到场景、人物选择和后续后果。

title.en: How to Write a Science-Fiction Novel from One “What If?”
title.zh: 科幻小说怎么写：从一个“如果”推演人物后果

seo_title.en: How to Write a Science-Fiction Novel

description.en: Start with one speculative change, trace its effects through work and relationships, and build a character story around the consequences.
description.zh: 从一个推想变化出发，追踪它对工作与关系的影响，再用后果搭建人物故事。

answer.en: A science-fiction story begins with a change to the familiar world and follows its consequences for people. Choose one central “what if,” decide what evidence or rule supports it, and ask who benefits, who pays, and what a protagonist wants within that world.
answer.zh: 科幻故事从熟悉世界的一项变化出发，追踪它对人的影响。选一个核心“如果”，明确支持它的证据或规则，再追问谁获益、谁承担代价，以及主角在其中想得到什么。

heading.en: Choose One Speculative Change
heading.zh: 选定一个推想变化

body.en:
Start with a change readers can understand: a city can store memories, an ocean settlement loses outside contact, or a new device makes a scarce resource cheap. Avoid stacking several unrelated inventions before the central question is clear.

Write what remains familiar and what changes. A stable baseline helps readers see the consequences.
body.zh:
从读者能理解的变化开始：城市能够储存记忆、海底聚居地失去外部联系，或新设备让稀缺资源变便宜。核心问题清楚前，别堆叠数项互不相关的发明。

写明哪些保持熟悉、哪些发生改变。稳定基线有助看清后果。

heading.en: Follow Social Effects into One Person’s Life
heading.zh: 把社会影响追到一个人的生活里

body.en:
Ask how the change affects housing, work, health, law, family, or access to information. Choose only effects that shape your protagonist’s decisions. A worldbuilding question becomes plot when someone must act because of it.

If memory can be stored, perhaps a worker must prove which version of an event they remember. The protagonist’s personal goal turns the broad idea into an immediate conflict.
body.zh:
追问变化会怎样影响住房、工作、健康、法律、家庭或信息获取。只保留会塑造主角决定的部分。有人因此必须行动时，世界观问题就变成了剧情。

若记忆可以储存，工人或许必须证明自己记得哪个版本的事件。主角的个人目标让宏大概念落入眼前冲突。

heading.en: Keep the Speculative Premise Consistent
heading.zh: 保持推想前提一致

body.en:
Write the limits, costs, and exceptions that matter to the plot. Do not use technical detail as proof when the story only needs one clear rule. If science is central, distinguish real-world fact from fictional extrapolation in your notes.

Before resolving the climax, check that the solution follows from evidence and rules readers have seen. A clever outcome should reward attention rather than introduce a convenient new capability.
body.zh:
记录影响剧情的限制、代价和例外。故事只需要一条清楚规则时，不要用技术细节充当证明。若科学是核心，笔记中要区分现实事实和虚构推演。

高潮解决问题前，检查答案是否来自读者见过的证据与规则。巧妙结局应奖励注意力，而不是临时发明方便能力。

q.en: Does science fiction need detailed science explanations?
q.zh: 科幻小说需要详细解释科学原理吗？

a.en: Only as much as the plot and reader promise require. Explain the fictional rule clearly and ground any real scientific claim in reliable research; spend the remaining space on choices and consequences.
a.zh: 只需达到剧情和读者承诺所需程度。清楚说明虚构规则，现实科学论断则需可靠研究；其余篇幅留给选择与后果。

text.en: Use premise, setting, and continuity references to define the speculative change and check its consequences across the outline.
text.zh: 用故事前提、设定和连续性资料定义推想变化，并沿大纲检查后果。

title.en: How to Write a Detective Novel with a Proactive Investigator
title.zh: 侦探小说怎么写：让调查者主动追线索，也承担误判后果

seo_title.en: How to Write a Detective Novel

description.en: Give the investigator a reason to pursue the case, build suspects with motives and access, and let evidence drive each change in theory.
description.zh: 给调查者追案理由，安排有动机与机会的嫌疑人，并让证据推动推断变化。

answer.en: A detective novel follows an investigator who turns evidence into choices. Give them a reason to take the case, a method for finding information, and limits that can lead to mistakes. Track what each suspect knows and what evidence changes the working theory before the final explanation.
answer.zh: 侦探小说跟随调查者把证据转化为行动。给侦探接案理由、获取信息的方法，以及可能导致误判的限制。追踪嫌疑人各自所知，以及哪些证据在最终解释前改变了当前推断。

heading.en: Give the Investigator a Reason to Stay on the Case
heading.zh: 给调查者继续追查的理由

body.en:
The investigator may be a professional, a witness, a family member, or someone whose work gives them access. Establish the reason they remain involved when the case becomes difficult.

A personal stake can deepen the investigation, but it should not make the investigator automatically correct. Let evidence challenge their assumptions and give other characters independent knowledge.
body.zh:
调查者可以是职业侦探、目击者、亲属，或因工作具备接触条件的人。要交代案件困难后他们为何仍继续。

私人利害能加深调查，却不代表侦探天然正确。让证据挑战其假设，也让其他人物掌握独立信息。

heading.en: Build Suspects from Motive, Access, and Evidence
heading.zh: 用动机、机会和证据塑造嫌疑人

body.en:
For each suspect, record motive, access, timeline, and something they hide. Their secret may be unrelated to the crime, which creates fair misdirection without making every suspect a caricature.

Plant evidence where the investigator and reader can encounter it. Keep notes on the first interpretation and the final explanation, and make sure the theory changes because of a specific discovery.
body.zh:
逐位记录嫌疑人的动机、接触机会、时间线和隐瞒之事。秘密可以与案件无关，这样既能公平误导，也不会把人人写成漫画式罪犯。

在线索可能被侦探和读者遇见的地方铺证据。记下首次理解和最终解释，并让推断因具体发现而改变。

heading.en: Make the Solution Follow from the Investigation
heading.zh: 让答案来自调查过程

body.en:
The final explanation should account for key clues, opportunity, and motive while addressing plausible alternatives. The investigator may need to revise a mistaken theory on the page.

After naming the culprit, show what the discovery changes for the investigator and affected people. A solved case can still leave a relationship, ethical, or community consequence that gives the ending weight.
body.zh:
最终解释应说明关键线索、机会与动机，并回应可信的替代方案。侦探可能需要在正文中修正先前错误推断。

揭示凶手后，展示发现如何改变调查者及相关人物。案件虽已解决，关系、伦理或社区后果仍能让结尾有分量。

q.en: Should readers know as much as the detective?
q.zh: 读者需要和侦探知道得一样多吗？

a.en: That depends on the reading experience you want. Fair-play mysteries make key evidence available to readers; other detective stories may emphasize suspense or the investigator’s limited access. Be consistent with the promise you make.
a.zh: 取决于你想提供的阅读体验。公平推理会向读者提供关键证据；其他侦探故事可以侧重悬念或调查者的信息限制。保持与开篇承诺一致。

text.en: Use mystery outlining and continuity tracking to connect each theory change to evidence, timeline, and who knows what.
text.zh: 用推理大纲和连续性追踪，把每次推断变化连到证据、时间线和人物认知。

title.en: How to Write Contemporary Fiction That Is More Than Daily Life
title.zh: 当代小说怎么写不流水账：让现实选择不断改变人物关系

seo_title.en: Write Contemporary Fiction

description.en: Choose a current-life pressure, connect it to a personal goal, and make everyday scenes change relationships, work, or identity.
description.zh: 选定当下生活压力并连到个人目标，让日常场景改变关系、工作或身份。

answer.en: Contemporary fiction can draw its momentum from work, family, money, friendship, identity, or change. Choose one pressure that shapes the protagonist’s daily decisions, then make ordinary scenes produce consequences. A story does not need a spectacular premise when relationships and choices keep changing.
answer.zh: 当代小说可以从工作、家庭、金钱、友情、身份或变化中获得动力。选一项塑造主角日常决定的压力，让普通场景产生后果。只要关系与选择持续变化，故事不必依赖惊天设定。

heading.en: Choose a Pressure with a Time or Relationship Limit
heading.zh: 选择带时间或关系限制的压力

body.en:
A deadline, lease renewal, caregiving duty, job change, or family promise can focus a contemporary story. The pressure should connect to someone the protagonist cares about or to an identity they are protecting.

Define what happens if nothing changes. This gives readers a reason to follow daily choices instead of receiving a list of ordinary events.
body.zh:
截止时间、续租、照护责任、换工作或家庭承诺，都能聚焦当代故事。压力要连到主角在乎的人，或他们试图维护的身份。

明确若一切不变会发生什么。读者因此有理由追踪日常选择，而非只看普通事件清单。

heading.en: Make Daily Scenes Change Something
heading.zh: 让日常场景推动变化

body.en:
A commute, meal, work meeting, or school pickup can matter if someone makes a choice, receives new information, or changes a boundary. Keep sensory detail that locates the character and cut routine steps that do not affect the next scene.

Use recurring locations to show change. The same kitchen can feel welcoming, tense, and then empty after a relationship shifts.
body.zh:
通勤、吃饭、工作会议或接孩子，只要有人作出选择、得到新信息或改变边界，就能成为有效场景。保留能定位人物的感官细节，删掉不影响下一场的例行步骤。

用反复出现的地点展示变化。同一间厨房可以随关系变化，先后显得温馨、紧张，最后空荡。

heading.en: Keep the Experience Specific to These Characters
heading.zh: 让经历属于这些具体人物

body.en:
Research details outside your own experience and let characters disagree about what an event means. One person may see a move as opportunity, another as abandonment. Avoid claiming that one family, workplace, or community represents everyone.

At the end, show what the protagonist can now do or admit. Contemporary stories feel complete when a relationship or self-understanding changes, even if daily life continues.
body.zh:
对自己不了解的经历做研究，也让人物对事件含义有不同理解。一人可能把搬家视作机会，另一人觉得被抛下。不要把一个家庭、职场或社区说成所有人的代表。

结尾展示主角如今能做什么或承认什么。即使日常还在继续，只要关系或自我认识变化，当代故事也能有完整感。

q.en: Does contemporary fiction need a dramatic plot twist?
q.zh: 当代小说需要戏剧性反转吗？

a.en: No. A difficult choice, changed relationship, or new understanding can provide the turn. The result should still alter what the protagonist can do next.
a.zh: 不需要。艰难选择、关系变化或新的理解都能形成转折，但结果仍应改变主角下一步能做什么。

text.en: Use scene and character workflows to turn everyday pressures into choices, consequences, and changing relationships.
text.zh: 用场景与人物流程把日常压力转成选择、后果和关系变化。

title.en: How to Write a Short Film Script with a Complete Arc
title.zh: 短片剧本怎么写完整：用一个选择完成一条人物弧线

seo_title.en: How to Write a Short Film Script

description.en: Focus on one urgent situation, a playable goal, limited locations, and an ending that changes the character’s options.
description.zh: 聚焦一个紧迫情境、可执行目标和有限场景，让结尾改变人物选择。

answer.en: A short film script works best when one situation forces a character to make a visible choice. Limit the cast and locations to what the conflict needs, let actions carry information, and end with a changed relationship or condition. A small story can feel complete without explaining the character’s whole life.
answer.zh: 短片剧本最好用一个情境逼人物作出可见选择。角色和地点只保留冲突所需，让行动承载信息，并以关系或处境变化收尾。小故事不必交代人物一生，也能完整。

heading.en: Choose One Situation That Forces a Choice
heading.zh: 选一个能逼出选择的情境

body.en:
A short film may follow a tenant deciding whether to return a lost key, a nurse choosing which message to deliver first, or a sibling hearing a voicemail before a family meeting. The situation should contain pressure that can resolve within the film.

Write the character’s goal and the consequence of failure in one sentence. If the setup needs several pages of backstory, find a more immediate entry point.
body.zh:
短片可以写房客要不要归还捡到的钥匙、护士先传达哪条消息，或手足在家庭会议前听见一段语音。情境应带有能在片长内解决的压力。

用一句话写下人物目标和失败后果。若铺垫需要好几页前史，就寻找更直接的切入口。

heading.en: Write for What the Camera and Actor Can Show
heading.zh: 为镜头和演员能呈现的内容写作

body.en:
Keep action visible and performable: a hand stops above the call button, a receipt is folded into a pocket, a chair is moved away from the table. Let dialogue carry only information or strategy that action cannot show.

Limit locations and speaking roles to what the story needs. Each new location costs screen time and production effort, so make it change the conflict or reveal a new side of the character.
body.zh:
动作要可见、可表演：手停在拨号键上方、收据被折进口袋、椅子被移出餐桌。只有动作无法表达的信息或策略才交给对白。

地点和台词角色只留故事所需。每个新地点都消耗片长和制作精力，因此它要改变冲突或揭示人物新面向。

heading.en: End on a Visible Change
heading.zh: 用可见变化收尾

body.en:
The ending can resolve the choice without answering every question. Show what the character does differently: sends the message, returns the key, or leaves the chair in place. The final image should grow from an earlier detail.

Read the script without camera directions and check that the action still makes sense. Then review the shot plan to confirm the key choice can actually be filmed.
body.zh:
结尾可以解决选择，不必回答每个问题。展示人物做了什么不同的事：发出消息、归还钥匙，或把椅子留在原位。最后画面要从早先细节生长出来。

去掉镜头说明朗读脚本，检查行动是否仍然清楚；再复核拍摄方案，确认关键选择真的拍得出来。

q.en: How many characters should a short film script have?
q.zh: 短片剧本应该有多少角色？

a.en: Use only the characters whose choices create or change the central conflict. A smaller cast gives each relationship more screen time and can simplify production.
a.zh: 只保留会制造或改变核心冲突的角色。角色少一些，每段关系有更多片长，也能简化制作。

text.en: Use script and storyboard workflows to keep visible action, scene changes, and production needs aligned with the short film’s central choice.
text.zh: 用剧本与分镜流程让可见动作、场景变化和制作需求围绕短片核心选择对齐。

title.en: How to Write a Film Trailer Script Without Spoiling the Story
title.zh: 电影预告片脚本怎么写：展示承诺，不提前讲完故事

seo_title.en: Write a Film Trailer Script
seo_title.zh: 电影预告片脚本怎么写

description.en: Choose the film’s audience promise, select images that build a question, and end before the central payoff is revealed.
description.zh: 提炼电影面向观众的承诺，用画面建立问题，并在核心回报揭晓前收住。

answer.en: A trailer script introduces the kind of experience a film offers without summarizing every plot turn. Choose a clear promise, build a sequence of images and lines that raises a question, and stop before the central payoff. Check every title card and sound cue against the footage and release requirements.
answer.zh: 预告片脚本要介绍电影提供的观影体验，而不是复述全部剧情。选定清楚承诺，用画面和台词逐步提出问题，并在核心回报前收住。逐一核对字幕卡、音效与素材及发行要求。

heading.en: Choose the Film’s Audience Promise
heading.zh: 提炼电影给观众的承诺

body.en:
Decide whether the trailer sells a mystery, romance, comedy, spectacle, or emotional journey. Lead with material that honestly represents that experience rather than forcing every genre into one montage.

Write the promise in one line. Use it to select footage and dialogue. A strong shot can be beautiful and still belong to a different film than the one the campaign needs to introduce.
body.zh:
确定预告片要呈现的是悬疑、爱情、喜剧、奇观还是情绪旅程。用诚实代表这种体验的素材开场，不要硬把所有类型塞进一段蒙太奇。

用一句话写下承诺，再据此选画面和对白。镜头再美，也可能不属于这次宣传要介绍的电影。

heading.en: Build a Question Through Images and Sound
heading.zh: 用画面与声音建立问题

body.en:
Arrange footage so each beat adds information or pressure: a familiar place changes, a character notices something, a choice is interrupted, or a sound returns with a new meaning. Use title cards only when they add context.

Mark music, dialogue, effects, and silence on the timeline. A pause before an image can carry more tension than a louder hit.
body.zh:
安排素材逐拍增加信息或压力：熟悉地点发生变化、人物发现异常、选择被打断，或某个声音以新含义重现。字幕卡只在补充背景时使用。

在时间线上标注音乐、对白、音效和静默。画面出现前的停顿，有时比更响的音效更紧张。

heading.en: Protect the Film’s Central Payoff
heading.zh: 保护电影核心回报

body.en:
List reveals, relationships, and outcomes the trailer should not disclose. Use setup images and partial lines to create anticipation, but do not imply a false plot or a scene that does not exist.

Watch the cut with someone unfamiliar with the film. Ask what they expect and whether that expectation is accurate. Revise a misleading sequence even if it makes a more dramatic trailer.
body.zh:
列出预告片不应泄露的揭示、关系和结果。可以用铺垫画面和不完整台词制造期待，但不要暗示并不存在的剧情或场景。

请没看过电影的人观看剪辑，问他们预期是什么、是否准确。即使误导版本更戏剧化，也应修改。

q.en: Should a trailer include dialogue from the film?
q.zh: 预告片应该使用电影原对白吗？

a.en: It can, when the line represents the film and remains accurate in context. Combine lines only if the edit does not change their meaning or imply a conversation that never happened.
a.zh: 可以，但台词要代表电影，并在语境中准确。拼接台词时不能改变含义，也不能暗示不存在的对话。

text.en: Use footage mapping and title-text review to align trailer narration, images, sound, and the film’s actual promise.
text.zh: 用画面映射和屏幕文字检查，让预告旁白、画面、声音与电影真实承诺一致。

title.en: How to Outline a TV Pilot That Sets Up the Series
title.zh: 电视剧试播集大纲怎么写：交代主线，也展示每集引擎

seo_title.en: Outline a TV Pilot

description.en: Introduce the lead, the series conflict, and a repeatable episode engine while giving the pilot its own beginning and payoff.
description.zh: 介绍主角、系列冲突和可重复的单集引擎，同时让试播集拥有完整起承转合。

answer.en: A pilot needs to work as one episode and show why the story can continue. Introduce the protagonist’s goal, establish the world’s central pressure, resolve a first problem, and demonstrate the kind of conflict future episodes can generate. End with a specific new question or commitment.
answer.zh: 试播集既要像一集完整故事，也要展示系列为何能继续。介绍主角目标、建立世界核心压力、解决第一个问题，并示范后续能持续产生哪类冲突。结尾提出具体新问题或承诺。

heading.en: Show What Can Generate Future Episodes
heading.zh: 展示后续各集如何持续生成

body.en:
A series engine is the repeatable source of new problems: a clinic receives a new case, a team investigates each missing record, or a family business faces a different customer crisis. It should grow from the lead’s role and the world’s rules.

Show the engine in action during the pilot. A sentence in the pitch cannot replace an episode that demonstrates how the next story begins.
body.zh:
系列引擎是持续产生新问题的来源：诊所接诊新病例、团队调查每条失踪记录，或家族企业面对不同顾客危机。它应来自主角职责和世界规则。

在试播集里实际展示引擎如何运作。提案里一句话不能替代一集对下一段故事如何开启的演示。

heading.en: Give the Pilot a Complete Problem and Result
heading.zh: 给试播集一个完整问题和结果

body.en:
The episode should answer one urgent question, even if the season conflict remains open. Let a decision lead to a result that changes the protagonist’s status, relationship, or access.

Do not use the pilot only to introduce names and locations. Readers and viewers need a reason to care about the cast before the final tease.
body.zh:
即使季线仍开放，本集也应回答一个紧急问题。让决定带来改变主角身份、关系或权限的结果。

试播集不能只负责介绍姓名和地点。最终悬念前，观众要先有理由关心角色。

heading.en: End with a Specific Next Question
heading.zh: 用具体的下一问收尾

body.en:
The closing beat can reveal a new case, a changed alliance, or a promise the protagonist cannot ignore. The question should arise from the episode’s resolution, not appear as unrelated bait.

Check that the ending previews a repeatable series conflict rather than promising a different show from the one the pilot delivered.
body.zh:
结尾可以揭开新案件、改变阵营，或提出主角无法忽视的承诺。这个问题应从本集解决过程产生，而不是无关的诱饵。

确认结尾预示的是系列会持续发展的冲突，而非承诺一部与试播集完全不同的剧。

q.en: Does a pilot need to end on a cliffhanger?
q.zh: 试播集一定要用悬念结尾吗？

a.en: No. It can end with a result and an inviting next question. A cliffhanger is useful only when it grows from the pilot’s story and the next episode can answer or deepen it.
a.zh: 不必。可以先给结果，再提出吸引人的下一问。悬念只有在来自试播集剧情、且下一集能回应或加深时才有效。

text.en: Use the story-development workflow to define the series engine, pilot goal, episode payoff, and the next recurring source of conflict.
text.zh: 用故事开发流程定义系列引擎、试播集目标、本集回报与后续冲突来源。

title.en: How to Outline a Short-Drama Season with Escalating Episodes
title.zh: 短剧整季大纲怎么写：每集结算一件事，整季升级一条线

seo_title.en: Outline a Short-Drama Season

description.en: Give each episode a result and next task, while the season arc changes relationships, power, and the central question.
description.zh: 让每集有结果和下集任务，同时让整季改变关系、权力和核心问题。

answer.en: Outline a short-drama season on two levels: what each episode resolves and how the larger conflict changes. Give every episode a concrete goal, reversal, and next task. Track the season’s relationship and power shifts so repeated hooks do not reset to the same situation.
answer.zh: 短剧整季要分两层规划：每集解决什么、大冲突如何变化。每集都安排具体目标、反转和下一任务。追踪整季关系与权力的改变，避免钩子反复把故事重置到同一处境。

heading.en: Map the Season’s Central Question and Outcome
heading.zh: 规划整季核心问题与结果

body.en:
Write the season question in a line: can the lead reclaim the family shop without exposing a sibling’s secret? Decide what would count as a complete season answer, even if a later season remains possible.

List the protagonist’s starting power, resources, and relationships. The season should change those facts rather than simply repeat a weekly problem.
body.zh:
用一句话写整季问题：主角能否夺回家族店铺，同时不暴露手足秘密？确定怎样算本季完整回应，即使未来还可能续季。

列出主角开局的权力、资源和关系。整季应改变这些事实，而非只重复每周遇到的问题。

heading.en: Give Each Episode a Result and a New Task
heading.zh: 让每集有结果，也有新任务

body.en:
For every episode, note the immediate goal, the obstacle, the decisive action, and what becomes possible or impossible afterward. The ending hook should grow from that result.

Vary the hook: a new person arrives, a deal expires, evidence changes sides, or a relationship turns. Do not end every episode with the same type of threat.
body.zh:
逐集记录眼前目标、阻碍、决定性行动，以及之后什么变得可能或不可能。结尾钩子要从结果中生长。

变化钩子类型：新人登场、交易到期、证据易手或关系转变。不要每集都用同一种威胁收尾。

heading.en: Track How Power and Relationships Escalate
heading.zh: 追踪权力和关系如何升级

body.en:
Use a season table for who controls the resource, who knows the secret, and who owes whom. Update it after each episode. A victory should shift at least one of these states or reveal a cost.

Mid-season and finale turns should change the plan rather than merely increase volume. At the end, resolve the season promise and leave only a specific next question.
body.zh:
用整季表格记录谁掌控资源、谁知道秘密、谁欠谁人情，并在每集后更新。一次胜利至少要改变其中一项，或揭露一笔代价。

季中和季终转折要改变计划，而不只是加大声量。结尾兑现本季承诺，只留下一个具体的下一问。

q.en: How far ahead should I outline a short-drama season?
q.zh: 短剧整季要提前规划多远？

a.en: Plan the season arc and every episode’s main turn before drafting, then leave room to adjust dialogue and scene execution. Keep a clear record of established facts so revisions do not break later hooks.
a.zh: 起草前先规划整季弧线和每集主要转折，同时给对白与场景执行留调整空间。清楚记录已定事实，避免修改破坏后续钩子。

text.en: Use episode maps and continuity notes to connect each installment’s payoff to the season’s changing relationship and power state.
text.zh: 用分集地图和连续性笔记，把单集回报连到整季关系与权力变化。

title.en: How to Write a Short-Drama Series Pitch Producers Can Evaluate
title.zh: 短剧项目提案怎么写：用一句话讲清人物、引擎和卖点

seo_title.en: Write a Short-Drama Series Pitch

description.en: State the premise, protagonist, repeatable story engine, audience promise, and first-season arc with concrete examples.
description.zh: 用具体内容说明故事前提、主角、持续剧情引擎、受众承诺和首季弧线。

answer.en: A short-drama pitch helps a producer judge what the series is, who drives it, and why episodes can continue. Lead with a concise premise, describe the protagonist and repeatable conflict, then summarize the first season’s change. Separate confirmed production facts from creative options.
answer.zh: 短剧提案要让制作方判断这是什么故事、谁推动它、为何能持续出集。先给简洁前提，介绍主角和可重复冲突，再概述首季变化。已确认的制作事实与创作选项要分开。

heading.en: Write a Specific Logline and Audience Promise
heading.zh: 写出具体的一句话故事和受众承诺

body.en:
Name the protagonist, the situation, the urgent goal, and the pressure. “A woman discovers a secret” is too vague; specify what the secret forces her to risk and what kind of episode conflict follows.

Describe the intended viewer experience in familiar language—romance, revenge, family conflict, or suspense—without inventing labels the audience would not search for.
body.zh:
写清主角、处境、紧急目标和压力。“女人发现秘密”太模糊；要说明秘密迫使她冒什么风险、后续会产生哪种单集冲突。

用观众熟悉的语言说明体验：恋爱、复仇、家庭冲突或悬念；不要自造受众不会搜索的标签。

heading.en: Show the Repeatable Episode Engine
heading.zh: 展示可持续的分集引擎

body.en:
Explain how new episodes arise: a case arrives, a new truth shifts family power, or the protagonist uses one resource to solve a problem and creates another. Give two different episode examples to prove the engine can vary.

A single big twist is not a series engine. Show the ongoing source of choices after that reveal.
body.zh:
说明新一集如何产生：案件到来、新真相改变家庭权力，或主角用一种资源解决问题又制造新问题。给出两个不同单集例子，证明引擎能变化。

一个重大反转不是系列引擎。还要展示揭示之后持续出现的选择来源。

heading.en: Summarize the First Season and State Production Facts
heading.zh: 概述首季，并如实说明制作信息

body.en:
Describe the protagonist’s starting point, two or three major turns, and the season’s payoff. Do not list every episode if the pitch only needs to show the arc.

Include the requested format, episode count, locations, cast needs, and current asset status when known. Mark estimates and open decisions clearly so creative ideas are not mistaken for approved commitments.
body.zh:
说明主角起点、两三个主要转折和首季回报。若提案只需展示整季弧线，就别逐集罗列。

按要求写明形式、集数、地点、角色需求和现有素材状态。明确标注估算和未决事项，避免创意想法被误解为已批准承诺。

q.en: How long should a short-drama pitch be?
q.zh: 短剧提案应该多长？

a.en: Follow the producer’s requested format. If none is given, keep the core pitch concise and attach only the materials needed to evaluate the premise, episode engine, and first-season arc.
a.zh: 按制作方要求的格式提交。若无要求，核心提案保持简洁，只附评估故事前提、分集引擎和首季弧线所需材料。

text.en: Use story development and episode outlining to support the pitch with a tested premise, engine, and season progression.
text.zh: 用故事开发与分集大纲支持提案，提供经过检验的故事前提、引擎与整季推进。

title.en: How to Write a Novel Chapter with Its Own Mini-Arc
title.zh: 小说单章怎么写完整：有眼前目标，也有状态变化

seo_title.en: Write a Complete Novel Chapter

description.en: Give each chapter a local question, a meaningful attempt, and a changed state that feeds the larger story.
description.zh: 为每章设置局部问题、有效尝试和新的结束状态，再连接全书主线。

answer.en: A chapter feels complete when it pursues a local goal, changes something, and leaves the larger story in a different state. It does not need to solve the novel’s main conflict. Give readers a clear question for this installment and make its final beat affect what happens next.
answer.zh: 一章有局部目标、改变了某件事，并让全书进入不同状态时，就会显得完整。它不必解决整本小说的核心冲突。给读者一个本章问题，并让结尾节拍影响下一步。

heading.en: Set a Local Goal for the Chapter
heading.zh: 给本章一个局部目标

body.en:
A chapter goal may be to convince a friend, reach a place, deliver a document, or learn who changed a record. It should be achievable or fail within the chapter, even when the cost carries forward.

State the goal in one line before drafting. If the chapter contains several unrelated objectives, split it or identify the one that changes the main story.
body.zh:
本章目标可以是说服朋友、抵达地点、递交文件，或查明是谁修改记录。无论代价是否延续，都应能在本章内成功或失败。

动笔前用一句话写明目标。若本章包含多个互不相关的目标，就拆开，或找出真正改变主线的那个。

heading.en: Make the Attempt Change Information or Options
heading.zh: 让尝试改变信息或选项

body.en:
The character’s attempt can succeed with a cost, fail while revealing a clue, or change a relationship. A chapter that ends exactly where it began may be intentional, but check whether a decision or new understanding can give it movement.

Track the beginning and ending state: what does the character know, possess, owe, or risk now? This also helps continuity when chapters are drafted out of order.
body.zh:
尝试可以成功但付出代价、失败却发现线索，或改变一段关系。章节结束时处境与开头完全相同并非绝对不行，但要检查是否能通过决定或新认知带来推进。

追踪起点与终点：人物如今知道、拥有、欠下或冒着什么？这也有助于打乱顺序起草时保持连续。

heading.en: Connect the Chapter Payoff to the Larger Story
heading.zh: 让本章回报连接全书

body.en:
The final beat can close the local question and open a consequence: the letter is delivered, but the recipient recognizes the handwriting; the team reaches the station, but the timetable has changed.

Check that the next chapter inherits a fact, task, or relationship change. This creates forward motion without requiring every chapter to end in danger.
body.zh:
结尾节拍可以解决局部问题，再开启后果：信送到了，收件人却认出笔迹；团队抵达车站，却发现时刻表已变。

确认下一章接住一项事实、任务或关系变化。这样故事会前进，而不必每章都以危险收尾。

q.en: Does every novel chapter need a cliffhanger?
q.zh: 小说每章都必须留悬念吗？

a.en: No. A chapter can end with a decision, payoff, image, or emotional shift. Make the ending create a reason to continue, but vary the kind of reason.
a.zh: 不必。章节可以以决定、回报、画面或情绪变化结束。结尾要提供继续阅读的理由，但理由可以多样。

text.en: Use the chapter outline workflow to define local goal, beats, word target, and the changed state that leads into the next chapter.
text.zh: 用章节细纲流程明确局部目标、节拍、字数目标和通往下一章的新状态。

title.en: How Long Should a Novel Chapter Be?
title.zh: 小说一章写多少字：按阅读体验和场景目标决定

seo_title.en: How Long Should a Novel Chapter Be?

description.en: Choose chapter length around the scene’s payoff, reader session, and publishing format instead of chasing one universal word count.
description.zh: 按场景回报、阅读时段和发布形式决定章节长度，不必追求统一字数。

answer.en: There is no single chapter length that fits every novel. End when the chapter has completed its local movement or reached a deliberate pause. Consider the genre, reading platform, release rhythm, and whether a shorter or longer installment gives the scene room to land.
answer.zh: 没有适用于所有小说的统一章节长度。章节完成局部变化或抵达有意设置的停顿点时即可结束。结合类型、阅读平台、发布节奏，以及场景是否需要更多篇幅来决定。

heading.en: Start with the Chapter’s Job
heading.zh: 从章节要完成的工作开始

body.en:
A chapter that stages a confrontation may need room for setup, choice, and aftermath. A brief transition between locations may not. Decide what changes before choosing a target length.

Outline the beats first, then estimate space for each. If the ending arrives before the key choice, expand the scene; if three paragraphs repeat the same result, shorten it.
body.zh:
对峙场景可能需要铺垫、选择和余波的篇幅；地点间的简短过渡则不需要。先决定章节要改变什么，再设字数目标。

先列节拍，再估算篇幅。结尾早于关键选择，就扩展场景；三段重复同一结果，就删短。

heading.en: Consider Reader Session and Publishing Format
heading.zh: 考虑阅读时段和发布形式

body.en:
A chapter read on a phone during a commute may need a different rhythm from a print novel read in longer sittings. Some platforms or contracts set guidance; check the current requirements instead of relying on old advice.

Use a consistent range when it helps readers know what to expect, but allow shorter chapters for a sharp turn and longer ones for a complete set piece.
body.zh:
通勤时在手机上阅读，与坐下来读纸质小说，节奏需求可能不同。平台或合同可能规定篇幅；应查看当前要求，不要照搬旧建议。

读者预期有帮助时，可保持大致稳定的范围；关键转折适合短章，完整大场面也可以稍长。

heading.en: End at a Useful Pause, Not an Arbitrary Count
heading.zh: 在有效停顿处结束，而不是凑字数

body.en:
Read the chapter aloud and mark where attention naturally pauses. A new scene, a decision, a change in knowledge, or a completed emotional beat can provide a clean break.

If you split a long chapter, make both parts feel purposeful. If you join two short ones, ensure the reader can still track time, place, and the change between them.
body.zh:
朗读章节并标出注意力自然停顿的位置。新场景、决定、认知变化或情绪节拍完成，都能形成干净断点。

长章拆开后，两部分都要有作用；短章合并时，仍要让读者看清时间、地点和变化。

q.en: Should all chapters in one novel be the same length?
q.zh: 一本小说的章节都要一样长吗？

a.en: No. A steady average can set expectations, but vary length when scene purpose and reading rhythm call for it. Avoid padding or cutting a scene only to match a number.
a.zh: 不必。平均长度稳定可以建立预期，但应按场景作用和阅读节奏调整。不要只为凑数字而扩写或删减。

text.en: Use chapter planning to set a purpose and word target, then check the finished chapter’s beats and ending before adjusting length.
text.zh: 用章节规划设定作用与字数目标，再检查完成稿的节拍和结尾后调整篇幅。

title.en: How to Write a Strong Opening for Any Novel Chapter
title.zh: 小说每章开头怎么写：先给读者定位，再引出变化

seo_title.en: Write a Strong Chapter Opening

description.en: Orient readers with a character, place, or immediate task, then introduce a question or change that gives the chapter direction.
description.zh: 用人物、地点或眼前任务定位读者，再引出推动章节的问题或变化。

answer.en: A chapter opening should quickly orient the reader and show why this installment begins now. Establish whose scene it is, where they are, and what needs attention; then introduce a changed fact, goal, or tension. Do not repeat the previous ending unless the new viewpoint adds something.
answer.zh: 章节开头要尽快让读者定位，并说明本章为何从此刻开始。交代视角人物、地点和需要关注的事，再引入新事实、目标或张力。除非新视角能补充信息，否则不要复述上一章结尾。

heading.en: Orient the Reader with One or Two Anchors
heading.zh: 用一两项锚点快速定位

body.en:
A name, location, time cue, or ongoing action can tell readers where they are. Choose the detail most relevant to the chapter’s immediate goal rather than giving a full recap.

If several chapters have passed or the viewpoint changes, add a brief reminder of the active question. Avoid explaining the entire plot again.
body.zh:
姓名、地点、时间或正在发生的动作，都能让读者知道身处何处。挑与本章眼前目标最相关的细节，不必全面回顾。

若隔了多章或切换视角，用简短提示提醒当前问题。不要重新讲一遍整个剧情。

heading.en: Introduce a New Pressure or Development
heading.zh: 引入新的压力或进展

body.en:
Begin with a task already underway, a new piece of information, or a choice that cannot wait. The opening need not be loud; it needs direction.

A character sorting receipts can create tension if one date proves the alibi false. A sunrise description can work when it signals a deadline or changed routine. Tie the image to what the character must do.
body.zh:
可以从正在进行的任务、新信息或不能拖延的选择开始。开头不必喧闹，但要有方向。

人物整理收据时发现某个日期推翻了不在场证明，就能产生张力。日出描写若代表截止时间或日常变化，也能有效。让画面连到人物必须做的事。

heading.en: Avoid Repeating Context Readers Already Have
heading.zh: 避免重复读者已掌握的背景

body.en:
Check the previous chapter’s last page and the next chapter’s first page. If both deliver the same reaction or explanation, start later or change the emphasis.

When a reminder is needed, attach it to the current action: the character reaches for the key they lost last chapter. This refreshes context while moving the scene.
body.zh:
对照上一章末页和下一章首页。如果两处都在呈现同一反应或解释，就从更晚处开场，或改变重点。

需要提醒时，把背景连到当前动作：人物伸手去拿上一章弄丢的钥匙。这样既刷新上下文，也推进场景。

q.en: Can a chapter start with description?
q.zh: 章节可以用环境描写开场吗？

a.en: Yes, if the detail establishes mood, location, or a pressure that matters to the scene. Move quickly from description to the character’s attention or action.
a.zh: 可以，只要细节能建立氛围、地点或场景压力。描写后尽快转向人物的注意点或行动。

text.en: Use chapter outlines to specify viewpoint, opening state, and the first change that makes this chapter necessary.
text.zh: 用章节细纲明确视角、开篇状态，以及让本章有必要发生的第一个变化。

title.en: How to End a Novel Chapter Without a Cliffhanger
title.zh: 不靠悬崖式断章怎么结尾：用决定、回报和新问题留读者

seo_title.en: End a Chapter Without a Cliffhanger
seo_title.zh: 不靠悬念怎么结束一章

description.en: Close a local question, reveal the cost of a choice, or leave a new task that gives readers a reason to continue.
description.zh: 解决局部问题、揭示选择代价，或留下新的任务，让读者愿意继续。

answer.en: A chapter can create momentum without stopping in the middle of danger. End on a decision, earned payoff, emotional shift, or a new question that grows from what just happened. Give readers a satisfying beat and a clear reason to turn the page.
answer.zh: 章节不必停在危险正中央，也能保持阅读动力。以决定、应得回报、情绪变化，或刚发生之事引出的新问题收尾。给读者一个完整节拍和继续翻页的理由。

heading.en: Close One Question and Open Another
heading.zh: 解决一个问题，再打开另一个

body.en:
The chapter may answer whether the character found the missing key, then reveal who returned it. This offers closure and curiosity at once.

Make the new question follow from the result. Avoid adding an unrelated threat solely because a quiet ending feels too calm.
body.zh:
本章可以回答人物是否找到钥匙，再揭示是谁还回来的。这样同时提供了收束和好奇。

新问题应从结果自然产生。不要只因安静结尾显得平淡，就硬塞无关威胁。

heading.en: End on a Decision or a Payoff
heading.zh: 以决定或回报收尾

body.en:
A choice can be a strong ending even before the outcome is known: the protagonist sends the message, signs the lease, or leaves the meeting. A payoff can end a chapter with relief while changing the next task.

Use these endings when suspense has already accumulated. Readers continue because they care what the decision means, not only because the page stopped mid-action.
body.zh:
结果尚未揭晓时，决定本身也能成为有力结尾：主角发出消息、签下租约或离开会议。回报也可以给章节一刻释然，同时改变下一项任务。

在悬念已累积时使用这类结尾。读者会因为关心决定意味着什么而继续，而不只是因为动作被截断。

heading.en: Vary the Rhythm of Chapter Endings
heading.zh: 变化章节结尾的节奏

body.en:
Alternate cliffhangers with emotional resolutions, discoveries, promises, and changes in status. A sequence of identical threats can make every ending feel interchangeable.

Review several chapter endings together. Each should offer a distinct reason to continue and connect to the next chapter’s opening without repeating the same beat.
body.zh:
交替使用悬念、情感落点、发现、承诺和身份变化。连续用同一种威胁，会让所有结尾都像一个模子。

把几章结尾放在一起审阅。每个都应提供独特的继续理由，并连接下一章开头，避免重复同一节拍。

q.en: Do chapter endings need to leave an unanswered question?
q.zh: 章节结尾一定要留下未答问题吗？

a.en: No. A resolved emotional beat or satisfying result can create momentum when it changes the character’s next choice. The larger story can carry the open question.
a.zh: 不需要。情绪节拍或结果得到满足后，只要它改变人物下一步选择，同样能推动阅读。未解问题可以留在更大的故事里。

text.en: Use chapter-hook and outline references to vary payoff types while connecting each ending to the next chapter’s task.
text.zh: 用章节钩子和大纲资料变化回报类型，并让结尾连接下一章任务。

title.en: How to Plan a Sustainable Web-Novel Release Schedule
title.zh: 网文更新计划怎么排：用库存、节奏和现实产能来定

seo_title.en: Plan a Web-Novel Release Schedule

description.en: Set a release rhythm around sustainable writing capacity, prepare a buffer, and review progress without sacrificing chapter quality.
description.zh: 按可持续产能安排更新频率、预留库存，并在复盘时保护章节质量。

answer.en: A release schedule should fit the writer’s real production pace and the platform’s current expectations. Estimate how long drafting, revision, and continuity checks take, build a buffer before promising frequent updates, and adjust when life or story complexity changes. Consistency is more useful than an unsustainable streak.
answer.zh: 更新计划要符合作者真实产能和平台当前要求。估算起草、改稿与连续性检查耗时，承诺高频更新前先积累库存，并在生活或剧情复杂度变化时调整。可持续的一致性比无法长期保持的连更更有用。

heading.en: Estimate Drafting, Revision, and Checks Together
heading.zh: 把起草、改稿和检查一起估算

body.en:
Track several normal work sessions, including planning and revision. A daily word count that ignores outlining, source research, and continuity work will overstate what you can publish.

Use your recent average as a starting point, not a permanent target. Leave room for chapters that require heavier research or major scene changes.
body.zh:
记录几次正常工作时段，包括规划和修改。若每日字数不计大纲、资料研究和连续性整理，就会高估可发布产量。

以近期平均作为起点，而非永久目标。为需要大量研究或重写关键场景的章节留余地。

heading.en: Build a Buffer Before Setting a Frequent Cadence
heading.zh: 确定高频更新前先积累库存

body.en:
A buffer absorbs illness, work demands, and revisions that take longer than expected. Decide how many completed chapters you want ready before announcing the schedule.

Check any platform or contract requirements directly because publication policies can change. Do not promise a daily cadence merely because other authors use one.
body.zh:
库存能吸收生病、工作繁忙或修改超时的影响。公开更新计划前，先决定至少要准备多少篇已完成章节。

平台规则或合同要求可能变化，直接核对当前要求。别只因其他作者日更就承诺每天更新。

heading.en: Review the Schedule Without Punishing Yourself
heading.zh: 复盘更新安排，不靠惩罚自己

body.en:
Review on a fixed interval: planned versus completed chapters, average turnaround, and remaining buffer. If the gap stays negative, reduce frequency before quality collapses.

Tell readers about a changed cadence clearly and briefly when needed. Use the time to finish a stronger arc rather than rushing chapters that need repair.
body.zh:
按固定周期复盘：计划与完成章节、平均周转时间、剩余库存。若总是入不敷出，就在质量下滑前降低频率。

需要调整时，清楚简短地告知读者。把时间用于完成更扎实的剧情弧线，别匆忙发布仍需修补的章节。

q.en: How many chapters should I prepare before serializing?
q.zh: 开始连载前要存多少章？

a.en: Prepare enough to cover the buffer you need for research, revision, and expected schedule risks. The right amount depends on your workflow and the platform’s requirements; verify both before announcing dates.
a.zh: 准备足以覆盖资料研究、修改和预期排期风险的库存。具体数量取决于工作流和平台要求；公开日期前先核实两者。

text.en: Use the daily and volume workflows to estimate output, maintain a buffer, and keep revision checks inside the release plan.
text.zh: 用日更与分卷流程估算产能、维护库存，并把改稿检查纳入更新计划。

title.en: How to Write Subtext in Dialogue
title.zh: 小说对白潜台词怎么写：让言外之意影响当下行动

seo_title.en: Write Subtext in Dialogue
seo_title.zh: 小说对白潜台词怎么写

description.en: Give speakers goals they will not state directly, let the words and actions diverge, and make the listener respond to the hidden pressure.
description.zh: 给说话人不愿明说的目标，让话语与行动形成落差，并让听者回应隐含压力。

answer.en: Subtext is the meaning beneath what a character says. It works when the speaker has a reason to avoid a direct statement and the listener has a reason to notice or misread it. Pair the spoken line with an action, omission, or response that lets readers infer what is at stake.
answer.zh: 潜台词是人物话语之下的意思。说话人有理由回避直说，听者也有理由察觉或误解时，潜台词才有作用。把台词与动作、省略或回应配在一起，让读者推断利害。

heading.en: Give the Speaker a Reason to Avoid Saying It
heading.zh: 给说话人回避直说的理由

body.en:
A character may want an apology but fear losing authority, ask about dinner to learn who will come, or offer help to avoid discussing a debt. The hidden goal should matter in this relationship.

Write the direct version first, then decide why the character will not say it. If there is no pressure or risk in being direct, subtext may only make the scene harder to understand.
body.zh:
人物可能想听道歉却怕失去权威，问晚饭是想知道谁会来，或主动帮忙来回避债务。隐藏目标要与这段关系有关。

先写直接说法，再决定人物为何不说。若直说没有压力或风险，潜台词只会让场景更难理解。

heading.en: Pair the Line with a Contrasting Action
heading.zh: 让台词与相反动作并置

body.en:
A person can say “I have plenty of time” while packing a bag, or praise the new paint while keeping a hand over the old nameplate. The action gives evidence without translating the line for readers.

Choose details the viewpoint character could notice. One precise gesture often carries more than a paragraph explaining that the speaker is lying.
body.zh:
人物可以边收拾行李边说“我时间多得很”，或一边夸新油漆一边用手遮住旧门牌。动作提供证据，却不替读者翻译台词。

选视角人物能看到的细节。一个准确动作往往胜过一段解释说话人在撒谎。

heading.en: Let the Listener Interpret or Miss the Meaning
heading.zh: 让听者解读，也允许他们错过

body.en:
The listener may answer the literal question, challenge the implication, or pretend not to hear. Their response reveals what they know and what they are willing to acknowledge.

Do not explain every hidden meaning immediately. Let the consequence of the exchange confirm or complicate the reader’s interpretation in a later beat.
body.zh:
听者可以只答字面问题、指出言外之意，或假装没听见。回应能揭示他们知道什么、愿意承认什么。

不要立刻解释每层隐藏含义。让后续行动确认或复杂化读者的推断。

q.en: Can every line of dialogue have subtext?
q.zh: 每句对白都要有潜台词吗？

a.en: No. Direct speech keeps a scene clear. Use subtext where a relationship, fear, or power difference makes direct language difficult, and vary it with honest lines.
a.zh: 不必。直说能让场景清楚。当关系、恐惧或权力差异使直说困难时再用潜台词，并和坦诚表达交替。

text.en: Use the dialogue mastery references to connect hidden intention, spoken wording, action, and the listener’s response.
text.zh: 用对白写作资料连接隐藏意图、表面措辞、动作和听者回应。

title.en: How to Write an Argument Scene That Changes the Relationship
title.zh: 小说争吵戏怎么写有变化：让双方各有目标和筹码

seo_title.en: Write an Argument Scene

description.en: Give each person a goal, let the dispute escalate through specific evidence, and end with a new boundary or consequence.
description.zh: 给双方不同目标，用具体证据逐步升级分歧，并以新边界或后果收尾。

answer.en: An argument scene needs more than raised voices. Give each person something they want, a different account of what happened, and a reason compromise is difficult. Let the exchange change knowledge, trust, or what the characters will do next.
answer.zh: 争吵戏不只是提高音量。给每个人一个目标、对事件的不同描述，以及难以妥协的理由。让交锋改变认知、信任或下一步行动。

heading.en: Define What Each Person Wants
heading.zh: 分别写清双方想要什么

body.en:
One person may want an apology; the other may want the meeting to continue without admitting fault. Write each goal separately and include what each is afraid will happen if they lose.

The goals can be incompatible without making one character irrational. Readers should understand the pressure on both sides even if the behavior is harmful.
body.zh:
一人可能想要道歉，另一人则想继续会议而不承认错误。分别写下双方目标，以及失去时各自怕发生什么。

目标可以互相冲突，却不必把任何一方写得不讲理。即使行为有害，读者也应理解双方承受的压力。

heading.en: Escalate Through New Evidence and Tactics
heading.zh: 用新证据和新策略升级

body.en:
Let the argument move from the triggering fact to a prior pattern, then to a choice about the present. A new receipt, remembered promise, or interruption can change what the other person can deny.

Vary tactics: ask, accuse, bargain, withdraw, or disclose something risky. Repeating the same accusation in louder words rarely changes the scene.
body.zh:
让争吵从导火索推进到旧模式，再落到当下选择。新收据、想起的承诺或一次打断，都可能改变对方还能否否认。

变化策略：提问、指责、交换条件、退出或透露有风险的信息。把同一句指控越说越大声，很少能改变场景。

heading.en: End with a Boundary, Choice, or Cost
heading.zh: 以边界、选择或代价收尾

body.en:
The scene might end in an agreement, a refusal, a pause, or a character leaving. Make the next action reflect the result. An unresolved argument can still create a clear new boundary.

Avoid settling the conflict with a sudden joke or apology unless the earlier exchange has earned that turn. Give the characters room to carry the disagreement into later scenes.
body.zh:
场景可以以达成协议、拒绝、沉默或离开结束，但下一步行动要体现结果。尚未解决的争执也能建立清楚的新边界。

除非前文铺垫充分，否则不要用突来的玩笑或道歉化解冲突。让分歧继续影响后续场景。

q.en: Should one person win an argument scene?
q.zh: 一场争吵一定要分出谁赢吗？

a.en: No. The useful result may be a boundary, new information, or a cost both must face. Decide what changed, even if neither person gets what they wanted.
a.zh: 不必。有效结果可以是边界、新信息或双方都要面对的代价。即使没人如愿，也要决定发生了什么变化。

text.en: Use conflict and dialogue references to track each speaker’s goal, tactic changes, and the relationship state after the scene.
text.zh: 用冲突与对白资料追踪双方目标、策略变化和场景后的关系状态。

title.en: How to Use Action Beats in Fiction Dialogue
title.zh: 小说对白动作提示怎么写：补充节奏，不重复台词

seo_title.en: Use Action Beats in Dialogue

description.en: Use a brief action to identify the speaker, change the rhythm, or reveal intention; cut gestures that repeat the line’s emotion.
description.zh: 用简短动作标明说话人、调整节奏或显露意图，删掉重复台词情绪的手势。

answer.en: An action beat is a short action placed around dialogue. It can identify who speaks, show a pause, or add meaning that the words alone do not carry. Choose a concrete action with a purpose and avoid assigning a gesture to every line.
answer.zh: 对白动作提示是放在对白前后的简短行动。它能标明说话人、展示停顿，或补充言语没有承载的含义。选择有作用的具体动作，不必每句台词都配一个手势。

heading.en: Give Each Action Beat a Job
heading.zh: 让每个动作提示有一项作用

body.en:
A beat can show a character handing over an object, refusing eye contact, or stopping an activity to listen. The action should change the scene’s focus or reader understanding.

If “she shrugged” appears only to separate two lines, use a clean speaker label or let the reply follow directly.
body.zh:
动作提示可以表现人物递出物件、避开视线，或停下手边工作倾听。行动应改变场景焦点或读者理解。

若“她耸耸肩”只是为了隔开两句对白，可直接用说话人标注，或让回应紧接上一句。

heading.en: Avoid Repeating What the Dialogue Already Says
heading.zh: 避免重复对白已经表达的情绪

body.en:
A line such as “I am furious” followed by a clenched fist may be redundant unless the physical action creates a risk. Pair action with words when they contrast or complicate each other: the character says yes while sliding the unsigned form back.

Use silence and stillness deliberately. A character who stops typing before answering may create more tension than several familiar gestures.
body.zh:
“我很生气”后面再写紧握拳头，可能重复表达，除非动作制造新风险。动作与对白有反差或复杂关系时再并置：人物说“好”，却把未签的表格推回去。

有意使用沉默和静止。人物先停下打字再回答，可能比一连串熟悉手势更紧张。

heading.en: Keep Objects and Movement Continuous
heading.zh: 保持物件和动作连续

body.en:
Track who holds the cup, where the letter sits, and whether someone has left the room. An action beat can establish these facts, but later lines should respect them.

Read the exchange aloud and check whether the beats interrupt the emotional flow. Trim actions that do not help the actor, reader, or continuity.
body.zh:
追踪杯子在谁手里、信放在哪里、人物是否已经离开房间。动作提示可以建立这些事实，后续对白也要尊重它们。

朗读对白，检查动作提示是否打断情绪流。删掉对演员、读者或连续性都无帮助的动作。

q.en: Can an action beat replace a dialogue tag?
q.zh: 动作提示可以替代对白引导语吗？

a.en: Yes, when the action clearly identifies the speaker and belongs to that character. Do not attach an action to the wrong person or use an unrelated gesture just to avoid “said.”
a.zh: 可以，只要动作明确标出说话人，且确实属于该角色。不要把动作挂错人，也别只为避免使用“说”而加无关手势。

text.en: Use dialogue craft references to balance speaker identification, physical action, silence, and line rhythm.
text.zh: 用对白技法资料平衡说话人辨识、身体动作、沉默和台词节奏。

title.en: How to Write an Apology Scene That Feels Real
title.zh: 小说道歉场景怎么写真实：承认具体伤害，也接受对方反应

seo_title.en: Write a Realistic Apology Scene

description.en: Name the action and harm, avoid demanding forgiveness, and let changed behavior continue after the conversation.
description.zh: 说清行为和伤害，不索取原谅，并让改正持续到谈话之后。

answer.en: A believable apology identifies what happened, acknowledges its effect, and offers repair without demanding immediate forgiveness. The harmed character gets to respond, set a boundary, or decline. Later behavior—not the speech alone—shows whether the apology changes the relationship.
answer.zh: 可信的道歉会指出发生了什么、承认造成的影响，并提出修复方式，而不要求对方立刻原谅。受伤者有权回应、设边界或拒绝。之后的行为而非这段话本身，才能证明关系是否改变。

heading.en: Name the Action and Its Impact
heading.zh: 说清行为及其影响

body.en:
Replace a vague “I am sorry for everything” with the specific choice: “I told the committee you agreed, even though you had not.” Then name the impact without turning the explanation into an excuse.

A character can explain pressure, but should still identify the choice they made. This gives the other person something real to answer.
body.zh:
把模糊的“所有事情我都很抱歉”改成具体选择：“你没答应，我却告诉委员会你同意了。”然后说清影响，不要把解释变成开脱。

人物可以交代压力，但仍要指出自己的决定。这样对方才有真实的回应对象。

heading.en: Offer Repair Without Demanding Forgiveness
heading.zh: 提出修复，但不索取原谅

body.en:
Ask what can be repaired or propose a practical step: correct the record publicly, return the money, or give the other person space. The harmed character may refuse the offer.

Avoid apology conditions such as “if you were hurt” or “I am sorry, but.” They shift responsibility. Let the character accept that trust may take time or never return.
body.zh:
询问什么可以修复，或提出实际行动：公开更正记录、归还钱款，或给对方空间。受伤者可以拒绝。

避免“如果你觉得受伤了”或“我道歉，但是”这类条件式表达，它们会转移责任。让道歉者接受信任可能需要时间，也可能永远回不来。

heading.en: Show Changed Behavior After the Conversation
heading.zh: 在谈话之后展示行为变化

body.en:
The next similar situation is the real test. A character who once spoke for someone else can pause and ask; a person who broke a promise can give advance notice when plans change.

Do not make one apology erase the relationship history. Let repair take place across actions and give the other person control over whether closeness returns.
body.zh:
下一次类似情境才是真正考验。曾替别人做主的人可以停下来先问；失约的人可以在计划变化时提前告知。

一次道歉不能抹去关系历史。让修复通过持续行动发生，也让对方决定是否恢复亲近。

q.en: Should the apology happen before the climax?
q.zh: 道歉应安排在高潮前吗？

a.en: Place it where the relationship choice matters. The apology may enable cooperation before the climax or arrive afterward as part of repair; do not use it to remove conflict without changed behavior.
a.zh: 安排在关系选择有分量的位置。道歉可以让高潮前的合作成为可能，也可以在高潮后开启修复；不要用它在行为未变时消除冲突。

text.en: Use relationship and dialogue references to write accountability, the harmed character’s response, and follow-through as separate beats.
text.zh: 用关系与对白资料分别安排承担责任、受伤者回应和后续行动。

title.en: How to Use Silence and Pauses in Fiction
title.zh: 小说里的沉默和停顿怎么写：让空白改变下一句的分量

seo_title.en: Write Silence and Pauses in Fiction

description.en: Use a pause when a character delays, withholds, or changes a response; anchor silence in an action or consequence.
description.zh: 人物迟疑、隐瞒或改口时使用停顿，并让沉默连着动作或后果。

answer.en: Silence matters when it changes what a character can say or what another person believes. Give the pause a cause—fear, calculation, grief, or refusal—and show how someone responds. Do not use ellipses as a substitute for an unchosen emotion.
answer.zh: 沉默会改变人物能说什么、他人相信什么时才有分量。为停顿安排原因——恐惧、权衡、悲伤或拒绝——并展示他人如何回应。不要用省略号替代尚未决定的情绪。

heading.en: Give the Pause a Cause
heading.zh: 给停顿一个原因

body.en:
A character may pause because the answer could expose a secret, change a relationship, or confirm a loss. Decide what they consider saying and what stops them.

A simple physical action can carry the pause: the character sets down a cup before answering, rereads a message, or closes a door. Avoid stacking multiple generic beats such as staring, sighing, and looking away.
body.zh:
人物可能因回答会暴露秘密、改变关系或确认失去而停顿。决定他们想说什么、又被什么拦住。

简单动作就能承载停顿：回答前放下杯子、重读消息，或关上门。避免连续堆叠凝视、叹气、移开目光等泛化动作。

heading.en: Show How Another Character Reads the Silence
heading.zh: 展示他人如何理解沉默

body.en:
The listener may wait, fill the gap, change the question, or interpret silence as refusal. Their reaction makes the pause part of the interaction rather than empty space.

Keep the interpretation viewpoint-based. A character can assume a pause means guilt and be wrong; the scene can use that mistake to create a new choice.
body.zh:
听者可以等待、填补空白、改变问题，或把沉默当作拒绝。对方反应让停顿成为互动的一部分，而不是空白。

解读要受视角限制。人物可能以为沉默代表心虚，却判断错了；场景可以借此引出新选择。

heading.en: Vary the Length and Form of Silence
heading.zh: 变化沉默的长短与形式

body.en:
A brief delay before a name differs from a full scene in which nobody can speak. Match the space on the page to the consequence. Use paragraph breaks, interrupted actions, or a sound that continues after the conversation stops.

Read the scene aloud and check the rhythm. If pauses occur after every serious line, they lose force. Keep the ones that change the relationship or the next action.
body.zh:
说出姓名前的一瞬停顿，与整场无人开口不同。按后果决定纸面篇幅。可以用段落间隔、被打断的动作，或谈话停止后仍持续的声音呈现。

朗读整场检查节奏。若每句严肃台词后都停顿，停顿就失去力量。保留能改变关系或下一步行动的部分。

q.en: Should I write “there was a long pause” directly?
q.zh: 可以直接写“沉默了很久”吗？

a.en: Yes, when duration matters and the viewpoint character can perceive it. Add one concrete reaction if readers need to understand what the silence changes.
a.zh: 可以，若时长本身重要且视角人物能感知。需要读者理解沉默改变了什么时，再补一个具体反应。

text.en: Use dialogue and emotion references to connect pauses to a character’s intention, the listener’s interpretation, and scene rhythm.
text.zh: 用对白与情绪资料把停顿连到人物意图、听者解读和场景节奏。

title.en: How to Brainstorm Fiction Ideas with AI Without Losing Your Voice
title.zh: 怎么用AI构思小说点子：让它拓展选择，不替你定故事

seo_title.en: Brainstorm Fiction Ideas with AI

description.en: Give AI a premise and creative limits, ask for contrasting directions, then select and reshape the idea using your own reader promise.
description.zh: 向AI提供前提和创作边界，要求生成不同方向，再按自己的读者承诺筛选和改写。

answer.en: Use AI to widen the options around a premise, not to decide what your story means. Provide a specific starting idea, name what must stay, and ask for several contrasting conflicts or consequences. Keep the ideas that fit your interests, then rewrite the premise in your own words before outlining.
answer.zh: 让AI拓展故事前提的可能性，而不是替你决定作品意义。给它具体起点，写明必须保留的内容，再要求提供几种不同冲突或后果。留下符合兴趣的方向后，用自己的话重写故事前提，再开始列纲。

heading.en: Give AI a Specific Seed and Clear Limits
heading.zh: 给AI具体种子和明确边界

body.en:
A useful seed includes a character, a pressure, and an image or question: “A night-shift baker finds a receipt dated tomorrow.” Add limits such as genre, tone, intended reader, and ideas to avoid.

Do not paste a favorite author’s text and ask for imitation. Describe the qualities you want in plain language—fast dialogue, close viewpoint, restrained description—and build an original direction.
body.zh:
有用的种子包含人物、压力和画面或问题：“夜班面包师发现一张日期在明天的收据。”再补上类型、语气、目标读者和要避开的方向。

不要贴喜欢作者的原文要求模仿。用朴素语言描述想要的特点——对白利落、视角贴近、描写克制——再发展原创方向。

heading.en: Ask for Contrasting Options, Not More of the Same
heading.zh: 要求不同方向，而非同一想法的重复

body.en:
Ask for three routes that differ in the protagonist’s goal, opposing force, or cost. For each, request the choice that starts the plot and a likely complication.

Reject options that rely on familiar twists without evidence or change only names and settings. The purpose is to surface possibilities you can evaluate, not to receive finished copy.
body.zh:
要求三条在主角目标、阻力或代价上不同的路线。每条都说明什么选择开启剧情，以及可能出现的复杂情况。

拒绝只换名字地点、却没有证据或变化的套路反转。目的是得到可评估的可能性，不是接收成品文案。

heading.en: Make the Selection and Promise Yours
heading.zh: 让最终选择与承诺回到自己手里

body.en:
Choose the option that raises a question you care about. Change the character, stakes, or outcome until it reflects what you want readers to experience. Record what you accepted and what you rejected.

Then test the premise with a short scene or outline. If the idea only sounds exciting in a summary but produces no meaningful choices, revise it before committing to a long draft.
body.zh:
选择那个能提出你真正关心的问题的方向。调整人物、利害或结果，直到它反映你希望读者体验什么。记录采纳与舍弃的部分。

再用短场景或大纲检验前提。若点子只在简介里听起来刺激，却无法产生有意义的选择，就在投入长篇前修改。

q.en: Can AI invent an original novel idea for me?
q.zh: AI能替我想出原创小说点子吗？

a.en: It can suggest combinations, but you decide what to keep and how to develop it. Check for familiar premises, revise the details, and make sure the final story reflects your own goals and choices.
a.zh: AI可以提供组合方向，但由你决定采纳什么、如何发展。检查是否落入熟悉套路，改写细节，并确认最终故事体现自己的目标与选择。

text.en: Use the setup workflow to turn selected brainstorm options into a tested premise, then keep the author’s decisions as the project source of truth.
text.zh: 用设定流程把筛选后的构思转成经过检验的故事前提，并以作者决定作为项目事实依据。

title.en: How to Ask AI for Useful Feedback on a Fiction Scene
title.zh: 怎么让AI点评小说场景：限定问题，要求引用原文证据

seo_title.en: AI Feedback on a Fiction Scene

description.en: Name one revision question, provide the scene and needed context, and ask for evidence-based observations before suggestions.
description.zh: 指定一个改稿问题，提供场景及必要背景，并要求先给文本证据再提建议。

answer.en: AI feedback is more useful when the task is narrow and tied to the supplied text. Ask about one issue—such as goal clarity or repeated information—require short quotations for each observation, and separate reader effect from suggested fixes. Keep final decisions with the author.
answer.zh: 任务范围窄、紧贴提供的原文时，AI反馈更有用。一次只问一个问题，例如目标是否清楚、信息是否重复；要求每条观察引用短句，并把读者感受与修改建议分开。最终决定由作者作出。

heading.en: Choose One Question for This Review
heading.zh: 为这轮审阅选一个问题

body.en:
A request such as “make this better” invites vague rewrites. Choose a question: can a reader identify the scene goal, does the argument escalate, or is a key fact introduced twice?

Tell the reviewer what the scene should accomplish and what kind of feedback is out of scope. A focused review is easier to verify and less likely to flatten the voice.
body.zh:
“把这段改好”容易得到泛泛重写。改成具体问题：读者能否看出场景目标、争论是否升级、关键信息是否重复出现？

告诉审阅者场景要完成什么，以及哪些反馈不在范围内。聚焦审阅更易核实，也较不容易抹平原有声音。

heading.en: Require Evidence from the Supplied Scene
heading.zh: 要求引用提供的场景证据

body.en:
Ask AI to quote the shortest line that supports each observation and label uncertain interpretations. It should not invent character facts, rewrite the passage, or treat its preference as a continuity error.

A simple instruction: “Review only whether the scene goal is clear. For each concern, quote the exact sentence and explain the likely reader question. Do not rewrite. Mark insufficient evidence when the text does not support a conclusion.”
body.zh:
要求AI为每条观察引用最短原文，并标记不确定推断。它不应编造人物事实、重写段落，或把个人偏好当成连续性错误。

可以这样要求：“只检查场景目标是否清楚。每项问题引用原句并说明读者可能产生的疑问。不要重写。若文本不足以支持结论，标为证据不足。”

heading.en: Decide What to Change and Recheck It
heading.zh: 决定是否采纳，再检查改动

body.en:
Treat each comment as a suggestion, not a verdict. Accept, reject, or test it in a copy of the scene. If you revise a fact, relationship, or action, check later chapters that rely on it.

After editing, ask a focused follow-up question using the revised text. Do not keep rerunning broad critiques until one produces the answer you wanted.
body.zh:
把每条意见当建议，而不是判决。在场景副本中采纳、拒绝或试改。若修改事实、关系或行动，要检查依赖它的后续章节。

改完后用新版文本提出一项聚焦复查。不要反复运行宽泛点评，直到某次给出想听的答案。

q.en: Should AI rewrite the scene after giving feedback?
q.zh: AI给完意见后应该替我重写场景吗？

a.en: Only if you want draft alternatives. Keep the critique and rewrite as separate tasks, and compare any proposed prose with the original so you retain voice and story facts.
a.zh: 只有在你需要草稿备选时才让它改写。点评和重写分开处理，并把提议稿与原文对照，保留声音和故事事实。

text.en: Use a scoped review mode or prompt, require exact textual evidence, and keep evaluation separate from the author’s revision decision.
text.zh: 使用范围明确的审阅模式或提示词，要求精确文本证据，并把评估与作者的改稿决定分开。

title.en: How to Use AI to Outline a Novel Chapter Without Breaking Continuity
