If removing a team member changes nothing, combine the role or give them a consequential decision. Avoid making everyone competent at everything.
body.zh:
分配会影响计划的技能和信息：一人熟悉建筑，一人负责车辆，第三人能鉴别档案。每个人都要有动机，也要对风险有不同理解。

若删掉某个成员后毫无变化，就合并职责或给其关键决定。不要让所有人样样精通。

heading.en: Prepare the Plan and Its Failure Point
heading.zh: 铺垫计划，也铺垫失败点

body.en:
Let readers understand the intended sequence and one vulnerable assumption before the action begins. During the job, introduce a complication that tests that assumption or reveals new information.

Avoid solving every problem with a tool never mentioned earlier. The team’s response should use established skills, require a tradeoff, or expose a relationship conflict.
body.zh:
行动开始前，让读者理解计划步骤和一个脆弱假设。执行中引入考验假设或揭示新信息的意外。

不要用此前从未提过的工具解决所有问题。团队应动用已建立的技能、付出取舍，或暴露关系冲突。

q.en: Should readers know the whole heist plan before it begins?
q.zh: 劫案开始前要让读者知道完整计划吗？

a.en: They need enough to understand the stakes and recognize when the plan changes. You can withhold a specific tactic if the reveal is fair and earlier facts support it.
a.zh: 读者需要了解利害，并能看出计划何时改变。具体策略可以暂时保留，但揭示要公平且有前文依据。

text.en: Use scene outlining and suspense references to track the target, roles, plan assumptions, complications, and changed state.
text.zh: 用场景细纲和悬念资料追踪目标、分工、计划假设、意外与状态变化。

title.en: How to Write a Chase Scene Readers Can Picture
title.zh: 追逐场景怎么写清楚：让路线、目标和障碍一目了然

seo_title.en: Write a Clear Chase Scene

description.en: Establish who is chasing whom, what each person wants, and how the environment changes the available route.
description.zh: 交代谁追谁、双方目标，以及环境如何改变可走路线。

answer.en: A chase scene is easy to follow when readers know the goal, direction, and immediate obstacle. Give the pursuer and the fleeing character different objectives, use a few stable landmarks, and let each turn change distance, access, or risk. Vary movement with brief decisions rather than listing every step.
answer.zh: 追逐场景让读者看懂，需要目标、方向和眼前障碍清楚。给追逐双方不同目标，用少量稳定地标定位，再让每次转向改变距离、权限或风险。通过简短决定变化节奏，不必罗列每一步。

heading.en: Establish Goal, Direction, and Geography
heading.zh: 建立目标、方向和场景地理

body.en:
Show where the character starts, where they need to go, and what stands between them. A train platform, locked gate, or crowded market can orient readers better than constant compass directions.

Keep the viewpoint’s location consistent. If a character crosses a street or changes levels, give the reader a cue before the next obstacle depends on it.
body.zh:
说明人物从哪里出发、要去哪里、中间有什么阻挡。站台、上锁的门或拥挤市场，比不断报方位更容易定位。

保持视角人物位置连贯。人物过街或换楼层时，下一道障碍依赖此事前先给提示。

heading.en: Give Each Side a Different Goal
heading.zh: 给追逐双方不同目标

body.en:
The fleeing character may protect a witness while the pursuer wants a phone, not the person. Their routes and choices should reflect those goals.

Add an obstacle that changes the plan: a closed stairwell, a crowd separating allies, or a vehicle that starts only with a key. Make the response reveal skill or desperation.
body.zh:
逃跑者可能在保护证人，追赶者要的却是手机，而非这个人。路线和决定要体现目标差异。

加入改变计划的障碍：楼梯间关闭、人群把同伴隔开，或车辆没钥匙无法启动。回应应显露能力或绝望。

heading.en: Vary Speed and Let the Chase Change the Story
heading.zh: 变化速度，并让追逐改变故事

body.en:
Alternate bursts of movement with a brief choice or discovery. A character may hide, misdirect, accept help, or abandon an object. Each pause should make the next movement different.

End with a clear result: someone is caught, the group escapes but loses evidence, or the pursuer learns who they were chasing. Update the next scene’s options.
body.zh:
交替安排快速移动与短暂决定或发现。人物可以躲藏、误导、接受帮助或丢下物件。每次停顿都要让下一段行动有所不同。

用清楚结果收尾：有人被抓、团队逃脱却丢失证据，或追赶者认出了目标。同步更新下一场的选项。

q.en: How many turns should a chase scene have?
q.zh: 追逐场景应该转几次弯？

a.en: Use enough changes to alter distance, route, or risk. Too many similar obstacles make the scene hard to picture and reduce the impact of the decisive turn.
a.zh: 只安排足以改变距离、路线或风险的变化。相似障碍太多会让场景难以想象，也削弱关键转折。

text.en: Use scene and action outlining to track geography, viewpoint, obstacles, and the result carried into the next scene.
text.zh: 用场景与动作细纲追踪地理、视角、障碍和带入下一场的结果。

title.en: How to Write a Rescue Scene That Gives Everyone Agency
title.zh: 营救场景怎么写：让被救者有行动，也让救援付出代价

seo_title.en: Write a Rescue Scene

description.en: Clarify the danger and time limit, let the person in danger make useful choices, and show what rescue costs afterward.
description.zh: 明确危险与时限，让受困者作出有效行动，并呈现营救之后的代价。

answer.en: A rescue scene works when danger, timing, and available help are clear. Give the person being rescued a way to act, make the rescuer choose under pressure, and let success change resources or relationships. Do not end the scene as soon as someone is physically safe; show the immediate consequence.
answer.zh: 营救场景要有效，危险、时限和可用帮助都要清楚。让受困者也能行动，让救援者在压力下选择，并让成功改变资源或关系。不要人在安全后立刻结束场景，还要展示直接后果。

heading.en: Make the Danger Specific and Time-Bound
heading.zh: 让危险具体且有时限

body.en:
Define what will happen if no one acts: the tide rises, the door locks at midnight, or the patient loses access to a needed dose. Give the rescuer enough information to make a plan, while preserving uncertainty about one key detail.

Avoid vague danger that can expand or disappear whenever the plot needs. Establish how the characters can test the limit.
body.zh:
明确无人行动会发生什么：潮水上涨、午夜门锁关闭，或病人失去必要剂量。给救援者足够信息制定计划，同时保留一个关键细节的不确定性。

避免危险随剧情需要任意扩大或消失。要建立人物能如何验证限制。

heading.en: Give the Person in Danger a Useful Choice
heading.zh: 让受困者也能作出有效选择

body.en:
The person may send a signal, share a crucial fact, refuse an unsafe route, or protect someone else. Their action should affect the rescue rather than make them a passive object.

Let the rescuer listen and adapt. A plan that changes because of the person’s knowledge can reveal trust.
body.zh:
受困者可以发信号、提供关键事实、拒绝不安全路线，或保护其他人。其行动应影响营救，而非让其成为被搬运的物件。

让救援者倾听并调整。计划因受困者知识而改变，也能体现信任。

heading.en: Show the Cost and Immediate Aftermath
heading.zh: 展示代价和直接余波

body.en:
A successful rescue may cost time, a resource, anonymity, or another opportunity. Track who now knows what and whether the group’s plan still works.

Give the characters a brief aftermath: medical help, a difficult conversation, or a decision about who takes responsibility. Safety is a result, not an instant emotional reset.
body.zh:
成功营救可能消耗时间、资源、隐私或另一项机会。追踪现在谁知道什么，以及团队计划是否仍可执行。

给人物一段简短余波：求医、艰难谈话，或决定由谁承担责任。安全是结果，不是情绪瞬间复位。

q.en: Does a rescue scene need a sacrifice?
q.zh: 营救场景一定要有人牺牲吗？

a.en: No. The cost can be time, trust, a lost opportunity, or a changed plan. Choose a consequence that follows from the danger and character decisions.
a.zh: 不必。代价可以是时间、信任、错失机会或计划改变。选择应来自危险本身和人物决定。

text.en: Use conflict and continuity tracking to define danger, available resources, each character’s actions, and the rescue’s changed state.
text.zh: 用冲突与连续性追踪明确危险、可用资源、各人物行动和营救后的状态变化。

title.en: How to Write a First-Kiss Scene That Changes the Relationship
title.zh: 小说初吻场景怎么写：让身体靠近回应此前建立的信任

seo_title.en: Write a First-Kiss Scene

description.en: Build the moment from prior attraction and trust, make consent and choice clear, and show how the kiss changes what happens next.
description.zh: 让初吻承接此前吸引与信任，写清同意和选择，并展示它如何改变后续。

answer.en: A first-kiss scene matters when it grows from the relationship and changes its next step. Prepare attraction through prior choices, make the moment mutually chosen, and give both characters room to respond. The kiss can deepen trust, create a boundary, or complicate the external goal.
answer.zh: 初吻场景从关系中生长、改变下一步时才有分量。通过此前选择铺垫吸引，让亲吻由双方选择，并留出回应空间。它可以加深信任、建立边界，也可以使外部目标更复杂。

heading.en: Prepare the Moment Through Earlier Choices
heading.zh: 用此前选择铺垫这个时刻

body.en:
Show why these characters want to be close: a kept promise, a repaired disagreement, a moment of mutual attention. A kiss should not do all the work of establishing intimacy.

Give the scene an immediate context—a goodbye, a quiet celebration, or a difficult truth—so the moment belongs to this story.
body.zh:
写明两人为何想靠近：兑现承诺、修复分歧，或彼此关注的时刻。亲吻不能独自承担建立亲密关系的全部工作。

给场景一个眼前情境：道别、短暂庆祝或艰难坦白，让这一刻属于这篇故事。

heading.en: Make the Choice Mutual and Readable
heading.zh: 让双方选择清楚且相互

body.en:
Show each person’s response through words or action and leave room to stop. Consent can be quiet and unambiguous; it need not interrupt the scene with a speech.

If one character is uncertain, let them communicate that and change what happens. Do not use silence, intoxication, or pressure as automatic permission.
body.zh:
通过言语或行动呈现双方回应，并保留停下的空间。同意可以安静但明确，不必用一段演讲打断场景。

若有人犹豫，就让他们表达，并改变后续。不要把沉默、醉酒或压力自动当成许可。

heading.en: Show What the Kiss Changes Afterward
heading.zh: 展示亲吻之后改变了什么

body.en:
The characters may speak differently, set a new boundary, or have to decide whether to tell someone. Let the external plot respond if the kiss changes teamwork or secrecy.

Avoid repeating the same sensory description for its own sake. One precise detail can carry the moment; the important payoff is what each person chooses next.
body.zh:
两人之后可能改变说话方式、建立新边界，或必须决定是否告诉别人。亲吻若改变合作或秘密，外部剧情也要回应。

不要为了描写而重复感官细节。一个准确细节足以承载时刻；关键回报是双方接下来如何选择。

q.en: Should a first kiss happen at the romance midpoint?
q.zh: 初吻应该安排在恋爱线中点吗？

a.en: Place it where the relationship has earned that change and where the moment affects later choices. The right position depends on the book’s promise and pacing.
a.zh: 安排在关系足以支撑变化、且会影响后续选择的位置。具体时点取决于本书承诺和节奏。

text.en: Use relationship, emotional-arc, and dialogue references to prepare the moment and record its effect on later scenes.
text.zh: 用关系、情绪弧线和对白资料铺垫初吻，并记录它对后续场景的影响。

title.en: How to Write a Breakup Scene That Feels Inevitable but Still Hurts
title.zh: 小说分手场景怎么写：让原因清楚，也让失去有重量

seo_title.en: Write a Breakup Scene

description.en: Connect the breakup to earlier patterns, give both people a clear position, and show the practical and emotional consequences.
description.zh: 把分手连到此前模式，让双方立场清楚，并展示现实与情感后果。

answer.en: A breakup scene feels earned when readers understand the pattern or decision that made the relationship unsustainable. Give both people a position, let them respond to what was actually said, and make the result change practical plans or boundaries. A painful scene does not need either person to become a villain.
answer.zh: 读者理解让关系无法持续的模式或决定时，分手才显得来之有因。让双方都有立场，并回应彼此真正说的话；结果应改变现实安排或边界。痛苦场景不必把谁写成反派。

heading.en: Prepare the Pattern Before the Breakup
heading.zh: 分手前先铺垫关系模式

body.en:
Show the recurring disagreement, unmet need, or broken promise in earlier scenes. The breakup should respond to something readers have seen rather than introduce a new grievance to force an ending.

Track what each character tried to change and what remained unresolved.
body.zh:
在前文呈现反复的分歧、未被满足的需要或破裂的承诺。分手应回应读者见过的问题，而不是临时新增怨言来强行结束。

记录双方尝试改变过什么、哪些问题仍未解决。

heading.en: Give Both People a Position and a Voice
heading.zh: 让双方都有立场和声音

body.en:
One may want to leave now; the other may want another conversation. Let each speak from their own goal and knowledge. Avoid making one person suddenly confess every flaw for the reader’s benefit.

Use silence, objects, and practical questions where they change the exchange. The characters might return a key, divide a shared task, or decide who will tell friends.
body.zh:
一人可能现在就要离开，另一人想再谈一次。让双方基于自己的目标和认知表达，不要让谁突然为了读者承认所有缺点。

在沉默、物件和现实问题会改变对话时使用它们。两人可以归还钥匙、分配共同任务，或决定谁告知朋友。

heading.en: Show How Life Changes After the Scene
heading.zh: 展示场景之后生活如何变化

body.en:
A breakup changes routines, housing, plans, and mutual friendships. Show at least one concrete consequence in the next scene so the decision does not vanish.

If reconciliation remains possible, require changed behavior or new conditions. The breakup should still matter even if the couple later reunites.
body.zh:
分手会改变日常、住处、计划和共同朋友。下一场至少展示一项具体后果，让决定不会凭空消失。

若之后可能复合，需要行为改变或新条件。即便最终和好，分手也应仍有分量。

q.en: Should a breakup scene explain every reason the relationship failed?
q.zh: 分手场景要讲清所有失败原因吗？

a.en: No. Use the reasons that shape the present decision and refer to earlier evidence. A concise scene can feel complete when the next actions show the result.
a.zh: 不必。只呈现影响当前决定的原因，并承接前文证据。后续行动展示结果时，简短场景也可以完整。

text.en: Use relationship tracking and dialogue references to connect the breakup to prior conflicts and carry its consequences forward.
text.zh: 用关系追踪与对白资料把分手连到旧冲突，并延续其后果。

title.en: How to Write a Game Side Quest That Adds More Than Loot
title.zh: 游戏支线任务怎么写有意义：补充世界，也改变玩家选择

seo_title.en: Write a Game Side Quest

description.en: Give an optional quest a distinct character goal, a meaningful choice, and a payoff that can affect later play.
description.zh: 给支线安排独立人物目标、有意义的选择和能影响后续玩法的回报。

answer.en: A side quest adds value when it reveals something about the world or characters and gives the player a meaningful choice. Keep it optional, define a complete local goal, and decide whether its result changes resources, relationships, or later access. Do not make every side quest a fetch task with the same reward.
answer.zh: 支线任务揭示世界或人物，并给玩家有意义的选择时才有价值。保持可选，安排完整的局部目标，并决定结果是否改变资源、关系或后续权限。不要把每条支线都做成同一种取物任务和奖励。

heading.en: Give the Side Quest Its Own Local Story
heading.zh: 给支线一段完整的小故事

body.en:
A shopkeeper may ask for a missing ledger because it proves a worker’s wages were withheld. The player can recover it, expose the owner, or offer another solution. The task has a human reason beyond “go to the marker.”

Keep the local arc compact: need, obstacle, decision, result. Let the player understand why the person asked for help.
body.zh:
店主可能在找一本失踪账册，因为它能证明工人工资被扣。玩家可以找回账册、揭发老板，或提出其他办法。任务有人的理由，不只是“去标记点”。

局部弧线保持紧凑：需求、障碍、决定、结果。让玩家理解求助原因。

heading.en: Connect the Choice to a World State
heading.zh: 让选择连接世界状态

body.en:
A choice can change who runs a business, what a neighborhood can afford, or which character will cooperate later. The effect need not alter the main plot, but it should be visible when it matters.

If the outcome only changes a number, consider a line of dialogue, a new object state, or access to a different route that shows the result.
body.zh:
选择可以改变谁经营店铺、街区能负担什么，或之后谁愿意合作。结果不必改变主线，但关键时刻要看得见。

若结局只改变数字，可以用一句对白、物件状态或新路线权限展示它。

heading.en: Respect the Player’s Time and the Main Goal
heading.zh: 尊重玩家时间和主线目标

body.en:
Make the quest length match its reward and complexity. If the player must leave the area, explain why the trip matters and give a clear return point.

Avoid interrupting a critical main-quest moment with optional content. Place side stories where players can choose a pause and resume the main task easily.
body.zh:
任务长度要匹配奖励和复杂度。若玩家需要离开当前区域，说明此行意义，并给出明确回归点。

不要在主线关键时刻插入可选内容。把支线放在玩家可以暂停并轻松回到主线的位置。

q.en: Can a side quest affect the main ending?
q.zh: 支线任务可以影响主结局吗？

a.en: Yes, if the connection is prepared and players can see why it matters. A small effect on trust, resources, or available help can be meaningful without creating a separate ending.
a.zh: 可以，只要提前铺垫关联，让玩家看出其重要性。信任、资源或可获得帮助的小变化，也能有意义而不必另设结局。

text.en: Use game-concept and narrative-state workflows to connect an optional task’s goal, player choice, feedback, and later consequence.
text.zh: 用游戏概念与叙事状态流程连接支线目标、玩家选择、反馈和后续后果。

title.en: How to Tell a Story Through a Game Environment
title.zh: 游戏环境叙事怎么做：让地点变化透露过去和选择

seo_title.en: Tell a Story Through Game Environments

description.en: Use object placement, damage, access, and repeated locations to show what happened and what players can infer.
description.zh: 用物件位置、破损、权限和重复地点展示发生过什么及玩家能推断什么。

answer.en: A game environment can communicate story through objects, layout, wear, and changes players can inspect. Give each detail a reason to be there, make important clues readable from the player’s path, and let exploration reveal information that supports a choice. Visual detail should complement, not replace, necessary clarity.
answer.zh: 游戏环境可以通过物件、布局、磨损和状态变化讲故事。每个细节都要有存在理由，关键线索应能从玩家路径中看见，探索得到的信息还要支持选择。视觉细节应补充清晰度，而非取代它。

heading.en: Choose What the Environment Should Answer
heading.zh: 决定环境要回答什么

body.en:
A room may reveal who left in a hurry, what resource is scarce, or which group controls the building. Start with one question, then place details that support it.

A broken chair alone is decoration; the chair wedged against a door and a dropped access badge tell a sequence of events.
body.zh:
一个房间可以揭示谁匆忙离开、哪种资源稀缺，或哪个团体控制建筑。先选一个问题，再放置支持它的细节。

单独一把坏椅子只是装饰；椅子顶着门、旁边掉着门禁卡，才讲出一连串事件。

heading.en: Guide Player Attention Without a Lecture
heading.zh: 引导玩家注意，但别讲课

body.en:
Use lighting, contrast, sound, or a changed route to make an important detail discoverable. Do not hide a required clue behind a visual trick players cannot reasonably notice.

Separate essential story facts from optional discoveries. Players who explore can gain context; everyone should still understand the next necessary action.
body.zh:
用光线、反差、声音或路线变化，让重要细节能被发现。不要把必需线索藏在玩家合理情况下注意不到的视觉把戏里。

区分必要事实和可选发现。探索者可以获得更多背景，但所有玩家都要明白下一步必做什么。

heading.en: Reuse Locations to Show What Has Changed
heading.zh: 通过重复地点展现变化

body.en:
Return to a room after an event and alter who is present, what has been moved, or which route is blocked. The changed environment can show a consequence without another explanation scene.

Track object states and access in your level notes so the world remembers player actions.
body.zh:
事件之后再次进入同一房间，改变在场者、物件位置或被封锁的路线。环境变化可以展示后果，不必再用一场解释戏。

在关卡笔记中追踪物件状态和权限，让世界记住玩家行动。

q.en: Can environmental storytelling replace dialogue?
q.zh: 环境叙事能完全替代对白吗？

a.en: It can carry some history and mood, but use direct text or dialogue when players need precise instructions, names, or a choice explained clearly.
a.zh: 它可以承载部分历史和氛围；玩家需要明确指示、姓名或选择说明时，仍应使用文字或对白。

text.en: Use world-design and narrative-mapping workflows to connect location details to evidence, player routes, and state changes.
text.zh: 用世界设计与叙事映射流程把地点细节连接到证据、玩家路线和状态变化。

title.en: How to Build a Game World That Supports Story and Play
title.zh: 游戏世界观怎么搭：让地图规则既能讲故事，也能支持玩法

seo_title.en: Build a Game World for Story and Play

description.en: Start with the player’s actions, define the world rules that shape them, and use locations to create distinct goals and constraints.
description.zh: 从玩家能做的事出发，定义塑造行动的世界规则，并用地点制造不同目标和限制。

answer.en: A game world should support both the story the player follows and the actions the game lets them take. Start with the player’s core activity, decide what rules shape access and risk, then build locations that produce varied decisions. Add lore when it explains a choice, conflict, or visible result.
answer.zh: 游戏世界要同时支持玩家追随的故事和游戏允许的行动。从核心玩法出发，确定影响权限与风险的规则，再设计能产生不同决定的地点。设定在解释选择、冲突或可见结果时再加入。

heading.en: Start with What the Player Does
heading.zh: 从玩家实际要做什么开始

body.en:
If players investigate, design places with evidence and access limits. If they manage a town, define who controls resources and what changes over time. The world’s daily life should create gameplay opportunities.

Avoid writing an encyclopedia before the core loop exists. A few usable rules can support a prototype; expand the history when a level or story question needs it.
body.zh:
玩家要调查，就设计有证据和权限限制的地点；玩家要经营城镇，就明确资源由谁控制、状态如何变化。世界日常要能产生玩法机会。

核心循环成形前别先写百科。少数可用规则足以支持原型；关卡或故事提出问题时再扩展历史。

heading.en: Define Rules That Shape Access and Risk
heading.zh: 明确影响权限和风险的规则

body.en:
Decide who can enter a place, use a tool, travel a route, or claim a resource. Make those rules visible through interfaces, characters, and consequences.

A setting rule becomes gameplay when it changes what the player can attempt. If a rule never affects action, it may remain background lore.
body.zh:
明确谁能进入地点、使用工具、走某条路线或占有资源。通过界面、人物和后果让规则可见。

设定改变玩家能尝试什么时，就成了玩法。如果规则从不影响行动，它可以留在背景。

heading.en: Make Each Location Change the Player’s Options
heading.zh: 让每个地点改变玩家选项

body.en:
A market may offer information for a price; a flooded tunnel may cut off a fast route; a quiet home may let the player revisit a relationship. Locations should create different constraints or opportunities.

Reuse locations after major events so players can see how the world responds. Track landmarks, exits, and object states across levels.
body.zh:
市场可能收费出售情报；淹水隧道会切断捷径；安静的家则能让玩家处理关系。地点应制造不同限制或机会。

重要事件后重复使用地点，让玩家看见世界如何回应。跨关卡追踪地标、出口和物件状态。

q.en: Should I write game-world history before designing levels?
q.zh: 设计关卡前要先写完整世界史吗？

a.en: No. Define enough history to support the first locations and conflicts, then fill gaps when gameplay needs them. Separate fixed facts from ideas still open to change.
a.zh: 不必。先写足以支撑首批地点和冲突的历史，玩法需要时再补全。把确定事实与仍可调整的想法分开。

text.en: Use world-design and game-concept workflows to connect player actions, setting constraints, location goals, and evolving state.
text.zh: 用世界设计与游戏概念流程连接玩家行动、设定限制、地点目标和状态变化。

title.en: How to Write Game Cutscenes That Keep the Player Engaged
title.zh: 游戏过场动画怎么写不拖：改变信息、目标或关系后尽快交还操作

seo_title.en: Write Game Cutscenes

description.en: Use a cutscene to reveal information or force a decision, keep its focus clear, and return control when the player can act.
description.zh: 用过场揭示信息或逼出决定，保持焦点清楚，并在玩家能行动时交还控制。

answer.en: A cutscene earns its length when it changes what the player knows, wants, or can do. Keep one dramatic focus, let characters act rather than explain everything, and return control at a meaningful decision or next task. If a sequence repeats gameplay information, shorten it or move that information into play.
answer.zh: 过场会改变玩家认知、目标或行动条件时，才值得占时长。保持一个戏剧焦点，让人物行动而非包办解释，并在有意义的决定或下一任务处交还控制。若内容重复玩法信息，就缩短或移进游戏。

heading.en: Give the Cutscene a Job the Player Cannot Do Yet
heading.zh: 给过场一项玩家暂时无法完成的工作

body.en:
A cutscene can show a distant event, reveal a character’s decision, or establish a change the player must respond to. It should add information or consequence the current mechanic cannot deliver.

Write the scene’s new fact and next player goal before drafting dialogue. This prevents the sequence from becoming background without a gameplay link.
body.zh:
过场可以呈现远处事件、揭示人物决定，或建立玩家必须回应的变化。它应增加当前机制无法交付的信息或后果。

写对白前，先确定新增事实和玩家下一目标，避免过场变成与玩法脱节的背景介绍。

heading.en: Keep One Dramatic Focus and Cut Repeated Exposition
heading.zh: 保持一个戏剧焦点，删掉重复说明

body.en:
Choose the main change: an alliance breaks, a deadline moves, or a character makes a promise. Give dialogue room to reveal intention or disagreement, not explain facts the player just saw.

Use camera direction only where it supports staging or information. Let animation and sound carry reactions when they are clear.
body.zh:
选定主要变化：同盟破裂、期限提前，或人物作出承诺。对白应揭示意图或分歧，不要解释玩家刚看到的事实。

镜头说明只在帮助调度或传递信息时使用。动画和声音能清楚表达反应时就让它们承担。

heading.en: Return Control When the Player Has a Purpose
heading.zh: 在玩家有事可做时交还控制

body.en:
End the sequence with a clear new task, location, or choice. A short playable action after a reveal can make the player experience its consequence.

Check the transition into the next objective, interface prompts, and any missed input. Keep the cutscene’s duration proportional to the change it delivers.
body.zh:
用清楚的新任务、地点或选择结束过场。揭示后立刻交付一项可玩动作，能让玩家体验其后果。

检查转入下一目标的衔接、界面提示和输入是否遗漏。过场时长要与交付的变化相称。

q.en: Can a game explain its backstory in cutscenes?
q.zh: 游戏可以通过过场解释背景故事吗？

a.en: Yes, when the history changes a current choice or relationship. Break up background with action and avoid explaining facts players already encountered in documents or play.
a.zh: 可以，当前史会改变选择或关系时尤其合适。用行动打断背景说明，避免重复玩家已从文件或玩法中了解的事实。

text.en: Use game-build and script workflows to align cutscene goals, player control handoff, dialogue, and level objectives.
text.zh: 用游戏构建与剧本流程对齐过场目标、控制权交接、对白和关卡目标。

title.en: How to Write an RPG Companion Arc That Changes Through Play
title.zh: RPG同伴角色弧线怎么写：让同行、任务和选择逐步改变关系

seo_title.en: Write an RPG Companion Arc

description.en: Give a companion an independent goal, connect trust to player actions, and resolve their arc through a choice the player can witness.
description.zh: 给同伴独立目标，让信任回应玩家行动，并用玩家亲历的选择收束弧线。

answer.en: An RPG companion feels like a person when they have a goal beyond following the player and react to events in the world. Define what they want, what earns or damages trust, and how their personal quest changes the relationship. Let gameplay reflect that change through dialogue, access, or cooperation.
answer.zh: RPG同伴拥有跟随玩家以外的目标、会回应世界事件时，才像真实人物。明确他们想要什么、何种行动建立或损害信任、个人任务如何改变关系。用对白、权限或合作方式让玩法体现变化。

heading.en: Give the Companion a Goal Beyond the Player
heading.zh: 给同伴一个玩家之外的目标

body.en:
The companion may search for a missing relative, protect a homeland, or prove a mentor wrong. They can support the player while still disagreeing about priorities.

Show what the companion does when off the main path through optional dialogue, letters, or changed locations. Their life should not pause whenever the player looks elsewhere.
body.zh:
同伴可能寻找失踪亲人、保护故乡，或证明导师错了。他们可以支持玩家，同时仍在优先级上有分歧。

通过可选对白、信件或地点变化呈现同伴不在主线时做什么。玩家暂时不关注时，他们的生活也不该停摆。

heading.en: Connect Trust to Player Actions and World Events
heading.zh: 让信任回应玩家行动和世界事件

body.en:
Track a few meaningful actions: honoring a promise, sharing a resource, or choosing whom to protect. Let the companion respond in a line, a refusal, or a new offer of help.

Avoid changing trust for hidden reasons the player cannot understand. If a decision will matter later, give a clear reaction or reminder.
body.zh:
追踪少数有意义的行动：兑现承诺、共享资源，或选择保护谁。让同伴通过一句回应、一次拒绝或新的帮助邀约作出反应。

不要因玩家无法理解的隐藏理由改变信任。决定若会影响后续，就给出清楚回应或提醒。

heading.en: Resolve the Personal Quest Through a Choice
heading.zh: 用选择解决个人任务

body.en:
The companion’s quest should ask them to do more than retrieve an item. They may choose between an old loyalty and a new responsibility, or decide whether to reveal a truth.

Show the result in later behavior and cooperation. A completed quest should change what the companion can offer or refuse, not just add a reward to inventory.
body.zh:
同伴任务不能只是找回物件。人物可以在旧忠诚和新责任间选择，或决定是否说出真相。

在后续行为和合作中展示结果。任务完成应改变同伴能提供或拒绝什么，而不只是增加背包奖励。

q.en: Can an RPG companion leave the party?
q.zh: RPG同伴可以离队吗？

a.en: Yes, when leaving follows from their goal and the player’s actions. Prepare the possibility, make the consequence understandable, and give the player a chance to respond when appropriate.
a.zh: 可以，只要离队来自其目标和玩家行动。提前铺垫可能性，说明后果，并在合适时给玩家回应机会。

text.en: Use character, relationship, and game-state tracking to connect companion goals, player choices, quest outcomes, and party behavior.
text.zh: 用人物、关系和游戏状态追踪连接同伴目标、玩家选择、任务结果与队伍行为。

title.en: How to Write a Movie Review Video Script with Evidence
title.zh: 电影评论视频脚本怎么写：用具体场景支撑观点

seo_title.en: Write a Movie Review Video Script

description.en: State your view of the film, support it with specific scenes, separate observation from opinion, and mark spoilers clearly.
description.zh: 先说影片评价，用具体场景作证，区分观察与观点，并清楚标注剧透。

answer.en: A movie-review video gives viewers a clear critical view supported by specific moments from the film. State the main judgment, choose a few scenes that demonstrate it, and explain how form, performance, or structure creates the effect. Mark spoilers before revealing plot details and distinguish interpretation from fact.
answer.zh: 电影评论视频要提出有证据支撑的判断。先给出核心评价，再挑几场戏说明，并解释表演、形式或结构如何产生效果。透露剧情前标记剧透，并区分解释和事实。

heading.en: State a Focused Opinion About the Film
heading.zh: 对电影提出聚焦观点

body.en:
Choose one argument viewers can follow: the film’s humor depends on timing, the central relationship changes too quickly, or the visual style makes isolation visible. Avoid summarizing the whole plot before stating your view.

Name who the review may help: viewers choosing what to watch, fans comparing craft, or people looking for a spoiler-free introduction.
body.zh:
选择一个观众能跟进的观点：电影幽默依赖节奏、核心关系变化过快，或视觉风格让孤独感可见。先别复述全部剧情。

说明评论适合谁：正在选片的人、比较创作手法的影迷，或想了解影片但不想被剧透的观众。

heading.en: Support the View with Specific Scenes
heading.zh: 用具体场景支撑观点

body.en:
Pick a few moments and note what viewers see or hear, what you infer, and why it supports your judgment. A scene detail is evidence; your explanation is the argument.

Avoid claiming that one moment proves what every viewer must feel. Describe the effect you observed and leave room for another reading.
body.zh:
挑几处时刻，记录观众看见或听见什么、你由此推断什么、它为何支持观点。场景细节是证据，你的解释才是论证。

不要宣称一处细节能证明所有观众都必须有同样感受。描述观察到的效果，也留出其他解读空间。

heading.en: Control Spoilers and Match Footage to Claims
heading.zh: 管理剧透，并让素材对应论点

body.en:
Signal spoiler level in the opening and before major reveals. Do not let an edit imply an event or reaction that the film does not show.

Use short clips, stills, or on-screen text to make the point inspectable. Check sources and rights for footage under your project’s rules, and avoid presenting a recreated image as original material.
body.zh:
开头和重大揭示前都要提示剧透程度。剪辑不能暗示影片中未出现的事件或反应。

用短片段、剧照或屏幕文字让观点可检视。按项目规则核查素材来源与版权，也别把重演画面伪装成原始素材。

q.en: Should a movie review video include a rating?
q.zh: 电影评论视频需要打分吗？

a.en: Only if the rating system helps your audience understand the recommendation. Explain what the score means and keep the reasoning visible in the review.
a.zh: 只有评分体系能帮助观众理解推荐时才需要。说明分数含义，并在评论里展示判断依据。

text.en: Use source and clip mapping to connect each evaluation claim to a scene while keeping interpretation and observation distinct.
text.zh: 用来源与片段映射让每条评价观点对应具体场景，并区分解释和观察。

title.en: How to Write a Book Review Video Script Readers Can Use
title.zh: 图书评论视频脚本怎么写：说明适读人群，并用细节作证

seo_title.en: Write a Book Review Video Script

description.en: Give a clear recommendation, name the intended reader, support opinions with spoiler-safe examples, and separate summary from critique.
description.zh: 给出明确推荐，说明适读人群，用不剧透的例子支撑观点，并区分梗概和评论。

answer.en: A useful book-review video helps viewers decide whether a book fits their interests. State your view, describe the reading experience without retelling every chapter, and support claims with specific but spoiler-safe examples. Explain who may enjoy the book and where it may not fit.
answer.zh: 有用的图书评论视频帮助观众判断书是否符合兴趣。先说观点，用阅读体验而非逐章复述来介绍，并用具体但不剧透的例子作证。说明谁可能喜欢、哪些读者或许不适合。

heading.en: Name the Reader and Your Recommendation
heading.zh: 说明读者对象和推荐结论

body.en:
Say whether you recommend the book and for whom: readers who like careful worldbuilding, short chapters, or a particular kind of relationship. A recommendation is more useful than “it is good.”

Give the author, title, and edition information clearly if relevant, then state whether the review contains spoilers.
body.zh:
说清是否推荐、推荐给谁：喜欢细致世界观、短章节或某种关系线的读者。“很好看”不如明确适读人群有用。

需要时清楚标注作者、书名和版本，并说明是否含剧透。

heading.en: Support Claims Without Retelling the Whole Book
heading.zh: 支撑观点，但别复述整本书

body.en:
Choose one or two moments that reveal pacing, voice, character, or structure without giving away a major turn. Explain what the passage does and how it shaped your experience.

Keep plot summary short and separate it from evaluation. If a detail is a spoiler, use a warning and decide whether it is necessary to the review.
body.zh:
挑一两个能体现节奏、声音、人物或结构、又不泄露重大转折的片段。解释段落做了什么、如何影响阅读体验。

梗概要短，并与评价分开。若某细节属于剧透，先提示，再判断它是否真有必要。

heading.en: Match the Review to the Viewer’s Decision
heading.zh: 让评论回应观众正在做的决定

body.en:
End with a practical fit statement: who should read it now, who may prefer another style, and what kind of experience to expect. Avoid declaring that a book is for everyone.

Pair narration with cover, page, or note visuals only when they support the review. Check that quoted text is brief, accurate, and permitted for your use.
body.zh:
结尾给出实际适配建议：谁现在适合读、谁可能偏好其他风格、预期会得到什么体验。别说一本书适合所有人。

封面、书页或笔记画面只在支持评论时使用。确认引文简短准确，也符合使用规则。

q.en: Can I spoil the ending in a book review?
q.zh: 图书评论可以剧透结局吗？

a.en: Yes, if you warn viewers before the reveal and the ending is necessary to your analysis. Offer a spoiler-free recommendation first so viewers can leave before that section.
a.zh: 可以，但要在揭示前提醒，且结局确实是分析所需。先给无剧透推荐，让观众能在进入剧透段前离开。

text.en: Use research and narration planning to separate plot facts, personal evaluation, spoiler level, and the reader decision.
text.zh: 用研究与旁白规划区分情节事实、个人评价、剧透程度和读者决策。

title.en: How to Write Interview Questions That Lead to a Clear Video Story
title.zh: 视频访谈问题怎么设计：从事实追问到选择与后果

seo_title.en: Write Interview Questions for Video
seo_title.zh: 视频访谈问题怎么设计

description.en: Start with open questions, ask for concrete examples and timelines, and use follow-ups to clarify choices without leading the guest.
description.zh: 从开放问题开始，追问具体例子和时间线，用后续问题澄清选择但不引导嘉宾。

answer.en: Good interview questions help a person explain what happened, what they chose, and what changed afterward. Prepare a short topic path, ask open questions, then follow up on details the guest introduced. Avoid putting your conclusion into the question or pressuring someone to disclose beyond their comfort.
answer.zh: 好的访谈问题帮助受访者说清发生了什么、作了什么选择、之后改变了什么。准备简短主题路径，提出开放问题，再追问嘉宾主动提到的细节。不要把结论塞进问题，也不强迫对方透露不愿说的事。

heading.en: Build a Topic Path Before the Interview
heading.zh: 访谈前先安排主题路径

body.en:
List the beginning situation, key decision, turning moment, and current result. Prepare open prompts for each: “What happened next?” “What did you know then?” “What made the choice difficult?”

Keep a few questions flexible. The strongest detail may appear in an answer you did not predict.
body.zh:
列出初始处境、关键决定、转折时刻和当前结果。为每项准备开放提示：“之后发生了什么？”“当时你知道什么？”“这个选择为什么困难？”

留出一些灵活问题。最有力的细节可能来自意料之外的回答。

heading.en: Ask for Concrete Examples and Timeline Details
heading.zh: 追问具体例子和时间线细节

body.en:
When a guest says “everything changed,” ask what changed first and what they can show or remember precisely. Confirm dates, names, and sequence in a separate fact-check pass.

Avoid leading prompts such as “You were angry, right?” Ask what they felt or noticed instead. Preserve the guest’s uncertainty when memory is incomplete.
body.zh:
嘉宾说“一切都变了”时，追问最先改变什么、有哪些能展示或准确记住的细节。姓名、日期和顺序另做事实核查。

避免“你当时很生气，对吧”这类引导性问题。改问对方感受或注意到了什么。记忆不完整时保留其不确定性。

heading.en: Use Follow-Ups and Respect Boundaries
heading.zh: 用追问补全信息，并尊重边界

body.en:
Follow the guest’s exact wording: “You said the call came later. How did you confirm that?” This clarifies evidence without arguing.

Offer a chance to pause or decline a sensitive question. In editing, do not cut an answer so its meaning reverses. Keep full context in the source notes and confirm any planned sensitive details.
body.zh:
沿着嘉宾的原话追问：“你说电话是后来打来的，当时怎么确认？”这能澄清证据，而不是争辩。

敏感问题允许暂停或拒答。剪辑时不能把回答剪到意思反转。来源笔记保留完整语境，敏感细节按计划确认。

q.en: Should interview questions be written word for word?
q.zh: 访谈问题要逐字写好吗？

a.en: Prepare the core questions, but listen and follow up naturally. A rigid script can cause you to miss a useful detail or clarification.
a.zh: 核心问题要准备，但要自然倾听和追问。死守脚本可能错过有用细节或澄清机会。

text.en: Use research and story-structure workflows to prepare a timeline, verify claims, and keep interview evidence distinct from narration.
text.zh: 用研究与故事结构流程准备时间线、核实论断，并区分访谈证据和旁白。

title.en: How to Edit an Interview into a Video Story Without Distorting It
title.zh: 访谈素材怎么剪成故事：整理叙事，但不改变原意

seo_title.en: Edit an Interview into a Video Story

description.en: Organize answers around a clear question, preserve context and uncertainty, and verify each narration bridge against the full interview.
description.zh: 围绕一个问题组织回答，保留语境和不确定性，并用完整访谈核对旁白衔接。

answer.en: Shape an interview video around a clear question and a sequence of events, but preserve what the speaker meant. Build a transcript with timecodes, group answers by topic, and verify every edit against the full recording. Use narration to bridge gaps without inventing what the guest did not say.
answer.zh: 围绕清晰问题和事件顺序组织访谈视频，同时保留说话者原意。整理带时间码的逐字稿，按主题组合回答，并对照完整录音核查每次剪辑。旁白可衔接空缺，但不能编造嘉宾没说过的话。

heading.en: Transcribe and Group Answers by Story Beat
heading.zh: 转录访谈，并按故事节拍归类

body.en:
Create a transcript with timecodes and mark the setup, choice, obstacle, and result. Keep answers that contain concrete details, not only the most polished sound bite.

If the interview jumps in time, place each section in the correct sequence and note what context the viewer needs.
body.zh:
制作带时间码的逐字稿，标记铺垫、选择、障碍和结果。保留包含具体细节的回答，不只挑听起来最漂亮的一句话。

访谈若时间跳跃，就按正确顺序排列，并记录观众需要哪些背景。

heading.en: Preserve Meaning, Context, and Uncertainty
heading.zh: 保留原意、语境和不确定性

body.en:
Do not remove a qualification or question that changes what an answer refers to. When two quotes are combined, check that the edit does not imply a false cause or timeline.

A speaker may say “I think” or correct a memory. Keep that uncertainty when it matters rather than making the story sound more certain than the evidence.
body.zh:
不要删去会改变回答指向的限制说明或问题。拼接两段引文时，确认剪辑没有暗示错误因果或时间线。

受访者可能说“我记得”或更正记忆。重要时保留这种不确定性，不要让叙事显得比证据更确定。

heading.en: Use Narration to Bridge Gaps, Not Invent Events
heading.zh: 用旁白衔接空缺，不要编造事件

body.en:
Narration can identify a date, explain a documented transition, or summarize a missing period. Keep source notes beside each factual line.

Watch the cut against the full interview. If the sequence makes the speaker appear to answer a different question or agree to a claim they rejected, restore context or restructure the segment.
body.zh:
旁白可以交代日期、解释有记录的转折，或概述未拍到的时段。每条事实性旁白都要附来源笔记。

对照完整访谈观看剪辑。若顺序让受访者看起来回答了另一个问题，或同意其曾拒绝的观点，就补回语境或重排片段。

q.en: Can I rearrange interview answers out of order?
q.zh: 访谈回答可以打乱顺序吗？

a.en: Yes, if the edit remains accurate and does not create a false timeline or causal claim. Use narration or on-screen dates to orient viewers when needed.
a.zh: 可以，但剪辑必须准确，不能制造虚假时间线或因果。需要时用旁白或屏幕日期帮助观众定位。

text.en: Use multi-video story editing and research notes to organize interview evidence while preserving timeline, context, and source traceability.
text.zh: 用多视频叙事剪辑与研究笔记组织访谈证据，同时保留时间线、语境和来源可追溯性。

title.en: How to Write a Personal Story Video Script That Has a Point
title.zh: 个人经历视频脚本怎么写：选一段变化，而不是讲完全部人生

seo_title.en: Write a Personal Story Video Script

description.en: Choose one experience and turning point, provide only the context viewers need, and end with what changed for you.
description.zh: 选一段经历和转折，只补观众需要的背景，并以自身变化收尾。

answer.en: A personal-story video works when one experience leads to a clear change or question. Choose a moment with a beginning, decision, and result; give enough context to understand it; and end with what you now see differently. Do not imply that one person’s experience proves a rule for everyone.
answer.zh: 个人经历视频从一段经历走向清楚变化或问题时才有效。选一个有开端、决定和结果的时刻，补足理解所需背景，再以如今不同的看法收尾。不要暗示个人经历能证明普遍规律。

heading.en: Choose One Moment Instead of a Whole Biography
heading.zh: 选一个时刻，而非讲完整人生

body.en:
Start with an event that changed a plan: a missed audition, a difficult move, or a conversation that altered a relationship. The moment should matter to you and be understandable to a viewer who lacks your full history.

Write the story’s point in one sentence before drafting. If you need several unrelated anecdotes to explain it, narrow the scope.
body.zh:
从改变计划的事件开始：错过试镜、艰难搬家，或改变关系的一场谈话。这个时刻对你重要，也应让不了解你全部经历的观众听得懂。

动笔前用一句话写明故事要点。若需要多个无关轶事才能说明，就缩小范围。

heading.en: Give Just Enough Context and a Clear Turning Point
heading.zh: 提供必要背景和明确转折

body.en:
Explain who was involved, what you expected, and what was at risk. Then describe the decision or fact that changed the course. Keep details that help viewers picture the event; remove background that does not affect it.

Distinguish what you remember from what you later learned or inferred.
body.zh:
交代相关人物、当时预期和利害，再描述改变走向的决定或事实。保留帮助观众想象事件的细节，删去不影响事件的背景。

区分你记得的事实与之后才得知或推断的内容。

heading.en: End with a Grounded Takeaway
heading.zh: 以有依据的收获收尾

body.en:
State what changed for you or what question remains. Avoid turning a personal outcome into advice that ignores different circumstances.

If the story includes other people, protect private details and avoid attributing motives you cannot know. End on a concrete action, reflection, or question tied to the opening.
body.zh:
说明自己改变了什么，或仍有什么疑问。不要把个人结果直接变成无视他人处境的建议。

若故事涉及他人，保护隐私，也不要断言自己无法确定的动机。结尾用与开篇相连的行动、反思或问题收住。

q.en: Should personal story videos include a lesson?
q.zh: 个人经历视频一定要有教训吗？

a.en: No. A specific reflection or open question can be enough. Make the connection to the event clear without claiming your response is universal.
a.zh: 不必。具体反思或开放问题就足够。说明它和事件的关系，但别宣称自己的回应普遍适用。

text.en: Use story and narration planning to separate what happened, what you inferred, and what the viewer should take away.
text.zh: 用故事与旁白规划区分发生事实、个人推断和观众收获。

title.en: How to Self-Edit a Novel Before You Share It
title.zh: 小说怎么自我编辑：给读者看之前的检查步骤

seo_title.en: How to Self-Edit a Novel

description.en: Use separate passes for structure, scene purpose, continuity, prose, and proofreading.
description.zh: 分轮检查结构、场景作用、前后连续、文字和错字。

answer.en: Self-editing works best as focused passes. Read for the whole story, then check scene purpose, continuity, sentence clarity, and mechanical errors separately.
answer.zh: 自我编辑适合分轮进行：先通读全篇，再分别检查场景作用、前后连续、句子清晰度和文字错误。

heading.en: Read for the whole experience
heading.zh: 先检查整体阅读体验

body.en: Read without polishing every paragraph. Note confusion, boredom, surprise, and engagement. Look for missing setup, repeated beats, and a middle that does not build toward the ending. Turn each note into a question about what readers need to know and what changes in the chapter.
body.zh: 先通读，不要逐段润色。记录困惑、乏味、意外或投入的地方，留意缺少铺垫、情节重复，以及没有朝结尾推进的中段。把批注变成问题：读者需要知道什么？本章发生了什么变化？

heading.en: Edit one kind of problem at a time
heading.zh: 一次处理一种问题

body.en: Make one pass for structure, one for continuity in names, dates, knowledge, and objects, then one for clarity and repetition. Keep a style sheet for decisions that must stay consistent.
body.zh: 先检查结构，再检查姓名、日期、认知和物件连续性，最后调整清晰度和重复表达。用风格表记录必须保持一致的决定。

heading.en: Proofread when content is stable
heading.zh: 内容稳定后再校对

body.en: Check repeated words, dialogue punctuation, tense shifts, and formatting. Read a formatted copy too; page breaks and dialogue layout reveal problems hidden in a draft. Ask a trusted reader specific questions.
body.zh: 检查重复用词、对话标点、时态跳变和格式。也要查看排版稿；分页和对话布局会暴露草稿中不明显的问题。向可信读者提出具体问题。

q.en: How many times should I edit my novel?
q.zh: 小说需要编辑几遍？

a.en: There is no fixed number. Stop when a focused pass no longer finds meaningful story, clarity, or consistency problems and the manuscript meets your sharing goal.
a.zh: 没有固定次数。当针对性检查已找不到明显的故事、表达或连续性问题，且稿件达到分享目标时就可以停。

text.en: Use the oh-story workflow to plan, draft, and revise the work while keeping decisions and consistency visible.
text.zh: 使用 oh-story 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Find and Fix Plot Holes in a Story
title.zh: 怎么发现并修补故事里的情节漏洞

seo_title.en: Find and Fix Plot Holes

description.en: Trace what each character knows and does, then repair missing causes, impossible timing, and unsupported solutions.
description.zh: 追踪人物的认知与行动，修补缺失原因、不可能的时间安排和缺少铺垫的解法。

answer.en: A plot hole is a contradiction or missing cause that makes an event hard to believe. Map who knows what, when events happen, and what each choice costs. Repair the broken link while preserving character agency and the central conflict.
answer.zh: 情节漏洞是会让重要事件难以相信的矛盾或缺失因果。梳理每个人何时知道什么、事件何时发生、每次选择付出什么代价，再修补断裂环节，同时保留人物能动性和核心冲突。

heading.en: Map knowledge and timing
heading.zh: 梳理认知和时间

body.en: List what each important character knows in major scenes and how they learned it. Check travel time, deadlines, injuries, money, and access against the timeline. A gap appears when the story uses information without showing how it arrived.
body.zh: 列出重要场景中每个人知道什么，以及如何得知。对照时间线核查路程、期限、伤势、金钱和场所权限。故事使用了却没交代来源的信息，就会形成断层。

heading.en: Test convenient solutions
heading.zh: 检验看似方便的解法

body.en: Trace each solution backward. Was the needed skill, object, relationship, or rule introduced? Could the character use it here? What cost or limit keeps it from solving every problem? Show the earlier rule when an exception changes it.
body.zh: 反向追查解法：所需技能、物件、关系或规则是否出现？人物此时能否使用？什么代价或限制能防止它解决所有问题？例外改变规则时，要让读者看见原规则。

heading.en: Repair the broken link
heading.zh: 修补断裂环节

body.en: Add a clue, decision, limit, or consequence where the chain breaks. Avoid a new coincidence that moves the gap elsewhere. Keep the fix consistent with what the character knows and wants.
body.zh: 在因果链断开的地方补充线索、决定、限制或后果。别再加一个只把漏洞挪到别处的巧合。修复要符合人物的认知和目标。

q.en: Do readers notice every plot hole?
q.zh: 读者会发现每个情节漏洞吗？

a.en: Readers vary, but contradictions around the protagonist goal, a major solution, or the ending tend to matter most. Fix what changes story logic or emotional payoff.
a.zh: 读者在意程度不同，但涉及主角目标、关键解法和结尾的矛盾通常最重要。优先修复会改变故事逻辑或情感回报的问题。

text.zh: 使用 oh-story 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Use Dialogue Tags Without Distracting Readers
title.zh: 对话标签怎么用：让读者顺畅读下去

seo_title.en: How to Use Dialogue Tags

description.en: Use simple speech tags for clarity, action beats for movement, and alternatives only when they add meaning.
description.zh: 用简单标签保证清晰，用动作承接节奏，只在能增加含义时变化表达。

answer.en: Dialogue tags identify the speaker; action beats show what a character does while speaking. Use said or asked when needed, omit tags when clear, and let action carry meaningful movement.
answer.zh: 对话标签说明谁在说话，动作承接展示说话时人物在做什么。需要时用“说”“问”，轮次清楚时可以省略；让动作承担有意义的变化。

heading.en: Tag unclear speakers
heading.zh: 发言人不清楚时标出来

body.en: In a two-person exchange, establish the first speaker and tag again when an action could obscure the turn. In a group, use names before readers have to guess. Read aloud to check each turn.
body.zh: 两人对话先明确开口者；动作可能模糊轮次时，再补标签。多人场景在读者需要猜之前就用名字标清楚。朗读检查每轮是否容易跟上。

heading.en: Let action beats do real work
heading.zh: 让动作承载有效信息

body.en: An action beat can reveal hesitation or change conversational power. Keep it near the line it supports and make it physically possible. Repeated gestures become filler and may contradict the words.
body.zh: 动作承接可以表现犹豫或改变谈话力量对比。把它放在对应台词旁，并确认动作做得到。重复动作会变成填充，还可能与台词矛盾。

heading.en: Keep tags compatible with speech
heading.zh: 让标签符合说话方式

body.en: Use whispered or shouted when volume matters. A character cannot smile a sentence; put the smile in an action beat. Use unusual tags only when they add information.
body.zh: 音量重要时用“低声说”或“喊道”。人物不能“微笑着一句话”，应把微笑写成动作。只有能增加信息时才用不寻常的标签。

q.en: Should I avoid the word said?
q.zh: 应该避免反复用“说”吗？

a.en: No. Familiar tags are easy to read. Vary sentence structure or add a useful action when the scene needs a new beat.
a.zh: 不必。常见标签容易阅读。场景需要新节奏时，可以改变句式或加入有作用的动作。

title.en: How to Write Smooth Transitions Between Chapters
title.zh: 章节之间怎么衔接：让读者愿意翻页

seo_title.en: Chapter Transitions That Flow

description.en: End chapters on a meaningful change and open the next with a clear time, viewpoint, or goal cue.
description.zh: 让章节以有意义的变化收尾，并在下一章标清时间、视角或目标。

answer.en: A smooth chapter transition carries a consequence, question, or changed goal forward while orienting readers in the next scene. Signal a cut, time jump, or viewpoint change and avoid recapping the previous chapter.
answer.zh: 顺畅的章节衔接会延续后果、疑问或变化后的目标，同时帮助读者进入下一场景。无论切章、跳时还是换视角，都要提示清楚，避免复述上一章。

heading.en: Carry a change across the cut
heading.zh: 让变化跨过切章点

body.en: Choose what readers carry: unfinished action, new information, a promise, or a relationship shift. End after it lands; begin where its consequence appears. The link can be emotional or causal.
body.zh: 决定要让读者带走什么：未完行动、新信息、承诺或关系转变。变化落地后结束旧场景，在后果显现处开启下一章。关联可以是情绪或因果。

heading.en: Orient readers after a jump
heading.zh: 跳转后帮助读者定位

body.en: After changing time or viewpoint, establish when and where the scene occurs and whose experience anchors it. A concrete detail can do more than recap. Connect a new thread to an existing question.
body.zh: 跳过时间或切换视角后，先交代时间、地点和体验中心人物。一个具体细节往往比回顾更有效。新线索要关联已有问题。

heading.en: Vary handoffs and cut repetition
heading.zh: 变化衔接方式，删掉重复

body.en: Alternate direct continuation, a consequence scene, and a purposeful time jump. Read the previous ending with the next opening; add orientation if unclear, or start later if it only recaps.
body.zh: 交替使用直接延续、展示后果和有目的的时间跳跃。连读上一章结尾和下一章开头；关系不清就补定位信息，如果只在复述就从更晚处开始。

q.en: Should every chapter end with a cliffhanger?
q.zh: 每章结尾都要留悬念吗？

a.en: No. A decision, discovery, emotional shift, or completed mini-goal can create forward pull. Repeating danger at every ending makes rhythm predictable.
a.zh: 不必。决定、发现、情感变化或完成阶段目标都能带来前进感。每章结尾都写危险会让节奏变得可预测。

title.en: How to Write Description in Fiction Without Slowing the Scene
title.zh: 小说描写怎么写：有画面又不拖慢情节

seo_title.en: Write Better Fiction Description

description.en: Choose details that shape mood, reveal viewpoint, or affect action; cut details that do none of those jobs.
description.zh: 选择能塑造氛围、体现视角或影响行动的细节，删掉没有这些作用的描写。

answer.en: Effective description filters a place or person through viewpoint and scene purpose. Choose details that affect mood, reveal attention, or change what someone can do.
answer.zh: 有效描写会通过视角人物和场景目的筛选地点与人物细节。挑选能影响氛围、体现注意力或改变行动可能性的细节。

heading.en: Describe what the viewpoint notices
heading.zh: 写视角人物注意到的东西

body.en: A nervous character may notice the exit, while a carpenter notices a damaged hinge. These choices reveal the room and observer without listing everything. Use details that fit the character’s experience.
body.zh: 紧张的人可能留意出口，木匠则注意损坏的合页。这些选择既呈现场景，也呈现观察者，不必罗列一切。选符合人物经验的细节。

heading.en: Tie details to mood and action
heading.zh: 让细节连上情绪和行动

body.en: A wet floor can make retreat risky; a familiar smell can recall a promise. Choose details that change what a character feels, notices, or can do. If nothing changes, the detail may not be needed.
body.zh: 湿滑地面令撤退危险，熟悉气味让人想起承诺。选择会改变人物感受、注意或行动可能性的细节。如果什么都没改变，这处描写可能不需要。

heading.en: Control density and placement
heading.zh: 控制密度和位置

body.en: Orient readers with one or two details, then add more as characters interact with the space. Break dense description with movement or dialogue. Keep images that support the emotional turn and trim the rest.
body.zh: 先用一两处细节帮助读者定位，再随着人物与空间互动补充信息。用动作或对话打断密集描写，保留支撑情绪转折的画面，删去冗余。

q.en: How much description should a novel have?
q.zh: 小说描写写多少合适？

a.en: Enough to orient readers and shape the scene. Add detail when it changes attention, mood, or action; cut passages that pause the story without a clear effect.
a.zh: 以帮助读者定位并塑造场景体验为准。细节能改变注意力、氛围或行动时就写；若只让故事暂停且没有明确效果，就删减。

title.en: How to Write a Novella: Plan a Focused Story for a Shorter Length
title.zh: 中篇小说怎么写：为较短篇幅规划完整故事

seo_title.en: How to Write a Novella

description.en: Build around one main change, a compact cast, and scenes that serve the same central line.
description.zh: 围绕一个核心变化、精简人物群和共同服务主线的场景，规划中篇小说。

answer.en: A novella has room for a full arc but less space for sprawling subplots. Choose one central change, limit competing goals, and make each scene advance the same pressure line. Length conventions vary by market.
answer.zh: 中篇小说篇幅较短，仍需完成完整弧线，但不适合铺开过多支线。选定一个核心变化，限制相互竞争的目标，让每场戏都推进同一条压力线。篇幅惯例因市场而异。

heading.en: Choose one central transformation
heading.zh: 选定一个核心变化

body.en: Describe what changes for the protagonist and what pressure forces it. A narrow time period, location, or relationship can create depth without many plotlines. Remove subplots that do not affect the choice or ending.
body.zh: 说明主角会发生什么变化，以及什么压力迫使其改变。限定时间段、地点或关系，能在不增加大量支线时做出深度。删掉不影响主角选择或结局的支线。

heading.en: Keep cast and settings purposeful
heading.zh: 让人物和场景各有作用

body.en: Give major characters distinct roles in the conflict. Combine characters with the same story function. Reuse a place when returning changes its meaning or power balance.
body.zh: 让重要人物在冲突中各有作用。承担相同叙事功能的人物可以合并。若重返某地会改变含义或力量关系，就重复使用它。

heading.en: Outline by turning points
heading.zh: 按转折规划

body.en: Mark the inciting pressure, first commitment, midpoint change, decisive choice, and aftermath. Give each beat the space it needs rather than forcing equal chapter lengths. Check that the ending answers the opening question.
body.zh: 标出触发压力、首次投入、中点变化、关键决定和后续影响。按转折所需分配篇幅，不必强求章节等长。检查结尾是否回答开篇问题。

q.en: How many words should a novella be?
q.zh: 中篇小说应该多少字？

a.en: Definitions differ by publisher, contest, and language. Check your intended market, then make sure the scope gives the central conflict a satisfying beginning, turn, and resolution.
a.zh: 出版社、比赛和语言市场的定义各不相同。先查目标渠道要求，再确认篇幅能让核心冲突有完整开端、转折和解决。

title.en: How to Write a Book Blurb That Makes Readers Curious
title.zh: 书籍简介怎么写：让读者想知道接下来会怎样

seo_title.en: How to Write a Book Blurb

description.en: Introduce the protagonist, disruption, stakes, and hook without summarizing the whole plot.
description.zh: 介绍主角、变故、利害和钩子，不要总结完整情节。

answer.en: A book blurb sells the reading experience with a protagonist, inciting problem, stakes, and a question readers want answered. Use concrete details, match the genre, and stop before major reveals.
answer.zh: 书籍简介通过主角、触发问题、利害和读者想知道的问题呈现阅读体验。使用具体细节，匹配作品类型，并在重要揭晓前停笔。

heading.en: Lead with character and disruption
heading.zh: 从人物和变故切入

body.en: Name the protagonist in a way that suggests identity or desire, then show what disrupts the life they expected. Avoid many names, invented terms, or a paragraph of history. Choose details readers can picture.
body.zh: 介绍主角时带出身份或渴望，再说明什么打破了原有生活。避免开头堆多个姓名、生造术语或大段背景史。选择读者容易想象的细节。

heading.en: Make stakes and hook clear
heading.zh: 说清利害与钩子

body.en: Explain what the protagonist could lose, what they must do, and why it is difficult. A hook may be an impossible choice, dangerous deadline, or relationship that complicates the goal. Do not promise what the book does not deliver.
body.zh: 说明主角可能失去什么、必须做什么，以及处境为何困难。钩子可以是两难选择、危险期限或让目标更复杂的关系。不要过度承诺。

heading.en: Stop before the answer
heading.zh: 在答案揭晓前结束

body.en: Stop when readers understand the conflict but do not know its outcome. Remove names and subplots unless they sharpen the dilemma. Replace explanations that need a world guide with concrete actions or consequences.
body.zh: 在读者理解冲突、却不知道结果时收住。除非人名和支线能强化困境，否则删去。把依赖设定表的解释换成具体行动或后果。

q.en: Should a book blurb reveal the ending?
q.zh: 书籍简介要透露结局吗？

a.en: Usually not. Reveal enough setup to make the central choice clear, then leave the outcome and consequential turn for the reading experience.
a.zh: 通常不必。透露足以说明核心选择的背景，然后把结果和重要转折留给正文。

title.en: How to Create a Character Profile That Helps You Write
title.zh: 人物档案怎么做：让设定真正帮助写作

seo_title.en: Create a Character Profile

description.en: Record character facts that shape choices, relationships, voice, or continuity in the story.
description.zh: 只记录会影响人物选择、关系、表达或前后连续的设定。

answer.en: A useful character profile is a working reference, not a biography. Record the goal, pressure, habits, relationships, voice, and facts that affect scenes. Mark uncertain details as open so guesses do not become canon.
answer.zh: 好用的人物档案是创作参考，不是完整传记。记录人物目标、压力、习惯、关系、表达方式和会影响场景的事实。未确定的内容标为待定，避免把猜测写成定论。

heading.en: Start with story-facing facts
heading.zh: 先记与故事有关的事实

body.en: Record the current goal, strongest pressure, resources, limits, and belief guiding choices. Separate observable facts from interpretation, such as avoids calls versus fears rejection.
body.zh: 记录人物当前目标、最大压力、资源、限制和指导选择的信念。区分可观察事实与解释，例如“回避打电话”与“害怕被拒绝”。

heading.en: Capture voice and relationships
heading.zh: 记录表达方式和关系

body.en: Use a sample line to note vocabulary, rhythm, humor, and what the character will not say directly. Map relationships by trust, conflict, and unmet expectations rather than writing a full life history.
body.zh: 用一句示例台词记录词汇、节奏、幽默感和人物不愿直说的内容。用信任、冲突和未满足的期待描述关系，不必写完整生平。

heading.en: Update the profile from the draft
heading.zh: 根据正文更新档案

body.en: After a major scene, add facts established in the manuscript or decisions you intend to keep. Mark contradictions for review. Remove details that never influence a scene, relationship, or continuity check.
body.zh: 重要场景后只补充正文已确立或打算保留的事实。标记矛盾供复核。删去从未影响场景、关系或连续性检查的内容。

q.en: What should a character profile include?
q.zh: 人物档案应该写什么？

a.en: Include facts that guide a scene: what the character wants, fears, knows, can do, and how they sound. Add backstory only when it shapes a present choice or continuity.
a.zh: 记录能指导场景的内容：人物想要什么、害怕什么、知道什么、会做什么，以及说话方式。只有影响当下选择或连续性的背景才需要加入。

title.en: How to Write a Novel Epilogue That Feels Earned
title.zh: 小说尾声怎么写：让结局后的补充有意义

seo_title.en: How to Write a Novel Epilogue

description.en: Show a meaningful consequence after the climax without reopening conflicts the ending has resolved.
description.zh: 展示高潮之后的重要变化，同时别重开结尾已经解决的冲突。

answer.en: An epilogue earns its place by showing a consequence, relationship change, or future direction the climax cannot show in the moment. Keep it focused and consistent with the ending.
answer.zh: 尾声应展示高潮当下无法呈现的后果、关系变化或未来方向。聚焦主题，并与结尾保持一致。

heading.en: Show what the climax cannot
heading.zh: 展示高潮无法呈现的变化

body.en: Readers may need to see what a choice costs, how a bond changes, or what the protagonist builds next. Choose one consequence instead of recapping the whole cast. Deepen the ending’s meaning rather than reverse its emotional answer.
body.zh: 读者可能想看到选择的代价、关系如何变化，或主角接下来建立什么。选一个后果展示，不必逐个汇报所有人物。尾声应加深结尾含义，不要推翻情感答案。

heading.en: Choose a useful time distance
heading.zh: 选择适合回报的时间距离

body.en: The next morning can show a difficult first step; a later jump can show lasting consequences. Use the shortest interval that makes change visible and plausible. Signal time and viewpoint clearly.
body.zh: 次日的场景可以展示艰难的第一步；更久之后可以呈现持续影响。选能让变化可信可见的最短间隔，并清楚标出时间和视角。

heading.en: End on a consequence
heading.zh: 以结果结束

body.en: Show a specific action or exchange that embodies change. Let readers infer ordinary details instead of explaining every career or loose thread. A new threat should not weaken closure unless a sequel hook is intended.
body.zh: 用具体行动或对话体现变化。普通细节可以留给读者推断，不必交代每个人的职业和所有支线。除非要引出续作，否则新威胁不应削弱收束。

q.en: How long should a novel epilogue be?
q.zh: 小说尾声应该多长？

a.en: As long as the new information needs. A brief scene can show a changed routine or relationship; skip a time jump that adds no story or emotional value.
a.zh: 以承载新信息所需为限。短场景足以展示日常或关系变化；若时间跳跃没有增加故事或情感价值，就省略。

title.en: How to Write a Tutorial Video Script People Can Follow
title.zh: 教程视频脚本怎么写：让观众跟得上每一步

seo_title.en: Write a Tutorial Video Script

description.en: Teach one outcome with a clear demo, short steps, visible results, and a recap viewers can use.
description.zh: 围绕一个结果安排演示、简短步骤、可见反馈和便于回看的总结。

answer.en: A clear tutorial video script promises one result, shows the finished state, and guides viewers through the smallest useful steps. Pair each instruction with an on-screen action, call out likely mistakes, then recap what to do when the process does not work.
answer.zh: 清晰的教程视频脚本先承诺一个结果，展示完成状态，再带观众走过必要步骤。每条说明都配屏幕操作，指出常见错误，并总结遇到问题时如何排查。

heading.en: Define the viewer’s starting point and result
heading.zh: 说清观众起点和目标

body.en: Name what viewers should be able to do by the end and what they need before starting. Show the target screen or finished object early so viewers can judge whether the tutorial answers their question.
body.zh: 说明观众看完应会做什么、开始前需要准备什么。尽早展示目标界面或成品，让观众判断教程是否解决自己的问题。

heading.en: Pair every instruction with a demonstration
heading.zh: 每条说明都配实际演示

body.en: Write one action per step and specify what appears on screen while the narrator explains it. Pause after a risky or unfamiliar choice; name the button, field, or decision viewers should look for.
body.zh: 每一步只安排一个操作，并写明旁白说明时屏幕上出现什么。遇到容易出错或不熟悉的选择要留出停顿，点明观众该找哪个按钮、字段或决定。

heading.en: Check the result and handle common errors
heading.zh: 核对结果并处理常见错误

body.en: After a key step, show the expected result and one sign that it went wrong. End with a short recap and a next action, not a second unrelated lesson. Test the script by following it without relying on knowledge you already have.
body.zh: 关键步骤后展示预期结果和一个错误信号。结尾用简短回顾和下一步收束，不要突然加入另一课题。试着不依赖已有经验照脚本操作，检查说明是否完整。

q.en: How long should a tutorial video be?
q.zh: 教程视频多长合适？

a.en: Use the time needed to teach the promised result clearly. Split unrelated tasks into separate videos, but keep steps together when viewers need them to finish one outcome.
a.zh: 以讲清承诺的结果所需时长为准。无关任务可拆成多条；若观众需要一组步骤才能完成同一个目标，就放在一起。

text.en: Use the video-recap workflow to plan, draft, and revise the work while keeping decisions and consistency visible.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Turn a Blog Post into a Video Script
title.zh: 怎么把博客文章改成视频脚本

seo_title.en: Turn a Blog Post into a Video

description.en: Keep the article’s useful claim, then rebuild it around spoken language, visual proof, and a clear viewer takeaway.
description.zh: 保留文章的核心价值，再围绕口语表达、画面证据和观众收获重写。

answer.en: Adapting an article for video means selecting its central promise, not reading the page aloud. Replace background-heavy passages with a spoken explanation, visual example, or demonstration, then order the points so each one earns the next.
answer.zh: 把文章改成视频，不是照着网页念。先提炼核心承诺，再把背景段落改成口头解释、画面案例或演示，并按一步步建立理解的顺序重排。

heading.en: Choose the one idea worth keeping
heading.zh: 选出最值得保留的一个观点

body.en: Write the viewer question and the article’s answer in one sentence each. Keep evidence and examples that support that answer; move side points to another video or a description link.
body.zh: 分别用一句话写出观众的问题和文章的答案。保留能支持答案的证据与案例；旁支内容另做视频或放到简介链接。

heading.en: Replace page structure with visual beats
heading.zh: 把文章结构改成画面节拍

body.en: A heading may become a question, comparison, screen capture, or before-and-after shot. For every spoken point, note what viewers can see that makes it easier to understand or believe.
body.zh: 小标题可以改成提问、对比、录屏或前后变化。每个口头观点都标注观众能看到什么，让它更容易理解或相信。

heading.en: Write for the ear and verify every claim
heading.zh: 按听觉写作并核对事实

body.en: Use shorter sentences, define terms at first use, and add transitions that explain why the next point follows. Compare the script with the source so simplification does not change the evidence or claim.
body.zh: 用更短的句子，首次出现术语时先解释，并补上说明下个观点为何接续的过渡。对照原文核查，确保简化表达没有改变证据或主张。

q.en: Can I use the article word for word as narration?
q.zh: 可以把文章原文直接当旁白吗？

a.en: Usually that sounds written rather than spoken. Preserve exact wording for quotations or technical terms, but rewrite the rest for clear listening and pair it with relevant visuals.
a.zh: 原文通常听起来像书面文章。引语或专业术语可以保留原句，其余内容应改成适合听的表达，并配上相关画面。

text.zh: 使用 video-recap 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Write a Montage Scene That Moves the Story Forward
title.zh: 蒙太奇场景怎么写：压缩时间也推进故事

seo_title.en: Write a Montage Scene

description.en: Use a montage to compress repeated work or time while showing a clear change in skill, pressure, or relationship.
description.zh: 用蒙太奇压缩重复行动或时间，同时呈现技能、压力或关系的明确变化。

answer.en: A montage earns its place when several brief images show progress, decline, or a pattern that would be slow as full scenes. Choose a starting state, a sequence of changing beats, and a result that affects the next scene.
answer.zh: 蒙太奇适合用一组短画面呈现进步、退步或反复模式，避免把缓慢过程写成完整场景。先确定起点，再安排变化节拍，最后让结果影响下一场戏。

heading.en: Choose what the sequence must change
heading.zh: 先确定这组镜头要改变什么

body.en: A montage can show training, preparation, routine, or a relationship shifting over time. State the before-and-after condition; if no meaningful state changes, one concise scene may work better.
body.zh: 蒙太奇可以呈现训练、准备、日常或关系随时间变化。先说清前后状态；如果没有重要变化，一场简洁的戏可能更合适。

heading.en: Make each beat add new information
heading.zh: 让每个节拍带来新信息

body.en: Vary the images through increasing difficulty, changing outcomes, a new obstacle, or a repeated action performed differently. Remove shots that only restate the same progress without raising a cost or revealing character.
body.zh: 通过难度递增、结果变化、新阻碍，或同一动作做法改变来区分画面。删掉只重复进展、既不增加代价也不揭示人物的镜头。

heading.en: Land on a consequence
heading.zh: 以明确后果落地

body.en: End on the proof or cost of the sequence: a successful performance, an exhausted character, a missed deadline, or a changed bond. Connect the final image to the next dramatic choice so the montage does not feel detachable.
body.zh: 以这段过程的成果或代价结束：成功表现、精疲力尽、错过期限或关系变化。把最后画面连到下一次戏剧选择，让蒙太奇真正属于故事。

q.en: Should a montage have dialogue?
q.zh: 蒙太奇需要对话吗？

a.en: Only when speech adds information or contrast that images cannot carry. Let action, sound, and changing details do most of the work when the sequence is meant to compress time.
a.zh: 只有当台词能补充画面无法表达的信息或对比时才需要。若蒙太奇的任务是压缩时间，就让动作、声音和变化细节承担主要表达。

text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Write a Scene Without Dialogue
title.zh: 没有对白的场景怎么写：让动作讲清楚

seo_title.en: Write a Scene Without Dialogue

description.en: Give a silent scene a goal, readable action, and a visible change so viewers can follow without explanation.
description.zh: 给无对白场景设置目标、可读动作和可见变化，让观众不用解释也能看懂。

answer.en: A dialogue-free scene still needs a clear want, obstacle, and change. Use gesture, object handling, distance, framing, and sound to show what the character tries and what the result means.
answer.zh: 没有对白的场景仍需清晰的目标、阻碍和变化。用手势、物件处理、距离、构图与声音呈现人物尝试，以及结果意味着什么。

heading.en: Make the character’s goal visible
heading.zh: 让人物目标可见

body.en: Show a concrete task such as hiding a letter, reaching a door, or returning an object. A viewer should understand what success looks like before the obstacle interrupts the attempt.
body.zh: 展示藏起信件、够到门把或归还物件等具体任务。阻碍出现前，观众就应能看懂成功是什么样子。

heading.en: Use objects and reactions as evidence
heading.zh: 用物件和反应传递证据

body.en: Let a prop reveal what changed, then show the character noticing and responding to it. Keep gestures distinct and motivated; a glance, pause, or choice of distance can carry more than a generic expression.
body.zh: 让道具揭示变化，再表现人物发现并作出回应。动作要明确且有动机；一个眼神、停顿或距离选择，往往胜过泛泛的表情。

heading.en: Check clarity without the script
heading.zh: 脱离剧本检查可读性

body.en: Watch the sequence with sound low or without reading dialogue notes. Can a viewer track the task, obstacle, and result? If not, simplify the blocking, sharpen the reaction, or add a visual clue before adding explanatory text.
body.zh: 把声音调低，或不看对白说明重看场景。观众能否跟上任务、阻碍和结果？如果不能，先简化调度、突出反应或补充视觉线索，再考虑说明文字。

q.en: Can a silent scene still show emotion?
q.zh: 无对白场景能表现情绪吗？

a.en: Yes. Let emotion change an action: a character grips, releases, avoids, or returns something differently. The shift in behavior gives viewers evidence to interpret.
a.zh: 可以。让情绪改变动作：人物以不同方式握住、放开、躲避或归还某物。行为的变化能给观众可判断的线索。

text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Design a Game Quest Chain with Escalating Stakes
title.zh: 游戏任务链怎么设计：让每一步都带来新变化

seo_title.en: Design a Game Quest Chain

description.en: Link quests through consequences, new decisions, and changing resources instead of repeating the same objective.
description.zh: 用后果、新决定和资源变化串联任务，避免反复做同一种目标。

answer.en: A strong quest chain lets each completed objective change what the player knows, can do, or risks next. Plan the initial promise, a consequence or complication after each quest, and a final choice that pays off the chain.
answer.zh: 有效的任务链会让每次完成目标都改变玩家的认知、能力或下一步风险。规划最初承诺、每个任务后的后果或复杂化因素，以及兑现整条任务线的最终选择。

heading.en: Give the chain one shared promise
heading.zh: 给整条任务线一个共同承诺

body.en: State the larger need behind the first request: protect a place, find someone, or change who controls a resource. Each quest can have its own reward, but should serve that larger line.
body.zh: 说清第一个委托背后的更大需求：保护某地、找到某人，或改变资源归属。每个任务可以有自己的奖励，但应服务同一条主线。

heading.en: Escalate through consequences
heading.zh: 用后果逐步升级

body.en: Let an outcome reveal new information, spend a resource, change an ally’s trust, or close one route while opening another. The next task should follow from that state change, not simply arrive from a new quest giver.
body.zh: 让任务结果揭示新信息、消耗资源、改变盟友信任，或关闭一条路线并打开另一条。下一项任务应从状态变化自然产生，而非又由陌生委托人凭空发布。

heading.en: Pay off the player’s accumulated choices
heading.zh: 兑现玩家一路积累的选择

body.en: Track important items, promises, and relationships across the chain. At the finale, let the player use that history to choose a method or accept a cost; show the result in the world afterward.
body.zh: 沿任务链记录重要物件、承诺和关系。到结尾时，让玩家利用这些经历选择方法或承担代价，并在之后的世界状态中呈现结果。

q.en: How many quests should a quest chain have?
q.zh: 一条任务链应该有几个任务？

a.en: Use as many as the player needs to understand the change and make the final choice. Combine steps that repeat the same action; split a step when it creates a distinct decision or consequence.
a.zh: 按玩家理解变化并作出最终选择所需安排。重复同一动作的步骤可以合并；若某一步带来独立决定或后果，就值得单列。

title.en: How to Storyboard a Dialogue-Heavy Scene
title.zh: 对白较多的场景怎么分镜：让谈话有画面变化

seo_title.en: Storyboard a Dialogue Scene

description.en: Use changes in attention, power, and reaction to choose shots instead of illustrating every line the same way.
description.zh: 根据注意力、力量关系和反应变化安排镜头，不要每句台词都用同一种拍法。

answer.en: A dialogue scene needs visual beats that reveal who has attention, leverage, or a changed understanding. Mark the turns in the conversation first, then choose coverage that makes those changes readable without cutting mechanically on every line.
answer.zh: 对白场景需要通过画面呈现谁掌握注意力、筹码或新的理解。先标出谈话转折，再安排能让变化清晰可读的镜头，不必每句台词都机械切换。

heading.en: Mark the turns before choosing shots
heading.zh: 选镜头前先标出谈话转折

body.en: Identify the opening balance, the line or action that shifts it, and the scene’s final state. A pause, interruption, withheld answer, or new evidence can be a stronger visual beat than another line of dialogue.
body.zh: 确定开场的力量关系、改变关系的台词或动作，以及结束时的状态。停顿、打断、避而不答或新证据，可能比又一句台词更值得成为画面节拍。

heading.en: Choose coverage for information and reaction
heading.zh: 按信息与反应安排镜头

body.en: Use a two-shot when shared space matters, a closer view when a reaction changes meaning, and an insert when an object carries evidence. Keep eyelines and screen direction consistent so the exchange remains easy to follow.
body.zh: 空间关系重要时用双人镜头；反应改变台词含义时靠近人物；物件承载证据时安排特写。保持视线和画面方向一致，让谈话易于跟上。

heading.en: Vary rhythm without hiding performance
heading.zh: 变化节奏，但别遮住表演

body.en: Hold on a speaker through a decisive line when their performance carries the turn. Cut to a listener when their response is the reveal. Review with dialogue muted: the visual progression should still show changing attention or control.
body.zh: 关键转折由说话者表演承载时，多留一拍；听者反应才是揭示时，就切到听者。静音回看，画面仍应传达注意力或控制权的变化。

q.en: Should every line of dialogue get its own shot?
q.zh: 每句对白都要单独切一个镜头吗？

a.en: No. Group lines that share one beat and cut when attention, information, or power changes. Fewer motivated shots often preserve performance better than constant coverage changes.
a.zh: 不必。属于同一节拍的台词可以放在同一镜头，等注意力、信息或力量关系改变时再切。少而有动机的镜头往往更能保留表演。

title.en: How to Adapt a Web Novel Chapter into a Short-Drama Episode
title.zh: 怎么把网文一章改成短剧一集

seo_title.en: Adapt a Novel Chapter for Short Drama

description.en: Keep the chapter’s dramatic turn, convert interior change into playable action, and end on a consequence.
description.zh: 保留章节戏剧转折，把内心变化转成可表演行动，并以新后果收尾。

answer.en: To adapt a web-novel chapter for short drama, identify its turn and character choice, then build a playable scene sequence around visible goals and obstacles. Compress repeated explanation while preserving the cause that makes the ending land.
answer.zh: 改编网文一章为短剧时，先找出章节转折和人物选择，再围绕可见目标与阻碍搭建场景。压缩重复解释，同时保留让结尾成立的因果。

heading.en: Find the chapter’s dramatic job
heading.zh: 找出章节承担的戏剧任务

body.en: Summarize what changes by the end: a secret is exposed, an alliance breaks, or the protagonist commits to a risky plan. Keep events that cause or test this change; move unrelated explanation elsewhere or remove it.
body.zh: 概括章末发生了什么变化：秘密揭开、同盟破裂，或主角决定冒险。保留造成或检验变化的事件，把无关解释移到别处或删掉。

heading.en: Turn interior narration into behavior
heading.zh: 把内心叙述转成行动

body.en: Translate thoughts into a visible choice, withheld response, changed tactic, or an object handled differently. Use dialogue when another person’s reaction changes the scene; do not make characters explain what both already know.
body.zh: 把想法转成可见选择、刻意不回应、策略变化，或人物处理物件的方式改变。只有当对方反应会改变场面时才用对白；别让人物解释彼此都知道的事。

heading.en: End with a playable next question
heading.zh: 用可继续演出的新问题收尾

body.en: Preserve the chapter’s payoff, then add a consequence that creates the next task, threat, or decision. Check that viewers can understand why it happens from the scenes you kept, even if they never read the source.
body.zh: 保留原章的情绪回报，再让后果带出下一项任务、威胁或决定。检查观众能否从保留的场景理解事情为何发生，即使他们没读过原文。

q.en: Should an adaptation keep every event from the chapter?
q.zh: 改编时要保留原章每件事吗？

a.en: No. Keep the events needed for the episode’s dramatic turn and causal clarity. Combine repeated beats, but preserve the setup that makes a choice or payoff understandable.
a.zh: 不必。保留推动单集转折和因果清晰所需的事件即可。可以合并重复节拍，但别删掉让人物选择或情绪回报成立的铺垫。

title.en: How to Introduce a Game Character Through Play
title.zh: 游戏角色怎么登场：让玩家通过行动认识人物

seo_title.en: Introduce a Game Character Through Play

description.en: Let a character’s first playable interaction show what they want, how they act, and what changes for the player.
description.zh: 用首次可玩的互动展示角色目标、做事方式和玩家处境变化。

answer.en: A memorable game-character introduction combines a readable action, a distinct response, and a useful change in the player’s options or understanding. Let players observe values through behavior before explaining backstory.
answer.zh: 令人记住的游戏角色登场，需要清楚的行动、鲜明的回应，以及玩家选项或认知的变化。先让玩家从角色行为看见其价值观，再补充背景。

heading.en: Give the character a clear first action
heading.zh: 给角色一个明确的首次行动

body.en: Show what the character chooses under pressure: protect a stranger, conceal a cost, or refuse an easy order. The action should be readable in play and reveal a trait relevant to the current problem.
body.zh: 展示角色在压力下如何选择：保护陌生人、隐瞒代价，或拒绝轻松的命令。行动要能在游玩中看懂，并揭示与当前问题有关的性格。

heading.en: Let the player respond or observe
heading.zh: 让玩家回应或观察

body.en: Give the player a small but meaningful way to react, ask, assist, or withhold help. If control stays with another character, make the playable objective reinforce the introduction instead of interrupting it.
body.zh: 给玩家一个小而有意义的回应方式：提问、帮忙或暂不出手。如果玩家操作主角，就让任务目标强化角色登场传达的信息，而非打断它。

heading.en: Pay off the introduction soon
heading.zh: 尽快兑现登场信息

body.en: Use the revealed trait in a later choice, mechanic, or relationship turn. This confirms the introduction mattered and lets players revise their first impression as new evidence appears.
body.zh: 在之后的选择、机制或关系转折中用上角色已展现的特质。这能证明登场信息有作用，也让玩家随新证据修正第一印象。

q.en: Should a game introduce a character with a cutscene?
q.zh: 游戏角色登场一定要用过场动画吗？

a.en: Not always. A short playable encounter can communicate personality and stakes while preserving agency. Use a cutscene when the current interaction cannot deliver necessary information or performance clearly.
a.zh: 不一定。简短的可玩遭遇也能传达性格和利害，同时保留玩家能动性。只有当当前互动无法清楚表达必要信息或表演时，才需要过场动画。

title.en: How to Design a Game Story Opening That Gets Players Moving
title.zh: 游戏剧情开场怎么设计：尽快让玩家开始行动

seo_title.en: Design a Game Story Opening

description.en: Introduce a goal, a reason to act, and a first playable choice before front-loading world history.
description.zh: 先交代目标、行动理由和首次可玩选择，再逐步展开世界背景。

answer.en: A strong game-story opening gives players a reason to act, a readable first objective, and a glimpse of the larger conflict. Deliver setting details through the task and its consequences so setup supports play instead of delaying it.
answer.zh: 好的游戏剧情开场先给玩家行动理由、清晰的首个目标和更大冲突的一角。通过任务及其后果传达设定，让故事铺垫支持玩法，而不是拖慢开始。

heading.en: Start with a concrete immediate goal
heading.zh: 从具体的眼前目标开始

body.en: Give the player something understandable to do: reach a person, protect an object, or escape a changing situation. A visible short-term goal helps players learn controls while the larger story remains a question.
body.zh: 给玩家一个容易理解的任务：找到某人、保护物件，或逃离正在变化的处境。可见的短期目标能帮助玩家学习操作，同时把更大故事留作疑问。

heading.en: Teach through a meaningful consequence
heading.zh: 通过有意义的后果教学

body.en: Introduce a rule through an action whose result matters to the scene. Let players see the outcome, then use the rule again with a changed risk or option so it feels like story information, not a detached instruction.
body.zh: 用会影响场面的行动结果介绍规则。先让玩家看见结果，再以不同风险或选项再次使用规则，使它成为故事信息，而非脱离情境的说明。

heading.en: Expand the world after engagement
heading.zh: 玩家投入后再展开世界

body.en: Add history, factions, and terminology when the next decision makes them relevant. End the opening sequence with a new question or changed plan that leads naturally into the main loop.
body.zh: 等玩家的下一项决定需要时，再补历史、阵营和术语。让开场序列以新问题或计划变化结束，自然接入核心玩法循环。

q.en: How much backstory should a game opening explain?
q.zh: 游戏开场应该解释多少背景？

a.en: Only what players need to understand the first goal and its immediate stakes. Introduce other facts when a later action, discovery, or choice gives them context.
a.zh: 只解释理解首个目标及眼前利害所需的信息。其他事实等后续行动、发现或选择赋予语境时再介绍。

text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Estimate Video Script Runtime from Word Count
title.zh: 怎么用字数估算视频脚本时长

seo_title.en: Estimate Video Script Runtime

description.en: Estimate narration time, then add room for pauses, demonstrations, transitions, and viewer comprehension.
description.zh: 先估算旁白时长，再为停顿、演示、转场和观众理解留时间。

answer.en: Estimate a video script’s runtime by dividing spoken words by a realistic delivery rate, then adding time for pauses and on-screen action. Read it aloud with the planned visuals; the final timing depends on performance and edit, not word count alone.
answer.zh: 用口播字数除以合理语速，再加上停顿和屏幕操作时间，估算视频脚本时长。配合计划画面朗读计时；最终时长还取决于表演和剪辑，不只由字数决定。

heading.en: Count spoken words separately
heading.zh: 单独统计口播内容

body.en: Separate narration from headings, captions, and shot notes. Choose a speaking rate that matches the format and speaker; a fast recap and a step-by-step tutorial need different room for comprehension.
body.zh: 把旁白与标题、字幕和镜头备注分开统计。按视频形式和说话者选择语速；快速解说和逐步教程需要不同的理解时间。

heading.en: Add time for what viewers watch
heading.zh: 为观众观看画面留出时间

body.en: Add pauses for demonstrations, reactions, examples, and transitions that do not have narration. A screen recording may need time for a cursor action; an emotional beat may need silence to land.
body.zh: 为没有旁白的演示、反应、案例和转场增加时间。录屏操作需要观众看清光标行动，情绪节拍也可能需要留白。

heading.en: Time a read with the actual sequence
heading.zh: 结合实际画面计时

body.en: Read at the intended delivery pace while following the shot outline. Mark rushed instructions and dead air, then cut or add material based on the viewer’s task rather than forcing an exact word target.
body.zh: 按预定语速配合镜头大纲朗读。标出太赶的说明和空等时间，再按观众任务增删内容，不要为了凑字数硬改。

q.en: How many words fit in a one-minute video?
q.zh: 一分钟视频能讲多少字？

a.en: It depends on language, speaking pace, pauses, and visuals. Time a sample read in the intended style, then use that rate as a planning estimate and verify it in an edit.
a.zh: 这取决于语言、语速、停顿和画面。按预定风格朗读一段样稿，以实测速度估算，再在剪辑中确认。

text.zh: 使用 video-recap 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Build a B-Roll Shot List from a Video Script
title.zh: 怎么根据视频脚本列 B-roll 镜头清单

seo_title.en: Build a B-Roll Shot List

description.en: Match supporting footage to claims, transitions, and moments where viewers need to see evidence.
description.zh: 把补充画面对准观点、转场，以及观众需要看见证据的时刻。

answer.en: Build a B-roll list by marking what each script beat needs viewers to understand, then choosing footage that proves, illustrates, or transitions that idea. Avoid generic coverage that decorates narration without adding context.
answer.zh: 先标出脚本每个节拍要让观众理解什么，再选能证明、说明或衔接观点的补充画面。避免使用只装饰旁白、没有增加语境的通用镜头。

heading.en: Mark the visual job for each beat
heading.zh: 标注每个节拍的画面任务

body.en: Label a line as evidence, example, context, emotion, or transition. That label helps decide whether you need a screen capture, location detail, archival image, object close-up, or no extra footage at all.
body.zh: 把旁白标为证据、案例、背景、情绪或转场。这个标签能帮助判断该用录屏、地点细节、资料影像、物件特写，还是根本不需要额外画面。

heading.en: List shots that support the claim
heading.zh: 列出能支撑观点的镜头

body.en: For each needed shot, note the subject, action, framing, source, and any rights or privacy check. Prefer footage that shows the relevant detail over a broad image that merely matches a keyword.
body.zh: 为每个镜头记录主体、动作、构图、来源，以及版权或隐私检查。优先选择呈现相关细节的画面，而不是只与关键词沾边的宽泛素材。

heading.en: Check coverage and repetition
heading.zh: 检查覆盖度和重复

body.en: Review the list beside the script. Confirm every important claim has suitable evidence and that repeated visuals do not make separate points feel identical. Track missing footage before recording or editing begins.
body.zh: 对照脚本检查镜头清单。确认重要观点有合适证据，并避免重复画面让不同观点看起来相同。在开拍或剪辑前记下缺失素材。

q.en: Does every line of narration need B-roll?
q.zh: 每句旁白都需要 B-roll 吗？

a.en: No. Stay on a speaker, graphic, or continuous scene when it carries the meaning. Add supporting footage when it clarifies a claim, gives needed context, or creates a deliberate transition.
a.zh: 不需要。说话者、图表或连续场景本身能传达意思时，可以继续保留。只有在画面能澄清观点、补足背景或完成有意转场时才加入素材。
