text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 将原作节拍转成可表演场景、分镜镜头和连续性清晰的制作参考。

title.en: How to Build a Scene-by-Scene Outline for a Movie Recap
title.zh: 如何为电影解说搭建逐场大纲

seo_title.en: Movie Recap Scene Outline

description.en: Track each scene's goal, turning point, new evidence, and emotional effect before writing narration.
description.zh: 写旁白前，梳理每场戏的目标、转折、新证据和情绪作用。

answer.en: A scene-by-scene recap outline records what the source shows and why each moment matters. Capture the scene's participants, goal, change, and evidence, then select only the events needed to deliver the recap's central promise.
answer.zh: 逐场解说大纲记录原片呈现了什么，以及每个时刻为何重要。记下场景人物、目标、变化和证据，再只选兑现解说核心承诺所需的事件。

heading.en: Log scenes from the source before interpreting them
heading.zh: 先依据原片记录场景，再作解读

body.en: Use timestamps and observable actions to describe what happens. Separate facts from interpretation so an early theory does not become a false recap claim.
body.zh: 用时间码和可观察行动描述事件。把事实与解读分开，避免过早形成的推测变成错误解说。

heading.en: Mark the change that earns a place in the recap
heading.zh: 标出值得纳入解说的变化

body.en: A scene may change the plan, reveal a relationship, add evidence, or shift the audience's question. If it repeats information without changing the story, summarize it briefly or omit it.
body.zh: 场景可能改变计划、揭示关系、增加证据或转变观众的问题。如果它没有带来变化，只重复已知信息，就简短带过或删去。

heading.en: Connect the chosen scenes with cause and evidence
heading.zh: 用因果和证据连接筛选后的场景

body.en: For each transition, state what the previous scene caused and what the next scene adds. Recheck source timestamps for key reveals and preserve the order that makes the story understandable.
body.zh: 每次转场都写清上一场造成什么、下一场增加什么。复核关键揭示的原片时间码，并保留便于理解的事件顺序。

q.en: Should a recap outline include every scene?
q.zh: 解说大纲需要记录所有场景吗？

a.en: Record enough to verify the story, then select scenes according to the video promise. A complete source map can be longer than the final outline or narration.
a.zh: 记录到足以核对故事即可，再按视频承诺筛选。完整原片地图可以比最终大纲和旁白更长。

text.en: Use video-recap to ground the script in source scenes and timestamps, then align narration, evidence, and editing.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 以原片场景和时间码为依据，再对齐旁白、证据与剪辑。

title.en: How to Choose Movie Clips That Support a Video Essay
title.zh: 如何挑选能支撑视频 essay 论点的电影片段

seo_title.en: Choose Clips for a Video Essay
seo_title.zh: 为视频 essay 选片段

description.en: Pair each claim with a verifiable scene detail and choose only the footage needed to show that evidence clearly.
description.zh: 为每个观点配上可核对的场景细节，只选择清晰呈现证据所需的画面。

answer.en: Choose a clip because it demonstrates a claim, not because it is recognizable or visually striking. Record the source and timestamp, state what the viewer should notice, and use the shortest excerpt that makes the evidence clear.
answer.zh: 片段应服务于论点，而非只因有名或好看。记录来源和时间码，说明观众该注意什么，并选用足以呈现证据的最短片段。

heading.en: Pair every claim with something visible or audible
heading.zh: 让每个观点对应可见或可听的证据

body.en: A claim about pacing might point to shot length; a claim about character can point to a gesture or repeated line. If the evidence is only in your explanation, revise the claim or find a better example.
body.zh: 关于节奏的观点可以指向镜头时长；关于人物的观点可以指向动作或重复台词。如果证据只能靠旁白说明，就调整观点或寻找更合适的例子。

heading.en: Keep source notes with the edit plan
heading.zh: 将来源记录和剪辑计划放在一起

body.en: Record the title, version, timestamp, and selected visual or sound detail. This makes it easier to verify accuracy when footage is moved, replaced, or shortened during editing.
body.zh: 记录片名、版本、时间码和选中的画面或声音细节。剪辑过程中移动、替换或缩短素材时，这些信息便于复核准确性。

heading.en: Use only enough footage to make the point
heading.zh: 只使用足以说明观点的画面

body.en: Introduce the evidence, give viewers time to observe it, then return to the argument. If a longer scene adds no new support, shorten it and explain the next point in your own words.
body.zh: 引出证据，留时间让观众观察，再回到论证。如果更长的场景没有增加支持，就缩短片段，并用自己的话讲下一个观点。

q.en: Can a montage support an analytical claim?
q.zh: 蒙太奇可以支持分析观点吗？

a.en: Yes, when the comparison is clear and the examples are labeled or contextualized. Make sure viewers can tell which detail in each shot supports the same claim.
a.zh: 可以，只要比较关系清晰，例子有标注或上下文。确保观众看得出每个镜头中的哪个细节支持同一观点。

text.en: Use video-recap to ground the script in source scenes and timestamps, then align narration, evidence, and editing.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 以原片场景和时间码为依据，再对齐旁白、证据与剪辑。

title.en: How to Build a Vertical Slice for a Story-Driven Game
title.zh: 如何为叙事游戏制作垂直切片

seo_title.en: Story-Driven Game Vertical Slice

description.en: Build one representative playable sequence to test the game's core action, story delivery, art direction, and technical risks.
description.zh: 制作一段有代表性的可玩流程，测试核心行动、叙事呈现、美术方向和技术风险。

answer.en: A vertical slice is a small, representative piece of a game built to test how its major parts work together. Choose one scene that exercises the core loop, player-facing story, visual target, and highest production risk, then define what evidence will count as success.
answer.zh: 垂直切片是用于检验游戏关键部分如何协同的一小段代表性内容。选择能覆盖核心循环、玩家可感知叙事、视觉目标和主要制作风险的场景，再设定何种证据代表成功。

heading.en: Choose a slice that represents the real game
heading.zh: 选择真正代表游戏的片段

body.en: Pick a sequence with a typical player action and a meaningful story response. A polished cinematic alone may not prove that exploration, choices, or combat can carry the intended experience.
body.zh: 选择一段包含典型玩家行动和有意义故事反馈的流程。单独打磨过场动画，无法证明探索、选择或战斗能否承载预期体验。

heading.en: Name the risk the prototype must answer
heading.zh: 明确原型必须验证的风险

body.en: The uncertainty may be whether a dialogue state can be tracked, an environment can teach a rule, or a mechanic can support a scene. Limit the slice so the team can test that question directly.
body.zh: 不确定点可能是对话状态能否追踪、环境能否教会规则，或某种机制能否服务场景。控制切片范围，让团队能直接验证问题。

heading.en: Review play evidence before polishing more
heading.zh: 先根据游玩证据复盘，再继续打磨

body.en: Watch players attempt the sequence and note where they hesitate, miss the story fact, or choose an unintended route. Use those observations to revise the interaction before expanding content.
body.zh: 观察玩家体验流程，记录他们何处犹豫、错过叙事信息或走上非预期路径。扩展内容前，先根据观察修改交互。

q.en: How long should a vertical slice be?
q.zh: 垂直切片应该多长？

a.en: Long enough to test the key interaction and production risk, but small enough to revise quickly. Define it by the question the team needs answered, not by a fixed playtime.
a.zh: 要足以测试关键交互与制作风险，同时短到可以快速修改。按团队要回答的问题来定范围，不必追求固定游玩时长。

text.en: Use novel-to-game to analyze source evidence, define player actions and story states, then test a playable adaptation.
text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 分析原作证据、定义玩家行动与故事状态，再测试可玩的改编方案。

title.en: How to Teach Game Controls Through the Story
title.zh: 如何通过游戏故事教会玩家操作

seo_title.en: Teach Game Controls Through Story

description.en: Introduce one action at a time through a believable situation, clear feedback, and a safe chance to try it.
description.zh: 在可信情境中逐步引入操作，并提供清晰反馈和安全的练习机会。

answer.en: A story-led tutorial teaches a control when the player has a reason to use it and can see the result. Introduce the action in context, let the player try it with low risk, and confirm success through readable feedback.
answer.zh: 当玩家有理由使用操作并能看见结果时，故事式教学才有效。在情境中引入动作，让玩家低风险尝试，再用清楚反馈确认成功。

heading.en: Teach a useful action at the moment it matters
heading.zh: 在操作真正有用时进行教学

body.en: A locked door can introduce interaction; an approaching threat can introduce movement or defense. Avoid teaching several unrelated controls in a pause that interrupts the story's urgency.
body.zh: 锁住的门可以引出互动操作，逼近的威胁可以引出移动或防御。避免在打断故事紧迫感的停顿中讲授一堆无关操作。

heading.en: Make the first attempt safe and observable
heading.zh: 让首次尝试安全且结果可见

body.en: Give players room to try, notice what happened, and try again without losing meaningful progress. The character's action and the game's response should make the control's effect clear.
body.zh: 给玩家尝试、观察结果并再次尝试的空间，不要让失败损失重要进度。人物行动与游戏反馈要清楚说明操作的效果。

heading.en: Fade help after the player demonstrates understanding
heading.zh: 玩家掌握后逐步撤去提示

body.en: Once the player succeeds in context, avoid repeating the full explanation. Later challenges can remix the same control with another rule, showing growth without turning the tutorial into a lecture.
body.zh: 玩家在情境中成功后，就别重复完整说明。后续挑战可把同一操作与新规则结合，在避免说教的同时体现成长。

q.en: Should every tutorial be part of the fiction?
q.zh: 所有教学都必须融入剧情吗？

a.en: No. A brief direct prompt can be clearer for accessibility or an uncommon control. Use story context when it helps players understand why the action matters.
a.zh: 不必。为了无障碍或说明少见操作，简短直接的提示可能更清楚。故事情境适合用来解释操作为何重要。

text.en: Use novel-to-game to analyze source evidence, define player actions and story states, then test a playable adaptation.
text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 分析原作证据、定义玩家行动与故事状态，再测试可玩的改编方案。

title.en: How to Storyboard an Action Scene for Short Drama
title.zh: 如何为短剧动作场面绘制分镜

seo_title.en: Storyboard a Short-Drama Action Scene

description.en: Make movement, geography, cause, and reaction readable across shots before creating or filming the sequence.
description.zh: 制作或拍摄动作场面前，让镜头间的移动、空间、因果和反应清晰可读。

answer.en: A readable action storyboard shows where each character begins, what changes, and how the next shot follows. Break movement into cause and response, keep key props visible, and reserve time for the audience to understand each result.
answer.zh: 清晰的动作分镜要说明人物起点、发生的变化，以及下一镜头如何承接。把动作拆成原因和反应，保持关键道具可见，并给观众理解结果的时间。

heading.en: Map the space before the movement
heading.zh: 先标出空间，再安排动作

body.en: Place doors, obstacles, and characters on a simple top-down sketch. Choose a screen direction and track who can see or reach each object before planning close shots.
body.zh: 用简单俯视图标出门、障碍和人物。决定画面方向，规划特写前先确认谁能看见或够到各个物件。

heading.en: Break the action into readable changes
heading.zh: 把动作拆成易懂的变化

body.en: Show the trigger, the character's move, the obstacle or counter-move, and the immediate result. Keep each shot focused on one important change instead of compressing several causes together.
body.zh: 呈现触发点、人物动作、障碍或反制，以及即时结果。每个镜头聚焦一个重要变化，别把多个因果挤在一起。

heading.en: Protect the reaction and aftermath
heading.zh: 保留反应和动作后果

body.en: A reaction can clarify fear, relief, or a changed plan. End the sequence with the new positions, injuries, missing prop, or open route the next scene depends on.
body.zh: 反应能说明恐惧、释然或计划变化。动作结束时交代新位置、伤势、失踪道具或下一场戏依赖的出口状态。

q.en: Do I need a separate storyboard frame for every movement?
q.zh: 每个动作都需要单独画一格分镜吗？

a.en: No. Draw when the audience's understanding or production plan changes. Combine continuous simple movement, and separate moments where a decision, impact, or reveal needs clear emphasis.
a.zh: 不需要。只在观众理解或制作安排发生变化时单独画格。简单连续动作可以合并；决定、碰撞或揭示需要强调时再分开。

text.en: Use drama-skills to turn source beats into performable scenes, storyboarded shots, and production references with clear continuity.
text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 将原作节拍转成可表演场景、分镜镜头和连续性清晰的制作参考。

title.en: How to Block a Two-Character Confrontation on Screen
title.zh: 如何调度银幕上的双人对峙

seo_title.en: Block a Two-Character Confrontation

description.en: Use distance, access, eyelines, and movement to show who has control as the conflict changes.
description.zh: 用距离、通道、视线和移动呈现冲突变化中的控制权。

answer.en: Blocking a confrontation is the planned position and movement of performers in a scene. Let distance, access to an exit or object, and changes in eyeline reflect each tactic, then check that camera coverage preserves the geography.
answer.zh: 对峙调度是预先设计场景中演员的位置和移动。用距离、出口或道具的掌控，以及视线变化表现策略，并检查镜头覆盖是否保留空间关系。

heading.en: Choose what each person controls
heading.zh: 明确每个人掌控什么

body.en: One character may control a doorway while the other holds evidence or the only key. Establish the advantage in the wide view so later movement has a clear meaning.
body.zh: 一人可能把守出口，另一人掌握证据或唯一钥匙。先用全景交代优势，让之后的移动有明确含义。

heading.en: Let position change with the tactic
heading.zh: 让站位随策略变化

body.en: A step closer can pressure; moving toward an exit can signal refusal. Change the distance when a tactic succeeds, fails, or gives someone new leverage, not simply to fill the frame.
body.zh: 靠近可以施压；走向出口可以表示拒绝。策略成功、失败或让人获得新筹码时再改变距离，不要只为填满画面而移动。

heading.en: Check eyelines and screen direction
heading.zh: 检查视线和画面方向

body.en: Keep sightlines consistent across coverage and know which side of the axis the camera occupies. Break the pattern only when a purposeful move helps the viewer feel the power shift.
body.zh: 不同镜头中的视线要连贯，并明确摄影机位于轴线哪一侧。只有有意改变能让观众感到权力转移时，才打破原有方向。

q.en: Should confrontations always get wider as they escalate?
q.zh: 对峙升级时镜头一定要越来越宽吗？

a.en: No. A close frame can increase pressure, while a wider frame may reveal a new exit or imbalance. Choose shot size for the information and feeling the beat needs.
a.zh: 不一定。近景能增加压迫感，全景则可揭示新出口或空间失衡。按节拍需要的信息和感受选择景别。

text.en: Use drama-skills to turn source beats into performable scenes, storyboarded shots, and production references with clear continuity.
text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 将原作节拍转成可表演场景、分镜镜头和连续性清晰的制作参考。

title.en: How to Make a Visual Continuity Guide for a Short Drama
title.zh: 如何为短剧制作视觉连续性指南

seo_title.en: Short-Drama Visual Continuity Guide

description.en: Record character, costume, prop, location, and lighting states that must match across generated or filmed shots.
description.zh: 记录生成或实拍镜头间必须一致的人物、服装、道具、地点和光线状态。

answer.en: A visual continuity guide is a compact reference for details that must remain consistent across scenes and shots. Track only story-visible facts, attach useful reference images, and update the guide when the script changes a character or prop state.
answer.zh: 视觉连续性指南是确保场景和镜头间细节一致的简明参考。只记录观众能看到且必须一致的事实，配上有效参考图；剧本改变人物或道具状态时同步更新。

heading.en: Record details that affect recognition or story
heading.zh: 记录影响辨认或剧情的信息

body.en: Note defining features, costume variants, held props, injuries, and location anchors. Avoid documenting every background detail; focus on what an audience might notice or what a later shot depends on.
body.zh: 记录辨识特征、服装变化、手持道具、伤势和地点锚点。不要记录所有背景细节；聚焦观众可能注意到或后续镜头依赖的内容。

heading.en: Label each reference by state and scene
heading.zh: 按状态和场景标注参考图

body.en: A single character may need separate images before and after a costume change or injury. Label when the reference applies and pair it with a scene or shot identifier to prevent accidental reuse.
body.zh: 同一人物在换装或受伤前后可能需要不同参考图。标明适用时点，并关联场次或镜头编号，避免误用。

heading.en: Update the guide with the production change
heading.zh: 制作内容变化时同步更新指南

body.en: When a prop breaks or a character learns new information, record the change at the correct point in story order. Review later shots against the updated state before approving continuity.
body.zh: 道具损坏或人物得知新信息时，按故事顺序记录变化。批准连续性前，用更新后的状态检查后续镜头。

q.en: Is a continuity guide the same as a character sheet?
q.zh: 连续性指南和人物设定表一样吗？

a.en: A character sheet defines who the person is and how they look. A continuity guide also tracks which version or state appears at a particular time in the story.
a.zh: 人物设定表定义人物身份与外观；连续性指南还要记录故事特定时点出现的是哪个版本或状态。

text.en: Use drama-skills to turn source beats into performable scenes, storyboarded shots, and production references with clear continuity.
text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 将原作节拍转成可表演场景、分镜镜头和连续性清晰的制作参考。

title.en: How to Write a Short Film Scene Without Dialogue
title.zh: 如何写出没有对白的短片场景

seo_title.en: Write a Silent Short-Film Scene

description.en: Tell a complete visual beat through a goal, readable actions, changed object states, and a final consequence.
description.zh: 用明确目标、易读动作、道具状态变化和最终后果完成视觉叙事。

answer.en: A scene without dialogue still needs a clear goal, resistance, and change. Give the audience observable clues, let action reveal the character's priorities, and make the final image show what the character has gained or lost.
answer.zh: 没有对白的场景仍需要清晰目标、阻力和变化。为观众提供可观察线索，让行动揭示人物优先考虑什么，并用最终画面展示人物得失。

heading.en: Pick a goal the audience can see
heading.zh: 选择观众看得见的目标

body.en: A person might try to hide a letter, repair a broken object, or reach someone before a door closes. Make progress and failure visible so viewers can follow without explanatory text.
body.zh: 人物可以试图藏起信件、修复破损物品，或赶在门关闭前找到某人。让进展和失败都可见，观众无需解释文字也能跟上。

heading.en: Use props and movement as evidence
heading.zh: 用道具和动作提供证据

body.en: Choose a few objects whose condition changes during the scene. A dry sleeve becoming wet or a key moving hands can communicate time, effort, and relationship without adding a sign or caption.
body.zh: 选几件会在场景中改变状态的物品。袖子由干变湿、钥匙换了主人，都能传达时间、努力和关系，无需增加标牌或字幕。

heading.en: End on a visible decision or cost
heading.zh: 以可见决定或代价收尾

body.en: Show the character leaving something behind, choosing who to help, or accepting a consequence. Let the final action resolve the question posed by the opening image.
body.zh: 呈现人物留下某物、选择帮助谁，或接受一个后果。让最后的动作回应开场画面提出的问题。

q.en: Can I use music or sound effects in a silent scene?
q.zh: 无对白场景可以使用音乐或音效吗？

a.en: Yes. “Silent” usually means no spoken dialogue. Sound can guide attention or carry a story fact, but do not let it explain what the image could show more clearly.
a.zh: 可以。“无对白”通常指没有口头台词。声音能引导注意或传达故事事实，但别用它解释本可由画面更清晰展示的内容。

text.en: Use drama-skills to turn source beats into performable scenes, storyboarded shots, and production references with clear continuity.
text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 将原作节拍转成可表演场景、分镜镜头和连续性清晰的制作参考。

title.en: How to Plan Camera Coverage for a Short-Film Scene
title.zh: 如何为短片场景规划摄影覆盖

seo_title.en: Plan Short-Film Camera Coverage

description.en: Decide which views protect the scene's geography, performance, key action, and essential information in the edit.
description.zh: 规划哪些镜头能在剪辑中保住场景空间、表演、关键动作和必要信息。

answer.en: Camera coverage is the set of views needed to shape a scene in the edit. Start from the scene's actions and turning point, then capture enough geography, performance, and detail to communicate what changes without collecting redundant angles.
answer.zh: 摄影覆盖是剪辑时塑造场景所需的一组镜头。先找场景动作和转折，再拍足以交代空间、表演和细节的素材，避免收集重复角度。

heading.en: Identify the moments the edit cannot lose
heading.zh: 找出剪辑绝不能丢失的时刻

body.en: Mark the line, movement, reaction, or reveal that changes the scene. Give each a clear shot plan, especially when continuity or a prop state makes the beat difficult to recreate.
body.zh: 标出改变场景的台词、动作、反应或揭示，并为每个时刻规划清晰镜头。连续性或道具状态难以复现时尤其如此。

heading.en: Cover geography and performance efficiently
heading.zh: 高效覆盖空间关系和表演

body.en: Capture a view that establishes positions, then closer performance angles that preserve eyelines and overlap. Add a separate insert only when it reveals a story fact or helps bridge an edit.
body.zh: 先拍交代位置的镜头，再拍保持视线和动作衔接的表演角度。只有特写揭示故事信息或帮助剪辑衔接时才单独补拍。

heading.en: Check for a complete edit path
heading.zh: 确认素材能组成完整剪辑路径

body.en: Ask whether the editor can move from setup to action to reaction and result. If a crucial transition has no coverage, plan a pickup or simplify the scene before production.
body.zh: 检查剪辑师能否从铺垫接到动作、反应和结果。如果关键转接没有素材，就安排补拍，或在制作前简化场景。

q.en: Does more coverage always make editing easier?
q.zh: 镜头拍得越多，剪辑就一定越容易吗？

a.en: No. Too many nearly identical angles can slow decisions and create continuity problems. Capture the views needed to tell the scene, plus useful options for performance and pace.
a.zh: 不一定。大量相近角度会拖慢选择，还可能产生连续性问题。拍好讲清场景所需的镜头，并为表演和节奏留少量有效选择。

text.en: Use drama-skills to turn source beats into performable scenes, storyboarded shots, and production references with clear continuity.
text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 将原作节拍转成可表演场景、分镜镜头和连续性清晰的制作参考。

title.en: How to Turn a Screenplay Beat into an AI Video Prompt
title.zh: 如何把剧本节拍改写成AI视频提示词

seo_title.en: Screenplay Beat to AI Video Prompt
seo_title.zh: 剧本节拍转AI视频提示词

description.en: Translate one playable action into a prompt with subject, starting state, movement, camera, and intended ending state.
description.zh: 将一个可表演动作转成提示词，写明主体、初始状态、运动、镜头和预期结束状态。

answer.en: Translate a script beat into a video prompt by isolating one visible action and its result. Specify the subject and starting state, movement and camera behavior, then the final state; keep dialogue and unrelated events out of the same prompt.
answer.zh: 把剧本节拍转成视频提示词时，先提取一个可见动作及其结果。写清主体和起始状态、运动与镜头方式，再写结束状态；避免将对白和无关事件塞进同一提示词。

heading.en: Choose one action the shot can show
heading.zh: 选择镜头能呈现的单一动作

body.en: A prompt works better when it asks for one beat, such as turning, reaching, or noticing. Split a sequence of separate actions into shots when the character's intention or camera position changes.
body.zh: 提示词只要求一个节拍，例如转身、伸手或察觉，通常更易控制。人物意图或机位变化时，把连续的不同动作拆成多个镜头。

heading.en: Describe start, movement, and end
heading.zh: 描述起始、运动和结束状态

body.en: State where the person and important props begin, what changes during the action, and the pose or object state at the end. This creates a checkable target for generation and editing.
body.zh: 说明人物和关键道具从何处开始、动作中有什么变化，以及结束时的姿势或物件状态。生成和剪辑便有可核对的目标。

heading.en: Separate performance from camera direction
heading.zh: 把表演要求和摄影指令分开

body.en: Describe what the character does and how the camera observes it in distinct phrases. Keep the shot's emotional purpose visible, and remove adjectives that do not affect action, look, or framing.
body.zh: 用不同短句分别描述人物动作和摄影机如何观察。明确镜头的情绪作用，删去不影响动作、风格或构图的形容词。

q.en: Should I put multiple camera moves in one prompt?
q.zh: 一个提示词里要写多个镜头运动吗？

a.en: Use one primary move unless a continuous move is essential to the beat. Multiple competing camera instructions can make the generated action difficult to read.
a.zh: 除非连续运动是节拍所必需，否则只写一种主要运动。多个互相竞争的摄影指令会让生成动作难以理解。

text.en: Use drama-skills to turn source beats into performable scenes, storyboarded shots, and production references with clear continuity.
text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 将原作节拍转成可表演场景、分镜镜头和连续性清晰的制作参考。

title.en: How to Fact-Check a Video Essay Before Editing
title.zh: 剪辑前如何核对视频 essay 的事实

seo_title.en: Fact-Check a Video Essay
seo_title.zh: 核对视频 essay 事实

description.en: Match factual claims to reliable source notes and footage timestamps before recording narration or building the final edit.
description.zh: 录制旁白或制作最终剪辑前，把事实观点对应到可靠资料和画面时间码。

answer.en: A fact-check sheet links each factual claim to its source, timestamp, and confidence. Separate what the source directly shows from interpretation, then verify names, dates, quotations, and causal claims before recording narration.
answer.zh: 事实核查表把每个事实观点关联到来源、时间码和可信程度。区分原片直接呈现与解读，并在录制旁白前核对姓名、日期、引语和因果判断。

heading.en: Break narration into checkable claims
heading.zh: 把旁白拆成可核查的观点

body.en: Review one claim at a time: a character's action, a date, a stated motive, or a production fact. Flag broad interpretations separately so they are not presented as direct evidence.
body.zh: 逐条检查人物行动、日期、明确动机或制作事实等观点。把宽泛解读单独标记，避免把它们当作直接证据呈现。

heading.en: Attach a source and exact location
heading.zh: 附上来源和准确位置

body.en: Record the source title or link, relevant page or timestamp, and a short note about what it supports. Recheck the original material when a quote or sequence order matters.
body.zh: 记录来源标题或链接、相关页码或时间码，以及它支持了什么。引语或事件顺序重要时，回到原始材料复核。

heading.en: Revise claims that outrun the evidence
heading.zh: 收窄超出证据范围的表达

body.en: Replace certainty with a supported description when sources disagree or leave a motive ambiguous. A precise claim makes the essay more credible and gives the edit clearer evidence to show.
body.zh: 来源不一致或动机不明时，把绝对结论改成证据支持的描述。准确观点更可信，也让剪辑更清楚地呈现证据。

q.en: Do opinions in a video essay need fact-checking?
q.zh: 视频 essay 中的观点也需要核查吗？

a.en: The interpretation is yours, but its factual basis should be checkable. Label opinion as analysis and verify the scene, quotation, or event it relies on.
a.zh: 解读可以是你的观点，但事实依据应可核对。把意见表述为分析，并核实它依赖的场景、引语或事件。

text.en: Use video-recap to ground the script in source scenes and timestamps, then align narration, evidence, and editing.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 以原片场景和时间码为依据，再对齐旁白、证据与剪辑。

title.en: How to Write a Movie Recap Opening That Sets Up the Story
title.zh: 如何写好电影解说开场并交代故事方向

seo_title.en: Write a Movie Recap Opening

description.en: Give viewers a clear reason to watch, establish the story situation, and move into the first essential event quickly.
description.zh: 告诉观众观看理由，交代故事情境，并迅速进入第一个关键事件。

answer.en: A movie recap opening should identify the viewing promise, orient the audience, and lead into the film's first necessary event. Start with a supported question or conflict, give only the context needed to follow, and avoid promising a twist the source does not deliver.
answer.zh: 电影解说开场要明确观看承诺、帮助观众定位，并引向影片第一个必要事件。用有依据的问题或冲突开场，只交代理解所需背景，不要承诺原片没有的反转。

heading.en: Choose a hook the source can support
heading.zh: 选择原片能够兑现的开场钩子

body.en: A strange choice, unresolved danger, or relationship question can create curiosity. Confirm that the film answers it and that the hook does not misstate who did what or when.
body.zh: 反常选择、未解危险或关系问题都能激发好奇。确认影片会回应这个问题，而且开场没有说错人物行为或时间。

heading.en: Orient viewers without retelling the whole premise
heading.zh: 交代必要背景，不必复述完整设定

body.en: Name the protagonist, immediate situation, and constraint only when the opening events require them. Let later scenes supply details at the moment they matter.
body.zh: 只有开场事件需要时，才说明主角、眼前状况和限制。其他细节留到后续场景真正用到时再交代。

heading.en: Move from promise to the first story beat
heading.zh: 从观看承诺进入第一个故事节拍

body.en: After the opening question, show what the character does and what changes. Cut repeated setup lines so viewers reach the film's actual movement rather than hearing the same premise twice.
body.zh: 提出开场问题后，讲清人物做了什么以及发生何种变化。删掉重复背景，让观众尽快进入影片实际推进，而非听两遍同一设定。

q.en: Should a recap opening spoil the ending?
q.zh: 解说开场该不该剧透结局？

a.en: Only when the video explicitly promises a full-story recap and the reveal is framed accurately. For a spoiler-free format, build curiosity around the setup without exposing the resolution.
a.zh: 只有当视频明确承诺完整剧情解说，且准确呈现揭示时才剧透。无剧透内容应围绕开端引发好奇，不暴露结局。

text.en: Use video-recap to ground the script in source scenes and timestamps, then align narration, evidence, and editing.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 以原片场景和时间码为依据，再对齐旁白、证据与剪辑。

title.en: How to Edit a Movie Recap Video for Clear Storytelling
title.zh: 如何剪辑电影解说，让故事更清楚

seo_title.en: Edit a Movie Recap for Clarity

description.en: Check chronology, visual evidence, narration overlap, and scene transitions in a recap edit.
description.zh: 检查解说剪辑中的时间顺序、画面证据、旁白重复和场景转接。

answer.en: Edit a movie recap by checking whether viewers can follow what happened, why it mattered, and what changed next. Verify chronology against the source, remove narration that repeats the image, and keep enough visual evidence for important claims.
answer.zh: 剪辑电影解说时，检查观众能否理解发生了什么、为何重要、接下来有什么变化。对照原片核实顺序，删去重复画面的旁白，并保留重要观点所需的视觉证据。

heading.en: Check the story chain before polishing transitions
heading.zh: 精修转场前先检查故事链

body.en: Follow the edit without reading the script. Mark any jump where a new character, motive, or consequence appears without enough context, then repair the narration or restore a needed source beat.
body.zh: 不看脚本，只跟着剪辑观看。标出人物、动机或后果突然出现而缺少上下文的跳跃，再修旁白或补回必要的原片节拍。

heading.en: Let images and narration do different jobs
heading.zh: 让画面和旁白承担不同任务

body.en: When a shot clearly shows an action, narration can explain its consequence or uncertainty rather than describe the same movement. Keep the voice-over when it adds context the footage cannot provide.
body.zh: 镜头已经清楚展示动作时，旁白可解释后果或不确定性，不必重复描述动作。画面无法提供的上下文则由旁白补充。

heading.en: Review reveals, names, and sound in context
heading.zh: 结合上下文检查揭示、姓名和声音

body.en: Watch important clues with the preceding and following shots. Confirm the right name and pronunciation, preserve a source sound that carries the beat, and ensure music does not hide key dialogue.
body.zh: 连同前后镜头一起观看关键线索。核对姓名和读音，保留承担叙事节拍的原片声音，并确保配乐没有盖住重要对白。

q.en: Should every scene from the film appear in the recap edit?
q.zh: 解说剪辑必须包含影片中的每场戏吗？

a.en: No. Keep scenes that deliver the promised story or prove an important point. Compress repeated beats while preserving causes, key reveals, and changes the next scene depends on.
a.zh: 不必。保留兑现故事承诺或证明重要观点的场景。可压缩重复节拍，但要保留后续依赖的原因、关键揭示和变化。

text.en: Use video-recap to ground the script in source scenes and timestamps, then align narration, evidence, and editing.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 以原片场景和时间码为依据，再对齐旁白、证据与剪辑。

title.en: When to Keep Original Film Audio in a Recap Video
title.zh: 电影解说什么时候该保留原片声音

seo_title.en: Use Original Audio in a Movie Recap

description.en: Keep source dialogue or effects when they carry emotion, evidence, or a beat narration would weaken.
description.zh: 当原片对白或音效承载情绪、证据或关键节拍时，保留它们而非用旁白削弱效果。

answer.en: Original film audio can carry performance, atmosphere, or evidence that narration cannot replace. Keep a source line or sound when viewers need to hear it directly, then give it room before or after the voice-over so the moment remains clear.
answer.zh: 原片声音能承载旁白无法替代的表演、氛围或证据。观众需要直接听到时就保留那句台词或声音，并在旁白前后留出空间，让时刻清晰呈现。

heading.en: Identify the sound's story job
heading.zh: 判断原片声音承担什么叙事作用

body.en: A whispered admission, a warning signal, or a sudden silence may be the evidence or emotional turn. Note what changes when you mute it; if the beat loses meaning, consider keeping the source audio.
body.zh: 低声承认、警告信号或突然安静，可能就是证据或情绪转折。试着静音看节拍失去了什么；若意义消失，就考虑保留原片声音。

heading.en: Give the source moment enough space
heading.zh: 为原片声音留出足够空间

body.en: Avoid talking over a line the audience must understand. Let dialogue or effect play, then use narration to connect the consequence or provide context that the shot alone cannot show.
body.zh: 观众必须听懂的台词上方不要压旁白。先让对白或音效完整呈现，再用旁白连接后果或补充画面无法说明的背景。

heading.en: Check the transition back to narration
heading.zh: 检查从原声切回旁白的衔接

body.en: Match loudness and ambience where needed, and avoid an abrupt cut that makes the moment feel accidental. Listen without watching the screen to catch clipped words or confusing overlaps.
body.zh: 必要时匹配音量和环境声，避免突兀切换让人觉得是失误。闭眼只听一遍，检查是否截断台词或产生混乱重叠。

q.en: Can I use original audio instead of narration for a whole scene?
q.zh: 整场戏都能用原片声音代替旁白吗？

a.en: Sometimes, if the scene itself carries the necessary action and context. Use narration where it clarifies a skip, time change, or causal link viewers would otherwise miss.
a.zh: 有时可以，只要场景本身包含必要行动和背景。观众可能错过时间变化或因果连接时，再用旁白说明。

text.en: Use video-recap to ground the script in source scenes and timestamps, then align narration, evidence, and editing.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 以原片场景和时间码为依据，再对齐旁白、证据与剪辑。

title.en: How to Write Branching Game Dialogue That Converges
title.zh: 如何写出可汇合的分支游戏对话

seo_title.en: Write Branching Dialogue That Converges
seo_title.zh: 写好可汇合的分支对话

description.en: Let dialogue choices change information, attitude, or resources while bringing branches back together without erasing player intent.
description.zh: 让对话选择改变信息、态度或资源，再自然汇合，避免抹去玩家意图。

answer.en: Convergent dialogue branches rejoin after a choice has made a meaningful difference. Decide what changes—knowledge, relationship, access, or cost—then carry that difference forward even when the next scene is shared.
answer.zh: 分支对话在选择产生有意义的差异后重新汇合。先决定变化的是认知、关系、权限还是代价；即使后续场景相同，也要延续这一差异。

heading.en: Define the branch's distinct outcome
heading.zh: 定义分支带来的不同结果

body.en: A choice can reveal a clue, change trust, or spend a resource. Record the immediate response and future state it sets so the branch is more than alternate wording before a reset.
body.zh: 选择可以揭示线索、改变信任或消耗资源。记录即时回应和后续状态，让分支不只是重置前的不同台词。

heading.en: Choose a sensible point of convergence
heading.zh: 选定合理的汇合点

body.en: Rejoin when characters reach the same necessary event, not before the choice has had time to register. Use a shared location or objective while allowing earlier branches to affect how it plays.
body.zh: 等人物抵达同一个必要事件后再汇合，不要在选择尚未产生影响前就收回分支。可共享地点或目标，同时让先前选择改变事件进程。

heading.en: Carry flags into later lines and scenes
heading.zh: 把选择状态延续到后续台词和场景

body.en: Use a small state table for facts the player revealed, favors owed, and relationship changes. Test both branches at the convergence and in a later scene to confirm the difference remains visible.
body.zh: 用简洁状态表记录玩家揭示的事实、欠下的人情和关系变化。在汇合点及后续场景分别测试两条分支，确认差异仍可见。

q.en: Does a convergent branch make a choice meaningless?
q.zh: 分支汇合会让选择失去意义吗？

a.en: No, if it changes what the player learns, pays, or how characters respond. Shared plot events can still reflect distinct paths through state, dialogue, and available options.
a.zh: 不会，只要选择改变玩家了解到什么、付出什么或人物如何回应。即使剧情事件相同，状态、台词和可选项仍能体现不同路径。

text.en: Use novel-to-game to analyze source evidence, define player actions and story states, then test a playable adaptation.
text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 分析原作证据、定义玩家行动与故事状态，再测试可玩的改编方案。

title.en: How to Turn a Novel Chapter into a Game Mission
title.zh: 如何把小说章节改编成游戏任务

seo_title.en: Novel Chapter to Game Mission
seo_title.zh: 小说章节改成游戏任务

description.en: Find the chapter's goal and obstacle, then build a playable mission around player actions and story consequences.
description.zh: 找出章节目标和障碍，再围绕玩家行动与故事后果设计可玩的任务。

answer.en: Adapt a chapter into a game mission by identifying its goal, obstacle, turning point, and consequence, then assigning the player actions that can express those beats. Preserve the source's key meaning while changing events that do not support play.
answer.zh: 把章节改成游戏任务时，先找出目标、障碍、转折和后果，再设计能表现这些节拍的玩家行动。保留原作关键含义，调整不利于游玩的事件。

heading.en: Extract the chapter's playable verbs
heading.zh: 提取章节中可转成玩法的动词

body.en: Look for actions such as search, persuade, protect, escape, or decide. A long internal realization may become a choice, evidence hunt, or relationship action rather than a cutscene explanation.
body.zh: 找出搜索、说服、保护、逃离或决定等行动。长篇内心领悟可以转成选择、寻找证据或关系互动，而不是过场解释。

heading.en: Build obstacles that change the plan
heading.zh: 设计会改变计划的障碍

body.en: Place the source's conflict into player-facing resistance: a locked route, competing request, limited resource, or uncertain clue. Let the obstacle require a decision instead of only delaying progress.
body.zh: 把原作冲突转成玩家能感受到的阻力：道路封锁、相互冲突的请求、有限资源或不确定线索。让障碍迫使玩家决定，而不只是拖延进度。

heading.en: Preserve the chapter's consequence
heading.zh: 保留章节带来的后果

body.en: After the mission, carry forward the relationship, knowledge, or cost that made the chapter matter. The exact event can change, but the adaptation should retain why the moment affects the larger story.
body.zh: 任务结束后，延续让原章节变得重要的关系、认知或代价。具体事件可以变化，但改编要保留这一刻影响整体故事的原因。

q.en: Should every chapter become a separate game mission?
q.zh: 每章都要改成一个单独任务吗？

a.en: No. Combine chapters when their goals and consequences form one playable sequence, or split a chapter when it contains several distinct player decisions.
a.zh: 不必。目标和后果组成一段可玩流程时可以合并章节；一章里包含多个不同玩家决定时，也可以拆开。

text.en: Use novel-to-game to analyze source evidence, define player actions and story states, then test a playable adaptation.
text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 分析原作证据、定义玩家行动与故事状态，再测试可玩的改编方案。

title.en: How to Design a Game Boss Encounter That Advances the Story
title.zh: 如何设计能推进故事的游戏首领战

seo_title.en: Design a Story-Driven Boss Encounter
seo_title.zh: 设计推进故事的首领战

description.en: Connect the boss's behavior, combat rules, and outcome to the conflict the player has been following.
description.zh: 让首领行为、战斗规则和结果回应玩家一路经历的冲突。

answer.en: A story-driven boss encounter makes the opponent's behavior and the player's required choices express the conflict. Tie the fight's rules to the character or world, give the player readable feedback, and let the outcome change a relationship, goal, or available path.
answer.zh: 叙事型首领战通过对手行为和玩家必须作出的选择表现冲突。让战斗规则关联人物或世界，反馈清晰，并让结果改变关系、目标或可走路线。

heading.en: Connect the opponent's mechanics to the conflict
heading.zh: 让对手机制回应故事冲突

body.en: An opponent may protect a resource, exploit a rule, or repeat a character's past tactic. Choose mechanics that make the conflict playable instead of relying on dialogue to explain why the encounter matters.
body.zh: 对手可以保护资源、利用规则，或重复人物过去的策略。选择能把冲突变成玩法的机制，而非只靠台词解释战斗为何重要。

heading.en: Teach patterns and signal their consequences
heading.zh: 清楚展示招式规律及其后果

body.en: Telegraph a dangerous move, show how the player's action changes it, and allow enough time to respond. The fight can surprise players while still making success feel tied to what they learned.
body.zh: 预示危险招式，展示玩家行动如何改变它，并留出反应时间。战斗可以制造惊喜，同时让胜利建立在玩家学到的东西上。

heading.en: Make victory or defeat alter the situation
heading.zh: 让胜负改变故事局势

body.en: After the encounter, show who gained access, lost trust, or learned a new fact. Avoid resetting the narrative state so the boss fight feels like a chapter in the story rather than a disconnected gate.
body.zh: 战斗后展示谁获得通行权、失去信任或学到新事实。避免重置叙事状态，让首领战成为故事的一章，而非无关卡点。

q.en: Does every major character need a boss fight?
q.zh: 每个重要角色都要安排首领战吗？

a.en: No. Use a boss encounter when it creates a compelling player challenge and expresses a conflict that benefits from play. A conversation, escape, or strategic choice may serve the story better.
a.zh: 不必。只有当首领战能带来有吸引力的玩家挑战，并用玩法表现适合互动的冲突时才采用。对话、逃脱或策略选择也许更适合。

text.en: Use novel-to-game to analyze source evidence, define player actions and story states, then test a playable adaptation.
text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 分析原作证据、定义玩家行动与故事状态，再测试可玩的改编方案。

title.en: How to Design an In-Game Journal Without Repeating the Story
title.zh: 如何设计游戏日志，避免重复剧情说明

seo_title.en: Design an In-Game Story Journal

description.en: Use journals to preserve clues and player discoveries, while keeping essential information available in the world and dialogue.
description.zh: 用日志整理线索与玩家发现，同时让关键内容也能从世界和对话中获得。

answer.en: An in-game journal should help players remember evidence, goals, and changes without replacing the story itself. Separate observed facts from character interpretation, update entries after meaningful events, and avoid making the journal the only way to understand a critical scene.
answer.zh: 游戏日志应帮助玩家记住证据、目标和变化，而不是取代故事本身。区分观察事实与人物解读，在重要事件后更新，并避免让关键场景只能靠日志理解。

heading.en: Decide what players may need to revisit
heading.zh: 判断玩家之后需要回看的信息

body.en: Track names, discovered clues, active objectives, or promised follow-ups that are easy to forget. Do not copy every dialogue line; retain the facts that support a later decision.
body.zh: 记录容易遗忘的人名、线索、当前目标或后续承诺。不要复制所有台词，只保留支持后续决定的事实。

heading.en: Distinguish evidence from the character's theory
heading.zh: 区分证据与人物推测

body.en: Label a discovered letter as evidence and the protagonist's explanation as an interpretation. When new information arrives, let entries change so the journal reflects updated understanding.
body.zh: 把发现的信件标为证据，把主角对它的解释标为推测。新信息出现后更新条目，让日志反映认知变化。

heading.en: Keep critical story facts present in play
heading.zh: 让关键故事事实能在游玩中获取

body.en: Important motives and consequences should appear through scenes, actions, or dialogue. The journal can reinforce or organize them, but players who miss an optional menu should still understand the central story.
body.zh: 重要动机和后果应通过场景、行动或对话呈现。日志可以强化和整理信息，但没打开可选菜单的玩家仍应看懂主线。

q.en: Should journal entries be written in the protagonist's voice?
q.zh: 日志条目需要用主角口吻写吗？

a.en: Use that voice when it deepens character or reveals bias. For basic objective tracking, concise neutral language can be easier to scan during play.
a.zh: 能深化人物或展现偏见时，可以用主角口吻。单纯追踪目标时，简洁中立的表达在游玩中更易查阅。

text.en: Use novel-to-game to analyze source evidence, define player actions and story states, then test a playable adaptation.
text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 分析原作证据、定义玩家行动与故事状态，再测试可玩的改编方案。

title.en: How to Choose Comparable Titles for a Novel
title.zh: 如何为小说选择可比作品

seo_title.en: Choose Novel Comparable Titles

description.en: Find recent books that share the right audience or reading promise, then explain both the overlap and the difference.
description.zh: 寻找读者群或阅读承诺相近的新书，并说清共同点和差异。

answer.en: Comparable titles help explain where a novel fits for readers, editors, or collaborators. Choose recent books with a meaningful audience or experience overlap, describe the shared appeal, and name how your story differs instead of claiming it is identical.
answer.zh: 可比作品能向读者、编辑或合作者说明小说定位。选择读者或阅读体验确有交集的近期作品，说明共同吸引力，并指出自身故事的差异。

heading.en: Start with the reader promise
heading.zh: 从读者承诺出发

body.en: Describe the feeling, genre blend, pace, or central relationship readers can expect. Search for books that deliver a similar promise, rather than matching only a surface detail such as setting or character age.
body.zh: 描述读者期待的情绪、类型组合、节奏或核心关系。寻找兑现相似承诺的作品，不要只匹配地点或人物年龄等表面特点。

heading.en: Prefer useful and recent comparisons
heading.zh: 优先选择有用且较新的参照

body.en: Choose titles your intended audience is likely to recognize and that reflect the current shelf or platform. An older classic can explain influence, but it may not communicate today's market position by itself.
body.zh: 选择目标读者可能熟悉、且能反映当下书架或平台的作品。经典旧作可以说明影响来源，但未必能单独呈现当前市场定位。

heading.en: State the difference in one concrete way
heading.zh: 用一个具体特点说明差异

body.en: Say what readers may like about each comparison and what your novel changes: viewpoint, setting, moral question, or relationship arc. Avoid “the next” or “exactly like” claims that overpromise.
body.zh: 说明读者可能喜欢参照作品的什么，再指出自己的小说在哪方面不同：视角、设定、道德问题或关系发展。避免使用“下一部”或“完全一样”等过度承诺。

q.en: How many comparable titles should I use?
q.zh: 需要列出多少部可比作品？

a.en: Use a small set that each proves a different part of the positioning. Two or three clear comparisons are usually easier to explain than a long list with weak connections.
a.zh: 选少量能分别证明定位不同方面的作品即可。两三部清楚的参照，通常比一长串牵强列表更好解释。

text.en: Use oh-story to research genre expectations, plan character-driven fiction, and revise against the story’s established facts.
text.zh: 使用 oh-story 研究类型预期、规划人物驱动的故事，并依据既有设定修改作品。

title.en: How to Research a Novel Genre Before You Draft
title.zh: 起稿前如何研究小说类型

seo_title.en: Research a Novel Genre

description.en: Study reader expectations and recent examples, then turn what you learn into a story promise you can make your own.
description.zh: 了解读者预期和近期作品，再把发现转化为属于自己的故事承诺。

answer.en: Genre research helps writers understand the experience readers come for, not copy a winning plot. Review current examples, note recurring promises and variations, and test your own premise against the expectations you choose to meet or subvert.
answer.zh: 类型研究帮助作者理解读者期待的体验，而不是复制成功剧情。阅读近期作品，记录常见承诺与变化，再对照自己准备遵循或颠覆的预期检验故事构想。

heading.en: Sample recent works from your target shelf
heading.zh: 阅读目标类型中的近期作品

body.en: Compare several books or serials that reach the audience you want. Track opening promise, point of view, conflict, pace, and the kind of payoff each delivers instead of relying on memory or a single example.
body.zh: 对照几部能触达目标读者的书或连载。记录开篇承诺、视角、冲突、节奏和回报类型，不要只凭记忆或单一作品判断。

heading.en: Separate conventions from optional choices
heading.zh: 分清类型惯例与可变选择

body.en: A convention helps readers recognize an experience; a familiar scene or trope is only one way to provide it. Note what appears consistently and where successful works make different choices.
body.zh: 惯例帮助读者识别阅读体验；熟悉场景或套路只是实现它的一种方式。记录哪些特征反复出现，以及成功作品在哪些方面各有选择。

heading.en: Write a promise your plot can deliver
heading.zh: 写下情节能够兑现的承诺

body.en: State the audience, central pleasure, and main source of tension in plain language. Draft a test scene that demonstrates the promise, then revise if the scene feels borrowed or points toward a different kind of book.
body.zh: 用直白语言说明目标读者、核心乐趣和主要张力来源。试写一场能体现承诺的戏；如果感觉像在借用别人的作品，或指向不同类型，就调整设定。

q.en: How many books should I study before starting?
q.zh: 开始写作前要研究多少本书？

a.en: Enough to notice both shared expectations and meaningful variation. A focused comparison of a few recent examples is more useful than collecting a large list without taking notes.
a.zh: 读到既能发现共同预期，也能看见明显变化即可。认真对照几部近期作品，比只收集大量书名更有用。

text.en: Use oh-story to research genre expectations, plan character-driven fiction, and revise against the story’s established facts.
text.zh: 使用 oh-story 研究类型预期、规划人物驱动的故事，并依据既有设定修改作品。

title.en: How to Write a Web-Serial Installment That Feels Complete
title.zh: 如何写出单篇完整的网络连载章节

seo_title.en: Write a Complete Serial Installment

description.en: Resolve a local question, change the larger story state, and leave readers with a reason to return.
description.zh: 解决本篇问题、改变主线状态，并给读者继续追更的理由。

answer.en: A satisfying serial installment gives readers a meaningful result while keeping the larger story in motion. Set a local goal, deliver progress or consequence, and end with a new question that grows from what just happened.
answer.zh: 令人满足的连载章节既要给读者阶段结果，也要推动长线故事。设定本篇目标，交付进展或后果，并以刚发生之事引出新的问题。

heading.en: Choose one local question to answer
heading.zh: 选定一个本篇要回应的问题

body.en: A chapter might ask whether the protagonist can keep a promise or uncover one clue. Give the reader a visible result by the end, even if the larger mystery or relationship remains unresolved.
body.zh: 本章可以追问主角能否守约，或能否找到一条线索。结尾给读者看得见的结果，即使大谜团或关系仍未解决。

heading.en: Advance the long story through the result
heading.zh: 让本篇结果推动长线故事

body.en: A win can create a debt, reveal a new constraint, or change who trusts the protagonist. Make the chapter's payoff alter the next available action instead of resetting everyone to the same state.
body.zh: 一次胜利可以带来人情债、揭示新限制或改变他人对主角的信任。让本章回报改变下一步的行动选择，而非把所有人重置。

heading.en: End with a consequence, not a random interruption
heading.zh: 用后果收尾，不要突然打断

body.en: A new task, cost, or discovery can create a strong return reason when it follows from the chapter's choice. Make the hook specific enough that readers know what question the next installment will tackle.
body.zh: 新任务、代价或发现若承接本章选择，就能形成继续追看的理由。钩子要具体，让读者知道下一篇将面对什么问题。

q.en: Does every serial chapter need a cliffhanger?
q.zh: 每个连载章节都需要悬念式结尾吗？

a.en: No. A reveal, emotional shift, new plan, or completed small goal can also close a chapter. Vary the ending while preserving a clear reason to continue.
a.zh: 不必。揭示、情绪变化、新计划或完成的小目标都能收束章节。可以变化结尾方式，但要保留继续阅读的理由。

text.en: Use oh-story to research genre expectations, plan character-driven fiction, and revise against the story’s established facts.
text.zh: 使用 oh-story 研究类型预期、规划人物驱动的故事，并依据既有设定修改作品。

title.en: How to Make the First Book in a Series Feel Complete
title.zh: 如何让系列小说第一部有完整感

seo_title.en: Write a Complete First Series Book

description.en: Resolve the first book's central conflict while opening a larger question the next installment can pursue.
description.zh: 解决第一部的核心冲突，同时为下一部开启更大的问题。

answer.en: The first book in a series needs a satisfying arc of its own and a credible path forward. Resolve the main promise introduced at the opening, then leave a consequence, relationship, or unresolved world problem that creates a new story rather than withholding the ending.
answer.zh: 系列第一部需要自身完整的故事弧线，也要留下可信的后续方向。兑现开篇的核心承诺，再通过后果、关系或未解决的世界问题开启新故事，而非故意扣住结局。

heading.en: Define what this book promises to finish
heading.zh: 明确本部承诺完成什么

body.en: Write the central question, the protagonist's goal, and what victory or failure will mean. Readers can accept a larger mystery continuing if the immediate conflict receives an earned result.
body.zh: 写清中心问题、主角目标，以及成败意味着什么。只要眼前冲突得到合理结果，读者可以接受更大谜团继续发展。

heading.en: Resolve the arc through a changed choice
heading.zh: 用改变后的选择完成故事弧线

body.en: Let the protagonist face a final decision that uses what the story has taught them. The ending should change a relationship or situation, not only announce that the next volume will explain more.
body.zh: 让主角面对能够运用故事经验的最终决定。结尾应改变关系或局势，而不是只宣布下一卷会解释更多。

heading.en: Plant a next story that follows from the ending
heading.zh: 从结尾自然引出下一部

body.en: A new responsibility, revealed danger, or altered alliance can launch the next installment. Seed it before the ending when possible so the continuation feels caused by this book's resolution.
body.zh: 新的责任、揭示的危险或改变的联盟都能开启下一部。尽量提前埋下线索，让后续像是本部结局自然造成的结果。

q.en: Can a series book end on a cliffhanger?
q.zh: 系列小说单部可以用悬念结尾吗？

a.en: It can, but the book should still resolve a meaningful local conflict. A cliffhanger works best as an added consequence after readers receive the payoff promised by this installment.
a.zh: 可以，但本部仍要解决一个有意义的局部冲突。读者先得到本卷承诺的回报，再出现额外悬念，效果通常更好。

text.en: Use oh-story to research genre expectations, plan character-driven fiction, and revise against the story’s established facts.
text.zh: 使用 oh-story 研究类型预期、规划人物驱动的故事，并依据既有设定修改作品。

title.en: How to Show a Character's Inner Conflict on Screen
title.zh: 如何在画面中呈现人物的内心冲突

seo_title.en: Show Inner Conflict on Screen

description.en: Translate competing wants into visible hesitation, conflicting actions, choices, and reactions instead of explanatory monologue.
description.zh: 把相互冲突的欲望转化为犹豫、矛盾行动、选择和反应，而非解释性独白。

answer.en: Screen drama shows inner conflict through choices and behavior. Identify what the character wants and what they fear losing, then stage an action where both pressures are visible and the decision changes the scene.
answer.zh: 影视戏剧通过选择和行为呈现内心冲突。找出人物想要什么、害怕失去什么，再设计一个让两种压力都可见、且决定会改变场景的行动。

heading.en: Turn competing desires into an immediate task
heading.zh: 把冲突欲望转成眼前任务

body.en: A person may want to tell the truth and protect a friend. Give them a document to sign, a call to answer, or a door to open so the conflict becomes playable.
body.zh: 人物可能既想说实话又想保护朋友。给他们一份要签的文件、一通要接的电话或一扇要打开的门，让冲突变成可表演的行动。

heading.en: Let the performance show resistance
heading.zh: 用表演呈现内心阻力

body.en: A delayed response, interrupted gesture, or change in eye contact can reveal pressure. Choose behavior tied to the character rather than a generic look of worry.
body.zh: 迟疑的回答、中断的动作或视线变化都能呈现压力。选择符合人物特征的行为，不要只用千篇一律的担忧表情。

heading.en: Make the decision visible in the aftermath
heading.zh: 通过后续结果呈现人物决定

body.en: Show what the character does after choosing and who notices. A consequence, altered relationship, or abandoned object can carry the meaning that a paragraph of explanation would have supplied.
body.zh: 呈现人物选择后的行动，以及谁注意到了。后果、改变的关系或被留下的物品，都能承载原本需要一段解释的含义。

q.en: Can voice-over express inner conflict?
q.zh: 旁白可以表达内心冲突吗？

a.en: Yes, when it adds a perspective the images cannot carry. Use behavior and consequence too, so the conflict remains understandable if viewers are watching rather than only listening.
a.zh: 可以，只要旁白提供画面无法承载的视角。同时保留行为和后果，让观众即使不只听旁白也能理解冲突。

text.en: Use drama-skills to turn source beats into performable scenes, storyboarded shots, and production references with clear continuity.
text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 将原作节拍转成可表演场景、分镜镜头和连续性清晰的制作参考。

title.en: How to Write a Short Drama Set in One Location
title.zh: 如何写好单一场景的短剧

seo_title.en: Write a One-Location Short Drama

description.en: Use limited space to create changing leverage, reveal information, and force decisions rather than repeating one argument.
description.zh: 通过变化的筹码、信息揭示和被迫决定利用有限空间，避免反复争吵。

answer.en: A one-location drama stays dynamic when the room changes meaning as characters act. Give the space a practical constraint, use objects and exits as leverage, and let each new fact change the negotiation or plan.
answer.zh: 人物行动不断改变房间含义时，单场景短剧才有变化。给空间设置实际限制，用物品和出口形成筹码，并让每条新信息改变谈判或计划。

heading.en: Make the location part of the conflict
heading.zh: 让地点成为冲突的一部分

body.en: A locked office, crowded kitchen, or waiting room can limit privacy, movement, or time. Choose a constraint that makes the characters respond differently instead of treating the setting as a backdrop.
body.zh: 锁住的办公室、拥挤的厨房或候诊室都能限制隐私、移动或时间。选择会改变人物反应的限制，不要让地点只作背景。

heading.en: Let control of the space shift
heading.zh: 让空间控制权发生变化

body.en: Who stands near the door, holds the phone, or controls the only chair can shift as bargaining changes. Track these details in stage directions and coverage so the audience understands the power change.
body.zh: 随着谈判变化，靠近门的人、拿着手机的人或占着唯一椅子的人都可能改变。把这些细节写入调度和镜头计划，让观众看懂权力转移。

heading.en: Escalate with new information or a forced action
heading.zh: 用新信息或被迫行动升级

body.en: Bring in a message, a deadline, a sound from outside, or a decision someone can no longer delay. Each beat should change what the characters know or can do.
body.zh: 加入消息、期限、门外声音，或一项无法继续拖延的决定。每个节拍都要改变人物的认知或行动可能。

q.en: Does a one-location short drama need a small cast?
q.zh: 单场景短剧必须只有少量人物吗？

a.en: Not necessarily, but every character should alter the pressure or information in the room. A focused cast often makes the changing alliances easier to follow.
a.zh: 不一定，但每个人物都应改变现场压力或信息。人数精简通常能让关系变化更容易理解。

text.en: Use drama-skills to turn source beats into performable scenes, storyboarded shots, and production references with clear continuity.
text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 将原作节拍转成可表演场景、分镜镜头和连续性清晰的制作参考。

title.en: How to Plan Reaction Shots That Clarify a Short-Drama Scene
title.zh: 如何规划反应镜头，让短剧场景更清楚

seo_title.en: Plan Short-Drama Reaction Shots

description.en: Use reactions to reveal changed understanding, hidden leverage, or a decision the dialogue alone does not show.
description.zh: 用反应呈现认知变化、隐藏筹码或仅凭台词无法表达的决定。

answer.en: A reaction shot matters when it shows how new information changes a character's next move. Plan the person who must receive the beat, what they hear or see, and the response that moves the scene forward.
answer.zh: 当反应镜头呈现新信息如何改变人物下一步行动时，它才有作用。规划谁需要接收到这个节拍、看见或听见什么，以及哪种反应能推动场景。

heading.en: Choose the reaction that changes the scene
heading.zh: 选择能改变场景的反应

body.en: A glance at a hidden key, a delay before answering, or a shift toward the exit can reveal what the character understood. Do not cut to faces automatically after every line.
body.zh: 瞥向藏起的钥匙、回答前的迟疑或转向出口，都能揭示人物理解了什么。不要每说一句台词就机械切到脸部。

heading.en: Give the reaction a clear trigger
heading.zh: 明确反应由什么触发

body.en: The audience should know what line, action, or sound the character reacts to. Keep enough of the trigger or its timing in the edit so the expression does not seem unrelated.
body.zh: 观众要明白人物对哪句话、动作或声音作出反应。剪辑中保留触发内容或准确时点，避免表情显得无关。

heading.en: Let the reaction affect the next action
heading.zh: 让反应影响后续行动

body.en: After the look or pause, change the tactic, reveal a decision, or alter the distance between characters. A reaction that produces no new information may not need its own shot.
body.zh: 目光或停顿之后，让策略变化、决定显露，或人物距离改变。没有带来新信息的反应可能不必单独成镜。

q.en: Can a reaction shot happen before the dialogue ends?
q.zh: 反应镜头能在台词结束前出现吗？

a.en: Yes, when the listener's response is part of the exchange. Cut when the new information lands, while keeping the speaker's line understandable and the emotional timing intact.
a.zh: 可以，听者反应本身就是互动的一部分时尤其有效。新信息落下时即可切镜，同时确保台词易懂、情绪节奏自然。

text.en: Use drama-skills to turn source beats into performable scenes, storyboarded shots, and production references with clear continuity.
text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 将原作节拍转成可表演场景、分镜镜头和连续性清晰的制作参考。

title.en: How to Write a TV Episode Recap Script
title.zh: 如何写电视剧单集解说脚本

seo_title.en: Write a TV Episode Recap Script

description.en: Track the episode's A and B stories, turning points, and ending change without reducing the recap to a scene list.
description.zh: 梳理单集主副线、转折和结尾变化，避免把解说写成场景清单。

answer.en: A TV episode recap should preserve the episode's main question and changes while helping viewers follow connected storylines. Identify each thread's goal and turning point, show where they affect one another, and finish with the consequence that carries into the next episode.
answer.zh: 电视剧单集解说要保留核心问题和变化，并帮助观众跟上交织的情节线。明确各线目标和转折，说明它们何处相互影响，并以延续到下一集的后果收尾。

heading.en: Choose the episode's main question
heading.zh: 确定本集的核心问题

body.en: Write what the protagonist or ensemble is trying to resolve during this episode. Let secondary threads support or complicate that question rather than giving every scene equal weight.
body.zh: 写清主角或群像本集试图解决什么问题。让副线支撑或复杂化主问题，不要给每场戏同等篇幅。

heading.en: Track turns within each storyline
heading.zh: 追踪各条故事线的转折

body.en: For each thread, note the initial plan, obstacle, new information, and changed outcome. Connect threads when a decision in one changes the options or stakes in another.
body.zh: 逐线记录初始计划、障碍、新信息和变化后的结果。一条线的决定改变另一条线的选项或利害时，将两者连起来讲。

heading.en: End with what the episode changed
heading.zh: 以本集造成的变化收尾

body.en: Summarize the final choice, reveal, or unresolved consequence that matters next. Verify the recap does not promote a teaser into an event that has not yet happened.
body.zh: 概括影响后续的最终选择、揭示或未决后果。核对解说没有把预告内容说成已经发生的剧情。

q.en: Should a TV recap include every subplot?
q.zh: 电视剧解说要覆盖每条副线吗？

a.en: Include a subplot when it changes the episode's main conflict, develops a recurring relationship, or sets up a later payoff. Compress threads that do not affect the episode's result.
a.zh: 副线会改变本集主冲突、发展长期关系或铺垫后续回报时才纳入。对不影响本集结果的线索可简要带过。

text.en: Use video-recap to ground the script in source scenes and timestamps, then align narration, evidence, and editing.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 以原片场景和时间码为依据，再对齐旁白、证据与剪辑。

title.en: How to Turn an Interview Transcript into a Documentary Outline
title.zh: 如何把采访文字稿整理成纪录片大纲

seo_title.en: Interview Transcript to Documentary Outline
seo_title.zh: 采访稿整理为纪录片大纲

description.en: Group interview evidence by story question, mark source timestamps, and build an outline around supported changes.
description.zh: 按故事问题归纳采访证据、标注来源时间码，并围绕有依据的变化搭建大纲。

answer.en: Turn a transcript into a documentary outline by grouping statements around a clear story question and verifying each passage against its source recording. Track who says what, when, and with what evidence; then arrange supported events into a coherent progression without making a quote prove more than it does.
answer.zh: 把文字稿整理成纪录片大纲时，先围绕清晰问题归类说法，再回听源录音核实。记录谁在何时说了什么、有什么证据；按有依据的事件组织顺序，不要让引语证明超出其含义的结论。

heading.en: Tag quotes by question and evidence
heading.zh: 按问题和证据给引语做标记

body.en: Group transcript passages by topic, claim, emotion, or contradiction. Keep speaker names and timestamps attached so a promising line can be checked in its original context.
body.zh: 按主题、观点、情绪或矛盾归类文字稿。保留发言人和时间码，方便回到原始上下文核对有用内容。

heading.en: Separate what a person remembers from what records show
heading.zh: 区分个人回忆与记录材料

body.en: An interview is evidence of what someone says and remembers; it may not independently establish a date or cause. Label claims that need documents, other witnesses, or scene footage before presenting them as fact.
body.zh: 采访能证明某人如何陈述和回忆，却未必能单独确定日期或原因。需要文件、其他证人或现场影像支持的观点要单独标记。

heading.en: Build the outline from supported turns
heading.zh: 围绕有依据的转折搭建大纲

body.en: Arrange moments where a goal changes, a new fact appears, or a conflict deepens. Balance interview clips with narration, images, and pauses, and return to the recording when the edit changes a quote's meaning.
body.zh: 按目标变化、新事实出现或冲突加深等时刻安排顺序。平衡采访、旁白、画面和停顿；剪辑可能改变引语含义时回听录音。

q.en: Can automated transcription be used as the documentary source?
q.zh: 自动转写可以直接作为纪录片来源吗？

a.en: Use it as a searchable draft, then verify important wording and timing against audio or video. Transcription can omit speakers, mishear names, or miss tone that affects meaning.
a.zh: 可把它当作便于搜索的初稿，但要对照音视频核实关键措辞和时间。转写可能漏掉发言者、听错姓名，或丢失影响含义的语气。

text.en: Use video-recap to ground the script in source scenes and timestamps, then align narration, evidence, and editing.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 以原片场景和时间码为依据，再对齐旁白、证据与剪辑。

title.en: How to Write a Conversational Voice-Over for Video
title.zh: 如何写出口语自然的视频旁白

seo_title.en: Write Conversational Video Voice-Over

description.en: Use short spoken sentences, clear transitions, and footage-aware context without sounding like an essay read aloud.
description.zh: 用简短口语句、清晰转折和贴合画面的背景说明，避免照读论文。

answer.en: Conversational voice-over sounds like a person guiding viewers through an idea, not a page read aloud. Write for the ear, use concrete language, leave room for pauses and footage, then read the script aloud at the intended pace.
answer.zh: 口语自然的旁白像有人带观众理解观点，而不是把文章念出来。按听觉写作，使用具体表达，为停顿和画面留空间，再按预定语速朗读检查。

heading.en: Write one thought per breath
heading.zh: 每口气只表达一个意思

body.en: Break long sentences at the point where a listener needs to process a new fact. Prefer familiar verbs and names over stacked abstractions, and read aloud to catch phrases that look clear but sound awkward.
body.zh: 在听众需要消化新信息的位置拆开长句。多用熟悉的动词和具体名称，少堆抽象词；朗读时留意书面上清楚、听起来拗口的表达。

heading.en: Connect each paragraph to the footage
heading.zh: 让每段旁白都连接画面

body.en: Use narration to explain context, consequence, or a detail the image does not communicate. If the footage already shows the action clearly, let the image breathe instead of describing it twice.
body.zh: 用旁白补充画面没表达的背景、后果或细节。画面已清楚呈现动作时，就留出观看空间，不要重复描述。

heading.en: Time the read with pauses included
heading.zh: 计时朗读时把停顿算进去

body.en: Record a rough read or estimate spoken words per minute, then mark pauses where a reaction or image needs time. Trim explanation before speeding up delivery until it becomes hard to follow.
body.zh: 试录一遍或估算每分钟口播字数，并标记反应或画面需要停留的时间。先删减解释，不要一味加快语速直到听不清。

q.en: Can a voice-over script include long sentences?
q.zh: 旁白脚本可以写长句吗？

a.en: Yes, when the thought is easy to follow aloud and the speaker has room to breathe. Test it by reading at recording speed and splitting where listeners would lose the thread.
a.zh: 可以，只要朗读时思路清楚，也留有换气空间。按录制语速试读，在听众可能跟丢的位置拆分。

text.en: Use video-recap to ground the script in source scenes and timestamps, then align narration, evidence, and editing.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 以原片场景和时间码为依据，再对齐旁白、证据与剪辑。

title.en: How to Create a Timestamped Source Log for a Video
title.zh: 如何为视频制作带时间码的来源记录

seo_title.en: Create a Timestamped Video Source Log
seo_title.zh: 制作视频来源时间码记录

description.en: Record where each important claim, scene, quotation, and visual detail comes from so editing stays accurate.
description.zh: 记录重要观点、场景、引语和画面细节的来源位置，保证剪辑准确。

answer.en: A timestamped source log links a draft, claim, or edit decision to the material that supports it. Record the file or source, time range, what appears or is said, and why the moment matters; then verify it again before publishing.
answer.zh: 带时间码的来源记录把草稿观点或剪辑决定关联到支撑材料。记录文件或来源、时间范围、画面或发言内容及其作用，发布前再次核验。

heading.en: Use one entry for each verifiable moment
heading.zh: 每个可核实片段单独记一条

body.en: Include a source name, timestamp or page, short factual note, and any related script line. Keep observation separate from interpretation so the edit can use evidence without overstating it.
body.zh: 记下来源名称、时间码或页码、简短事实说明和关联脚本句。将观察与解读分开，让剪辑使用证据时不过度推断。

heading.en: Keep version and speaker details
heading.zh: 保留版本和发言人信息

body.en: Record which cut, episode, recording, or language version you reviewed. Add the speaker or character name when it matters; the same scene may differ across releases or transcripts.
body.zh: 记录查阅的是哪个剪辑版、集数、录音或语言版本。必要时标注发言人或角色；不同发行版本或转写可能存在差异。

heading.en: Use the log during review and correction
heading.zh: 在复核和纠错时使用记录

body.en: When narration changes, revisit the linked source rather than trusting an old summary. If an edit omits context, extend the clip or rewrite the claim to match what remains visible.
body.zh: 旁白修改时回看关联来源，不要依赖旧摘要。如果剪辑删掉了上下文，就延长素材，或把观点改成与剩余画面一致的表述。

q.en: Do I need timestamps for every source note?
q.zh: 每条来源记录都需要时间码吗？

a.en: Use precise locations for video and audio moments; use page, section, or document identifiers for text sources. The goal is to make verification quick and repeatable.
a.zh: 视频和音频片段应标时间码，文字来源可记录页码、章节或文件标识。目标是让核验快速且可重复。

text.en: Use video-recap to ground the script in source scenes and timestamps, then align narration, evidence, and editing.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 以原片场景和时间码为依据，再对齐旁白、证据与剪辑。

title.en: How to Turn a Story Theme into Game Mechanics
title.zh: 如何把故事主题转化为游戏机制

seo_title.en: Turn a Story Theme into Game Mechanics

description.en: Translate a story's central question into player actions, rules, costs, and feedback that make the theme playable.
description.zh: 把故事核心问题转成玩家行动、规则、代价和反馈，让主题通过玩法呈现。

answer.en: A game expresses theme when its rules ask players to make the kinds of decisions the story explores. Identify the theme as a tension or question, then design actions and consequences that let players experience it instead of only hearing it explained.
answer.zh: 当规则要求玩家作出故事探讨的那类决定时，游戏就能表达主题。先把主题说成矛盾或问题，再设计行动和后果，让玩家亲身经历，而不只是听解释。

heading.en: Phrase the theme as a playable tension
heading.zh: 把主题改写成可玩的矛盾

body.en: “Trust matters” is broad; “trusting an ally grants power but risks losing control” suggests a decision. State the competing values and what the player can do to test them.
body.zh: “信任很重要”过于宽泛；“信任盟友能获得力量，却可能失去控制”则暗示选择。写清冲突价值，以及玩家能做什么来验证它。

heading.en: Make rules create the tension repeatedly
heading.zh: 让规则反复制造这种矛盾

body.en: The player might share resources, delegate control, or choose whose information to believe. Let the mechanic recur in meaningful situations and change its cost as the story develops.
body.zh: 玩家可以分享资源、委托控制权，或选择相信谁的信息。让机制在有意义的情境中重复出现，并随着故事发展改变代价。

heading.en: Give feedback that reveals the consequence
heading.zh: 用反馈揭示行动后果

body.en: Show how a choice changes access, relationships, or future options. A character response or altered system state can reinforce the theme without a scene that states the moral directly.
body.zh: 展示选择如何改变权限、关系或后续选项。人物反应或系统状态变化能强化主题，无需安排角色直接说教。

q.en: Does every game mechanic need to represent the theme?
q.zh: 每种游戏机制都要表达主题吗？

a.en: No. Focus thematic mechanics on the central decisions and recurring actions. Basic movement or interface rules can serve usability without carrying a symbolic meaning.
a.zh: 不必。让主题性机制聚焦中心决定和反复行动即可。移动或界面等基础规则可以只服务可用性，不必承担象征含义。

text.en: Use novel-to-game to analyze source evidence, define player actions and story states, then test a playable adaptation.
text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 分析原作证据、定义玩家行动与故事状态，再测试可玩的改编方案。

title.en: How to Make the Consequences of Player Choices Visible
title.zh: 如何让玩家看见选择带来的后果

seo_title.en: Show Player Choice Consequences

description.en: Reflect decisions through later dialogue, access, resources, relationships, and story outcomes rather than a hidden score alone.
description.zh: 通过后续对话、权限、资源、关系和剧情结果体现决定，不要只藏在数值里。

answer.en: Players understand that a choice mattered when later play reflects it. Decide what should change, show a timely response, and carry the state into a later moment where the player can recognize the connection.
answer.zh: 后续游玩反映出变化时，玩家才会明白选择产生了作用。先设定要改变什么，及时反馈，再把状态延续到玩家能认出因果的时刻。

heading.en: Choose a consequence the player can recognize
heading.zh: 选择玩家能察觉的后果

body.en: A changed greeting, a locked route, a resource debt, or a different ally can make the result legible. Match the scale of the response to the importance of the choice.
body.zh: 不同的问候、封闭路线、资源债务或盟友变化都能让结果可见。让反馈规模与选择的重要程度相称。

heading.en: Signal the result without overexplaining
heading.zh: 说明结果，但别过度解释

body.en: A brief reaction or world-state change can confirm that the game registered the decision. Keep feedback in character and avoid an immediate system message that spells out every hidden value.
body.zh: 简短反应或世界状态变化就能说明游戏记录了决定。保持人物口吻，不要立刻用系统消息解释所有隐藏数值。

heading.en: Carry consequences to a later payoff
heading.zh: 把后果延续到之后兑现

body.en: Track the decision in the narrative state and use it when it can alter access, trust, or the final outcome. A later callback helps players connect their action with the world they shaped.
body.zh: 在叙事状态中记录决定，并在它能改变权限、信任或最终结果时调用。后续呼应能帮助玩家把行动与自己塑造的世界联系起来。

q.en: Do choices need a different ending to matter?
q.zh: 选择必须带来不同结局才算有影响吗？

a.en: No. A choice can change the path, cost, relationship, or information while the central ending remains shared. Make the difference noticeable and consistent with the choice's stakes.
a.zh: 不必。即使核心结局相同，选择也能改变路线、代价、关系或信息。只要差异明显，并符合选择的利害程度即可。

text.en: Use novel-to-game to analyze source evidence, define player actions and story states, then test a playable adaptation.
text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 分析原作证据、定义玩家行动与故事状态，再测试可玩的改编方案。

title.en: How to Adapt a Novel's Climax into Gameplay
title.zh: 如何把小说高潮改编成游戏玩法

seo_title.en: Adapt a Novel Climax into Gameplay

description.en: Preserve the climax's central decision and consequence, then give players actions that make the resolution playable.
description.zh: 保留高潮中的核心决定与后果，再为玩家安排能亲自完成结局的行动。

answer.en: Adapt a novel's climax into gameplay by identifying its decisive choice, opposition, and irreversible consequence. Give the player control over an action that expresses that choice, and use pacing or dialogue to preserve source meaning without turning the climax into a passive cutscene.
answer.zh: 改编小说高潮时，找出决定性选择、对抗和不可逆后果。让玩家控制能表达这一选择的行动，再通过节奏或对白保留原意，避免高潮变成被动过场。

heading.en: Find the climax's decision, not just its spectacle
heading.zh: 寻找高潮里的决定，而不只是场面

body.en: A battle, confession, or escape may be memorable because of what the protagonist chooses under pressure. Name that choice and the value it costs before designing mechanics or set pieces.
body.zh: 战斗、告白或逃离令人记住，可能是因为主角在压力下作出的选择。设计机制和大场面前，先明确选择及其代价。

heading.en: Give the player a meaningful action
heading.zh: 让玩家执行有意义的行动

body.en: Let play involve selecting an ally, protecting a resource, taking a risk, or changing a plan. Avoid asking the player to repeat a series of inputs that cannot affect how the choice is experienced.
body.zh: 让玩家选择盟友、保护资源、承担风险或改变计划。避免只要求重复输入，却无法影响选择体验的操作序列。

heading.en: Carry the resolution into the next state
heading.zh: 让结局延续到之后的状态

body.en: Show what the climax changed in the world, relationship, or player goal. When the game diverges from the source, preserve the emotional or thematic consequence the adaptation set out to keep.
body.zh: 展示高潮如何改变世界、关系或玩家目标。游戏改编偏离原作时，也要保留改编决定延续的情绪或主题后果。

q.en: Should the player be able to change the source ending?
q.zh: 玩家应该能改变原作结局吗？

a.en: That depends on the adaptation's promise. If the ending is fixed, give players agency in how they reach it and what they learn; if it branches, make the alternate outcomes follow established rules.
a.zh: 取决于改编承诺。结局固定时，让玩家决定如何抵达并学到什么；如果结局分支，让不同结果遵循已建立的规则。

text.en: Use novel-to-game to analyze source evidence, define player actions and story states, then test a playable adaptation.
text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 分析原作证据、定义玩家行动与故事状态，再测试可玩的改编方案。

title.en: How to Write a Legal Thriller with a Clear Case
title.zh: 如何写好案件清晰的法律惊悚小说

seo_title.en: Write a Legal Thriller

description.en: Build suspense from a winnable case, contested evidence, legal deadlines, and a protagonist with something to lose.
description.zh: 用可争取的案件、争议证据、法律期限和有所牵挂的主角构建悬念。

answer.en: A legal thriller turns a dispute into a story of evidence, procedure, risk, and choice. Give the protagonist a clear case goal, establish the rules readers need to understand, and make each revelation change the strategy or stakes.
answer.zh: 法律惊悚小说把争议写成证据、程序、风险与选择的故事。给主角明确案件目标，交代读者需要理解的规则，并让每次揭示改变策略或利害。

heading.en: Make the case understandable before making it complex
heading.zh: 先让案件容易理解，再增加复杂度

body.en: State what the protagonist must prove and what could happen if they fail. Introduce only the procedure needed for the current decision, and define legal terms through context rather than a lecture.
body.zh: 说明主角必须证明什么，以及失败会发生什么。只介绍当前决定所需的程序，并通过情境说明术语，不要写成课堂讲解。

heading.en: Let evidence force strategy changes
heading.zh: 让证据迫使策略改变

body.en: A witness recants, a document is challenged, or a new timeline emerges. Make each development change what can be argued and what risk the characters must take.
body.zh: 证人翻供、文件受到质疑，或新的时间线出现。让每个进展改变可提出的主张和人物必须承担的风险。

heading.en: Balance courtroom pressure with personal stakes
heading.zh: 平衡庭审压力与个人利害

body.en: The case can threaten a career, family, reputation, or belief. Show the cost through decisions outside court as well, and verify procedural details when accuracy affects the plot.
body.zh: 案件可以威胁职业、家庭、名誉或信念。在法庭外的决定中也呈现代价；程序准确性会影响剧情时要核实细节。

q.en: Does a legal thriller have to end in court?
q.zh: 法律惊悚小说必须以法庭结尾吗？

a.en: No. Investigation, negotiation, or a settlement can resolve the central conflict if the case's evidence and choices reach a clear consequence.
a.zh: 不必。只要案件证据和人物选择得到明确后果，调查、谈判或和解都能解决核心冲突。

text.en: Use oh-story to research genre expectations, plan character-driven fiction, and revise against the story’s established facts.
text.zh: 使用 oh-story 研究类型预期、规划人物驱动的故事，并依据既有设定修改作品。

title.en: How to Write a Medical Thriller Readers Can Follow
title.zh: 如何写出读者看得懂的医疗惊悚小说

seo_title.en: Write a Medical Thriller

description.en: Ground suspense in a clear medical problem, limited time, conflicting evidence, and credible human decisions.
description.zh: 用清晰的医疗问题、有限时间、矛盾证据和可信的人物决定建立悬念。

answer.en: A medical thriller makes health, science, or care decisions drive the suspense. Explain the immediate problem in plain language, verify technical details that affect the outcome, and center the story on the choices people make under pressure.
answer.zh: 医疗惊悚小说用健康、科学或救治决定推动悬念。用通俗语言说明眼前问题，核实影响结局的专业细节，并聚焦人物在压力下的选择。

heading.en: Give readers a concrete problem to track
heading.zh: 给读者一个具体问题去追踪

body.en: Clarify who is at risk, what is known, and what must happen next. A reader can follow a difficult diagnosis or trial when the story explains why the result changes a character's options.
body.zh: 说明谁处于危险、已知信息是什么、接下来必须做什么。只要解释结果如何改变人物选择，读者就能跟上复杂诊断或试验。

heading.en: Separate verified detail from dramatic invention
heading.zh: 区分核实过的细节与戏剧化设计

body.en: Research procedures, timelines, and terminology that determine what characters can do. If you simplify a process, keep its consequence plausible and avoid using technical language to hide a plot gap.
body.zh: 核实决定人物能做什么的流程、时间和术语。简化流程时要让后果可信，不要用专业词汇掩盖剧情漏洞。

heading.en: Make the human decision the turning point
heading.zh: 让人物决定成为转折

body.en: A test result alone is information; a choice about disclosure, treatment, or responsibility changes the story. Let the pressure expose relationships and values rather than turning patients into plot devices.
body.zh: 检测结果只是信息；是否告知、如何治疗或由谁负责的决定才能改变故事。让压力揭示关系和价值观，不要把患者写成剧情工具。

q.en: How much medical terminology should I include?
q.zh: 医疗惊悚里该写多少专业术语？

a.en: Use a term when characters would naturally use it or when it matters to a decision. Define it through a concise context clue, and keep the immediate stakes easier to understand than the procedure.
a.zh: 只有人物会自然使用或对决定重要时才加入术语。用简短上下文解释，并让眼前利害比流程本身更容易理解。

title.en: How to Write a Dark-Academia Novel with More Than Atmosphere
title.zh: 如何写出不止有氛围的暗黑学院小说

seo_title.en: Write a Dark-Academia Novel

description.en: Tie academic ambition, group loyalty, secrets, and institutional pressure to the characters' choices and consequences.
description.zh: 把学术野心、群体忠诚、秘密和制度压力连到人物选择与后果上。

answer.en: A dark-academia novel needs an active story beneath its books, rituals, and atmosphere. Give characters a concrete academic or social goal, make the institution reward and punish specific behavior, and let secrecy change their relationships and choices.
answer.zh: 暗黑学院小说需要在书本、仪式和氛围之下有主动推进的故事。给人物具体学术或社交目标，让机构奖惩具体行为，并让秘密改变关系与选择。

heading.en: Make the institution shape the conflict
heading.zh: 让学院制度塑造冲突

body.en: Decide who controls access, recognition, money, or belonging. A ritual or tradition should affect what characters can do, rather than appearing only as decorative atmosphere.
body.zh: 明确谁掌握资源、认可、金钱或归属感。仪式或传统应影响人物行动，而不只是装饰气氛。

heading.en: Give the group a reason to stay together
heading.zh: 给群体继续结盟的理由

body.en: Shared ambition, blackmail, friendship, or complicity can bind the cast. Let members disagree about the cost of success so loyalty becomes an ongoing choice.
body.zh: 共同野心、把柄、友情或共谋都能维系群体。让成员对成功代价有分歧，使忠诚成为持续的选择。

heading.en: Make the secret carry a human cost
heading.zh: 让秘密带来真实的人际代价

body.en: A hidden act should protect someone, preserve status, or conceal harm—and create pressure when discovered. Track who knows the truth and what each person risks by speaking.
body.zh: 隐藏的行为应在保护某人、维持地位或掩盖伤害，并在曝光时带来压力。记录谁知道真相，以及每个人开口要冒什么风险。

q.en: Does dark academia need a murder mystery?
q.zh: 暗黑学院小说必须有谋杀谜案吗？

a.en: No. A scandal, theft, disappearance, or ethical conflict can drive the plot. Choose a central problem that tests the characters' loyalties and the institution's values.
a.zh: 不必。丑闻、盗窃、失踪或伦理冲突都能推动剧情。选择能考验人物忠诚和学院价值观的核心问题即可。

title.en: How to Write a Space Opera with a Human Story at Its Center
title.zh: 如何写出以人物为核心的太空歌剧

seo_title.en: Write a Space Opera

description.en: Balance a large-scale conflict with a viewpoint character, understandable world rules, and personal consequences.
description.zh: 用清晰视角人物、易懂的世界规则和个人后果平衡宏大冲突。

answer.en: Space opera combines large-scale adventure with relationships and decisions readers can follow. Keep a human-scale goal at the center, explain only the technology and politics needed for the scene, and show how distant events alter a character's immediate choices.
answer.zh: 太空歌剧把宏大冒险与读者能跟上的关系和决定结合起来。以人物层面的目标为中心，只解释场景所需的科技与政治，并呈现远方事件如何改变眼前选择。

heading.en: Anchor the scale in one character's goal
heading.zh: 用一个人物目标锚定宏大尺度

body.en: A war or political shift becomes easier to grasp when it affects a home, crew, promise, or mission. Give readers someone to follow through the scale change.
body.zh: 战争或政治变化影响到家园、船员、承诺或任务时，更容易理解。让读者跟随一个人物经历尺度变化。

heading.en: Introduce world rules at the point of use
heading.zh: 在规则发挥作用时介绍它

body.en: Show how travel, communication, or weapons work when they change an available choice. Keep rules consistent, and let a limit create a tactical or emotional cost.
body.zh: 旅行、通信或武器会改变选项时再说明其运作方式。保持规则一致，并让限制带来策略或情感代价。

heading.en: Connect the spectacle to a consequence
heading.zh: 让宏大场面带来后果

body.en: After a fleet battle or political reveal, show what changes for the crew, community, or objective. A large event matters when it removes options or forces a new commitment.
body.zh: 舰队战或政治揭示之后，展示船员、社群或目标发生了什么变化。宏大事件只有在关闭选项或迫使新承诺时才真正重要。

q.en: Do readers need a map of the galaxy?
q.zh: 读者需要一张银河系地图吗？

a.en: Only if location choices affect the story. A small route or relationship sketch may be clearer than a large map full of places that never matter.
a.zh: 只有地点选择会影响故事时才需要。简单航线或关系示意图，可能比布满无关地点的大地图更清楚。

title.en: How to Write a Romantic-Suspense Novel That Balances Both Plots
title.zh: 如何平衡爱情线与悬疑线，写好浪漫惊悚小说

seo_title.en: Write a Romantic-Suspense Novel

description.en: Make the external danger pressure the relationship while both the mystery and romance move toward earned resolutions.
description.zh: 让外部危险给关系施压，同时推动悬疑和爱情走向可信的解决。

answer.en: Romantic suspense works when danger changes the relationship and the relationship changes how characters face danger. Give the external threat a fair cause-and-effect path, build trust through choices, and resolve both the safety question and the romantic promise.
answer.zh: 外部危险会改变关系、关系也改变人物应对危险的方式时，浪漫惊悚才成立。让威胁有清晰因果，通过选择建立信任，并同时解决安全问题和爱情承诺。

heading.en: Make the danger affect the relationship
heading.zh: 让危险影响人物关系

body.en: The threat can force cooperation, test a boundary, or expose a difference in risk tolerance. Keep each character's practical goal alive so romance does not pause the suspense plot.
body.zh: 威胁可以迫使合作、考验边界或暴露风险偏好的差异。让每个人物仍追求具体目标，不要让爱情暂停悬疑线。

heading.en: Build trust through costly choices
heading.zh: 通过有代价的选择建立信任

body.en: A character can share evidence, respect a refusal, or accept help despite a past betrayal. Let trust grow from actions under pressure rather than from attraction alone.
body.zh: 人物可以分享证据、尊重拒绝，或在经历背叛后接受帮助。让信任从压力下的行动中成长，而非只靠吸引力。

heading.en: Resolve both promises in the climax
heading.zh: 在高潮兑现两条故事承诺

body.en: The confrontation should answer what happens to the threat and what the characters choose about each other. Make the emotional resolution follow from how they acted together.
body.zh: 最终对抗要回应危险如何解决，以及人物如何选择彼此。让情感结局来自他们共同经历中的行动。

q.en: Should the romance begin before the suspense plot?
q.zh: 爱情线应该先于悬疑线开始吗？

a.en: Either order can work. Establish both the danger and the relationship's potential early enough that neither feels attached after the story is already underway.
a.zh: 两种顺序都可以。要尽早建立危险和关系潜力，避免故事已经展开后才生硬添加其中一条线。
