text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Write Screenplay Exposition Through Conflict
title.zh: 电影剧本怎么用冲突自然交代背景

seo_title.en: Write Screenplay Exposition
seo_title.zh: 电影剧本背景信息写法

description.en: Reveal necessary backstory through goals, disagreements, and objects that change what characters can do.
description.zh: 通过目标、分歧和改变人物行动的物件揭示必要背景。

answer.en: Write screenplay exposition where a character needs the information, resists it, or uses it to change a decision. Introduce only the context viewers need at that moment, then let action or disagreement show its consequence. If dialogue only tells the audience what every character already knows, move the information into a choice or reveal.
answer.zh: 当人物需要某条信息、抗拒它或用它改变决定时，再把背景信息写进剧本。只介绍观众当下需要的内容，再用行动或分歧展现其后果。如果对白只是在告诉角色们早已知道的事，就把信息转成选择或揭示。

heading.en: Decide What Viewers Need to Know Now
heading.zh: 判断观众此刻需要知道什么

body.en:
List the facts necessary to understand the current goal, risk, or relationship. Hold back details that will not change what viewers think about the scene.

Give the information to a character who has a reason to raise it. A question, accusation, request, or misunderstanding can introduce context while giving the scene an immediate objective.
body.zh:
列出理解当前目标、风险或关系所需的事实。不会改变观众对场景判断的细节，可以暂时留着。

让有理由的人物提出信息。提问、指责、请求或误会能在交代背景的同时赋予场景眼前目标。

heading.en: Make Information Change the Scene
heading.zh: 让信息改变场景走向

body.en:
Let the information create disagreement, alter leverage, or force a new choice. A document, object, or visible reaction can carry part of the context so dialogue does not have to explain everything.

Cut lines that repeat what the image already shows. When characters do explain, let them speak from different knowledge or interests rather than reciting a shared history for the audience.
body.zh:
让信息制造分歧、改变筹码或迫使人物作出新选择。文件、物件或可见反应可以承载部分背景，减少对白解释。

删去重复画面内容的台词。人物必须说明时，也要让他们因知识或利益不同而各自表达，而不是替观众复述共同历史。

heading.en: Check That the Exposition Plays on Screen
heading.zh: 检查背景信息是否能通过画面成立

body.en:
Read the scene without the explanatory lines and see whether action still makes sense. Add a visual cue or brief exchange where the audience genuinely needs orientation.

Give viewers a little time to register names, dates, or relationships before asking them to follow a new turn. The scene should remain active while the context becomes clear.
body.zh:
去掉解释台词后重读场景，看看行动是否仍然成立。观众确实需要定位时，再补画面线索或简短交流。

在要求观众跟上新转折前，给他们一点时间记住人名、日期或关系。交代背景时场景仍应保持行动。

q.en: Can screenplay exposition appear in dialogue?
q.zh: 电影剧本可以用对白交代背景吗？

a.en: Yes, when the character has a reason to say it and the information affects the conversation or decision. Dialogue becomes cumbersome when it exists only to inform viewers about facts the characters share.
a.zh: 可以，只要人物有理由说出来，而且信息会影响谈话或决定。对白只为了让观众知道人物们共同熟知的事实时，就容易显得累赘。

text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Use Flashbacks in a Screenplay
title.zh: 电影剧本里的闪回怎么用

seo_title.en: Use Flashbacks in a Screenplay

description.en: Use a flashback to change the meaning of a present choice, reveal needed evidence, or alter a relationship.
description.zh: 让闪回改变当下选择的含义、揭示必要证据或改变人物关系。

answer.en: Use a screenplay flashback when the past changes how viewers understand the present or what a character chooses next. Give it a clear trigger, show information the current scene cannot deliver as effectively, and return to the present with a consequence. Cut flashbacks that only repeat what the dialogue already explains.
answer.zh: 当过去会改变观众对当下的理解或人物下一步选择时，再在剧本中使用闪回。给它明确触发点，展现当前场景不易传达的信息，并带着后果回到现在。删去只重复对白说明的闪回。

heading.en: Choose What the Flashback Changes
heading.zh: 明确闪回要改变什么

body.en:
Decide whether the flashback reveals a fact, changes a relationship, or reframes a character’s memory. It should affect the audience’s reading of the present rather than simply provide biography.

If dialogue, an object, or a present-day action can deliver the same information with more force, use the simpler option.
body.zh:
确定闪回要揭示事实、改变关系，还是重新解释人物记忆。它应改变观众对当下的理解，而非只提供人物履历。

如果对白、物件或当下行动能更有力地传达同一信息，就选择更简单的方式。

heading.en: Trigger and Stage the Flashback Clearly
heading.zh: 清楚触发并呈现闪回

body.en:
Connect the transition to something the character sees, hears, touches, or avoids. Use a distinct visual or sound shift where needed so viewers can tell the time has changed.

Keep the flashback focused on its story job. Enter close to the relevant event and leave when the new information is complete; avoid staging an entire past scene if one action carries the point.
body.zh:
让转场和人物看见、听见、触碰或回避的东西相连。必要时用明显画面或声音变化，让观众知道时间已经改变。

让闪回聚焦于故事作用。接近关键事件时再进入，信息完成时就离开；一个动作已经说明问题时，不必重拍整段往事。

heading.en: Return to the Present with a Consequence
heading.zh: 带着后果回到当下

body.en:
Show what the character does differently after remembering or witnessing the past. The return should alter a plan, expose hesitation, or change how another person is treated.

Track chronology and what each character knows. A later reveal can reinterpret the same event, but the screenplay should make the relationship between the remembered version and the new evidence understandable.
body.zh:
呈现人物回忆或看见过去后有何不同做法。回到当下时应改变计划、暴露迟疑，或改变对待他人的方式。

追踪时间顺序和人物所知。后续揭示可以重新解释同一事件，但要让观众理解记忆版本与新证据之间的关系。

q.en: Should a screenplay show a flashback as soon as a character remembers something?
q.zh: 人物一想起往事，剧本就应该切进闪回吗？

a.en: Only when showing the past improves the scene. A line, reaction, or object may carry the memory more efficiently; use a full flashback when the event’s image or action changes the story’s meaning.
a.zh: 只有呈现过去能让场景更有效时才需要。台词、反应或物件可能更简洁地承载记忆；当事件画面或行动会改变故事含义时，再用完整闪回。

text.zh: 使用 drama-skills 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Create a Visual Motif for a Screenplay
title.zh: 电影剧本的视觉母题怎么设计

seo_title.en: Create a Visual Motif for a Film

description.en: Repeat an image or object with a changing meaning to connect scenes and make character change visible.
description.zh: 重复出现会改变含义的画面或物件，连接场景并让人物变化可见。

answer.en: Create a visual motif by choosing an image, object, or composition tied to a character’s concern, then repeating it at moments when its meaning can change. Let the motif connect scenes, reveal a shift in perspective, or prepare a payoff. Avoid repeating it so often that it becomes decoration or explanation.
answer.zh: 选择与人物在意之事相关的画面、物件或构图，并在含义可能变化的时刻重复出现，以此设计视觉母题。让它连接场景、揭示视角变化或铺垫回报。不要重复过多，让它沦为装饰或说明。

heading.en: Choose a Motif Connected to the Story
heading.zh: 选择与故事相关的母题

body.en:
Start with an object or image already present in the character’s world: a doorway, a damaged photograph, a repeated arrangement, or a particular color. Decide what it means at the beginning.

Choose something the production can show clearly and the audience can recognize without an explanation. A motif works best when it belongs naturally in the story world.
body.zh:
从人物世界中已经存在的物件或画面开始：门口、受损照片、重复摆放，或某种颜色。先确定它在开头代表什么。

选择制作上容易呈现、观众无需解释就能认出的元素。母题自然属于故事世界时效果最好。

heading.en: Repeat It When Its Meaning Can Change
heading.zh: 在含义能够变化时重复出现

body.en:
Bring the motif back after a decision, reveal, loss, or change in a relationship. Alter the framing, condition, or context so the audience feels a difference rather than seeing an identical insert.

Do not force it into every scene. Track its appearances in the outline and remove any repetition that adds no new information or feeling.
body.zh:
在决定、揭示、失去或关系变化后让母题重现。调整构图、状态或语境，让观众感到差异，而非看到完全相同的插入镜头。

不要强迫它进入每场戏。在提纲里追踪出现位置，删去没有新增信息或情绪的重复。

heading.en: Pay Off the Motif Through Action
heading.zh: 用行动兑现母题

body.en:
Near the climax, let a character interact with the image or object in a way that shows a changed belief, choice, or relationship. The audience should be able to read the shift from the action and prior appearances.

Review the motif without dialogue. If its progression is impossible to notice, strengthen the visual changes; if it explains the theme too directly, let the story’s conflict carry more meaning.
body.zh:
接近高潮时，让人物以不同方式触碰或使用画面、物件，体现信念、选择或关系的变化。观众应能从行动和此前的出现方式读出转变。

去掉对白复核母题。如果变化难以察觉，就加强视觉差异；如果它把主题说得太直白，就让冲突承担更多含义。

q.en: Does a visual motif need to appear in every act?
q.zh: 视觉母题必须每一幕都出现吗？

a.en: No fixed schedule is required. Return to it when the story has created a meaningful change in context, and leave space between appearances so each one can register.
a.zh: 不需要固定频率。故事语境出现有意义的变化时再让它重现，并在两次出现之间留出间隔，让每次变化都能被注意到。

title.en: How to Write an Anime Recap Script for New Viewers
title.zh: 动漫剧情解说稿怎么写给新观众看

seo_title.en: Write an Anime Recap Script

description.en: Summarize the story clearly, preserve the character motives and turning points, and explain only the context new viewers need.
description.zh: 清楚概述剧情，保留人物动机和关键转折，只解释新观众需要的背景。

answer.en: Write an anime recap around the season or story question viewers need to understand. Introduce characters by their goals, connect major events through cause and effect, and select scenes that change the situation. Mark spoilers clearly and avoid listing every episode beat when a concise arc summary will serve the audience better.
answer.zh: 围绕观众需要理解的季度或故事问题编写动漫解说。通过目标介绍人物，用因果连接主要事件，并选择真正改变局势的场景。清楚标示剧透；能用简洁弧线概括时，不必罗列每集所有节拍。

heading.en: Set the Recap Scope and Spoiler Promise
heading.zh: 确定解说范围与剧透承诺

body.en:
Name the season, arc, or set of episodes the video covers and tell viewers whether it contains major spoilers. Decide the audience: people returning to a series, newcomers, or fans checking one character’s story.

Use that promise to choose what to explain. A newcomer needs a little more world context; a returning viewer may mainly need the relationships and unresolved question restored.
body.zh:
说明视频覆盖哪一季、哪条故事线或哪些集，并告诉观众是否包含重大剧透。确定受众是回归观众、新观众，还是关注某个人物剧情的粉丝。

按承诺决定解释多少背景。新观众需要多一点世界设定；回归观众则可能只需要恢复人物关系和未解决的问题。

heading.en: Organize Events by Cause and Effect
heading.zh: 按因果关系组织剧情事件

body.en:
Build a short timeline of decisions and consequences rather than copying the episode order into narration. Explain how one character’s action changes another person’s goal, knowledge, or risk.

Keep names and relationships clear on first mention. When several factions or supernatural rules matter, introduce only what helps the audience follow the current conflict.
body.zh:
把人物决定及其后果整理成简短时间线，不要把集数顺序原样念进旁白。说明一个人的行动如何改变另一个人的目标、认知或风险。

首次提到人物时交代清楚姓名和关系。多个阵营或超自然规则都重要时，也只引入跟上当前冲突所需的内容。

heading.en: Select Turning Points Instead of Every Beat
heading.zh: 选关键转折，不必覆盖每个节拍

body.en:
Keep scenes that establish a goal, change an alliance, reveal new information, or create a lasting consequence. Combine repeated attempts that lead to the same result.

Check the recap against the actual episode and maintain a source note for details. A summary can be concise, but it should not change what a character knew or why they acted.
body.zh:
保留建立目标、改变同盟、揭示新信息或造成持续后果的场景。多次尝试若结果相同，可以合并概述。

对照原集复核解说，并记录细节来源。摘要可以简洁，但不能改写人物知道什么或行动原因。

q.en: How much of an anime season should a recap include?
q.zh: 动漫季度解说要包括多少内容？

a.en: Include the events needed to explain the arc’s central change and the characters’ current situation. Leave out scenes that do not alter goals, relationships, or understanding, unless viewers specifically need them for context.
a.zh: 包括解释故事弧线核心变化和人物当前处境所需的事件。不会改变目标、关系或认知的场景可略去，除非观众需要它们理解背景。

text.en: Use the video-recap workflow to plan, draft, and revise the work while keeping decisions and consistency visible.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Write a Video Essay About a Film Performance
title.zh: 如何围绕电影表演写视频论文

seo_title.en: Video Essay About a Film Performance

description.en: Analyze an actor’s choices with evidence from voice, movement, framing, and scene context.
description.zh: 结合声音、动作、镜头构图和场景语境，用证据分析演员的表演选择。

answer.en: Build a video essay about a film performance around one claim about what the actor’s choices accomplish. Support it with specific moments in voice, movement, timing, and interaction with the frame. Briefly explain the scene context, then connect the performance details to character, relationship, or audience effect.
answer.zh: 围绕“演员的表演选择带来了什么效果”提出一个主张。用声音、动作、时机和画面互动中的具体时刻支撑它。简要交代场景背景，再把表演细节联系到人物、关系或观众感受。

heading.en: Make One Claim About What the Performance Does
heading.zh: 提出一个关于表演效果的主张

body.en:
Choose a scene or arc and state what changes because of the performance: a character hides fear, gains authority, or shifts a relationship without saying so directly. Keep the claim small enough for the available examples.

Separate observation from interpretation. Describe what the actor does first, then explain what the choice may communicate and how the scene supports that reading.
body.zh:
选择一场戏或一段人物弧线，说明表演带来了什么变化：人物藏起恐惧、取得主动权，或在没有直说时改变关系。主张范围要适合手头的例子。

区分观察与解释。先描述演员做了什么，再说明这个选择可能传达什么，以及场景如何支持这种理解。

heading.en: Select Specific Performance Evidence
heading.zh: 选择具体表演证据

body.en:
Note vocal pace, pauses, emphasis, posture, gesture, gaze, and how the actor responds to a scene partner. Use only details that strengthen the claim.

When making a point about framing or editing, name those choices separately. The actor’s performance interacts with the camera and cut, but the essay should not attribute every effect to the actor alone.
body.zh:
记录语速、停顿、重音、姿势、手势、视线，以及演员如何回应搭戏者。只使用能加强主张的细节。

分析构图或剪辑时要单独说明。表演会与镜头和剪辑互动，但不要把所有效果都归因于演员。

heading.en: Connect the Performance to the Scene and Film
heading.zh: 把表演联系到场景与全片

body.en:
Give viewers enough context to understand what the character wants and what is at risk in the scene. Then show how a performance choice affects that goal or the relationship.

Use a second moment only when comparison makes the change clearer. End by returning to the claim and explaining what the evidence lets viewers notice on a rewatch.
body.zh:
交代理解人物目标和场景风险所需的背景，再展示表演选择如何影响目标或关系。

只有当对比能让变化更清楚时才使用第二个时刻。结尾回到主张，说明这些证据能让观众重看时注意到什么。

q.en: Can a video essay analyze an actor without discussing the script?
q.zh: 分析演员表演时可以不谈剧本吗？

a.en: Yes, but scene context helps explain what the actor is responding to. Focus the essay on observable performance while noting relevant writing, direction, framing, or editing when they shape the evidence.
a.zh: 可以，但场景语境能说明演员在回应什么。分析重点可放在可观察到的表演上；剧本、导演、构图或剪辑确实影响证据时也应说明。

text.en: Use the video-recap workflow to plan, draft, and revise the work while keeping decisions and consistency visible.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Write Body Language in Fiction
title.zh: 小说人物的肢体语言怎么写

seo_title.en: Write Body Language in Fiction

description.en: Use posture, gestures, movement, and distance to show what a character notices, hides, or chooses.
description.zh: 通过姿势、手势、动作和距离，呈现人物注意、隐藏或选择的内容。

answer.en: Write body language by choosing a physical detail that fits the character, scene, and emotion, then let it affect the interaction. Avoid treating gestures as fixed translations for feelings. Combine movement, timing, and distance with dialogue or setting so readers can infer what the character wants or avoids.
answer.zh: 根据人物、场景和情绪选择合适的身体细节，并让它影响互动。不要把某个动作固定翻译成某种情绪。将动作、时机和距离与对白或环境结合，让读者推断人物想要什么、在回避什么。

heading.en: Choose a Detail Specific to the Character
heading.zh: 选择符合人物特点的动作细节

body.en:
Notice what this character does under pressure: handle an object, turn away, hold still, move closer, or change pace. Their habit can reflect personality, but the current context should shape what it means.

Prefer an observable action over a label such as “nervous” or “confident.” Make the detail specific enough to picture, and avoid giving every character the same set of gestures.
body.zh:
观察人物在压力下会做什么：摆弄物件、转身、保持不动、靠近或改变步速。习惯可以体现性格，但当下语境要决定动作的含义。

用可见动作替代“紧张”“自信”等标签。细节要具体到能想象，也避免所有人物都用同一套动作。

heading.en: Connect Movement to the Interaction
heading.zh: 让动作参与人物互动

body.en:
Let movement change what another person can do: a character steps between two people, closes a door, or keeps an object out of reach. Show how the other person notices, responds, or fails to notice.

Use distance and timing as part of the scene. A pause before answering, a delayed handoff, or a shift in posture can change the meaning of spoken words.
body.zh:
让动作改变另一个人能做什么：人物挡在两人之间、关上门，或把物品留在对方够不到的地方。写出对方是否注意到、如何回应。

把距离和时机也写进场景。回答前的停顿、迟来的递交或姿势变化，都可能改变台词含义。

heading.en: Avoid Turning Gestures into a Dictionary
heading.zh: 不要把动作写成固定情绪词典

body.en:
The same gesture can mean different things in different situations. A folded arm may be comfort, cold, impatience, or simply how someone stands; the surrounding action should guide the reader.

Use body language selectively. If a gesture repeats without changing the relationship, mood, or choice, remove it. Let dialogue and action provide the rest of the emotional evidence.
body.zh:
同一动作在不同情境中可能含义不同。抱臂可能表示自我安慰、寒冷、不耐烦，也可能只是站姿；周围行动要帮助读者理解。

有选择地使用肢体语言。如果一个动作反复出现，却没有改变关系、情绪或选择，就删去。情感证据还可以由对白和行动补足。

q.en: Can body language replace dialogue in fiction?
q.zh: 小说里可以用肢体语言代替对白吗？

a.en: Sometimes. An action can show hesitation, refusal, or care more effectively than an explanation, but important information may still need words. Choose the form that creates the clearest scene.
a.zh: 有时可以。动作可能比解释更有效地表现迟疑、拒绝或关心，但重要信息仍可能需要语言。选择最能让场景清楚成立的表达方式。

text.zh: 使用 oh-story 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Build Tension in a Fiction Scene
title.zh: 小说场景中的张力怎么递增

seo_title.en: Build Tension in a Fiction Scene

description.en: Increase tension through a clear goal, a credible obstacle, and decisions that make the outcome less certain.
description.zh: 用明确目标、可信阻碍和降低结果确定性的决定逐步增强张力。

answer.en: Build scene tension by giving a character a goal, adding an obstacle with a credible cost, and making each attempt change the available options. Let the reader understand what can be lost, vary the pressure, and end the scene with a result or decision that changes what happens next. Suspense works best when the character’s actions—not arbitrary delay—create uncertainty.
answer.zh: 先给人物一个目标，加入带有可信代价的阻碍，再让每次尝试改变可选方案，以此增强场景张力。让读者理解可能失去什么，变化压力，并以结果或决定改变后续的方式结束场景。悬念最好来自人物行动，而非刻意拖延。

heading.en: Give the Scene an Urgent, Understandable Goal
heading.zh: 为场景设定紧迫且清楚的目标

body.en:
State what the viewpoint character wants before the scene ends: gain an answer, protect someone, keep a secret, or leave safely. The goal should be possible to recognize through action.

Name what failure costs. A consequence can be emotional, practical, or relational, but it should matter to this character now rather than only to the story in general.
body.zh:
说明视角人物在场景结束前想得到什么：找到答案、保护某人、守住秘密或安全离开。目标应能从行动中看出来。

明确失败的代价。后果可以关乎情感、现实或关系，但必须对人物当下重要，而不只是对故事大局重要。

heading.en: Make Obstacles Change the Plan
heading.zh: 让阻碍迫使人物调整计划

body.en:
Let the first attempt reveal a complication, then require a different tactic. Each response can spend time, expose information, damage trust, or reduce access to a resource.

Avoid repeating the same delay. If an obstacle does not alter a choice or raise the cost, cut it or connect it to a consequence that matters.
body.zh:
让第一次尝试揭示复杂情况，迫使人物采用新办法。每次回应都可能消耗时间、暴露信息、损害信任或减少资源。

避免重复同一种拖延。如果阻碍没有改变选择或提高代价，就删掉，或让它连接到重要后果。

heading.en: Control Information Without Cheating the Reader
heading.zh: 控制信息，但不要误导读者

body.en:
Decide what the character and reader know at each beat. A missing fact can create suspense when the viewpoint has a believable reason not to notice it; withholding information the character clearly understands may feel unfair.

Vary the pressure with a brief pause, new evidence, or an unexpected cost. Let the scene end when the goal changes, an answer arrives, or the character must make a harder choice.
body.zh:
逐个节拍确认人物和读者分别知道什么。只要视角人物确实有理由没发现，信息缺失就能制造悬念；人物明明理解却故意不让读者知道，则可能显得不公平。

用短暂停顿、新证据或意外代价变化压力。目标改变、答案出现或人物必须作出更难选择时，可以结束场景。

q.en: Does every scene in a novel need tension?
q.zh: 小说的每个场景都需要张力吗？

a.en: Every scene should change something or deepen what readers understand, but not every scene needs danger or urgency. Quiet scenes can create anticipation, reveal relationships, or give a later conflict more meaning.
a.zh: 每场戏都应改变局势或加深读者理解，但不必每场都有危险和紧迫感。安静场景也能制造期待、揭示关系，或让后续冲突更有分量。

text.zh: 使用 oh-story 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Write a Story for an RPG
title.zh: 角色扮演游戏的故事怎么写

seo_title.en: Write a Story for an RPG
seo_title.zh: 角色扮演游戏剧情写作

description.en: Connect the player character’s goal, companions, quests, and progression into one campaign arc.
description.zh: 把玩家角色目标、同伴、任务和成长连接成一条战役弧线。

answer.en: Write an RPG story around a player character with a clear reason to act, companions with their own goals, and quests that change the campaign state. Let character progression affect relationships or choices, not only statistics. Balance a central arc with optional stories that enrich the world without making the main goal unclear.
answer.zh: 围绕有明确行动理由的玩家角色、各有目标的同伴，以及会改变战役状态的任务来写RPG故事。让人物成长影响关系或选择，而不只改变数值。平衡核心主线和可选故事，让后者丰富世界却不模糊主要目标。

heading.en: Define the Player’s Role and Campaign Goal
heading.zh: 明确玩家角色和战役目标

body.en:
Give the player character a reason to join the central conflict and enough agency to affect its direction. The role can be open-ended, but the goal and current stakes should be understandable.

Connect the campaign objective to the game’s main actions. If progress depends on exploration, negotiation, or combat, let story events make those actions matter.
body.zh:
为玩家角色设定参与核心冲突的理由，并给予影响进展的主动性。身份可以开放，但目标和当前利害要清楚。

让战役目标与游戏主要行动相连。如果进展依赖探索、谈判或战斗，就让剧情事件体现这些行动的意义。

heading.en: Weave Companions and Quests into the Campaign
heading.zh: 把同伴与任务编进战役主线

body.en:
Give companions goals that sometimes align and sometimes conflict with the player’s path. Use quests to change knowledge, trust, resources, or the state of a place—not simply to send the player elsewhere.

Keep optional stories optional while allowing their outcomes to matter. A side quest can change a later encounter or reveal a new perspective without becoming the only way to understand the main plot.
body.zh:
让同伴目标有时与玩家一致，有时产生冲突。任务应改变认知、信任、资源或地点状态，而不只是把玩家派到别处。

可选故事仍可产生影响，但要保持真正可选。支线可以改变后续相遇或揭示新视角，不应成为理解主线的唯一途径。

heading.en: Make Progression Affect More Than Numbers
heading.zh: 让成长不只改变数值

body.en:
Connect new abilities, titles, or relationships to fresh options in dialogue and objectives. Players should see how growth changes what they can attempt or how others respond.

Track story flags and character knowledge across the campaign. When players can complete quests in different orders, write state-aware lines and summaries that preserve the main causal chain.
body.zh:
把新能力、称号或关系连接到对白与目标中的新选项。让玩家看见成长如何改变可尝试的行动，或他人如何回应。

跨战役追踪剧情标记和人物认知。玩家能以不同顺序完成任务时，要编写识别状态的台词和回顾，保持主要因果链清楚。

q.en: How do you balance main quests and side quests in an RPG?
q.zh: RPG里主线和支线任务怎么平衡？

a.en: Keep the main goal visible and let side quests add relationships, context, or consequences. Players should be able to return to the central arc without completing every optional story.
a.zh: 让主线目标始终清楚，并让支线增加关系、背景或后果。玩家应能不做完所有可选故事，也回到核心弧线。

text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Plan an Episodic Game Story
title.zh: 分章节发布的游戏剧情怎么规划

seo_title.en: Plan an Episodic Game Story

description.en: Give each episode a local payoff while building a larger arc players can follow between releases.
description.zh: 让每章都有阶段回报，同时逐步构建玩家能追踪的长线故事。

answer.en: Plan an episodic game story with one local question and resolution per release, plus a larger character or world change that develops over time. Make every episode understandable when played alone, preserve consequences across chapters, and provide a concise recap so returning players can resume the story.
answer.zh: 为每次发布安排一个阶段问题与解决，同时逐步推进更大的角色或世界变化。让每章单独游玩也能理解，跨章节保留后果，并提供简短回顾帮助回归玩家接上剧情。

heading.en: Give Each Episode a Local Story Arc
heading.zh: 让每章都有自身故事弧线

body.en:
State what the player is trying to accomplish in this installment, what complicates it, and what changes by the end. A local resolution creates satisfaction even when the larger mystery or relationship continues.

Avoid ending every episode on the same kind of cliffhanger. Use a decision, discovery, victory, or cost to create a distinct close that grows from the episode’s events.
body.zh:
明确玩家本章要完成什么、什么使它复杂化，以及结束时有何变化。即使长线谜题或关系继续发展，阶段解决也能带来满足感。

不要每章都用同一种悬念收尾。用决定、发现、胜利或代价形成不同结尾，并让它来自本章事件。

heading.en: Carry Choices and Consequences Between Episodes
heading.zh: 让选择与后果跨章节延续

body.en:
Track decisions, relationships, character knowledge, and changed locations that later chapters must respect. Decide which states alter dialogue, objectives, or available paths.

If a major branch reunites, preserve the player’s distinct costs, information, or relationships. Convergence should reduce content scope without pretending every route was identical.
body.zh:
记录后续章节必须承认的决定、关系、人物认知和地点变化，明确哪些状态会影响对白、目标或路线。

重要分支汇合时也要保留玩家承担的不同代价、获得的信息或关系变化。汇合可以控制内容规模，却不能假装各条路线完全相同。

heading.en: Help Players Return After a Break
heading.zh: 帮助隔一段时间后回归的玩家

body.en:
Give a short recap of the current goal, recent consequence, and unresolved question. Include the context needed for the next action without replaying every previous scene.

Test transitions between releases. Confirm that saved choices load correctly, the episode opens on a clear objective, and a player who missed an optional installment can still follow the main story.
body.zh:
简短回顾当前目标、最近后果和未解决的问题。提供执行下一步所需背景，不必重播此前每场戏。

测试章节之间的衔接：存档选择能正确载入，开篇目标清楚，错过可选章节的玩家仍能跟上主线。

q.en: Should each episode of a game end on a cliffhanger?
q.zh: 游戏每一章都应该用悬念结尾吗？

a.en: No. End on the payoff that fits the episode: a resolved objective, difficult choice, discovery, or new consequence. Reserve a cliffhanger for a turn that genuinely creates a compelling next question.
a.zh: 不必。根据章节内容选择结尾：完成目标、艰难决定、发现真相或新后果。只有真正带来重要新问题时才用悬念。

title.en: How to Explain a TV Series Ending with Evidence
title.zh: 电视剧结局解析视频怎么用证据讲清楚

seo_title.en: Explain a TV Series Ending

description.en: Track the finale’s main questions, payoffs, and open threads, then support your interpretation with scenes from the series.
description.zh: 梳理结局回应的问题、完成的铺垫和保留的线索，再用剧集场景支撑解读。

answer.en: Explain a TV series ending by stating what the finale resolves, what it leaves open, and how earlier scenes support that reading. Track character arcs and long-running story questions across the relevant seasons, distinguish what the show confirms from interpretation, and avoid treating every unanswered detail as a hidden clue.
answer.zh: 解析剧集结局时，说明终集解决了什么、留下了什么，以及早先哪些场景支持你的解读。跨相关季数追踪人物弧线和长期问题，区分剧集明确表达的内容与个人推论，别把所有未回答细节都当成隐藏线索。

heading.en: State the Main Questions the Finale Answers
heading.zh: 说明结局回答了哪些核心问题

body.en:
Write the questions viewers have followed: what happens to a character, whether a conflict ends, or what a major choice means. Separate questions resolved by the finale from those intentionally left open.

Keep a scope note for which seasons or story threads the video covers. A whole-series ending explanation may need more context than a recap of one season’s final episode.
body.zh:
写下观众一直追踪的问题：某个人物的去向、冲突是否结束，或重大选择意味着什么。区分结局已解决的问题和有意保留的问题。

注明视频覆盖哪些季数和故事线。解析全剧结局所需背景，通常多于复述一季的终集。

heading.en: Gather Evidence from the Relevant Episodes
heading.zh: 从相关剧集中搜集证据

body.en:
Build a short evidence list with episode, scene, and what the moment establishes. Include character decisions, repeated images, dialogue, or changes in relationship that genuinely connect to the finale.

Check chronology and context before quoting or showing a moment. A line can mean something different before or after later information, so preserve the surrounding scene in your explanation.
body.zh:
列一份简短证据表，记下集数、场景及其确立的信息。选取真正与结局相关的人物决定、重复画面、对白或关系变化。

引用或展示场景前核对时间顺序和语境。后续信息出现前后，同一句话的含义可能不同；解析时要保留周边情境。

heading.en: Separate Confirmed Facts from Interpretation
heading.zh: 区分剧集确认内容与个人解读

body.en:
Mark which claims the episode states directly and which are your reading of the evidence. Explain why one interpretation fits the scenes, and acknowledge a plausible alternative when the series leaves ambiguity.

End by returning to the viewer’s central question. Avoid adding invented canon or claiming that a future season is guaranteed; make clear what the existing story supports.
body.zh:
标明哪些观点是剧集直接确认的，哪些是你对证据的解读。说明某种解释为何符合场景；剧集有意留白时，也可承认合理的其他读法。

结尾回到观众最关心的问题。不要补造正史，也别断言续作一定存在；清楚说明现有故事能够支持什么。

q.en: Should an ending explanation cover every loose end in a series?
q.zh: 结局解析需要解释剧集的每个悬念吗？

a.en: Focus on threads that affect the finale’s central outcome or character choices. Distinguish intentionally open questions from details that the show simply does not answer, and do not force a theory where evidence is missing.
a.zh: 聚焦影响终局和人物选择的故事线。区分有意保留的问题与剧集没有回答的细节；证据不足时不要硬套理论。

text.zh: 使用 video-recap 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Continue a Novel Without Losing Continuity
title.zh: 续写小说时怎么保持前后连贯

seo_title.en: Continue a Novel with Continuity

description.en: Review character state, viewpoint, location, and unresolved promises before choosing the next action or scene.
description.zh: 确定下一个行动或场景前，先复核人物状态、视角、位置和未回收的铺垫。

answer.en: Continue a novel by checking the current scene state before drafting: who is present, what each person knows, what they want, and what has changed. Choose one next action that follows from the last consequence, keep the established viewpoint and voice, and update notes when the story changes. Do not restart the whole outline unless a contradiction shows the plan no longer works.
answer.zh: 续写小说前先检查当前场景状态：谁在场、每个人知道什么、想要什么，以及刚发生了什么变化。选择一个由上一段后果自然引出的行动，保持既定视角和文风；故事变化时及时更新记录。除非发现矛盾表明计划失效，不必重做整份大纲。

heading.en: Review the Current Scene State
heading.zh: 复核当前场景状态

body.en:
Write a short snapshot of each character’s location, physical condition, knowledge, goal, and relationship to others. Include the time, setting, and any object or promise that must carry forward.

Separate confirmed facts from a character’s assumptions. A person may act on a mistaken belief, but the narration should not accidentally treat that belief as truth.
body.zh:
简要记录每个人物的位置、身体状态、认知、目标和关系，再记下时间、地点，以及需要延续的物件或承诺。

区分已确认事实和人物假设。人物可以基于错误认知行动，但叙述不能无意间把误解写成事实。

heading.en: Choose the Next Action from the Last Consequence
heading.zh: 从上一段后果推导下一个行动

body.en:
Ask what the last event makes someone do, avoid, or decide. A new scene can follow another character or move in time, but it should preserve the cause that makes the transition useful.

Write the next scene’s goal and obstacle in a sentence before drafting. If the action does not grow from the current state, add the missing motivation or choose a different next beat.
body.zh:
思考上一件事会让谁采取行动、回避什么或作出什么决定。新场景可以转向别的人物或跳过时间，但要保留让转场有用的原因。

动笔前用一句话写出下一场的目标和阻碍。若行动无法从当前状态生长出来，就补上缺少的动机或另选节拍。

heading.en: Preserve Voice and Update Continuity Notes
heading.zh: 保持文风并更新连续性记录

body.en:
Carry forward point of view, tense, character knowledge, and unresolved setups. Read the prior passage aloud if needed, then draft a small section and compare it with the established voice.

After a new decision changes a relationship, location, or timeline, update the reference notes. Keep the record short and useful; a concise state summary is easier to trust than pages of notes that no longer match the draft.
body.zh:
延续叙事视角、时态、人物认知和未解决的铺垫。必要时朗读上一段，再起草一小段并对照既有文风。

人物决定改变关系、地点或时间线后，及时更新参考记录。记录应简短实用；准确的状态摘要比与草稿脱节的长篇笔记更可靠。

q.en: Should I reread the whole novel before continuing a draft?
q.zh: 继续写之前需要重读整本小说吗？

a.en: Reread the latest relevant scenes and consult a concise continuity summary. Return to earlier chapters when a relationship, promise, or fact needs verification; targeted review usually helps more than restarting from page one.
a.zh: 先重读最近的相关场景，并查看简明的连续性摘要。需要核实关系、承诺或事实时再回看早期章节；针对性复核通常比从第一页重读更有效。

text.en: Use the oh-story workflow to plan, draft, and revise the work while keeping decisions and consistency visible.
text.zh: 使用 oh-story 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Design a Story for a Simulation Game
title.zh: 模拟经营游戏的故事怎么设计

seo_title.en: Design a Simulation Game Story

description.en: Let player systems, recurring decisions, and visible changes create a story that grows through play.
description.zh: 让玩家系统、重复决策和可见变化共同生成随游玩发展的故事。

answer.en: Design a simulation game story around the systems players manage and the changes they create over time. Give recurring actions consequences for people or places, add goals that introduce new decisions, and make progress visible. The story can emerge from play without requiring a fixed cutscene after every action.
answer.zh: 围绕玩家管理的系统及其随时间产生的变化来设计模拟游戏故事。让重复行动影响人物或地点，加入带来新决定的目标，并让进展看得见。故事可以从游玩中涌现，不必每个行动后都安排固定过场。

heading.en: Identify the System Players Will Shape
heading.zh: 明确玩家将要改变的系统

body.en:
Choose what the player manages: a town, team, farm, household, business, or ecosystem. Establish the system’s starting need and what success or neglect changes.

Let the setting and rules create story pressure. Scarcity, growth, maintenance, and competing priorities can generate choices without inventing a crisis unrelated to the simulation.
body.zh:
确定玩家要管理什么：城镇、队伍、农场、家庭、企业或生态。说明系统初始需求，以及改善或疏于管理会带来什么变化。

让环境和规则制造剧情压力。稀缺、发展、维护和优先级冲突都能生成选择，不必凭空增加与模拟无关的危机。

heading.en: Make Repeated Actions Create Visible Change
heading.zh: 让重复行动带来可见变化

body.en:
Show how a routine task affects a character, resource, or place. A change can be small, but it should accumulate so players can recognize the result of their decisions.

Use characters to express different needs within the system. Their requests should connect to mechanics the player understands, and their responses should update when conditions change.
body.zh:
呈现日常任务如何影响人物、资源或地点。变化可以很小，但应逐步累积，让玩家看见决定的结果。

用人物表达系统内不同需求。他们的请求应连接到玩家理解的玩法，条件变化时回应也要更新。

heading.en: Connect Milestones with Emergent Stories
heading.zh: 把发展里程碑和自然生成的故事连接起来

body.en:
Create milestones that introduce a new system, goal, or relationship rather than only increasing numbers. Let player priorities affect which events happen first and what state they reach.

Offer concise recaps or journals for long-running simulations. Players should be able to see what has changed, what remains unresolved, and which actions could lead to a new development.
body.zh:
设置会引入新系统、目标或关系的里程碑，而不只是增加数值。让玩家优先事项影响事件顺序和世界状态。

为长期模拟提供简明回顾或日志。玩家应能看出发生了什么变化、还有什么未解决，以及哪些行动可能带来新进展。

q.en: Does a simulation game need a fixed main story?
q.zh: 模拟游戏一定要有固定主线剧情吗？

a.en: No, but players need goals and consequences that make their actions matter. A set of milestones, relationships, or changing community needs can provide direction while leaving room for player-led stories.
a.zh: 不一定，但玩家需要有意义的目标与后果。发展里程碑、人际关系或社区需求变化能提供方向，同时保留玩家主导故事的空间。

text.en: Use the novel-to-game workflow to plan, draft, and revise the work while keeping decisions and consistency visible.
text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Write a Story Mode for a Fighting Game
title.zh: 格斗游戏的故事模式怎么写

seo_title.en: Fighting Game Story Mode

description.en: Connect a roster of fighters through rivalries, shared stakes, and match outcomes that move the central conflict.
description.zh: 用竞争关系、共同利害和影响冲突的比赛结果连接角色阵容。

answer.en: Write a fighting game story mode by giving the roster a shared conflict and distinct reasons to enter it. Let rivalries, alliances, and match outcomes change what characters know or want. Keep the central arc clear across playable routes, and give each fighter a meaningful role beyond appearing for one battle.
answer.zh: 给整套角色阵容一个共同冲突，并让每人都有不同的参战理由，以此编写格斗游戏故事模式。让竞争、同盟和比赛结果改变人物认知或目标。跨可玩路线保持主线清楚，也让每名角色不只打一场就退场。

heading.en: Give the Roster a Shared Conflict
heading.zh: 为角色阵容建立共同冲突

body.en:
Choose an event, threat, tournament, or resource that brings fighters together. State what each key character wants from it and what they risk.

Different motives create more engaging matchups than a bracket of unrelated fights. Let characters pursue different goals even when the game returns them to the same central event.
body.zh:
选择能让格斗者聚在一起的事件、威胁、赛事或资源。写清关键角色各自想得到什么、会承担什么风险。

人物动机不同，比安排一连串互不相关的比赛更有吸引力。即使角色都回到同一核心事件，也可以各自追求不同目标。

heading.en: Connect Matches to Character Arcs
heading.zh: 让每场对决推进人物弧线

body.en:
Use a fight to reveal a rivalry, test a belief, or force a character to recognize another person’s strength. The result should alter a relationship, plan, or understanding of the conflict.

Avoid making every match carry a long dialogue scene. A changed stance, rematch promise, or new objective can show the consequence and keep play moving.
body.zh:
让对决揭示竞争、检验信念，或迫使人物承认对手的实力。结果应改变关系、计划或对冲突的理解。

不必每场比赛后都安排长对白。态度变化、再战约定或新目标都能表现后果，并保持游玩节奏。

heading.en: Handle Character Routes and the Main Ending
heading.zh: 安排人物路线和核心结局

body.en:
Decide which scenes are shared, which differ by character, and what information each route contributes. Keep each route understandable without requiring players to complete the whole roster in a fixed order.

Bring routes together around a final conflict that pays off the shared stakes. Individual endings can add character closure, but they should not contradict the campaign’s established events without a clear reason.
body.zh:
确定哪些场景共用、哪些随角色变化，以及每条路线带来什么信息。不要要求玩家按固定顺序完成全阵容，才能看懂单条路线。

让各路线围绕兑现共同利害的最终冲突汇合。个人结局可以补足人物收束，但除非有明确理由，不应与战役既定事件矛盾。

q.en: Does every fighter need a separate story route?
q.zh: 每个格斗角色都需要单独剧情路线吗？

a.en: Not necessarily. Give each character a distinct motive and contribution, then use shared scenes where they fit. A short personal ending or response can create closure without repeating the full main story.
a.zh: 不一定。为每名角色安排独特动机和贡献，适合时使用共同场景。简短个人结局或回应也能形成收束，不必重复完整主线。

text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Adapt a Short Story into a Game
title.zh: 短篇小说怎么改编成游戏

seo_title.en: Adapt a Short Story into a Game

description.en: Preserve the source’s strongest choice or emotional turn while building a playable loop with enough room to respond.
description.zh: 保留原作最有力的选择或情感转折，同时构建有回应空间的可玩循环。

answer.en: Adapt a short story into a game by identifying its central choice, emotional payoff, and most playable action. Expand the interaction around that core rather than adding unrelated plot. Keep the game’s objective complete, and use context, exploration, or replay to deepen the source without stretching a compact story into filler.
answer.zh: 先找出短篇小说的核心选择、情感回报和最适合玩家参与的行动。围绕这些核心扩展互动，不要增加无关情节。让游戏目标完整，并用背景、探索或重玩加深原作体验，避免把短故事拉长成填充内容。

heading.en: Identify the Short Story’s Core Experience
heading.zh: 找出短篇原作的核心体验

body.en:
State the protagonist’s goal, the decision or discovery that changes the story, and what the ending makes readers feel or reconsider. Short fiction often depends on a concentrated turn rather than a large cast or broad world.

Choose which moment the player can influence, observe, or approach from a new perspective. Preserve the emotional job of a scene even if its events change.
body.zh:
写清主角目标、改变故事的决定或发现，以及结尾让读者感受到或重新思考什么。短篇小说往往依靠集中的转折，而非庞大角色阵容或广阔世界。

选择玩家可以影响、观察或从新视角接近的时刻。即使事件改变，也要保留场景原本的情感作用。

heading.en: Expand Interaction Without Adding Filler
heading.zh: 扩展互动，但不要堆填充内容

body.en:
Let gameplay test the story’s central pressure: gather incomplete evidence, manage a scarce resource, or choose whether to reveal something. Each added loop should create new feedback or understanding.

If a segment repeats an action without changing state, shorten it, add a meaningful decision, or keep it as concise narration instead of forcing interaction.
body.zh:
让玩法检验故事的核心压力：搜集不完整证据、管理稀缺资源，或决定是否揭示某事。新增循环都应带来新的反馈或理解。

如果一段内容重复行动却不改变状态，就缩短、加入有意义的决定，或用简洁叙述代替强行互动。

heading.en: Build a Complete Playable Payoff
heading.zh: 设计完整且可玩的回报

body.en:
Give players a clear objective and an ending that resolves or transforms the source’s main question. Optional paths can add context, but the core experience should not depend on hours of extra content.

Playtest whether the climax carries the same emotional force when the player has acted, not only watched. Adjust feedback, pacing, and choice consequences until the game’s payoff grows from its mechanics.
body.zh:
给玩家明确目标，并用结尾解决或转化原作的核心问题。可选路线可以补充背景，但核心体验不应依赖数小时额外内容。

试玩检验玩家亲自行动后，高潮是否仍有情感力量，而非只能旁观。调整反馈、节奏和选择后果，让游戏回报从玩法中生长出来。

q.en: Should an adaptation make a short story longer?
q.zh: 短篇改编成游戏时需要把故事拉长吗？

a.en: Only if the added play deepens the central conflict, viewpoint, or payoff. A concise game can preserve a short story better than a longer version padded with repeated tasks.
a.zh: 只有新增游玩能深化核心冲突、视角或回报时才需要扩展。简洁游戏有时比塞满重复任务的长版本更能保留短篇魅力。

title.en: How to Turn a Story Idea into a Clear Premise
title.zh: 怎样把故事创意发展成清晰前提

seo_title.en: Turn a Story Idea into a Premise

description.en: Define the protagonist, goal, obstacle, and change that make an idea capable of sustaining a story.
description.zh: 明确主角、目标、阻碍和变化，让创意能够支撑完整故事。

answer.en: Turn a story idea into a premise by naming who the story follows, what they want, what opposes them, and what could change if they act. Test the idea with one concrete situation and a consequence. If it only describes a world or theme, add a character decision that makes the concept move.
answer.zh: 通过明确故事跟随谁、人物想要什么、什么阻碍他们，以及行动可能带来什么变化，把创意发展成前提。用一个具体情境和后果检验它。如果创意只描述世界或主题，就加入推动概念发展的角色决定。

heading.en: Name the Character and What They Want
heading.zh: 明确人物是谁、想要什么

body.en:
Write the protagonist’s role in plain language, then state a goal they can pursue through action. “A city where memories can be sold” is a setting idea; “a clerk must recover the memory that proves her brother’s innocence” is a story direction.

Choose a goal that matters to this character and can create more than one attempt. A premise needs a person whose choices can carry it.
body.zh:
先用日常语言写出主角身份，再明确一个能通过行动追求的目标。“记忆可以买卖的城市”是设定创意；“一名职员必须找回证明哥哥清白的记忆”则是故事方向。

选择对人物重要、且可以引发多次尝试的目标。前提需要由人物选择来推动。

heading.en: Add Resistance and a Consequence
heading.zh: 加入阻力与后果

body.en:
Choose what makes the goal difficult: an opponent, a rule, limited time, a relationship, or a belief the protagonist holds. Explain why the obvious solution will not work.

Name what failure costs and what new option the protagonist may have to accept. Consequences turn a situation into a plot problem that can escalate.
body.zh:
选择让目标变难的因素：对手、规则、时间不足、关系，或主角自身的信念。说明显而易见的办法为何行不通。

明确失败的代价，以及主角可能不得不接受的新选项。后果能把情境变成可升级的情节问题。

heading.en: Test the Premise in One Scene
heading.zh: 用一个场景检验故事前提

body.en:
Imagine the first scene where the protagonist must act. State the immediate objective, obstacle, and result, then ask what new problem that result creates.

If the scene only explains the idea, find a choice that exposes its pressure. A workable premise generates scenes because the goal and resistance keep changing, not because the author adds unrelated events.
body.zh:
想象主角必须行动的第一个场景。写清眼前目标、阻碍和结果，再问这个结果带来什么新问题。

如果场景只是在介绍创意，就寻找能暴露压力的选择。可发展的前提会不断改变目标与阻力，而非依靠添加无关事件生成场景。

q.en: What is the difference between a story idea and a premise?
q.zh: 故事创意和故事前提有什么区别？

a.en: An idea may be a subject, setting, image, or question. A premise connects it to a protagonist, goal, resistance, and consequence so the writer can see how a story might develop.
a.zh: 创意可以是主题、设定、画面或问题；前提则把它连接到主角、目标、阻力和后果，让作者看见故事如何发展。

title.en: How to Revise a Novel for Better Pacing
title.zh: 修改小说节奏：找出拖慢或跳过的部分

seo_title.en: Revise a Novel for Better Pacing

description.en: Find slow, rushed, or repetitive sections by tracking scene changes, reader questions, and emotional intensity across the draft.
description.zh: 通过追踪场景变化、读者疑问和情绪强度，找出拖沓、仓促或重复的段落。

answer.en: Revise a novel’s pacing by mapping what changes in each scene or chapter: goal, knowledge, relationship, risk, or expectation. Mark long stretches with no meaningful change and fast turns that lack enough setup. Then cut repetition, expand the decision that matters, or move a reveal so the emotional rhythm feels deliberate.
answer.zh: 逐场或逐章标记目标、认知、关系、风险或预期发生了什么变化，以此修改小说节奏。圈出很久没有实质变化的段落，以及铺垫不足的快速转折。再删掉重复内容、扩写关键决定，或调整揭示位置，让情绪节奏更有意图。

heading.en: Map Changes Across the Draft
heading.zh: 梳理整份草稿中的变化

body.en:
Create a simple scene list and note what changes by the end of each scene. Include emotional intensity and any question the reader is waiting to have answered.

Look for several scenes in a row that repeat the same conflict, or a major reveal followed immediately by another before readers can absorb it. The pattern shows where pacing needs attention.
body.zh:
列出场景清单，记录每场结束时发生的变化，并标注情绪强度和读者等待回答的问题。

找出连续多场重复同一冲突的地方，或读者还来不及消化一个揭示就接着出现另一个揭示的部分。这些模式能指出节奏问题。

heading.en: Diagnose Slow and Rushed Sections
heading.zh: 判断哪些地方拖沓或过快

body.en:
A slow section may repeat intentions, delay a decision, or explain a result already visible. A rushed section may jump past a choice, emotional response, or causal step that makes the next event believable.

Ask whether the reader needs more time to understand, feel, or anticipate. Length alone does not determine pace; a quiet scene can move quickly when its relationship changes.
body.zh:
拖沓段落可能重复意图、推迟决定，或解释已经看得见的结果；仓促段落则可能跳过让后续可信所需的选择、情绪反应或因果步骤。

判断读者是否需要更多时间理解、感受或期待。篇幅本身不决定节奏；关系发生变化时，安静场景也能推进很快。

heading.en: Revise for Rhythm, Not Just Speed
heading.zh: 为节奏感修改，而不只是加快速度

body.en:
Cut repeated beats, combine scenes with the same job, or expand the decision that changes the story. Place a pause after a major consequence when the reader needs to register it.

Read the revision in sequence. Check that quieter moments alternate with pressure in a way that supports the genre and character arc, and that each acceleration has enough setup to feel earned.
body.zh:
删去重复节拍，合并作用相同的场景，或扩写真正改变故事的决定。重大后果之后，读者需要消化时就留出停顿。

按顺序通读修改稿，检查较平静的时刻是否与压力交替并服务类型和人物弧线，也要确认每次加速都有足够铺垫。

q.en: Does a fast-paced novel need short chapters?
q.zh: 节奏快的小说一定要用短章节吗？

a.en: No. Chapter length and story pace are related but not identical. A long chapter can move quickly through changing goals and consequences, while a short chapter can feel slow if nothing changes.
a.zh: 不一定。章节长度和故事节奏相关但不相同。目标与后果不断变化时，长章节也能推进很快；短章节若没有变化，也可能显得拖沓。

title.en: How to Write a Live Shopping Video Script
title.zh: 直播带货脚本怎么写得清楚可信

seo_title.en: Write a Live Shopping Video Script

description.en: Plan product demonstrations, audience questions, clear offer details, and a close that viewers can act on.
description.zh: 安排产品演示、观众提问、清晰的活动信息和可执行的收尾。

answer.en: Write a live shopping script as a flexible run of show: introduce the need, demonstrate the product, answer likely questions, explain accurate offer details, and give viewers a direct next step. Keep claims supportable, repeat essential information for late joiners, and leave room to respond to chat without losing the main sequence.
answer.zh: 把直播带货脚本写成灵活流程：介绍需求、演示产品、回答常见问题、说明准确的活动信息，并给出直接下一步。确保产品说法有依据，为中途进入的观众重复关键信息，同时给聊天互动留空间又不丢主线。

heading.en: Organize Products Around Viewer Needs
heading.zh: 围绕观众需求安排产品内容

body.en:
Choose the audience problem each product or feature addresses. Open with a useful context, then show the item in a real task instead of listing specifications without a reason.

Decide the order and transition between products. Mention only the inventory, price, eligibility, and timing details you can verify, and note which points must be repeated for late arrivals.
body.zh:
明确每件产品或功能解决什么观众问题。先交代有用场景，再在实际任务中展示产品，不要无缘由地逐条念规格。

安排产品顺序和转场。只介绍能够核实的库存、价格、适用条件与时间信息，并标记哪些内容要向后进入的观众重复。

heading.en: Demonstrate and Answer Questions Clearly
heading.zh: 清楚演示并回答问题

body.en:
Show the product from the angle that supports the claim: setup, use, comparison, or result. Give a moderator or host a question queue for safety, fit, limitations, and common objections.

Prepare a truthful fallback when chat asks something the host cannot verify. Do not guess; say what is known, what needs checking, and where an updated answer will appear.
body.zh:
从支撑产品说法的角度演示：安装、使用、对比或结果。为主持人或场控准备问题列表，覆盖安全、适用性、限制和常见顾虑。

遇到无法核实的问题时，准备诚实的回应方式。不要猜测；说明已知信息、需要确认的部分，以及之后在哪里更新答案。

heading.en: Close with Clear Offer Details and Next Steps
heading.zh: 清楚说明活动条件与下一步

body.en:
State the current offer, its conditions, and how viewers can act. Use a visible card or pinned link so spoken details do not have to carry everything.

Close the segment with a concise recap, then transition to the next item or audience question. Check the script against the final landing page and campaign terms before going live.
body.zh:
说明当前活动、适用条件和观众如何参与。用屏幕卡片或置顶链接展示信息，不要把所有内容都压在口播里。

用简短回顾结束产品段，再转到下一个商品或观众问题。开播前逐项核对脚本、最终页面和活动条款。

q.en: Should a live shopping stream script include every host line?
q.zh: 直播带货脚本要写出主持人的每句话吗？

a.en: Script exact offer details, product claims, transitions, and closing instructions. Use cue cards or a timed outline for demonstrations and questions so the host can respond naturally without losing accuracy.
a.zh: 活动条件、产品说法、转场和收尾指引适合写准确台词；演示和问答则用提示卡或计时提纲，让主持人自然回应又不失准确。

text.en: Use the video-recap workflow to plan, draft, and revise the work while keeping decisions and consistency visible.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Outline a Solo Podcast Video Episode
title.zh: 单人视频播客一期节目怎么列提纲

seo_title.en: Outline a Solo Podcast Episode

description.en: Give a solo episode one clear question, a sequence of useful ideas, and on-camera variation that keeps the audience oriented.
description.zh: 用一个核心问题串起实用观点，并安排镜头变化帮助观众跟上单人节目。

answer.en: Outline a solo podcast video around one audience question. Start with the promise, move through a few connected points with examples, and use changes in visual or delivery to mark transitions. A solo host does not need to sound improvised; a clear beat outline supports natural speech while keeping the episode focused.
answer.zh: 围绕观众的一个问题列单人视频播客提纲。先说明本期承诺，再用案例展开几个相连要点，并通过画面或表达变化标记转场。单人主持不必假装即兴；清楚的节拍提纲能让表达自然、主题聚焦。

heading.en: Choose One Listener Question and a Point of View
heading.zh: 选定一个听众问题和表达角度

body.en:
State the question the episode answers and what perspective or experience the host brings. Narrow the subject so listeners know what the episode will and will not cover.

Write the opening promise and a short first example. Avoid spending several minutes on introductions before viewers hear the episode’s value.
body.zh:
写清本期要回答的问题，以及主持人能提供什么角度或经验。收窄范围，让听众知道会讲什么、不会讲什么。

准备开场承诺和一个简短例子。不要先花几分钟自我介绍，让观众迟迟听不到节目价值。

heading.en: Structure the Points as a Conversational Argument
heading.zh: 把要点组织成自然的口头论证

body.en:
Arrange points in a sequence: what is happening, why it matters, an example, and what the listener can do with the insight. Add transitions that explain how one point leads to the next.

Use notes rather than writing every line when the topic is familiar. Script exact wording for definitions, sensitive claims, or complex explanations that must remain precise.
body.zh:
按“发生了什么、为何重要、举例说明、听众可以怎么用”安排要点，并用转场解释前后关系。

熟悉的主题可以用提示笔记，不必逐字写完。定义、敏感说法或必须准确的复杂解释，则应提前写好。

heading.en: Plan Visual Variation and a Clear Close
heading.zh: 安排画面变化并清楚收尾

body.en:
Note when to use a prop, screen share, graphic, chapter label, or camera change. Every visual should clarify, demonstrate, or signal a new section rather than decorate the frame.

Summarize the answer and give one next action. Read the outline aloud to find repeated points and check that the episode title matches what the host actually covers.
body.zh:
标出何时使用物件、屏幕共享、图示、章节标题或镜头变化。每个画面都应解释、演示或标记新章节，而不只是装饰。

总结答案并给出一个下一步。朗读提纲，找出重复要点，并确认节目标题符合实际内容。

q.en: Should a solo video podcast be fully scripted?
q.zh: 单人视频播客需要写完整台词吗？

a.en: Use a full script when accuracy or timing matters; use a detailed outline for familiar topics where natural delivery is useful. Test a short section on camera and adjust the scripting level.
a.zh: 准确性或时长很重要时用完整稿；熟悉且适合自然表达的主题可用详细提纲。先对镜试讲一小段，再调整稿件细度。

text.en: Use the video-recap workflow to plan, draft, and revise the work while keeping decisions and consistency visible.
text.zh: 使用 video-recap 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Plan a Live Panel Discussion
title.zh: 直播圆桌讨论流程怎么设计

seo_title.en: Plan a Live Panel Discussion

description.en: Give a panel one audience question, distinct speaker roles, balanced turns, and a useful synthesis at the end.
description.zh: 围绕一个观众问题安排嘉宾分工、均衡发言和有用的总结。

answer.en: Plan a live panel around one audience question and a sequence that gives each speaker a distinct contribution. Set ground rules, prepare follow-ups and time cues, and decide how the moderator will handle disagreement or unanswered questions. Close by synthesizing the panel’s useful points instead of ending as soon as the scheduled time runs out.
answer.zh: 围绕观众的一个问题规划直播圆桌，并安排能体现嘉宾不同贡献的讨论顺序。设定基本规则，准备追问和时间提示，决定主持人如何处理分歧或未答问题。结尾要提炼有用观点，不要时间一到就仓促结束。

heading.en: Define the Question and Speaker Roles
heading.zh: 明确讨论问题与嘉宾分工

body.en:
Choose a question narrow enough for the allotted time. Invite speakers who bring different but relevant experience, and note what each can clarify.

Tell panelists the format, audience, time limit, and whether they may disagree. This helps keep the conversation focused without requiring identical opinions.
body.zh:
选择适合既定时长的聚焦问题。邀请经验不同但相关的嘉宾，并标注每个人可以说明什么。

提前告知嘉宾讨论形式、受众、时限和是否允许公开分歧。这样能保持聚焦，也不要求观点完全一致。

heading.en: Sequence Discussion Rounds and Follow-Ups
heading.zh: 安排讨论轮次与追问

body.en:
Open with a shared framing question, then move to concrete examples, disagreement, and audience questions. Give each speaker room to answer without asking everyone to repeat the same point.

Prepare neutral follow-ups for vague claims and a time cue for long answers. Decide how questions will be selected and what the moderator will say when no clear answer is available.
body.zh:
先用共同的框架问题开场，再转向具体案例、分歧和观众提问。给每位嘉宾充分表达空间，不要让每个人重复相同观点。

为模糊说法准备中性追问，为冗长回答准备时间提示。确定如何挑选观众问题，也决定没有明确答案时主持人如何回应。

heading.en: Synthesize and Close the Panel
heading.zh: 综合观点并完成讨论收尾

body.en:
Reserve time for the moderator to summarize points of agreement, meaningful differences, and a useful next step. Invite each speaker to add one concise final thought if the format allows.

Prepare a backup closing in case technical problems or an overlong answer cut the discussion short. Make sure viewers can find the recording, sources, or follow-up resources mentioned during the panel.
body.zh:
预留时间让主持人总结共识、重要分歧和实用下一步。形式允许时，可让每位嘉宾补充一句简短结语。

若技术问题或超时回答压缩讨论，准备备用收尾。确保观众能找到圆桌中提到的回放、资料来源或后续资源。

q.en: How many panelists should a live discussion have?
q.zh: 直播讨论应该邀请几位嘉宾？

a.en: Invite only as many speakers as the audience can follow within the available time. Each panelist should add a distinct perspective, and the moderator needs enough room to connect their answers.
a.zh: 嘉宾数量以观众能在既定时长内听清为准。每位嘉宾都应带来不同视角，并给主持人留出串联回答的时间。

text.zh: 使用 video-recap 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Write a Customer Testimonial Video Script
title.zh: 客户证言视频脚本怎么写得真实

seo_title.en: Customer Testimonial Video Script

description.en: Help a customer tell a specific before-and-after story with claims, context, and outcomes viewers can understand.
description.zh: 帮助客户讲清具体的前后变化、背景和观众能理解的结果。

answer.en: Write a customer testimonial video as a guided story, not a list of praise. Establish the customer’s situation, the problem they needed to solve, what they actually did, and the result they can support. Ask open questions, preserve important context, and distinguish personal experience from a general product claim.
answer.zh: 把客户证言视频写成有引导的故事，而不是赞美清单。交代客户原本处境、要解决的问题、实际做过什么，以及能够证明的结果。使用开放式问题，保留重要背景，并区分个人体验与普遍产品说法。

heading.en: Choose a Specific Customer Story
heading.zh: 选择一个具体的客户故事

body.en:
Select a customer whose experience illustrates a real use case and who can describe the context in their own words. Define the audience the story serves and what viewers should understand after watching.

Agree on the facts, permissions, and topics that should remain private before recording. Do not promise results that the customer cannot document or that depend on conditions the video omits.
body.zh:
选择经历能说明真实用途、也能用自己的话讲清背景的客户。明确故事服务哪类观众、观众看完要理解什么。

录制前确认事实、授权和需要保密的内容。不要承诺客户无法证明的结果，也不要删去会改变结论的条件。

heading.en: Ask Open Questions and Preserve Context
heading.zh: 用开放问题提问并保留语境

body.en:
Ask what the customer was trying to do, what made it difficult, what they tried, and what changed. Follow up for a concrete example or measure rather than suggesting the answer in the question.

Keep meaningful qualifications and time frames. Edit for clarity, but do not splice statements into a claim the customer did not make.
body.zh:
询问客户当时想做什么、难点在哪里、尝试过什么，以及后来有何变化。追问具体例子或衡量方式，不要在问题里暗示答案。

保留重要条件和时间范围。可以为清晰度剪辑，但不能把不同说法拼成客户从未表达过的结论。

heading.en: Shape the Story and Review Every Claim
heading.zh: 组织故事并复核每项说法

body.en:
Arrange the interview as situation, decision, experience, and outcome. Use only supporting details that help viewers understand the change.

Review the final edit with the customer for factual accuracy and confirm that captions, figures, and product descriptions match the source. Close with a next step that fits the viewer’s needs rather than an unsupported guarantee.
body.zh:
按原有处境、决定、使用体验和结果组织访谈，只保留帮助观众理解变化的细节。

请客户核对最终成片的事实准确性，并确认字幕、数字和产品描述与资料一致。结尾给出符合观众需求的下一步，不做没有依据的保证。

q.en: Should I give a customer exact lines to say in a testimonial?
q.zh: 客户证言需要提前写好逐字台词吗？

a.en: Prepare prompts and clarify the story goal, but let customers describe their experience in their own words. Script narration or transitions separately, and verify any factual edits with the speaker.
a.zh: 准备提问并说明故事目标，但让客户用自己的话描述经历。旁白和转场可以单独写稿；事实性剪辑应由讲述者核实。

text.zh: 使用 video-recap 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Design a Story for a Survival Game
title.zh: 生存游戏的故事怎么围绕资源压力展开

seo_title.en: Design a Survival Game Story

description.en: Make resource decisions, environmental risks, and changing trust advance both survival and character story.
description.zh: 让资源取舍、环境风险和信任变化同时推动生存与人物故事。

answer.en: Design a survival game story around the choices players make to stay alive and the costs those choices impose. Connect scarce resources, environmental threats, and relationships to clear goals. Let success and failure change what the group can do next, so survival mechanics produce narrative consequences rather than repeating pressure without progress.
answer.zh: 围绕玩家为生存作出的选择及其代价来设计故事。把稀缺资源、环境威胁和关系连接到明确目标。让成功与失败改变群体下一步能做什么，使生存机制带来剧情后果，而非不断重复压力却没有进展。

heading.en: Connect Survival Needs to Story Goals
heading.zh: 把生存需求连接到故事目标

body.en:
Give the group an immediate need—food, shelter, medicine, safe passage—and a reason it matters beyond filling a meter. The need can expose a disagreement or require travel into a risky place.

Keep a longer objective visible, such as reaching safety or protecting someone. Short-term survival choices should affect the route or cost of pursuing it.
body.zh:
为群体设定眼前需求：食物、住所、药品或安全通道，并说明它为何不只是填满数值条。需求可以暴露分歧，也可能迫使人物进入危险地点。

让长期目标保持清楚，例如抵达安全处或保护某人。短期生存选择要影响追求长期目标的路线或代价。

heading.en: Make Resource Choices Carry a Cost
heading.zh: 让资源选择承担后果

body.en:
Decide what resources are limited, how players obtain them, and what they must give up when supplies run low. A choice can affect health, time, trust, or a future opportunity.

Avoid making every shortage a punishment with no response. Give players information and a meaningful decision, then show the outcome in the world or in a relationship.
body.zh:
明确哪些资源有限、玩家如何获得，以及短缺时必须放弃什么。选择可以影响健康、时间、信任或未来机会。

不要让每次短缺都变成无法回应的惩罚。提供足够信息和有意义的决定，再通过世界或关系展示结果。

heading.en: Let Survival Change Relationships
heading.zh: 让生存压力改变关系

body.en:
Give group members different priorities, skills, and limits. Show how the player’s treatment of others affects later cooperation, information, or conflict.

Track who knows what and what the group has lost or gained. When players can reach encounters in different orders, keep character responses consistent with their actual history.
body.zh:
让群体成员拥有不同优先级、技能和限制。展示玩家如何对待他人，并让这种待遇影响后续合作、信息或冲突。

记录每个人知道什么、群体失去或得到什么。玩家以不同顺序抵达相遇时，人物回应要符合实际经历。

q.en: Should a survival game punish every failed resource check?
q.zh: 生存游戏每次资源检定失败都要惩罚玩家吗？

a.en: Failure should create a consequence that players can understand and respond to. Vary setbacks with lost time, changed plans, or relationship pressure rather than relying only on health loss.
a.zh: 失败应带来玩家能理解并回应的后果。可以改变时间、计划或关系压力，不要只依赖扣生命值来制造挫折。

text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Design a Story for a Horror Game
title.zh: 恐怖游戏的故事怎么结合玩家行动

seo_title.en: Design a Horror Game Story

description.en: Build dread through player choices, readable threat rules, and discoveries that change how a space feels.
description.zh: 通过玩家选择、清楚的威胁规则和改变空间感受的发现营造恐惧。

answer.en: Design a horror game story so the player understands the immediate goal but remains uncertain about danger, knowledge, or cost. Tie fear to mechanics: limited resources, risky observation, hiding, or escape. Reveal what the threat can do through consequences, and make discoveries change the player’s plan rather than pause play for exposition.
answer.zh: 让恐怖游戏玩家清楚眼前目标，同时对危险、信息或代价保持不确定。把恐惧连接到玩法：稀缺资源、带风险的观察、躲藏或逃脱。通过后果揭示威胁能做什么，并让新发现改变计划，而不是暂停游玩讲解设定。

heading.en: Give the Player a Readable Immediate Goal
heading.zh: 给玩家清楚的眼前目标

body.en:
State what the player is trying to reach, learn, or protect. Keep uncertainty around what may happen, not around basic controls or the next obvious objective.

Use sound, light, space, and interface feedback to signal risk consistently. A mystery can feel unsettling without making the player guess what the game is asking them to do.
body.zh:
说明玩家要抵达、查明或保护什么。可以让后果未知，但不要让基本操作或下一步明显目标也含糊不清。

用声音、光线、空间和界面反馈持续传递风险。谜团可以令人不安，但不该让玩家猜游戏要他们做什么。

heading.en: Tie Fear to Decisions and Limited Resources
heading.zh: 把恐惧连接到决定与资源限制

body.en:
Let the player decide whether to investigate, conserve supplies, make noise, or take a risky route. Make the cost legible enough that the choice feels tense rather than arbitrary.

Use quiet moments to let players anticipate danger, then change what they believe through a consequence or new evidence. Repeating a loud surprise without altering the plan quickly loses effect.
body.zh:
让玩家决定是否调查、保留物资、制造声音或走危险路线。代价要清楚到让选择紧张，却不显得随意。

用安静时刻让玩家预想危险，再通过后果或新证据改变他们的判断。若惊吓只重复出现，却不改变计划，很快就会失效。

heading.en: Make Discoveries Change the Meaning of a Space
heading.zh: 让发现改变空间的含义

body.en:
Reveal how a room, object, or repeated route connects to the threat or character history. After a discovery, adjust sound, access, enemy behavior, or the player’s objective so the space feels different.

Track what the player knows and when. If a clue is optional, do not make it the only way to understand a mandatory danger or ending.
body.zh:
揭示房间、物件或重复路线如何联系威胁或人物经历。发现之后，可以改变声音、通行、敌人行为或玩家目标，让空间感受随之变化。

追踪玩家何时知道什么。可选线索不要成为理解必经危险或结局的唯一途径。

q.en: Should horror game players be able to fight back?
q.zh: 恐怖游戏要让玩家反击吗？

a.en: That depends on the intended fear and gameplay. If players can fight, make ammunition, timing, or consequences support the tension; if they cannot, give them understandable ways to hide, observe, or escape.
a.zh: 取决于预期恐惧感和玩法。允许反击时，让弹药、时机或后果支撑紧张；不能反击时，也要提供可理解的躲藏、观察或逃脱方法。

text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Write a Story for an Adventure Game
title.zh: 冒险游戏的故事怎么跟着探索推进

seo_title.en: Write an Adventure Game Story

description.en: Connect exploration, puzzles, and character decisions so discoveries move the story forward.
description.zh: 连接探索、谜题和人物决定，让发现推动剧情发展。

answer.en: Write an adventure game story by giving the player a goal that exploration can advance and puzzles can meaningfully complicate. Make discoveries change what the player knows or can do, and provide enough feedback to show why a clue or solution matters. Let the ending pay off the journey’s central question.
answer.zh: 给玩家一个能通过探索推进、又会被谜题有意义地复杂化的目标，以此编写冒险游戏故事。让发现改变玩家认知或行动能力，并提供足够反馈说明线索或解法为何重要。让结尾兑现旅程的核心问题。

heading.en: Set a Goal That Exploration Can Advance
heading.zh: 设定能通过探索推进的目标

body.en:
Tell players what they are trying to find, repair, learn, or reach. Use locations that offer new context or obstacles rather than spaces that exist only to be crossed.

Give an immediate next step while keeping the wider question open. A player should understand why a location is relevant even when the solution is not yet obvious.
body.zh:
说明玩家要寻找、修复、弄清或抵达什么。地点应提供新背景或阻碍，而不是只供穿越。

给出眼前下一步，同时保留更大的疑问。即使解法尚不明显，玩家也应理解该地点为何相关。

heading.en: Make Puzzles Change Story State
heading.zh: 让谜题改变剧情状态

body.en:
Connect each puzzle to a discovery, access change, relationship, or decision. Teach the rule before combining it with harder challenges, and give feedback that helps players understand their progress.

If solving a puzzle only opens another locked door, make sure the new space changes the goal, reveals useful information, or creates a different kind of play.
body.zh:
让每道谜题关联发现、通行变化、关系或决定。先教会规则，再组合更难挑战，并提供帮助玩家理解进度的反馈。

如果解谜只为再打开一扇锁门，就确保新空间会改变目标、揭示有用信息，或带来不同玩法。

heading.en: Let Player Reasoning Drive the Payoff
heading.zh: 让玩家推理推动剧情回报

body.en:
Place important clues where players can notice them, and keep required solutions consistent with the rules the game taught. A useful hint can redirect attention without solving the puzzle outright.

At the end, connect the player’s discoveries to the characters and central conflict. The solution should feel like a result of the journey, not an unrelated explanation that appears in the final scene.
body.zh:
把重要线索放在玩家能发现的位置，必要解法也要符合游戏教过的规则。提示可以引导注意力，但不必直接说出答案。

结尾要把玩家的发现和人物、核心冲突连接起来。解决方案应像旅程的结果，而不是最后一场戏突然出现的无关解释。

q.en: How do you keep an adventure game from getting stuck?
q.zh: 怎样避免玩家在冒险游戏里卡关？

a.en: Make goals and clue relationships readable, then provide graduated hints when players stall. Preserve the challenge of reasoning while ensuring they can discover what kind of information or action they need next.
a.zh: 让目标和线索关系清楚，并在玩家停滞时逐步提供提示。保留推理挑战，同时让玩家能发现下一步需要什么信息或行动。

text.en: Use the novel-to-game workflow to plan, draft, and revise the work while keeping decisions and consistency visible.
text.zh: 使用 novel-to-game 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Choose a Point of View for a Novel
title.zh: 小说视角怎么选

seo_title.en: How to Choose a Point of View for a Novel

description.en: Choose the point of view that gives readers the right access to the conflict while preserving what the story needs to withhold.
description.zh: 选择能让读者理解冲突、又保留必要悬念的叙事视角。

answer.en: Choose the point of view that gives readers the right access to the conflict while preserving what the story needs to withhold. Test a pivotal scene in two viewpoints before committing.
answer.zh: 选择能让读者理解冲突、又保留必要悬念的叙事视角。先用两种视角试写关键场景，再决定全书采用哪一种。

heading.en: Start with the reader’s question
heading.zh: 先明确读者需要知道什么

body.en: List what the reader must know, may wonder about, and should not learn yet. A close first-person voice creates intimacy and limits information; third person can stay close to one character or move between characters when the story needs broader access.
body.zh: 先列出读者必须知道、可以好奇、暂时不该知道的信息。第一人称贴近人物，但受限于叙述者所知；第三人称既能贴近单个角色，也能按需要切换人物视角。

heading.en: Test the same scene twice
heading.zh: 把同一场景试写两遍

body.en: Draft a scene where the protagonist makes a consequential choice in two plausible viewpoints. Compare how much tension comes from access to thoughts, what the reader can infer from behavior, and how naturally each version handles information the viewpoint character does not know.
body.zh: 挑选主角做出重要决定的一场戏，用两种合适的视角各写一遍。比较内心信息带来的张力、读者能否从行为推断情况，以及叙述者如何处理视角人物不知道的事。

heading.en: Keep the rule consistent
heading.zh: 保持视角规则稳定

body.en: After choosing, mark every point where the narration reports a thought, sensation, or fact. Confirm the viewpoint character could know it. If you switch viewpoint, make the transition legible with a scene break and a clear new anchor.
body.zh: 确定视角后，检查每处内心、感受和事实信息，确认视角人物确实能够知道。若要切换人物，应通过分场和明确的新视角锚点让读者跟得上。

q.en: Can a novel change point of view?
q.zh: 小说可以切换叙事视角吗？

a.en: Yes, when each switch is clear and serves the story. Give a new viewpoint its own scene or chapter and a distinct reason to exist.
a.zh: 可以，但每次切换都要清楚且对故事有用。最好用新的场景或章节承接，并让新视角提供不可替代的信息。

text.zh: 使用 oh-story 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Write a Novel with Multiple POVs
title.zh: 多视角小说怎么写

seo_title.en: How to Write a Novel with Multiple POVs

description.en: Give each viewpoint character a distinct role in the central conflict, then make every switch change what readers know or expect.
description.zh: 让每位视角人物都以不同方式参与核心冲突，并确保每次切换都会改变读者掌握的信息或预期。

answer.en: Give each viewpoint character a distinct role in the central conflict, then make every switch change what readers know or expect. A viewpoint that adds no new pressure or information can usually be cut.
answer.zh: 让每位视角人物都以不同方式参与核心冲突，并确保每次切换都会改变读者掌握的信息或预期。若某个视角没有带来新信息或压力，通常可以删去。

heading.en: Assign each viewpoint a story job
heading.zh: 给每个视角安排叙事作用

body.en: Write one sentence for each character describing what only their viewpoint can reveal: a hidden cost, a competing goal, or the consequence of another character’s decision. Avoid adding viewpoints merely to repeat an event.
body.zh: 用一句话说明每位角色的视角能独家揭示什么：隐藏代价、相互冲突的目标，或他人决定造成的后果。不要只为重复同一事件而增加视角。

heading.en: Plan switches around change
heading.zh: 围绕变化安排切换

body.en: Place a switch when the current scene has produced a result and a different character can complicate its meaning. Track time, location, and knowledge so two characters do not unknowingly narrate the same beat without a fresh consequence.
body.zh: 当前场景已经产生结果、另一位人物能让结果变得复杂时，再考虑切换视角。记录时间、地点和各自掌握的信息，避免两人重复叙述同一段而没有新后果。

heading.en: Audit voice and balance
heading.zh: 检查声音与篇幅平衡

body.en: Read only the opening paragraphs assigned to each character. The vocabulary, attention, and judgments should reveal who is noticing the world. Compare page time with story importance, then give each viewpoint a meaningful decision rather than an equal chapter quota.
body.zh: 只读每位人物视角的开篇段落，检查词汇、关注点和判断是否能区分人物。再比较篇幅和剧情重要性，让每个视角都做出有意义的选择，不必机械平均章节数。

q.en: How many POV characters should a novel have?
q.zh: 一部小说应该有几个视角人物？

a.en: Use the fewest viewpoints needed to show the full conflict. Add a character only when their perspective creates a different decision, consequence, or piece of evidence.
a.zh: 用能完整呈现冲突的最少视角即可。只有当新视角能带来不同决定、后果或证据时，才值得加入。

title.en: How to Write a Romance Scene That Changes the Relationship
title.zh: 爱情场景怎样推动关系变化

seo_title.en: How to Write a Romance Scene That Changes the Relationship
seo_title.zh: 爱情场景怎样推动关系变化

description.en: Build a romance scene around a choice that changes what the characters can admit, trust, or risk with each other.
description.zh: 围绕一个会改变角色坦白程度、信任或承担风险的选择来写爱情场景。

answer.en: Build a romance scene around a choice that changes what the characters can admit, trust, or risk with each other. Let the next scene show the consequence so the relationship does not reset.
answer.zh: 围绕一个会改变角色坦白程度、信任或承担风险的选择来写爱情场景。下一场要呈现选择的后果，避免关系无故回到原点。

heading.en: Name the relationship’s current limit
heading.zh: 明确关系目前的边界

body.en: Before drafting, state what the characters want from each other and what each fears losing. A useful scene presses on one boundary—honesty, time, loyalty, or vulnerability—instead of relying on a romantic setting to create intimacy by itself.
body.zh: 动笔前写明角色想从对方得到什么，又各自害怕失去什么。有效场景会触碰一条边界，例如诚实、时间、忠诚或脆弱，而不是只靠浪漫布景制造亲密感。

heading.en: Make an action carry the risk
heading.zh: 让行动承载风险

body.en: Give one character a concrete action that could change the relationship: asking a difficult question, sharing a costly truth, or showing up when leaving would be easier. Let the other character respond in a way that confirms, refuses, or reshapes the offer.
body.zh: 安排一项可能改变关系的具体行动：提出难回答的问题、坦白代价高的事实，或在离开更容易时选择留下。让对方以接受、拒绝或重新定义这份心意作答。

heading.en: Track the aftereffect
heading.zh: 写出场景之后的影响

body.en: Carry the scene into later behavior. A new confidence may allow cooperation but make a lie harder to hide; a rejection may force a character to change their plan. If nothing in later scenes is different, sharpen the choice or cut the scene.
body.zh: 让场景影响后续行为。新的信任可能促成合作，却让隐瞒更困难；一次拒绝也可能迫使人物改变计划。若后续没有任何变化，就强化选择的分量或删掉场景。

q.en: Does every romance scene need a confession or kiss?
q.zh: 每个爱情场景都要告白或接吻吗？

a.en: No. A change in trust, honesty, boundaries, or willingness to take a risk can move the relationship even when the characters do not name their feelings.
a.zh: 不需要。信任、坦诚、边界或承担风险的意愿发生变化，都能推动关系，即使人物没有说出自己的感情。

text.zh: 使用 oh-story 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Use Foreshadowing in a Novel
title.zh: 小说伏笔怎么埋

seo_title.en: How to Use Foreshadowing in a Novel

description.en: Foreshadow a later event with an earlier detail that feels natural now and gains meaning after the reveal.
description.zh: 用前文中自然出现的细节为后续事件铺垫，让它在揭示之后获得新含义。

answer.en: Foreshadow a later event with an earlier detail that feels natural now and gains meaning after the reveal. The clue should reward attention without making the outcome certain too soon.
answer.zh: 用前文中自然出现的细节为后续事件铺垫，让它在揭示之后获得新含义。线索应奖励读者留意，但不要过早让结局变得确定。

heading.en: Choose the payoff first
heading.zh: 先确定伏笔要回收什么

body.en: Write down the later revelation, decision, or danger the clue will support. Then identify what the reader should recognize in retrospect. This keeps the detail tied to a real payoff instead of adding ominous objects or suspicious lines at random.
body.zh: 先写清伏笔要支撑哪项揭示、决定或危险，再确定读者回头看时应该认出什么。这样细节会服务于真实回收，而不是随意堆放阴森物件或可疑台词。

heading.en: Plant it in a scene with another purpose
heading.zh: 把伏笔放进有其他任务的场景

body.en: Introduce the clue while the scene is already advancing character or conflict. Give it an ordinary explanation at first and avoid spotlighting it with an unnatural pause. Repetition can help, but each recurrence should add context or alter the reader’s interpretation.
body.zh: 趁场景正在推进人物或冲突时引入线索。初次出现时给它一个普通解释，不要用不自然的停顿刻意强调。可以重复出现，但每次都要补充背景或改变读者的理解。

heading.en: Check fairness after the reveal
heading.zh: 揭示后检查线索是否公平

body.en: Read the setup and payoff together. The ending should make the earlier clue clearer, not invent a new rule or hidden fact. Remove clues that point too directly to the answer, and strengthen any reveal that depends on information the reader never received.
body.zh: 把铺垫和回收连起来检查。结局应让早先线索更清晰，而非临时发明新规则或隐情。删去过于直接泄底的线索，并补足读者此前根本没得到的信息。

q.en: How early should foreshadowing appear?
q.zh: 伏笔应该提前多久出现？

a.en: Plant it early enough for the detail to feel earned, but close enough that readers can remember or rediscover it. The right distance depends on the story’s pace and the importance of the payoff.
a.zh: 应早到让结果显得有铺垫，也要近到读者能记住或重新发现。具体间隔取决于故事节奏和回收的重要程度。

text.zh: 使用 oh-story 工作流规划、起草和修改作品，同时看清创作决定与前后连续。

title.en: How to Write an Unreliable Narrator
title.zh: 不可靠叙述者怎么写

seo_title.en: How to Write an Unreliable Narrator

description.en: Let the narrator’s account differ from the evidence readers can observe, and give the gap a character-based reason.
description.zh: 让叙述者的说法与读者能观察到的证据存在差距，并为这种差距安排符合人物的原因。

answer.en: Let the narrator’s account differ from the evidence readers can observe, and give the gap a character-based reason. Readers should be able to question the account without needing information the story has hidden unfairly.
answer.zh: 让叙述者的说法与读者能观察到的证据存在差距，并为这种差距安排符合人物的原因。读者应能质疑叙述，却不必依赖故事不公平地藏起的信息。

heading.en: Decide why the account is unreliable
heading.zh: 确定叙述不可靠的原因

body.en: Choose whether the narrator is mistaken, self-protective, limited, or deliberately deceptive. These causes create different reading experiences. A narrator who lies to avoid shame needs different clues from one who misunderstands a situation honestly.
body.zh: 先决定叙述者是误解事实、自我保护、视野受限，还是有意欺骗。不同原因会带来不同阅读体验。为避免羞耻而说谎的人，需要与真诚误读局势的人不同的线索。

heading.en: Give readers observable evidence
heading.zh: 提供读者能观察的证据

body.en: Place contradictions in actions, records, other characters’ reactions, or details the narrator dismisses too quickly. Keep the narrator’s voice coherent; an unexplained change in tone can feel like an author hiding the answer rather than a person revealing a blind spot.
body.zh: 把矛盾放在行动、记录、他人反应，或叙述者轻轻带过的细节里。保持叙述声音连贯；无缘由的语气变化会像作者在藏答案，而非人物暴露盲点。

heading.en: Make the discovery change the story
heading.zh: 让发现改变故事走向

body.en: A reveal should revise what readers believe about motive, responsibility, or risk. Revisit earlier scenes to check that the truth was available in some form. End with a consequence for the narrator, not only a clever explanation.
body.zh: 揭示应改变读者对动机、责任或风险的判断。回查早期场景，确认真相曾以某种形式出现。结尾应让叙述者承担后果，而不只是给出巧妙解释。

q.en: Can an unreliable narrator lie to the reader?
q.zh: 不可靠叙述者可以对读者撒谎吗？

a.en: Yes, but the story should offer clues that make the lie retrospectively understandable. Deliberately withholding basic facts without a character reason can make readers feel tricked rather than engaged.
a.zh: 可以，但故事应提供能让读者事后理解谎言的线索。若没有人物动机却刻意隐瞒基本事实，读者会觉得被耍，而不是参与推理。

title.en: How to Write a Mystery with Fair Clues
title.zh: 悬疑小说怎么公平铺线索

seo_title.en: How to Write a Mystery with Fair Clues
seo_title.zh: 悬疑小说怎么公平铺线索

description.en: Give readers access to the important evidence before the solution, then make the answer follow from facts the detective could explain.
description.zh: 在揭晓之前让读者看到关键证据，并确保答案能从侦探解释的事实中推出。

answer.en: Give readers access to the important evidence before the solution, then make the answer follow from facts the detective could explain. Red herrings can distract, but they should not depend on false rules or withheld essentials.
answer.zh: 在揭晓之前让读者看到关键证据，并确保答案能从侦探解释的事实中推出。误导线索可以分散注意力，但不能依赖虚假规则或被藏起来的必要信息。

heading.en: Build the solution backward
heading.zh: 从真相反向搭建线索

body.en: Decide who did what, why, and how before planting clues. List the evidence that proves each part of the explanation, then separate what the detective sees from what the reader can reasonably notice. This prevents the ending from relying on a last-minute fact.
body.zh: 先确定谁做了什么、为什么、如何做到，再安排线索。列出能证明每部分解释的证据，并区分侦探看见什么、读者合理上能注意到什么，避免结局靠临时补充事实。

heading.en: Give each clue a scene-level purpose
heading.zh: 让每条线索在场景中发挥作用

body.en: Introduce evidence through an active scene: a search, interview, argument, or contradiction. A clue can have an innocent first interpretation, but later context should change its meaning. Make red herrings plausible and traceable to a character’s real motive or misunderstanding.
body.zh: 通过搜查、访谈、争执或矛盾来呈现证据。线索初看可以有无害解释，但后续背景应改变其含义。误导线索应合情合理，并能追溯到人物的真实动机或误解。

heading.en: Audit the reveal
heading.zh: 审查最终揭晓

body.en: At the solution, show how the evidence connects and why the obvious alternatives fail. Then reread as a first-time reader: mark every fact needed to solve the case and confirm it appeared before the answer. Repair missing evidence or adjust the solution.
body.zh: 揭晓时说明证据如何相连，以及显而易见的其他解释为何不成立。再以初读者视角检查：标出解案所需的每项事实，确认它们都在答案前出现。补足缺失证据，或调整真相。

q.en: Should readers be able to solve the mystery before the detective?
q.zh: 读者应该能比侦探更早破案吗？

a.en: They should have a fair chance to form a theory from the same essential evidence. The detective may interpret clues differently, but the solution should not rely on facts readers could never access.
a.zh: 读者应有机会根据相同的关键证据提出猜测。侦探可以有不同解读，但答案不应依赖读者从未接触到的事实。
